class ClockworkKeepScene(Scene):
    """One floor of the clockwork tower.

    Each floor is a separate Scene instance. Elevators trigger
    scene transitions to the next floor.
    """

    NAME = 'Clockwork Keep'
    VERSION = '1.0'
    # Cap dt so a hitch (focus loss, Cmd-Tab, ...) advances the game at most 50 ms (20 fps).
    # The engine caps the dt dt_tick and the camera aim receive. A capped tick still moves a
    # falling Tinker 40 px, so the ground check sweeps the fall (_resolve_ground_collision)
    # rather than relying on the cap to keep it from passing through a platform
    MAX_FRAME_SECONDS = 0.05

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        floor_index: int | None = None,
        player_score: int = 0,
        player_lives: int = 3,
        options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the floor scene.

        Args:
            floor_index: Which floor (0=Boiler Room, 1=Gear Works, 2=Clock Face). None (the
                engine's first scene, built from options alone) takes the --floor option.
            player_score: Score carried from previous floor.
            player_lives: Lives carried from previous floor.
            options: Command-line options.
            groups: Sprite group.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()
        super().__init__(options=options, groups=groups)

        self.floor_index = self._starting_floor_index(floor_index=floor_index, options=options)
        # The score and lives carried onto this floor, as it began (replay_arguments)
        self.starting_player_score = player_score
        self.starting_player_lives = player_lives
        self.floor_data: FloorData = ALL_FLOORS[self.floor_index]
        # Game time on this floor (capped dt, frozen after game over); drives the floor-3 clock
        self.floor_elapsed_time: float = 0.0

        # Theme colors
        platform_color, top_color, self.led_color = _FLOOR_THEMES[self.floor_index]

        # Background
        bg_color = [
            (40, 25, 15),  # Boiler Room
            (35, 35, 40),  # Gear Works
            (15, 15, 35),  # Clock Face
        ][self.floor_index]
        self.background_color = bg_color

        # Camera: vertical scroll only (tower is 1 screen wide)
        self.camera = Camera2D(
            screen_width=self.screen_width,
            screen_height=self.screen_height,
            lead_x=CAMERA_LEAD_X,
            lead_y=CAMERA_LEAD_Y,
            shake_intensity=self.options.get('screen_shake_intensity', 1.0),
        )
        self.camera.set_bounds(
            min_x=0.0,
            max_x=0.0,  # No horizontal scroll
            min_y=0.0,
            max_y=float(self.floor_data.height - self.screen_height),
        )

        # Background parallax
        shows_clock = _FLOOR_BACKGROUNDS[self.floor_index] is draw_clock_background
        bg_func = (
            self._draw_timed_clock_background
            if shows_clock
            else _FLOOR_BACKGROUNDS[self.floor_index]
        )
        self.camera.add_background_layer(
            scroll_factor=PARALLAX_FAR,
            draw_function=bg_func,
            layer_depth=LAYER_FAR_BACKGROUND,
            groups=self.all_sprites,
            # The clock's hands show the floor's elapsed game time, not just the camera offset,
            # so that layer redraws every frame; the other floors' walls depend on camera_y only
            animated=shows_clock,
        )

        # Build terrain (in this order: sprites of one layer draw in the order they are added)
        self.platform_sprites: list[Platform] = self._build_platforms(
            platform_color=platform_color, top_color=top_color
        )
        self.elevator_sprites: list[Elevator] = self._build_elevators()
        self.moving_gear_sprites: list[MovingGear] = self._build_moving_gears()
        self.collectible_sprites: list[CogCollectible] = self._build_collectibles()

        # Player
        self.player = Tinker(
            world_x=float(self.floor_data.spawn_x),
            world_y=float(self.floor_data.spawn_y),
            groups=self.all_sprites,
        )
        self.player.score = player_score
        self.player.lives = player_lives
        self.player.floor = self.floor_index

        # Collision layers: cog pickups (and the debug overlay) use these collision rects
        self.collisions.add_layer('player').add(self.player)
        cog_layer = self.collisions.add_layer('cogs')
        for cog in self.collectible_sprites:
            cog_layer.add(cog)

        # Game state
        self.game_over_triggered: bool = False
        # The moving gear the player stood on after the last ground collision, if any
        self.riding_gear: MovingGear | None = None
        # The platform the player stood on after the last ground collision, if any
        self.supporting_platform: Platform | None = None
        # The top floor's highest platform: standing on it wins the game (None on the floors
        # below, which an elevator leaves)
        self.victory_platform: Platform | None = self._find_victory_platform()
        # Where the player's world y was before this tick moved it: the ground check sweeps
        # the fall from there (None outside dt_tick: no sweep)
        self._player_world_y_before_tick: float | None = None

        # Sound
        self.sounds = SoundBank(ALL_RECIPES)
        self._was_grounded: bool | None = None  # Set from the first real collision result
        self._elevator_motor: LiveVoice | None = None
        self._elevator_peak_velocity = 1.0

        # Persistence
        self.saves: SaveManager = open_saves(app_name='clockwork-keep')

        # Input
        self.actions = self._create_action_map(options=self.options)

        # HUD
        self.hud_font: pygame.font.Font | None = None

    def _build_platforms(
        self: Self, *, platform_color: tuple[int, int, int], top_color: tuple[int, int, int]
    ) -> list[Platform]:
        """Build the floor's platforms from its level data.

        Args:
            platform_color: The floor theme's platform body color.
            top_color: The floor theme's platform top edge color.

        Returns:
            The platforms, in level-data order.

        """
        return [
            Platform(
                world_x=float(platform_x),
                world_y=float(platform_y),
                width=platform_width,
                platform_color=platform_color,
                top_color=top_color,
                groups=self.all_sprites,
            )
            for platform_x, platform_y, platform_width in self.floor_data.platforms
        ]

    def _build_elevators(self: Self) -> list[Elevator]:
        """Build the floor's elevators from its level data.

        Returns:
            The elevators, in level-data order.

        """
        return [
            Elevator(world_x=float(elevator_x), world_y=float(elevator_y), groups=self.all_sprites)
            for elevator_x, elevator_y in self.floor_data.elevators
        ]

    def _build_moving_gears(self: Self) -> list[MovingGear]:
        """Build the floor's moving gear platforms from its level data.

        Returns:
            The moving gears, in level-data order.

        """
        return [
            MovingGear(
                world_x=float(gear_data.world_x),
                world_y=float(gear_data.world_y),
                groups=self.all_sprites,
                move_range_x=gear_data.move_range_x,
                move_range_y=gear_data.move_range_y,
                speed=gear_data.speed,
                size=gear_data.size,
            )
            for gear_data in self.floor_data.moving_gears
        ]

    def _build_collectibles(self: Self) -> list[CogCollectible]:
        """Build the floor's cogs from its level data.

        Returns:
            The cogs, in level-data order.

        """
        return [
            CogCollectible(
                world_x=float(cog_x),
                world_y=float(cog_y),
                cog_type=cog_type,
                groups=self.all_sprites,
            )
            for cog_x, cog_y, cog_type in self.floor_data.collectibles
        ]

    def _find_victory_platform(self: Self) -> Platform | None:
        """Return the platform that wins the game: the top floor's highest one.

        Returns:
            The victory platform, or None on a floor below the top.

        """
        if self.floor_index < len(ALL_FLOORS) - 1:
            return None
        return min(self.platform_sprites, key=lambda platform: platform.world_y)

    @staticmethod
    def _starting_floor_index(*, floor_index: int | None, options: dict[str, Any] | None) -> int:
        """Return the floor to build: the one named, else the --floor option (BUGS.md #79).

        Args:
            floor_index: The floor the caller names (the elevator, a playback's rebuild), or None
                for the engine's first scene, which it builds from options alone.
            options: Command-line options.

        Returns:
            The floor index.

        """
        if floor_index is not None:
            return floor_index
        return int((options or {}).get('floor', 0))

    @classmethod
    def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> None:
        """Add game-specific arguments.

        Args:
            parser: Argument parser.

        """
        parser.add_argument(
            '--floor',
            type=int,
            default=0,
            choices=range(len(ALL_FLOORS)),
            help='Starting floor (0=Boiler Room, 1=Gear Works, 2=Clock Face)',
        )

    @override
    def replay_arguments(self: Self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Rebuild this floor with the score and lives carried onto it.

        Returns:
            The constructor arguments the floor was built with (besides options).

        """
        return {
            'floor_index': self.floor_index,
            'player_score': self.starting_player_score,
            'player_lives': self.starting_player_lives,
        }

    @override
    def setup(self: Self) -> None:
        """Set up the floor scene."""
        super().setup()
        self.hud_font = pygame.font.Font(None, 28)
        # Render every sound now so the elevator clank does not render on the slam frame
        self.sounds.prerender()
        # The engine aims the camera at the player each frame (both axes; the bounds above
        # keep it from scrolling sideways) and places every world sprite from it
        self.camera.follow(target=self.player, axes=FollowAxes.BOTH)
        log.info(
            'Clockwork Keep: Floor %d (%s) — %dx%d',
            self.floor_index,
            self.floor_data.name,
            self.floor_data.width,
            self.floor_data.height,
        )

    @override
    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Master tick: input, physics, collision (the engine then aims the camera).

        Args:
            dt: Delta time in seconds.

        """
        super().dt_tick(dt)

        if self.game_over_triggered:
            return

        self.floor_elapsed_time += dt

        # Check elevator BEFORE begin_frame() clears just_pressed
        self._check_elevator()

        self._process_movement_input()

        world_y_before_tick = self.player.world_y

        # Tick all sprites
        for sprite in self.all_sprites:
            sprite.dt_tick(dt)

        # A gear carries its rider before collision, so the rider is still on it to land
        carried_y = self._ride_moving_gear()

        # The ground check sweeps the fall from where the player was, carried by its gear (the
        # ride is not part of the fall; BUGS.md #205)
        self._player_world_y_before_tick = world_y_before_tick + carried_y

        # Ground collision
        self._resolve_ground_collision()
        self._player_world_y_before_tick = None
        self._play_land_on_touchdown()

        # Pit death
        if (
            not self.player.is_respawning
            and self.player.world_y > self.floor_data.height + PIT_DEATH_THRESHOLD
        ):
            self._player_die()

        # Collectibles (before the victory check, so the cog above the top platform counts)
        self._check_collectibles()

        # Victory: standing on the top floor's highest platform
        if (
            self.victory_platform is not None
            and self.supporting_platform is self.victory_platform
            and not self.player.is_respawning
        ):
            self._win()

    @staticmethod
    def _create_action_map(*, options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> ActionMap:
        """Bind the controls: arrows, SPACE, W, left shift, ESC, Q by position; D-pad, A, Y, X.

        Args:
            options: The engine's options: the map follows its input mode and axis deadzone
                (``ActionMap.from_engine_options``).

        Returns:
            The action map (the golden replays' controls check reads it too).

        """
        actions = ActionMap.from_engine_options(options)
        # Every control binds a physical key position (a scancode: the same place on every
        # keyboard layout), pause and quit included (ActionMap module docstring)
        actions.bind(
            'move_right',
            scancode=pygame.KSCAN_RIGHT,
            controller_button=pygame.CONTROLLER_BUTTON_DPAD_RIGHT,
        )
        actions.bind(
            'move_left',
            scancode=pygame.KSCAN_LEFT,
            controller_button=pygame.CONTROLLER_BUTTON_DPAD_LEFT,
        )
        actions.bind(
            'jump',
            scancode=pygame.KSCAN_SPACE,
            controller_button=pygame.CONTROLLER_BUTTON_A,
        )
        actions.bind('jump', scancode=pygame.KSCAN_UP)
        actions.bind(
            'interact',
            scancode=pygame.KSCAN_W,
            controller_button=pygame.CONTROLLER_BUTTON_Y,
        )
        actions.bind(
            'run',
            scancode=pygame.KSCAN_LSHIFT,
            controller_button=pygame.CONTROLLER_BUTTON_X,
        )
        actions.bind('pause', scancode=pygame.KSCAN_ESCAPE)
        actions.bind('quit', scancode=pygame.KSCAN_Q)
        return actions

    # --- Movement ---

    def _process_movement_input(self: Self) -> None:
        """Apply held movement actions from ActionMap each frame."""
        self.actions.begin_frame()
        if self.player.is_respawning:
            return
        running = self.actions.is_held('run')
        if self.actions.is_held('move_right'):
            self.player.move_right(running=running)
        elif self.actions.is_held('move_left'):
            self.player.move_left(running=running)
        else:
            self.player.stop_horizontal()

    # --- Collision ---

    def _resolve_ground_collision(self: Self) -> None:
        """Check player against all platforms and snap to ground."""
        # Support comes from the collision rect (hitbox): its left/right edges and its bottom
        # (the visible feet), not the whole drawn image
        player_rect = get_sprite_collision_rect(self.player)
        _, player_offset_y = collision_rect_offset(self.player)
        feet_below_world_y = player_offset_y + player_rect.height
        player_bottom = self.player.world_y + feet_below_world_y
        # Where the feet were before this tick moved them (the swept fall starts there)
        feet_start = self._feet_before_tick(player_bottom=player_bottom)

        self.player.on_ground = False
        self.supporting_platform = None

        for platform in self.platform_sprites:
            plat_top = platform.world_y
            plat_left = platform.world_x
            plat_right = platform.world_x + platform.rect.width

            # Player must be falling onto the platform and within horizontal bounds
            if (
                self._feet_reach_surface(
                    player_bottom=player_bottom, feet_start=feet_start, surface_top=plat_top
                )
                and player_rect.right > plat_left
                and player_rect.left < plat_right
            ):
                self.player.world_y = plat_top - feet_below_world_y
                self.player.velocity_y = 0.0
                self.player.on_ground = True
                self.supporting_platform = platform
                break

        # Also check elevators as ground
        for elevator in self.elevator_sprites:
            elev_top = elevator.world_y
            elev_left = elevator.world_x
            elev_right = elevator.world_x + elevator.rect.width

            if (
                self._feet_reach_surface(
                    player_bottom=player_bottom, feet_start=feet_start, surface_top=elev_top
                )
                and player_rect.right > elev_left
                and player_rect.left < elev_right
            ):
                self.player.world_y = elev_top - feet_below_world_y
                self.player.velocity_y = 0.0
                self.player.on_ground = True
                self.supporting_platform = None
                break

        self.riding_gear = None
        if not self.player.on_ground:
            self._land_on_moving_gear(
                player_rect=player_rect, player_bottom=player_bottom, feet_start=feet_start
            )

    def _feet_before_tick(self: Self, *, player_bottom: float) -> float:
        """Return where the feet were before this tick moved them (no higher than now).

        Outside dt_tick there is no previous position: the feet start where they are.

        Args:
            player_bottom: The world y of the player's feet (its hitbox bottom) now.

        Returns:
            The world y the swept fall starts from.

        """
        if self._player_world_y_before_tick is None:
            return player_bottom
        return min(
            player_bottom,
            player_bottom - (self.player.world_y - self._player_world_y_before_tick),
        )

    def _feet_reach_surface(
        self: Self, *, player_bottom: float, feet_start: float, surface_top: float
    ) -> bool:
        """Whether a falling (or standing) player's feet land on a surface this tick.

        The feet land when they end the tick at or below the surface's top and started it no
        more than GROUND_SNAP_TOLERANCE below it: the fall is swept from where the feet were,
        so a long tick at terminal speed (40 px in a capped 50 ms tick) cannot carry them
        through a platform (BUGS.md #205). Without a previous position (outside dt_tick) the
        feet must end within the tolerance, as before the sweep.

        Args:
            player_bottom: The world y of the player's feet (its hitbox bottom) now.
            feet_start: Where the feet were before this tick (_feet_before_tick).
            surface_top: The world y of the surface's top.

        Returns:
            True if the feet land on the surface.

        """
        return feet_land_on_surface(
            velocity_y=self.player.velocity_y,
            feet_now=player_bottom,
            feet_start=feet_start,
            surface_top=surface_top,
            tolerance=GROUND_SNAP_TOLERANCE,
        )

    def _land_on_moving_gear(
        self: Self, *, player_rect: pygame.Rect, player_bottom: float, feet_start: float
    ) -> None:
        """Stand the player on the moving gear its hitbox lands on, if any.

        A gear supports like a platform, by the gear's collision rect (its visible pixels):
        the player's feet go on its drawn top, so they never float or sink while it moves.

        Args:
            player_rect: The player's collision rect (world coordinates).
            player_bottom: The world y of the player's feet (its hitbox bottom).
            feet_start: Where the feet were before this tick (_feet_before_tick).

        """
        _, player_offset_y = collision_rect_offset(self.player)
        feet_below_world_y = player_offset_y + player_rect.height
        for moving_gear in self.moving_gear_sprites:
            gear_rect = get_sprite_collision_rect(moving_gear)
            if (
                self._feet_reach_surface(
                    player_bottom=player_bottom, feet_start=feet_start, surface_top=gear_rect.top
                )
                and player_rect.right > gear_rect.left
                and player_rect.left < gear_rect.right
            ):
                self.player.world_y = gear_rect.top - feet_below_world_y
                self.player.velocity_y = 0.0
                self.player.on_ground = True
                self.riding_gear = moving_gear
                return

    def _ride_moving_gear(self: Self) -> float:
        """Carry the player by the gear it stands on: as far as the gear moved this tick.

        Runs after every sprite's dt_tick (so the gear has moved) and before ground
        collision, which then finds the player on the gear again. A jump clears on_ground,
        so a player leaving the gear is not carried.

        Returns:
            How far down the gear carried the player (0.0 when it rode no gear).

        """
        if self.riding_gear is None or not self.player.on_ground:
            return 0.0
        self.player.world_x += self.riding_gear.moved_x
        self.player.world_y += self.riding_gear.moved_y
        return self.riding_gear.moved_y

    def _play_land_on_touchdown(self: Self) -> None:
        """Play land on the frame the player touches down.

        Ground collision resets on_ground to False and back every frame, so this compares
        with the previous frame's result. The first result only initializes the edge (the
        transition's off-screen dt_tick must not play it), and respawning resets it (the
        respawn tween sets on_ground directly).
        """
        if self.player.is_respawning:
            self._was_grounded = None
            return
        grounded = self.player.on_ground
        if self._was_grounded is False and grounded:
            self.sounds.play('land')
        self._was_grounded = grounded

    def _try_jump(self: Self) -> None:
        """Jump if standing on something, with its sound."""
        if self.player.on_ground:
            self.player.jump(running=self.actions.is_held('run'))
            self.sounds.play('jump')

    def _check_collectibles(self: Self) -> None:
        """Collect cogs whose collision rect overlaps the player's (via the collision layers)."""
        self.collisions.check_overlap('player', 'cogs', callback=self._on_player_collect_cog)

    def _on_player_collect_cog(self: Self, _player: Tinker, cog: CogCollectible) -> None:
        """Award a cog's points and remove it everywhere."""
        self.player.score += cog.points
        self.sounds.play('cog_pickup')
        cog.kill()
        self.collectible_sprites.remove(cog)
        self.collisions.get_layer('cogs').remove(cog)

    def _check_elevator(self: Self) -> None:
        """Ride the elevator when the player stands on it and presses interact.

        Jump is deliberately not accepted: jumping clears on_ground before this check runs,
        so it could never ride (BUGS.md #24), and jump should always jump.
        """
        if not self.actions.just_pressed('interact'):
            return

        for elevator in self.elevator_sprites:
            elev_top = elevator.world_y
            elev_left = elevator.world_x
            elev_right = elevator.world_x + elevator.rect.width

            # Player must be standing on the elevator
            player_rect = get_sprite_collision_rect(self.player)
            _, player_offset_y = collision_rect_offset(self.player)
            player_bottom = self.player.world_y + player_offset_y + player_rect.height
            on_elevator = (
                self.player.on_ground
                and abs(player_bottom - elev_top) < ELEVATOR_SNAP_TOLERANCE
                and player_rect.right > elev_left
                and player_rect.left < elev_right
            )

            if on_elevator and self.floor_index < len(ALL_FLOORS) - 1:
                self._go_to_next_floor()
                return

    def _draw_timed_clock_background(
        self: Self, surface: pygame.Surface, camera_x: float, camera_y: float
    ) -> None:
        """Draw the floor-3 clock showing this floor's elapsed game time."""
        draw_clock_background(
            surface,
            camera_x,
            camera_y,
            clock_seconds=CLOCK_START_SECONDS + self.floor_elapsed_time,
        )

    def _go_to_next_floor(self: Self) -> None:
        """Ride the elevator to the next floor."""
        next_floor = self.floor_index + 1
        log.info('Elevator activated! Floor %d → %d', self.floor_index, next_floor)

        # The shaft walls take the current floor's platform colours (body and top edge)
        platform_color, top_color, _led_color = _FLOOR_THEMES[self.floor_index]

        next_scene = ClockworkKeepScene(
            floor_index=next_floor,
            player_score=self.player.score,
            player_lives=self.player.lives,
            options=self.options,
        )
        transition = ElevatorTransition(
            duration=ELEVATOR_RIDE_DURATION,
            easing=ELEVATOR_RIDE_EASING,
            wall_color=platform_color,
            wall_accent=top_color,
            player_surface=self.player.image,
            on_update=self._update_elevator_motor,
        )
        self._elevator_peak_velocity = max(
            transition.eased_velocity_at(step / ELEVATOR_SPEED_SAMPLES)
            for step in range(ELEVATOR_SPEED_SAMPLES + 1)
        )
        self._elevator_motor = self._start_elevator_motor(owner=transition)
        transition.add_cue(1.0, self._elevator_arrived)
        self.transition_to(next_scene, transition)

    def _start_elevator_motor(self: Self, *, owner: object) -> LiveVoice | None:
        """Start the motor voice owned by the ride; None (silent ride) if no channel is free.

        Returns:
            The running voice, or None.

        """
        try:
            motor = self.scene_manager.live_audio.create_voice(
                owner=owner,
                waveform=Waveform.SAWTOOTH,
                frequency=ELEVATOR_MOTOR_IDLE_FREQUENCY,
                volume=ELEVATOR_MOTOR_MINIMUM_VOLUME,
                low_pass_cutoff=ELEVATOR_MOTOR_LOW_PASS_CUTOFF,
                tremolo=Tremolo(
                    rate_hz=ELEVATOR_MOTOR_TREMOLO_RATE, depth=ELEVATOR_MOTOR_TREMOLO_DEPTH
                ),
            )
            motor.start()
        except ValueError, AudioUnavailableError:
            log.warning('No live voice or audio available; the elevator rides without its motor')
            return None
        return motor

    def _update_elevator_motor(self: Self, transition: Transition) -> None:
        """Drive motor pitch and volume from the car's speed (the easing's slope).

        Runs from the transition after this scene was cleaned up, so it only touches the
        motor voice, never sprites or the camera.

        Args:
            transition: The running elevator transition.

        """
        # The arrival cue (progress 1.0) fires before on_update on the completing frame and
        # clears the rumble; updating again here would re-start it and never stop.
        if transition.progress >= 1.0:
            return
        speed_fraction = min(
            1.0, transition.eased_velocity_at(transition.progress) / self._elevator_peak_velocity
        )
        # Rumble does not depend on the motor voice: a ride without a free voice still hums
        self.scene_manager.rumble.set_sustained(
            low_frequency=ELEVATOR_ASCENT_RUMBLE_LOW * speed_fraction,
            high_frequency=ELEVATOR_ASCENT_RUMBLE_HIGH * speed_fraction,
        )
        if self._elevator_motor is None:
            return
        self._elevator_motor.frequency = (
            ELEVATOR_MOTOR_IDLE_FREQUENCY
            + (ELEVATOR_MOTOR_PEAK_FREQUENCY - ELEVATOR_MOTOR_IDLE_FREQUENCY) * speed_fraction
        )
        self._elevator_motor.volume = (
            ELEVATOR_MOTOR_MINIMUM_VOLUME
            + (ELEVATOR_MOTOR_MAXIMUM_VOLUME - ELEVATOR_MOTOR_MINIMUM_VOLUME) * speed_fraction
        )

    def _elevator_arrived(self: Self) -> None:
        """The car slams into the floor: stop the motor, clank, shake and rumble.

        Uses only SceneManager-owned services (SCREEN shake), because this scene has been
        cleaned up by the time the ride ends.
        """
        if self._elevator_motor is not None:
            self._elevator_motor.stop_now()
            self._elevator_motor = None
        self.scene_manager.rumble.clear_sustained()
        self.sounds.play('elevator_clank')
        self.shake(ELEVATOR_STOP_BOUNCE, targets=ShakeTarget.SCREEN)
        self.shake(ELEVATOR_STOP_RATTLE, targets=ShakeTarget.SCREEN)

    # --- Victory ---

    def _win(self: Self) -> None:
        """Reaching the top of the Clock Face: save the score and show the victory screen.

        dt_tick returns early once game_over_triggered is set, so this runs once.
        """
        self.game_over_triggered = True
        log.info('Victory! Score: %d', self.player.score)
        # The floor (and its camera) stand still from here on: stop following
        self.camera.follow(target=None)
        self.sounds.play('victory')
        self._save_high_score()
        # A shake still running would carry into the fade; end it first (as at game over)
        self.scene_manager.screen_shake.clear()
        victory = ClockworkKeepVictoryScene(
            final_score=self.player.score,
            high_scores=self._load_high_scores(),
            options=self.options,
        )
        self.transition_to(victory, FadeTransition(duration=1.0))

    # --- Death / Respawn ---

    def _player_die(self: Self) -> None:
        """Handle player death."""
        if self.game_over_triggered:
            return

        self.player.lives -= 1
        log.info('Player died! Lives: %d', self.player.lives)

        if self.player.lives <= 0:
            self.game_over_triggered = True
            # The floor (and its camera) stand still from here on: stop following
            self.camera.follow(target=None)
            self.sounds.play('game_over')
            self._save_high_score()
            # Spec revision 3: a shake still running would carry into the fade; end it first.
            self.scene_manager.screen_shake.clear()
            high_scores = self._load_high_scores()
            game_over = GameOverScene(
                final_score=self.player.score,
                high_scores=high_scores,
                options=self.options,
            )
            self.transition_to(game_over, FadeTransition(duration=1.0))
        else:
            self.sounds.play('death')
            self._respawn_player()

    def _respawn_player(self: Self) -> None:
        """Respawn with fade animation."""
        self.player.is_respawning = True
        self.player.velocity_x = 0.0
        self.player.velocity_y = 0.0
        self.player.stop_horizontal()

        spawn_x = float(self.floor_data.spawn_x)
        spawn_y = float(self.floor_data.spawn_y)

        def _reposition_and_fade_in() -> None:
            self.player.world_x = spawn_x
            self.player.world_y = spawn_y
            self.player.on_ground = True
            # The spawn point stands on no gear: the gear faded out on carries no one
            self.riding_gear = None
            self.player.is_respawning = False
            self.tweens.tween(
                target=self.player,
                property_name='alpha',
                end_value=255.0,
                duration=0.3,
                easing='ease_out_quad',
            )

        self.tweens.tween(
            target=self.player,
            property_name='alpha',
            end_value=0.0,
            duration=0.2,
            easing='ease_in_quad',
            on_complete=_reposition_and_fade_in,
        )

    # --- Save / Load ---

    def _save_high_score(self: Self) -> None:
        """Save score and highest floor to persistent storage."""
        max_entries = 10
        try:
            existing = self.saves.load('high_scores')
            scores: list[dict[str, int]] = existing.get('scores', [])
        except SaveNotFoundError:
            scores = []

        scores.append({
            'score': self.player.score,
            'floor': self.floor_index,
        })
        scores.sort(key=lambda entry: entry.get('score', 0), reverse=True)
        scores = scores[:max_entries]
        self.saves.save('high_scores', {'scores': scores})

    def _load_high_scores(self: Self) -> list[dict[str, int]]:
        """Load high scores from persistent storage.

        Returns:
            List of high score dicts.

        """
        try:
            data = self.saves.load('high_scores')
            return data.get('scores', [])
        except SaveNotFoundError:
            return []

    # --- Input handlers ---

    @override
    def on_window_focus_lost_event(self: Self, event: WindowEvent) -> None:
        """Auto-pause when the window loses focus (Cmd-Tab, etc.).

        Args:
            event: The focus lost event.

        """
        super().on_window_focus_lost_event(event)
        if not self.game_over_triggered:
            self.next_scene = PauseScene(options=self.options)

    @override
    def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key presses.

        Args:
            event: The key down event.

        """
        self.actions.handle_event(event)
        action = self.actions.get_action(event)
        if action == 'jump':
            self._try_jump()
        elif action == 'pause':
            self.next_scene = PauseScene(options=self.options)
        elif action == 'quit':
            # A QUIT event ends the run (next_scene = None does not: the scene manager reads it
            # as no switch pending)
            self.scene_manager.quit()
        elif action is None:
            super().on_key_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_key_up_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key releases.

        Args:
            event: The key up event.

        """
        self.actions.handle_event(event)

    @override

        Args:
            event: The joystick button down event.

        """
        self.actions.handle_event(event)
        action = self.actions.get_action(event)

            self._try_jump()

    @override

        """Handle joystick axis motion.

        Args:
            event: The joystick axis motion event.

        """
        self.actions.handle_event(event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_down_event(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle controller button presses.

        Args:
            event: The controller button down event.

        """
        self.actions.handle_event(event)
        action = self.actions.get_action(event)
        if action == 'jump':
            self._try_jump()

    @override

        """Handle controller button releases.

        Args:
            event: The controller button up event.

        """
        self.actions.handle_event(event)

    # --- Rendering ---

    @override
    def render(self: Self, screen: pygame.Surface) -> None:
        """Render the floor.

        Args:
            screen: Display surface.

        """
        # Set in __init__ (the setter takes no None); the getter is typed for before Scene.__init__
        assert self.background_color is not None
        screen.fill(self.background_color)
        self.all_sprites.clear(screen, self.background)
        self.all_sprites.draw(screen)
        self._draw_hud(screen)
        self.rects = None  # Full screen update

    def _draw_hud(self: Self, screen: pygame.Surface) -> None:
        """Draw score, lives, and floor indicator.

        Args:
            screen: Display surface.

        """
        if self.hud_font is None:
            return

        antialias = FontManager.antialias()
        score_text = f'Score: {self.player.score}'
        lives_text = f'Lives: {self.player.lives}'
        floor_text = f'Floor: {self.floor_data.name}'

        # Score (top left)
        shadow = self.hud_font.render(score_text, antialias, HUD_SHADOW_COLOR)
        screen.blit(shadow, (11, 11))
        text = self.hud_font.render(score_text, antialias, HUD_TEXT_COLOR)
        screen.blit(text, (10, 10))

        # Lives (top right)
        shadow = self.hud_font.render(lives_text, antialias, HUD_SHADOW_COLOR)
        screen.blit(shadow, (self.screen_width - 109, 11))
        text = self.hud_font.render(lives_text, antialias, HUD_TEXT_COLOR)
        screen.blit(text, (self.screen_width - 110, 10))

        # Floor name (top center)
        shadow = self.hud_font.render(floor_text, antialias, HUD_SHADOW_COLOR)
        floor_x = (self.screen_width - shadow.get_width()) // 2
        screen.blit(shadow, (floor_x + 1, 11))
        text = self.hud_font.render(floor_text, antialias, HUD_TEXT_COLOR)
        screen.blit(text, (floor_x, 10))

def __init__(
    self: Self,
    floor_index: int | None = None,
    player_score: int = 0,
    player_lives: int = 3,
    options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize the floor scene.

    Args:
        floor_index: Which floor (0=Boiler Room, 1=Gear Works, 2=Clock Face). None (the
            engine's first scene, built from options alone) takes the --floor option.
        player_score: Score carried from previous floor.
        player_lives: Lives carried from previous floor.
        options: Command-line options.
        groups: Sprite group.

    """
    if groups is None:
        groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()
    super().__init__(options=options, groups=groups)

    self.floor_index = self._starting_floor_index(floor_index=floor_index, options=options)
    # The score and lives carried onto this floor, as it began (replay_arguments)
    self.starting_player_score = player_score
    self.starting_player_lives = player_lives
    self.floor_data: FloorData = ALL_FLOORS[self.floor_index]
    # Game time on this floor (capped dt, frozen after game over); drives the floor-3 clock
    self.floor_elapsed_time: float = 0.0

    # Theme colors
    platform_color, top_color, self.led_color = _FLOOR_THEMES[self.floor_index]

    # Background
    bg_color = [
        (40, 25, 15),  # Boiler Room
        (35, 35, 40),  # Gear Works
        (15, 15, 35),  # Clock Face
    ][self.floor_index]
    self.background_color = bg_color

    # Camera: vertical scroll only (tower is 1 screen wide)
    self.camera = Camera2D(
        screen_width=self.screen_width,
        screen_height=self.screen_height,
        lead_x=CAMERA_LEAD_X,
        lead_y=CAMERA_LEAD_Y,
        shake_intensity=self.options.get('screen_shake_intensity', 1.0),
    )
    self.camera.set_bounds(
        min_x=0.0,
        max_x=0.0,  # No horizontal scroll
        min_y=0.0,
        max_y=float(self.floor_data.height - self.screen_height),
    )

    # Background parallax
    shows_clock = _FLOOR_BACKGROUNDS[self.floor_index] is draw_clock_background
    bg_func = (
        self._draw_timed_clock_background
        if shows_clock
        else _FLOOR_BACKGROUNDS[self.floor_index]
    )
    self.camera.add_background_layer(
        scroll_factor=PARALLAX_FAR,
        draw_function=bg_func,
        layer_depth=LAYER_FAR_BACKGROUND,
        groups=self.all_sprites,
        # The clock's hands show the floor's elapsed game time, not just the camera offset,
        # so that layer redraws every frame; the other floors' walls depend on camera_y only
        animated=shows_clock,
    )

    # Build terrain (in this order: sprites of one layer draw in the order they are added)
    self.platform_sprites: list[Platform] = self._build_platforms(
        platform_color=platform_color, top_color=top_color
    )
    self.elevator_sprites: list[Elevator] = self._build_elevators()
    self.moving_gear_sprites: list[MovingGear] = self._build_moving_gears()
    self.collectible_sprites: list[CogCollectible] = self._build_collectibles()

    # Player
    self.player = Tinker(
        world_x=float(self.floor_data.spawn_x),
        world_y=float(self.floor_data.spawn_y),
        groups=self.all_sprites,
    )
    self.player.score = player_score
    self.player.lives = player_lives
    self.player.floor = self.floor_index

    # Collision layers: cog pickups (and the debug overlay) use these collision rects
    self.collisions.add_layer('player').add(self.player)
    cog_layer = self.collisions.add_layer('cogs')
    for cog in self.collectible_sprites:
        cog_layer.add(cog)

    # Game state
    self.game_over_triggered: bool = False
    # The moving gear the player stood on after the last ground collision, if any
    self.riding_gear: MovingGear | None = None
    # The platform the player stood on after the last ground collision, if any
    self.supporting_platform: Platform | None = None
    # The top floor's highest platform: standing on it wins the game (None on the floors
    # below, which an elevator leaves)
    self.victory_platform: Platform | None = self._find_victory_platform()
    # Where the player's world y was before this tick moved it: the ground check sweeps
    # the fall from there (None outside dt_tick: no sweep)
    self._player_world_y_before_tick: float | None = None

    # Sound
    self.sounds = SoundBank(ALL_RECIPES)
    self._was_grounded: bool | None = None  # Set from the first real collision result
    self._elevator_motor: LiveVoice | None = None
    self._elevator_peak_velocity = 1.0

    # Persistence
    self.saves: SaveManager = open_saves(app_name='clockwork-keep')

    # Input
    self.actions = self._create_action_map(options=self.options)

    # HUD
    self.hud_font: pygame.font.Font | None = None

@override
def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
    """Master tick: input, physics, collision (the engine then aims the camera).

    Args:
        dt: Delta time in seconds.

    """
    super().dt_tick(dt)

    if self.game_over_triggered:
        return

    self.floor_elapsed_time += dt

    # Check elevator BEFORE begin_frame() clears just_pressed
    self._check_elevator()

    self._process_movement_input()

    world_y_before_tick = self.player.world_y

    # Tick all sprites
    for sprite in self.all_sprites:
        sprite.dt_tick(dt)

    # A gear carries its rider before collision, so the rider is still on it to land
    carried_y = self._ride_moving_gear()

    # The ground check sweeps the fall from where the player was, carried by its gear (the
    # ride is not part of the fall; BUGS.md #205)
    self._player_world_y_before_tick = world_y_before_tick + carried_y

    # Ground collision
    self._resolve_ground_collision()
    self._player_world_y_before_tick = None
    self._play_land_on_touchdown()

    # Pit death
    if (
        not self.player.is_respawning
        and self.player.world_y > self.floor_data.height + PIT_DEATH_THRESHOLD
    ):
        self._player_die()

    # Collectibles (before the victory check, so the cog above the top platform counts)
    self._check_collectibles()

    # Victory: standing on the top floor's highest platform
    if (
        self.victory_platform is not None
        and self.supporting_platform is self.victory_platform
        and not self.player.is_respawning
    ):
        self._win()

@override
def setup(self: Self) -> None:
    """Set up the floor scene."""
    super().setup()
    self.hud_font = pygame.font.Font(None, 28)
    # Render every sound now so the elevator clank does not render on the slam frame
    self.sounds.prerender()

    self.camera.follow(target=self.player, axes=FollowAxes.BOTH)

class CogCollectible(Sprite):
    """A collectible cog with bobbing animation.

    Args:
        world_x: X position in world space.
        world_y: Y position in world space.
        cog_type: One of 'bronze', 'silver', 'gold'.
        groups: Sprite group to add to.

    """

    # A world sprite: the engine places it from the camera
    COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD

    def __init__(
        self,
        world_x: float,
        world_y: float,
        cog_type: str,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the cog collectible."""
        self._layer = LAYER_COLLECTIBLES
        super().__init__(
            x=world_x,
            y=world_y,
            width=COG_SIZE,
            height=COG_SIZE,
            name='Cog',
            groups=groups,
        )
        self.world_x = world_x
        self._base_world_y = world_y
        self.world_y = world_y
        self.cog_type = cog_type
        self.color, self.points = _COG_TYPES.get(cog_type, _COG_TYPES['bronze'])
        self.image = pygame.Surface((COG_SIZE, COG_SIZE), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        self._timer: float = 0.0
        self.dirty = 2

    @override

Uses PhysicsBody for platformer movement and an animation state machine for visual states. A world sprite: the engine places it from the camera.

Source code in src/games/clockwork-keep/src/clockwork_keep/player.py 
class Tinker(Sprite):
    """The Tinker — a goggled mechanic exploring the clockwork tower.

    Uses PhysicsBody for platformer movement and an animation state
    machine for visual states. A world sprite: the engine places it from the camera.
    """

    COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD

    IDLE = 'idle'
    RUNNING = 'running'
    JUMPING = 'jumping'
    FALLING = 'falling'

    def __init__(
        self,
        world_x: float,
        world_y: float,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the Tinker.

        Args:
            world_x: Starting X in world coordinates.
            world_y: Starting Y in world coordinates.
            groups: Sprite group to add to.

        """
        self._layer = LAYER_PLAYER

        super().__init__(
            x=world_x,
            y=world_y,
            width=PLAYER_WIDTH,
            height=PLAYER_HEIGHT,
            name='Tinker',
            groups=groups,
        )

        self.image = pygame.Surface((PLAYER_WIDTH, PLAYER_HEIGHT), pygame.SRCALPHA)

        # Side walls: refitted to the hitbox every tick (see _fit_playfield_bounds_to_hitbox)
        self._playfield_bounds = BoundsConstraint(
            min_x=float(PLAYFIELD_LEFT),
            max_x=float(PLAYFIELD_RIGHT - PLAYER_WIDTH),
        )
        # Kept so the move methods set its target directly (the body always has it)
        self._acceleration_behavior = AccelerationBehavior(
            acceleration=PLAYER_ACCELERATION,
            deceleration=PLAYER_DECELERATION,
        )
        self.physics: PhysicsBody = PhysicsBody(
            world_x=world_x,
            world_y=world_y,
            behaviors=[
                GravityBehavior(strength=GRAVITY, terminal_velocity=MAX_FALL_SPEED),
                self._acceleration_behavior,
            ],
            constraints=[self._playfield_bounds],
        )

        # Animation state machine
        from glitchygames.animation import AnimationStateMachine

        self.state: str = self.IDLE
        self.animation_timer: float = 0.0
        self.state_machine = AnimationStateMachine(self)
        self.state_machine.add_transition('idle', 'running', when='abs(velocity_x) > 0.1')
        self.state_machine.add_transition('running', 'idle', when='abs(velocity_x) <= 0.1')
        self.state_machine.add_transition('idle', 'jumping', when='velocity_y < -10.0')
        self.state_machine.add_transition('running', 'jumping', when='velocity_y < -10.0')
        self.state_machine.add_transition('falling', 'idle', when='on_ground')
        self.state_machine.add_transition('jumping', 'idle', when='on_ground')
        falling_when = f'velocity_y > {FALLING_VELOCITY_THRESHOLD} and not on_ground'
        self.state_machine.add_transition('idle', 'falling', when=falling_when)
        self.state_machine.add_transition('jumping', 'falling', when=falling_when)
        self.state_machine.set_state(self.IDLE)

        # Game state
        self.lives: int = STARTING_LIVES
        self.score: int = 0
        self.floor: int = 0

        # Visual effects
        self.alpha: float = 255.0
        self.is_respawning: bool = False

        self.dirty = 2

    # --- Property delegates to PhysicsBody ---

    @property
    def world_x(self) -> float:
        """X position in world space."""
        return self.physics.world_x

    @world_x.setter
    def world_x(self, value: float) -> None:
        self.physics.world_x = value

    @property
    def world_y(self) -> float:
        """Y position in world space."""
        return self.physics.world_y

    @world_y.setter
    def world_y(self, value: float) -> None:
        self.physics.world_y = value

    @property
    def velocity_x(self) -> float:
        """Horizontal velocity."""
        return self.physics.velocity_x

    @velocity_x.setter
    def velocity_x(self, value: float) -> None:
        self.physics.velocity_x = value

    @property
    def velocity_y(self) -> float:
        """Vertical velocity."""
        return self.physics.velocity_y

    @velocity_y.setter
    def velocity_y(self, value: float) -> None:
        self.physics.velocity_y = value

    @property
    def on_ground(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the player is on the ground."""
        return self.physics.on_ground

    @on_ground.setter
    def on_ground(self, value: bool) -> None:
        self.physics.on_ground = value

    @property
    def facing_right(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the player faces right."""
        return self.physics.facing_right

    @facing_right.setter
    def facing_right(self, value: bool) -> None:
        self.physics.facing_right = value

    # --- Physics ---

    @override
    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Advance physics and animation, then draw this frame's pose.

        The pose is drawn here, not in update(), because the hitbox is trimmed to the drawn
        pixels: collision (the side walls here, the floor's ground and cog checks after this)
        must use this frame's pose, not the previous frame's (the pose-before-collision rule,
        plans/2026-10-18-engine-world-space.md section 1).

        Args:
            dt: Delta time in seconds.

        """
        super().dt_tick(dt)
        self.animation_timer += dt
        self._fit_playfield_bounds_to_hitbox()
        self.physics.tick(dt)

        context = self.physics.get_animation_context()
        self.state_machine.evaluate(context, dt)
        self.state = self.state_machine.current_state

        self._draw_pose()
        # The new pose (facing or state) can move the hitbox inside the image, so the side
        # walls are refitted to it and applied again: the hitbox never enters a wall
        self._fit_playfield_bounds_to_hitbox()
        self._playfield_bounds.apply(self.physics, dt)

    def _draw_pose(self: Self) -> None:
        """Redraw the image for the current state, facing and animation time."""
        self.image.fill((0, 0, 0, 0))
        draw_tinker(
            self.image,
            self.state,
            facing_right=self.facing_right,
            animation_timer=self.animation_timer,
        )

    def _fit_playfield_bounds_to_hitbox(self: Self) -> None:
        """Set the side-wall bounds so the hitbox, not the whole image, meets the walls.

        The figure's transparent margin moves with its pose and facing (4 px on the side it
        faces away from), so the bounds are refitted from the current collision rect each
        tick: its left edge stops at PLAYFIELD_LEFT and its right edge at PLAYFIELD_RIGHT.
        """
        hitbox = get_sprite_collision_rect(self)
        offset_x, _ = collision_rect_offset(self)
        self._playfield_bounds.min_x = float(PLAYFIELD_LEFT - offset_x)
        self._playfield_bounds.max_x = float(PLAYFIELD_RIGHT - (offset_x + hitbox.width))

    def jump(self, *, running: bool = False) -> None:
        """Initiate a jump if on the ground.

        Args:
            running: If True, use the higher running jump velocity.

        """
        if self.on_ground:
            self.velocity_y = JUMP_VELOCITY_RUNNING if running else JUMP_VELOCITY
            self.on_ground = False

    def move_right(self, *, running: bool = False) -> None:
        """Start moving right.

        Args:
            running: If True, use run speed instead of walk speed.

        """
        speed = PLAYER_RUN_SPEED if running else PLAYER_WALK_SPEED
        self._acceleration_behavior.target_velocity_x = speed
        self.facing_right = True

    def move_left(self, *, running: bool = False) -> None:
        """Start moving left.

        Args:
            running: If True, use run speed instead of walk speed.

        """
        speed = PLAYER_RUN_SPEED if running else PLAYER_WALK_SPEED
        self._acceleration_behavior.target_velocity_x = -speed
        self.facing_right = False

    def stop_horizontal(self) -> None:
        """Decelerate to a stop."""
        self._acceleration_behavior.target_velocity_x = 0.0

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Apply the respawn fade (purely visual; the pose is drawn in dt_tick)."""
        self.image.set_alpha(round(self.alpha))

def bell(*, frequency: float, offset: float, duration: float, volume: float) -> tuple[Tone, ...]:
    """Return one struck bell: its partials, each fading out over the bell's duration.

    Args:
        frequency: The fundamental (Hz).
        offset: When it is struck (seconds into the sound).
        duration: How long it rings.
        volume: Its loudness, before the recipe's.

    Returns:
        The bell's tones.

    """
    return tuple(
        Tone(
            waveform=Waveform.SINE,
            start_frequency=frequency * ratio,
            duration=duration,
            offset=offset,
            envelope=Envelope(attack=0.003, decay=0.08, sustain_level=0.5, release=duration * 0.7),
            volume=volume * partial_volume,
        )
        for ratio, partial_volume in BELL_PARTIALS
    )

A gear-shaped platform that moves on a sine path.

A floor builds its gears from its level data (FloorData.moving_gears) and supports the player on them like a platform; a player standing on one is carried by moved_x and moved_y, how far the gear's last dt_tick moved it (ClockworkKeepScene._ride_moving_gear).

class MovingGear(Sprite):
    """A gear-shaped platform that moves on a sine path.

    A floor builds its gears from its level data (FloorData.moving_gears) and supports the
    player on them like a platform; a player standing on one is carried by moved_x and
    moved_y, how far the gear's last dt_tick moved it (ClockworkKeepScene._ride_moving_gear).

    Args:
        world_x: Center X of the movement range.
        world_y: Center Y of the movement range.
        move_range_x: Horizontal movement amplitude in pixels.
        move_range_y: Vertical movement amplitude in pixels.
        speed: Movement speed (radians/sec).
        size: The gear bar's width in pixels (its height is a quarter of it: a toothed bar,
            not a round gear).
        groups: Sprite group to add to.

    """

    # A world sprite: the engine places it from the camera
    COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD

    def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments]
        self,
        world_x: float,
        world_y: float,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any],
        *,
        move_range_x: float = 0.0,
        move_range_y: float = 0.0,
        speed: float = 1.5,
        size: int = 40,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the moving gear."""
        self._layer = LAYER_TERRAIN
        super().__init__(
            x=world_x,
            y=world_y,
            width=size,
            height=size // 4,
            name='MovingGear',
            groups=groups,
        )
        self._center_x = world_x
        self._center_y = world_y
        self._move_range_x = move_range_x
        self._move_range_y = move_range_y
        self._speed = speed
        self._timer: float = 0.0
        self.world_x = world_x
        self.world_y = world_y
        # How far the last dt_tick moved the gear: the floor carries a standing rider by it
        self.moved_x: float = 0.0
        self.moved_y: float = 0.0

        self.image = pygame.Surface((size, size // 4), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        self.image.fill((140, 130, 110))
        # Gear teeth along edges
        for tooth_x in range(0, size, 8):
            pygame.draw.rect(self.image, (120, 110, 90), (tooth_x, 0, 4, 2))
        self.dirty = 2  # Always redraw (moving)

    @override
    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Move the gear along its path, keeping how far it moved (moved_x, moved_y).

        Args:
            dt: Delta time in seconds.

        """
        super().dt_tick(dt)
        self._timer += dt
        previous_world_x = self.world_x
        previous_world_y = self.world_y
        self.world_x = self._center_x + self._move_range_x * math.sin(self._timer * self._speed)
        self.world_y = self._center_y + self._move_range_y * math.sin(self._timer * self._speed)
        self.moved_x = self.world_x - previous_world_x
        self.moved_y = self.world_y - previous_world_y

docs.text:
Drawing Fire: a pencil-on-paper stick-figure battle.

The battle model: soldiers, pistols, bullets, sandbags and the winner.

This module is pure: no pygame, no drawing, no randomness and no clock. Time only comes from the dt passed to Battle.step, and every driver (computer or human) steers a soldier the same way, with an Intent.

Drawing Fire's pencil look: the battle drawn as a child's war drawing, in pencil on paper.

Everything here draws onto a surface it is given, from the battle model. Nothing here draws from a random stream: a hand-drawn line wanders by wobble, a deterministic hash of where it is, so the same picture is drawn every time.

The computer driver: it looks at the battle and produces an Intent for one soldier.

Every driver produces an Intent and the battle applies it the same way, so nothing here touches the rules. The computer's randomness (aim error, drawn once per shot, and reaction delay) comes only from the random stream passed in, which is that one soldier's own stream.

Drawing Fire: a pencil-on-paper stick-figure battle.

This cut is the battlefield (paper, and the ground with its hills) and a battle the computer plays, the winner (or a draw) announced and the next battle started on its own. Players join it at any time (seats): START on the keyboard (Enter) or a controller chooses a side and takes over one of its soldiers. drawing and seat_drawing draw it all in pencil.

Player input: a device (the keyboard and mouse, or a game controller) becomes an Intent.

A player's input is turned into an Intent like any other driver's, so the battle's rules never depend on who drives a soldier. Everything is read from an InputSnapshot (the engine's current_input()), never from pygame directly, and nothing here uses a clock or randomness.

Drawing the seats in pencil: the join note, each player's card, and the choosing highlight.

Kept apart from drawing (which draws the battle) so neither grows too long. The same rules hold: text is rendered once per content (drawing.text_surface), fonts are made once, and a hand-drawn line wanders by drawing.wobble, never by a random stream.

Seats: players join a running battle, choose a side and a soldier, take over and leave.

A player presses START on a device with no seat, chooses a side (Random by default, then the Pencil Platoon or the Graphite Brigade), then chooses one of that side's computer soldiers and drives him. When he dies the player takes another of his side, picked from the seats' own random stream (or waits when there is none). Holding BACK, or unplugging the controller, leaves, and the soldier goes back to the computer at once.

Nothing here draws or reads pygame input: it works on ButtonEdges and Devices, and its only randomness is the stream it is given, so a seat changing hands never shifts a soldier's stream.

Swatches: recolouring a sprite by palette swap.

A sprite file lists swatch sets beside its palette. A set names parts of the sprite (a helmet, a uniform), and each part lists palette characters: the first is the part's base colour, the rest are shades of it (a shadow) that keep their brightness ratio when the part is recoloured.

[swatches.livery.helmet]
colors = ["h", "H"]
role = "primary"

A Scheme gives colours to parts by name or by role, and recolor_surface() swaps them in. Nothing here names a game: it is written to move into the engine.

The battlefield's ground: flat paper with a few seeded hills.

class Battle:
    """The whole battle: two armies, the sandbags, the bullets in flight and the clock."""

    def __init__(
        self, *, terrain: Terrain, soldiers_per_side: int, sandbag_xs: Sequence[float]
    ) -> None:
        """Muster both armies and lay the sandbags.

        Args:
            terrain: The ground everything stands on.
            soldiers_per_side: How many soldiers each army has.
            sandbag_xs: The x positions of the sandbags.

        """
        self.terrain = terrain
        self.soldiers: list[Soldier] = []
        self.sandbags = [Sandbag(x=x, width=SANDBAG_WIDTH, sand=1.0) for x in sandbag_xs]
        self.bullets: list[Bullet] = []
        self.seconds = 0.0

        fifth = terrain.width * SPAWN_FRACTION
        for side in Side:
            fifth_start = 0.0 if side is Side.PLATOON else terrain.width - fifth
            facing = 0.0 if side is Side.PLATOON else math.pi
            for index in range(soldiers_per_side):
                # Spread evenly through the fifth, never on its edges
                x = fifth_start + fifth * (index + 0.5) / soldiers_per_side
                self.soldiers.append(
                    Soldier(
                        soldier_id=len(self.soldiers),
                        side=side,
                        x=x,
                        y=terrain.ground_y(x),
                        health=SOLDIER_HEALTH,
                        aim_angle=facing,
                        cooldown=0.0,
                    )
                )

    def living(self, side: Side) -> list[Soldier]:
        """Find an army's soldiers who are still standing.

        Args:
            side: The army.

        Returns:
            The living soldiers, in id order.

        """
        return [soldier for soldier in self.soldiers if soldier.side is side and soldier.alive]

    def soldier(self, soldier_id: int) -> Soldier:
        """Find a soldier by id.

        Args:
            soldier_id: The soldier's id.

        Returns:
            The soldier.

        """
        return self.soldiers[soldier_id]

    @property
    def over(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the battle has ended: either side, or both (a draw), has no living soldiers."""
        return not self.living(Side.PLATOON) or not self.living(Side.BRIGADE)

    @property
    def winner(self) -> Side | None:
        """The side with soldiers left when the other has none.

        None while both fight, and in a draw (both armies fell in the same step): ``over``
        tells the two apart.
        """
        platoon_alive = bool(self.living(Side.PLATOON))
        brigade_alive = bool(self.living(Side.BRIGADE))
        if platoon_alive and not brigade_alive:
            return Side.PLATOON
        if brigade_alive and not platoon_alive:
            return Side.BRIGADE
        return None

    def step(self, *, dt: float, intents: Mapping[int, Intent]) -> list[BattleEvent]:
        """Advance the battle: apply every intent, then fly the bullets.

        Soldiers and bullets are processed in list order, so the same inputs always give
        the same battle.

        Args:
            dt: The seconds to advance.
            intents: What each soldier wants to do, by soldier id (missing ones stand still).

        Returns:
            What happened this step.

        """
        self.seconds += dt
        events: list[BattleEvent] = []
        for soldier in self.soldiers:
            if soldier.alive:
                soldier.cooldown = max(0.0, soldier.cooldown - dt)
                # A soldier without an intent stands still, keeping the aim it had
                intent = intents.get(soldier.soldier_id)
                if intent is not None:
                    self._apply_intent(soldier, intent, dt=dt)
        self.bullets = [
            bullet for bullet in self.bullets if not self._fly(bullet, dt=dt, events=events)
        ]
        return events

    def _apply_intent(self, soldier: Soldier, intent: Intent, *, dt: float) -> None:
        """Walk, aim and maybe fire one soldier's pistol."""
        move = min(max(intent.move, -1.0), 1.0)
        target_x = soldier.x + move * WALK_SPEED * dt
        target_x = min(max(target_x, 0.0), float(self.terrain.width - 1))
        soldier.x = self._stop_at_sandbags(soldier.x, target_x)
        soldier.y = self.terrain.ground_y(soldier.x)
        soldier.aim_angle = intent.aim_angle
        if intent.fire and soldier.cooldown <= 0.0:
            muzzle_x, muzzle_y = soldier.muzzle
            self.bullets.append(
                Bullet(
                    x=muzzle_x,
                    y=muzzle_y,
                    velocity_x=BULLET_SPEED * math.cos(soldier.aim_angle),
                    # Screen y grows downward, so aiming up gives negative velocity
                    velocity_y=-BULLET_SPEED * math.sin(soldier.aim_angle),
                    side=soldier.side,
                    distance_left=PISTOL_RANGE,
                    ignored_sandbags=self._own_cover(soldier),
                )
            )
            soldier.cooldown = PISTOL_COOLDOWN

    def _own_cover(self, soldier: Soldier) -> frozenset[int]:
        """Find the sandbags a soldier's shot never hits: those he stands inside or next to.

        A sandbag counts when the soldier stands inside its width or within MUZZLE_DISTANCE of
        its nearer edge (judged when he fires), so his muzzle may already be inside it.

        Args:
            soldier: The soldier firing.

        Returns:
            The sandbags' indices.

        """
        return frozenset(
            index
            for index, sandbag in enumerate(self.sandbags)
            if abs(soldier.x - sandbag.x) - sandbag.width / 2 <= MUZZLE_DISTANCE
        )

    def _stop_at_sandbags(self, start_x: float, target_x: float) -> float:
        """Stop a walk at the edge of a sandbag that is tall enough to block it.

        Args:
            start_x: Where the walk starts.
            target_x: Where the walk would end.

        Returns:
            Where the walk really ends.

        """
        stopped_x = target_x
        for sandbag in self.sandbags:
            if not sandbag.blocks_walking:
                continue
            left_edge = sandbag.x - sandbag.width / 2
            right_edge = sandbag.x + sandbag.width / 2
            # Only a walk that starts outside the sandbag and reaches it is stopped, so a
            # soldier already standing inside one can still walk out
            if start_x <= left_edge < stopped_x:
                stopped_x = left_edge
            elif start_x >= right_edge > stopped_x:
                stopped_x = right_edge
        return stopped_x

    def _fly(self, bullet: Bullet, *, dt: float, events: list[BattleEvent]) -> bool:
        """Move a bullet along its path.

        Args:
            bullet: The bullet.
            dt: The seconds to fly.
            events: Where to add what the bullet hits.

        Returns:
            Whether the bullet is spent.

        """
        distance = min(BULLET_SPEED * dt, bullet.distance_left)
        checks = max(1, math.ceil(distance / BULLET_CHECK_DISTANCE))
        check_distance = distance / checks
        direction_x = bullet.velocity_x / BULLET_SPEED
        direction_y = bullet.velocity_y / BULLET_SPEED
        for _ in range(checks):
            bullet.x += direction_x * check_distance
            bullet.y += direction_y * check_distance
            bullet.distance_left -= check_distance
            if self._bullet_is_spent(bullet, events=events):
                return True
        return bullet.distance_left <= 0.0

    def _bullet_is_spent(self, bullet: Bullet, *, events: list[BattleEvent]) -> bool:
        """Check a bullet against the field, the ground, the sandbags and the enemy.

        Args:
            bullet: The bullet.
            events: Where to add what the bullet hits.

        Returns:
            Whether the bullet hit something and is spent.

        """
        if not 0.0 <= bullet.x <= self.terrain.width - 1:
            return True
        if bullet.y >= self.terrain.ground_y(bullet.x):
            return True
        for index, sandbag in enumerate(self.sandbags):
            if index not in bullet.ignored_sandbags and self._sandbag_is_hit(bullet, sandbag):
                sandbag.sand = max(0.0, sandbag.sand - SAND_PER_HIT)
                if sandbag.flattened:
                    events.append(SandbagFlattened(index=index))
                return True
        for soldier in self.living(bullet.side.opponent):
            chest_x, chest_y = soldier.chest
            if math.hypot(bullet.x - chest_x, bullet.y - chest_y) <= SOLDIER_HIT_RADIUS:
                soldier.health = max(0, soldier.health - PISTOL_DAMAGE)
                if not soldier.alive:
                    events.append(SoldierKilled(soldier_id=soldier.soldier_id))
                return True
        return False

    def _sandbag_is_hit(self, bullet: Bullet, sandbag: Sandbag) -> bool:
        """Check whether a bullet is inside a standing sandbag.

        Args:
            bullet: The bullet.
            sandbag: The sandbag.

        Returns:
            Whether the bullet is inside it.

        """
        if sandbag.flattened:
            return False
        if abs(bullet.x - sandbag.x) > sandbag.width / 2:
            return False
        return bullet.y >= self.terrain.ground_y(sandbag.x) - sandbag.height

def step(self, *, dt: float, intents: Mapping[int, Intent]) -> list[BattleEvent]:
    """Advance the battle: apply every intent, then fly the bullets.

    Soldiers and bullets are processed in list order, so the same inputs always give
    the same battle.

    Args:
        dt: The seconds to advance.
        intents: What each soldier wants to do, by soldier id (missing ones stand still).

    Returns:
        What happened this step.

    """
    self.seconds += dt
    events: list[BattleEvent] = []
    for soldier in self.soldiers:
        if soldier.alive:
            soldier.cooldown = max(0.0, soldier.cooldown - dt)
            # A soldier without an intent stands still, keeping the aim it had
            intent = intents.get(soldier.soldier_id)
            if intent is not None:

@dataclass
class Sandbag:
    """A sandbag wall that loses sand when shot and flattens."""

    x: float
    width: float
    sand: float  # 1.0 full .. 0.0 flat

    @property
    def height(self) -> float:
        """How tall the sandbag stands now."""
        return SANDBAG_HEIGHT * self.sand

    @property
    def blocks_walking(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the sandbag is tall enough (at least half a soldier) to stop a walk.

        The computer driver uses this same rule for "tall enough to cover a soldier".
        """
        return self.height >= SOLDIER_HEIGHT / 2

    @property
    def flattened(self) -> bool:
        """Whether all the sand is gone."""
        return self.sand <= 0.0

def sandbag_positions(*, terrain: Terrain, random: Random) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """Choose where the sandbags go: two or three per side, away from the spawn fifths.

    Each side's stretch (from just past its spawn fifth to the middle) is cut into one
    slot per sandbag, so the sandbags never overlap. A bag's spot is redrawn (from the same
    stream, so it stays deterministic) until the ground under it is level to within
    ``SANDBAG_MAX_GROUND_VARIATION``; if no try is, the flattest is used.

    Args:
        terrain: The ground the sandbags go on.
        random: The seeded stream the positions are drawn from.

    Returns:
        The sandbags' x positions, from left to right.

    """
    half_width = SANDBAG_WIDTH / 2
    stretch_start = terrain.width * SPAWN_FRACTION + half_width
    stretch_end = terrain.width / 2 - half_width
    positions: list[float] = []
    for side in Side:
        count = random.randint(*SANDBAGS_PER_SIDE_RANGE)
        slot_width = (stretch_end - stretch_start) / count
        for slot in range(count):
            candidates = [
                random.uniform(
                    stretch_start + slot * slot_width, stretch_start + (slot + 1) * slot_width
                )
                for _ in range(SANDBAG_PLACEMENT_ATTEMPTS)
            ]
            position = _level_position(terrain=terrain, candidates=candidates)
            # Brigade's stretch mirrors Platoon's
            positions.append(position if side is Side.PLATOON else terrain.width - position)
    return tuple(sorted(positions))

def draw_banner(surface: pygame.Surface, lines: Sequence[str]) -> None:
    """Show a hand-lettered message across the middle of the sky, a line at a time.

    The first line is centred BANNER_HEIGHT_FRACTION down the screen (where a one-line banner
    always is); each further line is centred under the one before it. Every line is lettered
    and kept on its own (``_banner_surface``, cached by its text).

    Args:
        surface: Where to draw.
        lines: The message's lines: the winner's one line, or a draw's two.

    """
    centre_x = surface.get_width() // 2
    previous: pygame.Rect | None = None
    for text in lines:
        banner = _banner_surface(text)
        if previous is None:
            rect = banner.get_rect(
                center=(centre_x, round(surface.get_height() * BANNER_HEIGHT_FRACTION))
            )
        else:
            rect = banner.get_rect(midtop=(centre_x, previous.bottom + BANNER_LINE_GAP_PIXELS))
        surface.blit(banner, rect)
        previous = rect

def draw_bullet(surface: pygame.Surface, bullet: Bullet) -> None:
    """Draw a bullet as a short pencil dash trailing behind it.

    Args:
        surface: Where to draw.
        bullet: The bullet.

    """
    speed = math.hypot(bullet.velocity_x, bullet.velocity_y)
    if speed < MINIMUM_BULLET_SPEED:
        pygame.draw.circle(
            surface=surface, color=PENCIL_COLOR, center=(bullet.x, bullet.y), radius=BULLET_WIDTH
        )
        return
    tail = (
        bullet.x - bullet.velocity_x / speed * BULLET_DASH_PIXELS,
        bullet.y - bullet.velocity_y / speed * BULLET_DASH_PIXELS,
    )
    pygame.draw.line(
        surface=surface,
        color=PENCIL_COLOR,
        start_pos=tail,
        end_pos=(bullet.x, bullet.y),
        width=BULLET_WIDTH,
    )

def draw_hud(surface: pygame.Surface, battle: Battle) -> None:
    """Write each army's name and living count in its own top corner.

    Args:
        surface: Where to draw.
        battle: The battle.

    """
    for side in Side:
        on_left = side is Side.PLATOON
        name = text_surface(ARMY_NAMES[side], size=HUD_NAME_FONT_SIZE)
        count = text_surface(f'soldiers {len(battle.living(side))}', size=HUD_COUNT_FONT_SIZE)
        chip = pygame.Rect(0, 0, HUD_CHIP_SIZE_PIXELS, HUD_CHIP_SIZE_PIXELS)
        top = HUD_MARGIN_PIXELS
        if on_left:
            chip.topleft = (HUD_MARGIN_PIXELS, top + (name.get_height() - chip.height) // 2)
            name_left = chip.right + HUD_LINE_GAP_PIXELS * 3
        else:
            chip.topright = (
                surface.get_width() - HUD_MARGIN_PIXELS,
                top + (name.get_height() - chip.height) // 2,
            )
            name_left = chip.left - HUD_LINE_GAP_PIXELS * 3 - name.get_width()
        pygame.draw.rect(surface=surface, color=ARMY_COLORS[side], rect=chip)
        pygame.draw.rect(surface=surface, color=PENCIL_COLOR, rect=chip, width=1)
        surface.blit(name, (name_left, top))
        surface.blit(count, (name_left, top + name.get_height() + HUD_LINE_GAP_PIXELS))

Draw a sandbag wall: it sags as it loses sand, and trickles sand once hit, until flat.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default surface Surface

Where to draw.

required sandbag Sandbag

The sandbag.

required terrain Terrain
