docs.title: glitchygames API Reference
docs.text:
glitchygames.color

glitchygames.color provides color utilities like palettes, helpers to do color conversion, etc...

glitchygames.engine

The glitchygames.engine module handles game initialization, event routing, minimal event loop that calls into the active scene's update method.

To start your game, pass your main Scene class to the engine.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bitrot Adventures."""
import argparse
import logging
import pathlib

import pygame
from glitchygames.engine import GameEngine
from glitchygames.scenes import Scene

# Instantiate a logger called "game" to enable glitchygames
# logging module. This is optional, but recommended.
LOG = logging.getLogger('game')

# Think of a scene as an encapsulated pygame screen.
#
# Each scene can handle its own events, update its own
# state, and draw its own graphics.
#
# The engine will handle switching between scenes
# and passing events to the current scene.
#
# The engine will also handle drawing the current
# scene to the screen.
class BitrotAdventures(Scene):
    """Draws a pixel to the screen"""

    NAME = 'Bitrot Adventures'
    VERSION = '0.0.0'

    def __init__(self, options):
        super().__init__(options=options)

    # This is called by glitchygames.GameEngine before
    # the class is instantiated.
    #
    # Note that GameEngine defines a few command line
    # options that are intended to be common across all
    # games, so it's worth checking your game with --help
    # before adding new options to ensure that you haven't
    # clobbered an existing option.
    @classmethod
    def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):
        """Game specific command line arguments."""
        parser.add_argument('-s', '--some-game-specific-option',
                            help='foo help')
        return parser



def main():
    # Note that the Scene (BitrotAdventures) is
    # passed in uninitialized - the engine
    # will initialize it for you.
    GameEngine(
        game=BitrotAdventures,
        icon='/path/to/icon'
    ).start()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

When we run ./bitrotadventures.py with the -h flag, we can see our command line option, along with options the engine and scene manager provide to us:

$ ./bitrotadventures.py -h
pygame-ce 2.5.8 (SDL 2.32.10, Python 3.14.8)
usage: Bitrot Adventures version 0.0.0 [-h] [-f TARGET_FPS] [--fps-log-interval-ms FPS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS]
                                       [-w | --windowed | --no-windowed] [-r RESOLUTION] [--use-gfxdraw]
                                       [--update-type {update,flip}] [--timer-backend {auto,fast,pygame}]
                                       [--sleep-granularity-ns SLEEP_GRANULARITY_NS] [--windows-timer-1ms] [--log-timer-jitter]
                                       [--perf-trim-percent PERF_TRIM_PERCENT] [--fps-histogram {equal-range,target-relative}]
                                       [--debug-overlay | --no-debug-overlay] [--debug-events] [--record-trace PATH]
                                       [--replay-trace PATH] [--replay-fps {recorded,real}] [--audit | --no-audit]
                                       [--compare-processing] [--max-processing-slowdown PERCENT] [--replay-pause-at-frame N]
                                       [--rebaseline NEW] [--replay-digest PATH] [--random-seed RANDOM_SEED]
                                       [--screen-shake-intensity SCREEN_SHAKE_INTENSITY] [--rumble-intensity RUMBLE_INTENSITY]
                                       [--live-voice-pool LIVE_VOICE_POOL] [--default-background {test-pattern,channel-3}]
                                       [--video-driver {cocoa,offscreen,dummy}] [--headless]
                                       [--input-mode {auto,joystick,controller}] [--font-name FONT_NAME] [--font-size FONT_SIZE]
                                       [--font-bold] [--font-italic] [--font-antialias | --no-font-antialias] [--font-dpi FONT_DPI]
                                       [--font-system {pygame,freetype}] [-l {debug,info,warning,error,critical}]
                                       [--no-unhandled-events] [-p] [-s SOME_GAME_SPECIFIC_OPTION]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

Graphics Options:
  -f, --target-fps TARGET_FPS
                        cap the framerate (default: the game's TARGET_FPS, else 60.01; 0 = uncapped)
  --fps-log-interval-ms FPS_LOG_INTERVAL_MS
                        how often to log the FPS counter in ms (default: 1000)
  -w, --windowed, --no-windowed
                        run in a window; --no-windowed runs fullscreen (default: windowed)
  -r, --resolution RESOLUTION
                        the resolution to use (default: 800x480)
  --use-gfxdraw         not used yet: stored, but nothing draws with pygame.gfxdraw because of it
  --update-type {update,flip}
                        update or flip (default: update)
  --timer-backend {auto,fast,pygame}
                        timer backend for draw loop pacing (default: auto, the fast backend with this machine's sleep delay
                        measured, so each sleep wakes in time; fast assumes sleeps wake on time; pygame is the legacy backend)
  --sleep-granularity-ns SLEEP_GRANULARITY_NS
                        how long before each frame deadline the fast backend is to wake from its sleep and spin (ns); 0 spins
                        only
  --windows-timer-1ms   on Windows, request 1ms system timer resolution
  --random-seed RANDOM_SEED
                        master seed for every engine random stream (default: a random 64-bit seed, logged in recordings)
  --screen-shake-intensity SCREEN_SHAKE_INTENSITY
                        screen shake strength from 0.0 (off) to 1.0 (default: 1.0)
  --rumble-intensity RUMBLE_INTENSITY
                        controller rumble strength from 0.0 (off) to 1.0 (default: 1.0)
  --live-voice-pool LIVE_VOICE_POOL
                        mixer channels reserved for real-time synth voices (default: 4)
  --default-background {test-pattern,channel-3}
                        the background of a scene that sets none: the TV test pattern or the channel 3 blue screen (default:
                        test-pattern)
  --video-driver {cocoa,offscreen,dummy}
                        SDL's video driver for the display (sets SDL_VIDEODRIVER for the run; default: SDL_VIDEODRIVER's own
                        value, then Wayland on a Linux Wayland session, then SDL's choice; --headless
                        overrides it)

Diagnostics Options:
  --log-timer-jitter    log frame pacing jitter statistics periodically
  --perf-trim-percent PERF_TRIM_PERCENT
                        percent of frames to trim from top and bottom in the game's global FPS report
  --fps-histogram {equal-range,target-relative}
                        FPS histogram buckets in the game's shutdown report: equal-range (10 equal buckets spanning the analyzed
                        min to max, default) or target-relative (10% steps of the target FPS)
  --debug-overlay, --no-debug-overlay
                        show the debug overlay at startup (F3 toggles, F4 cycles panels)
  --debug-events        log a warning the first time each unhandled event type arrives (--no-unhandled-events raises on one
                        instead)
  --record-trace PATH   record the session (sprites, frame times, input events, random seed) to a gzip JSON Lines trace for
                        inspection and later replay (default: off)
  --replay-trace PATH   replay a --record-trace recording exactly through the engine, comparing every frame with it and
                        reporting the first divergence (default: off)
  --replay-fps {recorded,real}
                        with --replay-trace: post FPS events from the recorded frame times (recorded, the default: exact, and
                        compared with the recording) or from this machine's measured frame times (real: what this machine
                        achieves; FPS events are then not compared, and sprites that draw the FPS value may diverge)
  --audit, --no-audit   with --replay-trace: instead of replaying, replay the recording twice in fresh headless processes with
                        different hash seeds and compare every frame with the recording and between the runs; exits 0 when both
                        match, 3 otherwise, 70 if a run could not finish
  --compare-processing  with --replay-trace --headless: measure each frame's processing time (its work, without presenting or
                        pacing) and report how it compares with the recording's (only meaningful on the machine that recorded)
  --max-processing-slowdown PERCENT
                        with --replay-trace --headless (implies --compare-processing): a replay that matched but took more than
                        PERCENT longer than the recording's processing time exits 8; a recording without processing times exits
                        65
  --replay-pause-at-frame N
                        with --replay-trace, watched: skip the start screen, run frames 0 to N - 1 without showing them, then
                        pause with frame N next (what step back restarts with; ignored with --headless)
  --rebaseline NEW      with --replay-trace OLD and --headless: replay OLD on the current code without stopping at divergences,
                        write the run's recording (OLD's inputs, the current sprites) to NEW, print a summary of the frames and
                        sprites that changed and exit 0
  --replay-digest PATH  with --replay-trace: write a SHA-256 of every replayed frame, then the divergence, to PATH as JSON lines
                        (used by --audit)
  --headless            run on SDL's dummy video and audio drivers: no window, no sound. With --replay-trace the replay also
                        runs unpaced and prints its report to stdout (exit 0 when it matches, 1 when it diverges, 65 for a
                        truncated recording)

Controller Options:
  --input-mode {auto,joystick,controller}
                        Which gamepads the game sees (default: auto, every device; a mapped pad sends controller events, any
                        other device joystick events; joystick: every device sends joystick events; controller: mapped pads
                        only)

Font Options:
  --font-name FONT_NAME
                        Font to use (default: the bundled Vera; the bundled variants are Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any
                        other name is looked up among the system's fonts)
  --font-size FONT_SIZE
                        size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own (default: 14)
  --font-bold           draw text bold
  --font-italic         draw text italic
  --font-antialias, --no-font-antialias
                        antialias text (default: True)
  --font-dpi FONT_DPI   the resolution, in dots per inch, font sizes are scaled at (a size is in pixels at 72) (default: 72)
  --font-system {pygame,freetype}
                        Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)

Game Options:
  -l, --log-level {debug,info,warning,error,critical}
                        set the logging level (default: warning; a bug report asks for info)
  --no-unhandled-events
                        fail on unhandled events
  -p, --profile         enable profiling

Bitrot Adventures v0.0.0 Options:
  -s, --some-game-specific-option SOME_GAME_SPECIFIC_OPTION
                        foo help

glitchygames.events

The glitchygames.events module extends the pygame event subsystem by giving you on_event callbacks. Note that you can use the normal pygame raw event mode by simply implementing a process_event(event) method in your Scene: the engine then calls it once for each raw pygame event, in order, instead of dispatching on_event callbacks.

This can be especially useful for porting games to glitchygames, but there are some advantages to using glitchygames' event subsystem.

The glitchygames.events subsystem detects events that your game does not handle: each type is reported once (with --debug-events), raised as an error under --no-unhandled-events, and counted in a table the engine logs at shutdown. See Event System.

Note that if you bypass the glitchygames game engine event processing, you'll lose some functionality like esc and q to quit, along with on_*_event handler support.

It is recommended that you use the glitchygames event subsystem.

TODO: Add some benchmark data comparing the two methods in various user scenarios to highlight the performance implications.

glitchygames.fonts

The glitchygames.fonts module is a module that extends pygame's font mechanisms.

glitchygames.interfaces

The glitchygames.interfaces module implements various interfaces, notably the Sprite and Scene interfaces, which provide an API contract for subclasses.

Note: Migrating to these interfaces is a work in progress. More to come.

glitchygames.movement

The glitchygames.movement module defines some common movement schemes.

glitchygames.pixels

The glitchygames.pixels module provides common pixel manipulation operations such as 565 conversion.

glitchygames.sprites

The glitchygames.sprites module provides extended subclasses for sprite handling that will enable glitchygames to provide common tools and file formats that are human readable and templatable in addition to common sprite sheet formats and other goodies.

glitchygames.ui

The glitchygames.ui module provides common UI elements such as menubars, buttons, sliders, etc...

Also in the reference: glitchygames.audio (synthesis, recipes, live voices), glitchygames.collision (layers and hitbox-aware detection), glitchygames.effects (easing, tweens, screen shake), glitchygames.input (action maps, devices, the per-frame input snapshot, rumble), glitchygames.physics, glitchygames.replay (gameplay replay), glitchygames.state (saves) and glitchygames.transitions (scene transitions).

Exit codes (ExitCode, glitchygames/exit_codes.py; logged as Exiting with ...):

  • SUCCESS.
  • GENERATION_REJECTED / EXTRACTION_REJECTED: the server answered an error status (other than 503) or a response that says the request failed.
  • SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: the server cannot be reached, stops answering, or answers 503.
  • OPTIONS_REFUSED: --server-url is not a usable URL.
  • MISSING_INPUT: the APNG to extract does not exist.
  • UNUSABLE_INPUT: an input file that cannot be read, or a response that cannot be decoded or is malformed (a missing field or one of the wrong type counts as the server's fault).
  • CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT: an output file or directory cannot be written.
  • INTERNAL_ERROR: any other exception (a client bug), logged with its traceback.
  • argparse's ARGUMENT_PARSER_ERROR for a usage error.

def create_apng_from_frames(
    frames_base64: list[str],
    frame_delay_ms: int = 100,
) -> bytes:
    """Create an APNG (Animated PNG) from a list of base64-encoded PNG frames.

    Args:
        frames_base64: List of base64-encoded PNG frame data
        frame_delay_ms: Delay between frames in milliseconds

    Returns:
        APNG file content as bytes

    """
    apng = APNG()

    for frame_base64 in frames_base64:
        frame_bytes = base64.b64decode(frame_base64)
        # Create PNG from bytes (apng library lacks type stubs)
        png: PNG = PNG.from_bytes(frame_bytes)
        # Add frame with delay (delay is in milliseconds, APNG uses delay/delay_den)
        apng.append(png, delay=frame_delay_ms, delay_den=1000)

    # Write to bytes buffer
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    apng.save(buffer)
    return buffer.getvalue()

def extract_apng_frames(
    server_url: str,
    apng_path: str,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Extract frames and metadata from an APNG file.

    Args:
        server_url: Base URL of the API server
        apng_path: Path to the APNG file

    Returns:
        API response with frames and metadata

    """
    url = f'{server_url.rstrip("/")}/sprites/extract-frames'

    # Read and encode the APNG file
    apng_bytes = Path(apng_path).read_bytes()
    apng_base64 = base64.b64encode(apng_bytes).decode('utf-8')

    payload = {
        'apng_base64': apng_base64,
    }

    LOG.debug('Sending extract request to %s', url)

    with httpx2.Client(timeout=60.0) as client:
        response = client.post(url, json=payload)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return _response_object(response=response)

def find_available_directory(base_dir: Path) -> Path:
    """Find an available directory path with incremented number.

    Always uses numbered format: base-001, base-002, etc.
    Finds the next available number.

    Args:
        base_dir: The base directory path (without number)

    Returns:
        An available directory path with -NNN suffix

    """
    name = base_dir.name
    parent = base_dir.parent

    counter = 1
    while counter < MAX_FILE_NUMBERING_ATTEMPTS:  # Safety limit
        new_dir = parent / f'{name}-{counter:03d}'
        if not new_dir.exists():
            return new_dir
        counter += 1

    # Fallback: use timestamp if we somehow hit 999 directories
    timestamp = int(clock.wall_clock_epoch_seconds())
    return parent / f'{name}-{timestamp}'

def find_available_path(base_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Find an available file path, auto-incrementing if necessary.

    If the base path doesn't exist, returns it unchanged.
    If it exists, tries base_001, base_002, etc. until finding an available name.

    Args:
        base_path: The desired file path

    Returns:
        An available file path (either the original or with _NNN suffix)

    """
    if not base_path.exists():
        return base_path

    # File exists, find next available number
    stem = base_path.stem
    suffix = base_path.suffix
    parent = base_path.parent

    counter = 1
    while counter < MAX_FILE_NUMBERING_ATTEMPTS:  # Safety limit
        new_path = parent / f'{stem}_{counter:03d}{suffix}'
        if not new_path.exists():
            return new_path
        counter += 1

    # Fallback: use timestamp if we somehow hit 999 files
    timestamp = int(clock.wall_clock_epoch_seconds())
    return parent / f'{stem}_{timestamp}{suffix}'

def generate_sprite(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments]
    server_url: str,
    prompt: str,
    output_formats: list[str],
    *,
    output_path: str | None = None,
    width: int | None = None,
    height: int | None = None,
    frame_count: int | None = None,
    film_strip_count: int | None = None,
    animation_duration: float | None = None,
    png_scale: int = 1,
    model: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Generate a sprite via the API.

    Args:
        server_url: Base URL of the API server
        prompt: Text description of the sprite
        output_formats: List of output formats ('toml', 'png')
        output_path: Directory to save files (optional)
        width: Sprite width in pixels (optional)
        height: Sprite height in pixels (optional)
        frame_count: Number of frames per animation (default: 1)
        film_strip_count: Number of film strips to create (optional)
        animation_duration: Duration of animation in seconds (optional)
        png_scale: Scale factor for PNG output
        model: AI model override: a role or an exact size (e.g., 'bonsai-2-9b')

    Returns:
        API response as a dictionary

    """
    url = f'{server_url.rstrip("/")}/sprites/generate'

    # Default frame_count to 1
    effective_frame_count = frame_count or 1

    payload: dict[str, str | list[str] | int | float] = {
        'prompt': prompt,
        'output_format': output_formats,
        'png_scale': png_scale,
        'frame_count': effective_frame_count,
    }

    if output_path:
        payload['output_path'] = output_path
    if width:
        payload['width'] = width
    if height:
        payload['height'] = height
    if film_strip_count:
        payload['film_strip_count'] = film_strip_count
    if animation_duration:
        payload['animation_duration'] = animation_duration
    if model:
        payload['model'] = model

    LOG.debug('Sending request to %s', url)
    LOG.debug('Payload: %s', json.dumps(payload, indent=2))

    with httpx2.Client(timeout=300.0) as client:
        response = client.post(url, json=payload)
        response.raise_for_status()
        return _response_object(response=response)

def main(args: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the CLI client.

    Args:
        args: Command line arguments (defaults to sys.argv[1:])

    Returns:
        The exit code (``ExitCode``; see the module docstring). A usage error exits through
        argparse instead (SystemExit with ``ExitCode.ARGUMENT_PARSER_ERROR``).

    """
    parser = create_parser()
    parsed_args = parser.parse_args(args)

    # Set up logging
    if parsed_args.verbose:
        logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format='%(levelname)s: %(message)s')
    elif parsed_args.quiet:
        logging.basicConfig(level=logging.ERROR, format='%(levelname)s: %(message)s')
    else:
        logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='%(message)s')

    # Validate that prompt is provided for generation
    if not parsed_args.extract_frames and not parsed_args.prompt:
        parser.error('prompt is required unless using --extract-frames')

    try:
        if parsed_args.extract_frames:
            exit_code = _handle_extract_frames(parsed_args)
        else:
            # Use default output formats if none specified
            output_formats = parsed_args.output_formats or DEFAULT_OUTPUT_FORMATS
            exit_code = _handle_generate_sprite(parsed_args, output_formats)
    except Exception:
        # The handlers map every error they expect, so anything else is a client bug
        LOG.exception('Unexpected error in the sprite client')
        exit_code = ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
    LOG.info('Exiting with %s', ExitCode(exit_code).describe())
    return ExitCode(exit_code)

def save_files_locally(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments]
    response: dict[str, Any],
    output_path: str,
    output_formats: list[str],
    *,
    animation_duration: float | None = None,
    extract_scale: int = 8,
    model_used: str | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Save files locally from the API response.

    Creates a directory for each sprite containing:
    - The .toml file
    - The .apng file (if animated)
    - An 'extracted' subdirectory with individual frame PNGs (upscaled nearest-neighbor)

    Args:
        response: API response dictionary
        output_path: Base directory to save files
        output_formats: List of requested output formats
        animation_duration: Total animation duration in seconds (for APNG timing)
        extract_scale: Scale factor for extracted frames (nearest-neighbor, default: 8)
        model_used: AI model used for generation (embedded in PNG metadata)

    Returns:
        List of saved file paths

    """
    saved_files: list[str] = []
    base_output_dir = Path(output_path)
    base_output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    sprite_name: str = response.get('sprite_name', 'sprite')
    # Sanitize sprite name for directory/filename
    safe_name: str = ''.join(c if c.isalnum() or c in '-_' else '_' for c in sprite_name)
    if not safe_name:
        safe_name = 'sprite'

    # Create a directory for this sprite
    sprite_dir = find_available_directory(base_output_dir / safe_name)
    sprite_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    LOG.info('Created sprite directory: %s', sprite_dir)

    # Save TOML if requested and available
    if 'toml' in output_formats and response.get('toml_content'):
        toml_path = sprite_dir / f'{safe_name}.toml'
        toml_path.write_text(response['toml_content'], encoding='utf-8')
        saved_files.append(str(toml_path))
        LOG.info('Saved TOML: %s', toml_path)

    # Save APNG and extracted frames if animation frames are available
    if response.get('all_frames_png_base64'):
        frames: list[str] = response['all_frames_png_base64']
        rendered_frames: list[dict[str, Any]] = response.get('rendered_frames', [])
        frame_count = len(frames)

        # Calculate frame delay for APNG
        # Use animation_duration if provided, otherwise default to 100ms per frame
        if animation_duration and frame_count > 0:
            frame_delay_ms = int((animation_duration * 1000) / frame_count)
        else:
            frame_delay_ms = 100  # Default: 10 FPS

        # Create and save APNG
        apng_path = sprite_dir / f'{safe_name}.apng'
        apng_path.write_bytes(create_apng_from_frames(frames, frame_delay_ms=frame_delay_ms))
        saved_files.append(str(apng_path))
        LOG.info('Saved APNG: %s (%s frames, %sms/frame)', apng_path, frame_count, frame_delay_ms)

        # Extract and save individual frames with metadata
        extracted_dir = sprite_dir / 'extracted'
        extracted_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

        if rendered_frames:
            # Use rendered_frames for proper animation-#-frame-#.png naming
            frame_entries: list[tuple[str, str, str, str]] = [
                (
                    (
                        f'animation-{info.get("animation_index", 0)}'
                        f'-frame-{info.get("frame_index", 0)}'
                    ),
                    str(info.get('animation_index', 0)),
                    str(info.get('frame_index', 0)),
                    str(info.get('png_base64', '')),
                )
                for info in rendered_frames
            ]
        else:
            # Fallback to old naming if rendered_frames not available
            frame_entries = [
                (f'animation-0-frame-{i}', '0', str(i), frame_base64)
                for i, frame_base64 in enumerate(frames)
            ]

        saved_files.extend(
            _save_extracted_frames(
                frame_entries=frame_entries,
                extracted_dir=extracted_dir,
                frame_count=frame_count,
                frame_delay_ms=frame_delay_ms,
                extract_scale=extract_scale,
                model_used=model_used,
            ),
        )

        LOG.info('Saved %s frames to: %s (scale: %sx)', frame_count, extracted_dir, extract_scale)

    # Save single PNG if requested, available, and no animation frames
    elif 'png' in output_formats and response.get('png_base64'):
        png_path = sprite_dir / f'{safe_name}.png'
        png_bytes = base64.b64decode(response['png_base64'])
        png_path.write_bytes(png_bytes)
        saved_files.append(str(png_path))
        LOG.info('Saved PNG: %s', png_path)

    return saved_files

docs.title: configure_server_logging()
docs.text:
Log INFO and above to standard error, as the server starts (never at import).

Called by run() and by the app's lifespan (uvicorn glitchygames.api.main:app starts no run(), and a --reload worker imports the module afresh). It was a logging.basicConfig at import: any process importing the API, the test suite included, logged every logger's INFO records from then on, whatever its own level was (BUGS.md #236). basicConfig does nothing once the root logger has a handler, so a process that configured its logging first keeps its own.

Source code in src/glitchygames/api/main.py 
def configure_server_logging() -> None:
    """Log INFO and above to standard error, as the server starts (never at import).

    Called by ``run()`` and by the app's lifespan (``uvicorn glitchygames.api.main:app`` starts
    no ``run()``, and a ``--reload`` worker imports the module afresh). It was a
    ``logging.basicConfig`` at import: any process importing the API, the test suite included,
    logged every logger's INFO records from then on, whatever its own level was (BUGS.md #236).
    ``basicConfig`` does nothing once the root logger has a handler, so a process that
    configured its logging first keeps its own.
    """
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format=SERVER_LOG_FORMAT)

def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    """Create and configure the FastAPI application.

    Returns:
        Configured FastAPI application

    """
    application: FastAPI = FastAPI(
        title='GlitchyGames Sprite Generation API',
        description=(
            'Generate pixel art sprites using AI. Supports static and animated sprites '
            'with TOML and PNG output formats.'
        ),
        version='1.0.0',
        docs_url='/docs',
        redoc_url='/redoc',
        lifespan=lifespan,
        openapi_tags=[
            {
                'name': 'health',
                'description': 'Health check and status endpoints',
            },
            {
                'name': 'sprites',
                'description': 'Sprite generation and refinement endpoints',
            },
        ],
    )

    # Add CORS middleware
    application.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=['*'],  # Configure appropriately for production
        allow_credentials=False,
        allow_methods=['*'],
        allow_headers=['*'],
    )

    # Include routers
    application.include_router(health_router)
    application.include_router(sprites_router)

    return application

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(application: FastAPI) -> AsyncGenerator[None]:  # ruff: ignore[unused-function-argument]
    """Manage application startup and shutdown lifecycle."""
    configure_server_logging()
    LOG.info('Starting GlitchyGames Sprite Generation API')

    # Pre-initialize renderer service to set up pygame in headless mode
    from glitchygames.services import RendererService

    RendererService()
    LOG.info('Renderer service initialized')

    try:
        yield
    finally:
        # Runs even if the app stops because of an error
        LOG.info('Shutting down GlitchyGames Sprite Generation API')

def run() -> None:
    """Entry point for the glitchygames-server command.

    This function is called when running `glitchygames-server` from the command line.
    """
    import uvicorn

    host = os.environ.get('GLITCHYGAMES_HOST', '127.0.0.1')
    port = int(os.environ.get('GLITCHYGAMES_PORT', '8000'))
    reload = os.environ.get('GLITCHYGAMES_RELOAD', 'false').lower() == 'true'

    configure_server_logging()

    LOG.info('Starting server on %s:%s', host, port)
    uvicorn.run(
        'glitchygames.api.main:app',
        host=host,
        port=port,
        reload=reload,
    )

@router.get('/health')
async def health_check() -> HealthResponse:
    """Check the health status of the API.

    Returns service status, version, and configuration information.

    Returns:
        HealthResponse: The result.

    """
    config = ServiceConfig.from_env()

    # Whether pygame is running now (renderer will initialize it if needed): not only whether
    # it was started once, which stays True after pygame.quit() (BUGS.md #113)
    pygame_initialized: bool = RendererService.pygame_running()

    return HealthResponse(
        status='healthy',
        version='1.0.0',
        ai_model=config.ai_model,
        pygame_initialized=pygame_initialized,
    )

@router.post('/extract-frames')
async def extract_apng_frames(request: ApngExtractRequest) -> ApngExtractResponse:
    """Extract individual frames and metadata from an APNG file.

    This endpoint decodes an APNG (Animated PNG) file and returns each frame
    as a separate PNG along with timing and metadata information.

    Args:
        request: APNG extraction request with base64-encoded APNG data

    Returns:
        Extracted frames and metadata. Bad base64 or an APNG that cannot be parsed is not an
        HTTP error: the response (200) has success=False and the reason in its error field.

    Raises:
        HTTPException: 500 for any unexpected error

    """
    try:
        response = _extract_apng_frames(apng_base64=request.apng_base64)
    except Exception as e:
        LOG.exception('Unexpected error extracting APNG frames')
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=500,
            detail=f'Internal server error: {e}',
        ) from e
    else:
        return response

@router.post('/generate')
async def generate_sprite(request: SpriteGenerationRequest) -> SpriteGenerationResponse:
    """Generate a new sprite from a text prompt.

    This endpoint uses AI to generate a sprite based on the provided text
    description. The sprite can be returned as TOML, PNG, or both.

    Args:
        request: Sprite generation request with prompt and options

    Returns:
        Generated sprite data in the requested format

    Raises:
        HTTPException: If AI provider is unavailable (503) or other errors (500)

    """
    generation_service, renderer_service = _get_services()

    try:
        # Generate the sprite
        LOG.info('Generating sprite from prompt: %s...', request.prompt[:50])
        if request.model:
            LOG.info('Using model override: %s', request.model)
        result = generation_service.generate_sprite(
            prompt=request.prompt,
            width=request.width,
            height=request.height,
            frame_count=request.frame_count,
            film_strip_count=request.film_strip_count,
            animation_duration=request.animation_duration,
            model=request.model,
        )
        response = _response_for_result(
            result=result,
            request=request,
            renderer_service=renderer_service,
            failure_label='Generation',
        )
    except AIProviderError as e:
        LOG.exception('AI provider error')
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=503,
            detail=f'AI provider unavailable: {e}',
        ) from e
    except HTTPException:
        # An answer already chosen (a refused output_path is a 400): passed on as it is, not
        # turned into a 500 by the handler below (BUGS.md #200 item 3)
        raise
    except Exception as e:
        LOG.exception('Unexpected error')
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=500,
            detail=f'Internal server error: {e}',
        ) from e
    else:
        return response

docs.title: glitchygames.audio
docs.text:
Audio module for GlitchyGames.

Provides the sound engine (scene_manager.audio, an AudioEngine: one-call sounds from names, paths and instruments, with pitches, waves and noise), controller audio I/O (microphone + speaker), text-to-speech, and a push-to-talk AI voice assistant for game controllers.

Usage

coin = self.scene_manager.audio.sound('coin') # in setup(): compiled once, cached coin.play() # in gameplay

from glitchygames.audio import render_to_file

render_to_file(coin, 'out/coin.wav') # offline, no audio device

from glitchygames.audio import VoiceAssistant

assistant = VoiceAssistant.for_controller('DualSense Wireless Controller') assistant.start_listening() # On mic button press assistant.stop_listening_and_respond() # On mic button release

class AudioEngine:
    """Sounds, plays, voices and buses for one engine context (impl spec 8).

    Attributes:
        waves: The context's wave registry.
        buses: The bus tree.
        tuning: The tuning pitches resolve with (part of what a sound is).
        sounds: The sound library (``warm``, ``names``, ``statistics``).
        accountant: The audio work accounting (impl spec 11.0).
        cache_mode: The cache mode.
    """

    def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - the engine's construction settings
        self,
        *,
        partition: ChannelPartition,
        cache: CacheMode = CacheMode.RAM,
        memory_limit_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES,
        scene_source: Callable[[], object | None] = _no_scene,
        frame_number: int | None = None,
        setup_mode: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Make an engine over a channel partition.

        Args:
            partition: The mixer's channel partition (``reserve_channels``).
            cache: The cache mode (``disk`` arrives in M3: ValueError).
            memory_limit_bytes: The bytes compiled sounds may hold under ``ram``.
            scene_source: Gives the scene plays belong to and short names resolve in (the scene
                in setup, else the active scene), or None.
            frame_number: The frame being run, for the compile log.
            setup_mode: Whether compiles count as setup from the start: True while a scene is
                in ``setup()`` or has run no logic frame since (and before the first scene);
                False for an engine first made during gameplay.
        """
        self.waves: WaveRegistry = current_wave_registry()
        self.buses = BusTree()
        self.tuning = Tuning()
        self.cache_mode = cache
        self.accountant = AudioAccountant()
        self.accountant.frame_number = frame_number
        self.accountant.setup_mode = setup_mode
        self._partition = partition
        self._scene_source = scene_source
        self._voices = VoiceTable(
            partition=partition, buses=self.buses, compile_for_play=self._compile_for_play
        )
        self.sounds = SoundLibrary(
            cache=cache,
            accountant=self.accountant,
            waves=self.waves,
            tuning_source=self._current_tuning,
            memory_limit_bytes=memory_limit_bytes,
            is_playing=self._voices.is_playing_sound,
        )
        # Scene classes' (package directory, sound directory), looked up once each
        self._scene_paths: dict[type, tuple[Path | None, Path | None]] = {}
        # Scenes that played, until their voices are cleaned up (compared by identity)
        self._owners: list[object] = []
        # (served seconds, compiles) per frame over the last second (compiles_last_second)
        self._compile_window: collections.deque[tuple[float, int]] = collections.deque()
        self._compile_window_seconds = 0.0
        self._compiles_counted = 0
        self._last_frame_account = AudioFrameAccount(audio_seconds=0.0, audio_work=())
        self._last_processing_seconds: float | None = None
        # Fades held until the next update (fade_out_at_next_update): the CRT's tail
        self._fades_at_next_update: list[tuple[SoundHandle, float]] = []
        self._closed = False

    # --- Sounds and plays (impl spec 8) ---

    def sound(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8
        self,
        source: str | Instrument,
        *,
        pitch: PitchLike | None = None,
        notes: str | Sequence[tuple[PitchLike, float]] | None = None,
        chord: Sequence[PitchLike] | None = None,
        length: float | None = None,
        transpose: float = 0.0,
        parameters: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    ) -> Sound:
        """Get a sound; the first request for what it is compiles it. Getting never plays.

        Args:
            source: A short name (looked up in the scene's ``SOUND_DIRECTORY``), a path
                (relative to the scene's package directory) or an ``Instrument``.
            pitch: A pitch (``pitch``, ``notes`` and ``chord`` are mutually exclusive).
            notes: A melody.
            chord: Pitches played together.
            length: Seconds per note or chord before release.
            transpose: Semitones to shift notes or a chord.
            parameters: Live parameters (M2).

        Returns:
            The sound; its ``play()`` plays it through this engine.
        """
        package_root, sound_directory = self._paths_for(self._scene_source())
        sound = self.sounds.sound(
            source,
            scene_sound_directory=sound_directory,
            package_root=package_root,
            pitch=pitch,
            notes=notes,
            chord=chord,
            length=length,
            transpose=transpose,
            parameters=parameters,
        )
        sound.attach_player(self._play_sound)
        return sound

    def engine_sound(
        self, instrument: Instrument, *, pitch: PitchLike | None, length: float | None
    ) -> Sound:
        """Get one of the engine's own sounds (the CRT power-on's): compiled once per process.

        The process's first request compiles it, counted and attributed here like any compile;
        every later one (another power-on, another engine context) reuses the compiled samples,
        a counted hit. The cache mode and the memory limit do not apply.

        Args:
            instrument: The instrument.
            pitch: Its pitch, or None for a noise.
            length: Seconds before the release.

        Returns:
            The sound; its ``play()`` plays it through this engine.
        """
        sound = self.sounds.engine_sound(instrument, pitch=pitch, length=length)
        sound.attach_player(self._play_sound)
        return sound

    def play(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8
        self,
        source: str | Instrument,
        *,
        pitch: PitchLike | None = None,
        notes: str | Sequence[tuple[PitchLike, float]] | None = None,
        chord: Sequence[PitchLike] | None = None,
        length: float | None = None,
        transpose: float = 0.0,
        parameters: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
        volume: float | None = None,
        pan: float | None = None,
        bus: str | None = None,
        priority: int | None = None,
        loop: bool | None = None,
        at_frame: int | None = None,
        persist: bool = False,
        position: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ) -> SoundHandle:
        """Get a sound and play it: ``sound(identity...).play(playback...)``.

        Args:
            source: As ``sound``.
            pitch: As ``sound``.
            notes: As ``sound``.
            chord: As ``sound``.
            length: As ``sound``.
            transpose: As ``sound``.
            parameters: As ``sound``.
            volume: As ``Sound.play``.
            pan: As ``Sound.play``.
            bus: As ``Sound.play``.
            priority: As ``Sound.play``.
            loop: As ``Sound.play``.
            at_frame: As ``Sound.play``.
            persist: As ``Sound.play``.
            position: As ``Sound.play``.

        Returns:
            The handle.
        """
        return self.sound(
            source,
            pitch=pitch,
            notes=notes,
            chord=chord,
            length=length,
            transpose=transpose,
            parameters=parameters,
        ).play(
            volume=volume,
            pan=pan,
            bus=bus,
            priority=priority,
            loop=loop,
            at_frame=at_frame,
            persist=persist,
            position=position,
        )

    def beep(
        self,
        *,
        pitch: PitchLike = 'A4',
        wave: str = 'square',
        length: float = 0.1,
        volume: float = 0.5,
        bus: str = 'effects',
    ) -> SoundHandle:
        """Play a basic waveform with a pluck envelope (feature spec W1); cached like any sound.

        Args:
            pitch: The pitch (a float is hertz).
            wave: The wave's name.
            length: Seconds before the release.
            volume: 0-1.
            bus: The bus.

        Returns:
            The handle.
        """
        return self.play(Instrument(wave=wave), pitch=pitch, length=length, volume=volume, bus=bus)

    def stop_all(self, *, fade: float = DEFAULT_STOP_FADE_SECONDS, bus: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Fade out every voice, or every voice on a bus and the buses under it.

        Persisted voices stop too.

        Args:
            fade: The fade in seconds (at least 5 ms).
            bus: A bus name, or None for every voice.
        """
        bus_names = None if bus is None else self._subtree(bus)
        self._voices.stop_buses(bus_names, fade_seconds=fade)

    def fade_out_at_next_update(self, handle: SoundHandle, *, fade: float) -> None:
        """Fade a voice out from the next ``update`` on, not now (impl spec 10.1).

        The CRT power-on carries its tail into the game this way: asked after the power-on's
        last frame, the fade starts at frame 0's first update, however long the game took to
        build.

        Args:
            handle: The voice.
            fade: The fade in seconds (as ``SoundHandle.stop``).

        Raises:
            ValueError: For a negative fade, when asked.
        """
        if not fade >= 0.0:
            message = f'fade must be >= 0 seconds, got {fade}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        self._fades_at_next_update.append((handle, fade))

    def diagnostics(self) -> AudioDiagnostics:
        """What the engine has done so far (feature spec W8).

        Returns:
            The counters.
        """
        accountant = self.accountant
        counters = self._voices.counters
        return AudioDiagnostics(
            voices_playing=self._voices.voice_count,
            voices_limit=len(self._partition.library),
            compiles=accountant.compile_count,
            compile_milliseconds=(
                accountant.setup_compile_milliseconds + accountant.gameplay_compile_milliseconds
            ),
            setup_compiles=accountant.setup_compile_count,
            setup_compile_milliseconds=accountant.setup_compile_milliseconds,
            gameplay_compiles=accountant.gameplay_compile_count,
            gameplay_compile_milliseconds=accountant.gameplay_compile_milliseconds,
            compiles_in_gameplay=accountant.gameplay_compiles,
            stolen_voices=counters.steals,
            delayed_plays=counters.delayed_plays,
            dropped_plays=counters.dropped_plays,
            device=_device_description(),
            cache=self.sounds.statistics(),
        )

    def last_frame_work_by_kind(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        """The last finished frame's audio work in seconds, by kind (the overlay's graph).

        Returns:
            The seconds per kind (empty when the frame did no audio work).
        """
        work_by_kind: dict[str, float] = {}
        for kind, _name, microseconds in self._last_frame_account.audio_work:
            work_by_kind[kind] = work_by_kind.get(kind, 0.0) + microseconds / 1_000_000
        return work_by_kind

    def snapshot(self) -> AudioDiagnosticsSnapshot:
        """The engine as the debug overlay's Audio panel draws it (ruling R3).

        Returns:
            The snapshot.
        """
        channels = self._voices.snapshot()
        statistics = self.sounds.statistics()
        requests = statistics.hits + statistics.misses
        return AudioDiagnosticsSnapshot(
            cache_mode=self.cache_mode,
            device=_device_description(),
            voices_live=sum(
                1 for channel in channels if channel.group == 'live' and channel.state != 'idle'
            ),
            voices_library=self._voices.voice_count,
            voices_legacy=sum(
                1 for channel in channels if channel.group == 'legacy' and channel.state != 'idle'
            ),
            compiles_last_second=sum(count for _seconds, count in self._compile_window),
            cache_hit_rate=None if requests == 0 else statistics.hits / requests,
            frame_work_by_kind=self.last_frame_work_by_kind(),
            frame_processing_seconds=self._last_processing_seconds,
            channels=channels,
            bus_levels={name: self.buses[name].effective_gain() for name in self.buses.names()},
            muted_buses=frozenset(name for name in self.buses.names() if self.buses[name].mute),
            soloed_buses=frozenset(name for name in self.buses.names() if self.buses[name].solo),
            recently_stolen_channels=self._voices.recently_stolen_channels(),
            compile_log=self.accountant.compile_log,
        )

    # --- The scene manager's calls, once per frame (impl spec 4.2 and 11.0) ---

    def begin_frame(self, *, frame_number: int) -> None:
        """Note the frame being run, for the compile log.

        Args:
            frame_number: The scene manager's frame number.
        """
        self.accountant.frame_number = frame_number

    def begin_scene_setup(self) -> None:
        """A scene's ``setup()`` begins: its compiles count as setup until its first logic frame."""
        self.accountant.setup_mode = True

    def begin_logic_frame(self) -> None:
        """A scene's logic frame begins: compiles now belong to their frame (impl spec 6.5).

        The first logic frame after a setup ends it: if the setup's compiles took more than
        50 ms, one INFO line names its slowest sounds.
        """
        if not self.accountant.setup_mode:
            return
        self.accountant.setup_mode = False
        total_milliseconds, slowest = self.accountant.take_setup_compiles()
        if total_milliseconds > SLOW_SETUP_MILLISECONDS:
            log.info(
                'Setup compiled sounds for %.1f ms (more than %.0f ms); the slowest: %s',
                total_milliseconds,
                SLOW_SETUP_MILLISECONDS,
                ', '.join(f'{record.name} {record.milliseconds:.1f} ms' for record in slowest),
            )

    def update(
        self,
        *,
        dt: float,
        active_scene: object | None,
        previous_scene: object | None,
        active_transitions: Sequence[object | None],
        paused_owners: Sequence[object] = (),
    ) -> None:
        """Apply the owner rules, then move every voice by the frame's served time.

        The arguments are ``LiveAudio.update``'s (see the module docstring).

        Args:
            dt: The frame's served time (a replay's recorded dt).
            active_scene: The active scene.
            previous_scene: The previous scene; held only while the active scene's
                ``debug_subject`` is it (a pause screen over it).
            active_transitions: The running and the pending transition (either may be None).
            paused_owners: Other owners whose voices pause (a playback scope's).
        """
        fades, self._fades_at_next_update = self._fades_at_next_update, []
        for handle, fade in fades:
            handle.stop(fade=fade)
        playing_owners = [
            SYSTEM_OWNER,
            *(owner for owner in (active_scene, *active_transitions) if owner is not None),
        ]
        # The previous scene is held only behind a pause screen showing it (ruling R33); a scene
        # switched away from directly is cleaned up
        shown_as_paused = getattr(active_scene, 'debug_subject', None) is previous_scene
        held_candidates = (previous_scene, *paused_owners) if shown_as_paused else paused_owners
        held_owners = [
            owner
            for owner in held_candidates
            if owner is not None and not _contains(playing_owners, owner)
        ]
        for owner in list(self._owners):
            if _contains(playing_owners, owner) or _contains(held_owners, owner):
                continue
            self._voices.stop_owner(owner, fade_seconds=SCENE_CLEANUP_FADE_SECONDS)
            self._owners = [kept for kept in self._owners if kept is not owner]
        self._voices.advance(dt=dt, paused_owners=held_owners)
        self._count_compiles(dt=dt)

    def take_frame_account(self, *, processing_seconds: float | None = None) -> AudioFrameAccount:
        """Return the frame's audio work and start the next frame's (impl spec 11.0).

        Args:
            processing_seconds: The frame's processing time, shown beside its audio work.

        Returns:
            The account.
        """
        self._last_frame_account = self.accountant.take_frame()
        self._last_processing_seconds = processing_seconds
        return self._last_frame_account

    def silenced(self, channel_index: int | None) -> None:
        """A channel (None: every channel) was stopped outside the engine: only it is quiet.

        Its voices go on in the voice table by frame time (``VoiceTable.silenced``), so
        ``is_playing``, voice ends and steals are those of the frames had they not been silenced.

        Args:
            channel_index: The mixer channel ``FrameSilencer`` stopped, or None after
                ``pygame.mixer.stop()``.
        """
        indices = self._partition.library if channel_index is None else (channel_index,)
        for index in indices:
            self._voices.silenced(index)

    def close(self, *, wait_seconds: float = SHUTDOWN_WAIT_SECONDS) -> None:
        """Fade every voice over 50 ms, then wait for the fades at most ``wait_seconds``.

        Later plays are silent. Without a mixer, or on a mixer restarted with fewer channels
        than the partition's (its channels are gone), the voices simply end. Again: nothing.

        Args:
            wait_seconds: The longest wait (impl spec 10.3: 100 ms); 0 does not wait.
        """
        if self._closed:
            return
        self._closed = True
        if not self._partition_fits_the_mixer():
            # No channel to fade: the voices end in the table
            self._voices.end_voices_without_the_device()
            self._voices.close(fade_seconds=SHUTDOWN_FADE_SECONDS)
            return
        self._voices.close(fade_seconds=SHUTDOWN_FADE_SECONDS)
        deadline = clock.raw_counter_seconds() + wait_seconds
        while self._a_library_channel_sounds() and clock.raw_counter_seconds() < deadline:
            clock.raw_sleep(SHUTDOWN_POLL_SECONDS)

    # --- Inside ---

    def _current_tuning(self) -> Tuning:
        """The tuning, read at each request.

        Returns:
            ``tuning``.
        """
        return self.tuning

    def _compile_for_play(self, sound: Sound) -> Sound:
        """The library's ``compile_for_play`` (the voice table calls it on every play).

        Returns:
            The sound to play.
        """
        return self.sounds.compile_for_play(sound)

    def _play_sound(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8's playback arguments
        self,
        sound: Sound,
        *,
        volume: float | None,
        pan: float | None,
        bus: str | None,
        priority: int | None,
        loop: bool | None,
        at_frame: int | None,
        persist: bool,
        position: tuple[float, float] | None,
    ) -> SoundHandle:
        """Play a sound for the current owner; None arguments take the sound's defaults.

        Returns:
            The handle.

        Raises:
            NotImplementedError: For ``at_frame`` (M2) or ``position`` (M4).
        """
        if at_frame is not None:
            raise NotImplementedError(SCHEDULED_PLAY_MESSAGE)
        if position is not None:
            raise NotImplementedError(POSITIONED_PLAY_MESSAGE)
        defaults = sound.playback_defaults
        owner = self._scene_source()
        if owner is None:
            owner = SYSTEM_OWNER
        elif not _contains(self._owners, owner):
            self._owners.append(owner)
        return self._voices.play(
            sound,
            volume=defaults.volume if volume is None else volume,
            pan=defaults.pan if pan is None else pan,
            bus=defaults.bus if bus is None else bus,
            priority=defaults.priority if priority is None else priority,
            loop=defaults.loop if loop is None else loop,
            persist=persist,
            owner=owner,
        )

    def _paths_for(self, scene: object | None) -> tuple[Path | None, Path | None]:
        """A scene's package directory and sound directory (ruling R21), looked up once a class.

        Returns:
            The package directory and the sound directory; either may be None.
        """
        if scene is None:
            return None, None
        scene_class = type(scene)
        known = self._scene_paths.get(scene_class)
        if known is not None:
            return known
        # Imported here: the replay tools import the scenes, which import this package
        from glitchygames.replay.tools.identity import game_identity

        # game_identity reads only the class's module, so any scene-like class will do
        package_root = game_identity(game=cast('type[Scene]', scene_class)).package_directory
        if package_root is None:
            package_root = _module_directory(scene_class.__module__)
        sound_directory_name: str | None = getattr(scene_class, 'SOUND_DIRECTORY', None)
        sound_directory = None
        if sound_directory_name is not None:
            directory = Path(sound_directory_name)
            if directory.is_absolute():
                sound_directory = directory
            elif package_root is not None:
                sound_directory = package_root / directory
        paths = (package_root, sound_directory)
        self._scene_paths[scene_class] = paths
        return paths

    def _subtree(self, bus: str) -> frozenset[str]:
        """A bus and every bus under it.

        Returns:
            Their names.
        """
        self.buses[bus]  # raises KeyError naming the buses for an unknown bus
        names = {bus}
        changed = True
        while changed:
            changed = False
            for name in self.buses.names():
                parent = self.buses[name].parent
                if name not in names and parent is not None and parent in names:
                    names.add(name)
                    changed = True
        return frozenset(names)

    def _count_compiles(self, *, dt: float) -> None:
        """Add this frame's compiles to the last second's window, dropping what left it."""
        compiled = self.accountant.compile_count
        self._compile_window.append((dt, compiled - self._compiles_counted))
        self._compiles_counted = compiled
        self._compile_window_seconds += dt
        while self._compile_window_seconds > COMPILE_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS:
            seconds, _count = self._compile_window.popleft()
            self._compile_window_seconds -= seconds

    def _partition_fits_the_mixer(self) -> bool:
        """Whether a mixer runs with every library channel of the partition.

        Returns:
            False without a mixer, or when the mixer has fewer channels (restarted since).
        """
        if pygame.mixer.get_init() is None:
            return False
        return all(index < pygame.mixer.get_num_channels() for index in self._partition.library)

    def _a_library_channel_sounds(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the device still plays (or fades) a library channel.

        Returns:
            True while one is busy.
        """
        return any(pygame.mixer.Channel(index).get_busy() for index in self._partition.library)

def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - the engine's construction settings
    self,
    *,
    partition: ChannelPartition,
    cache: CacheMode = CacheMode.RAM,
    memory_limit_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES,
    scene_source: Callable[[], object | None] = _no_scene,
    frame_number: int | None = None,
    setup_mode: bool = True,
) -> None:
    """Make an engine over a channel partition.

    Args:
        partition: The mixer's channel partition (``reserve_channels``).
        cache: The cache mode (``disk`` arrives in M3: ValueError).
        memory_limit_bytes: The bytes compiled sounds may hold under ``ram``.
        scene_source: Gives the scene plays belong to and short names resolve in (the scene
            in setup, else the active scene), or None.
        frame_number: The frame being run, for the compile log.
        setup_mode: Whether compiles count as setup from the start: True while a scene is
            in ``setup()`` or has run no logic frame since (and before the first scene);
            False for an engine first made during gameplay.
    """
    self.waves: WaveRegistry = current_wave_registry()
    self.buses = BusTree()
    self.tuning = Tuning()
    self.cache_mode = cache
    self.accountant = AudioAccountant()
    self.accountant.frame_number = frame_number
    self.accountant.setup_mode = setup_mode
    self._partition = partition
    self._scene_source = scene_source
    self._voices = VoiceTable(
        partition=partition, buses=self.buses, compile_for_play=self._compile_for_play
    )
    self.sounds = SoundLibrary(
        cache=cache,
        accountant=self.accountant,
        waves=self.waves,
        tuning_source=self._current_tuning,
        memory_limit_bytes=memory_limit_bytes,
        is_playing=self._voices.is_playing_sound,
    )
    # Scene classes' (package directory, sound directory), looked up once each
    self._scene_paths: dict[type, tuple[Path | None, Path | None]] = {}
    # Scenes that played, until their voices are cleaned up (compared by identity)
    self._owners: list[object] = []
    # (served seconds, compiles) per frame over the last second (compiles_last_second)
    self._compile_window: collections.deque[tuple[float, int]] = collections.deque()
    self._compile_window_seconds = 0.0
    self._compiles_counted = 0
    self._last_frame_account = AudioFrameAccount(audio_seconds=0.0, audio_work=())
    self._last_processing_seconds: float | None = None
    # Fades held until the next update (fade_out_at_next_update): the CRT's tail
    self._fades_at_next_update: list[tuple[SoundHandle, float]] = []
    self._closed = False

Later plays are silent. Without a mixer, or on a mixer restarted with fewer channels than the partition's (its channels are gone), the voices simply end. Again: nothing.

def close(self, *, wait_seconds: float = SHUTDOWN_WAIT_SECONDS) -> None:
    """Fade every voice over 50 ms, then wait for the fades at most ``wait_seconds``.

    Later plays are silent. Without a mixer, or on a mixer restarted with fewer channels
    than the partition's (its channels are gone), the voices simply end. Again: nothing.

    Args:
        wait_seconds: The longest wait (impl spec 10.3: 100 ms); 0 does not wait.
    """
    if self._closed:
        return
    self._closed = True
    if not self._partition_fits_the_mixer():
        # No channel to fade: the voices end in the table
        self._voices.end_voices_without_the_device()
        self._voices.close(fade_seconds=SHUTDOWN_FADE_SECONDS)
        return
    self._voices.close(fade_seconds=SHUTDOWN_FADE_SECONDS)
    deadline = clock.raw_counter_seconds() + wait_seconds
    while self._a_library_channel_sounds() and clock.raw_counter_seconds() < deadline:
        clock.raw_sleep(SHUTDOWN_POLL_SECONDS)

def engine_sound(
    self, instrument: Instrument, *, pitch: PitchLike | None, length: float | None
) -> Sound:
    """Get one of the engine's own sounds (the CRT power-on's): compiled once per process.

    The process's first request compiles it, counted and attributed here like any compile;

def fade_out_at_next_update(self, handle: SoundHandle, *, fade: float) -> None:
    """Fade a voice out from the next ``update`` on, not now (impl spec 10.1).

    The CRT power-on carries its tail into the game this way: asked after the power-on's
    last frame, the fade starts at frame 0's first update, however long the game took to
    build.

    Args:
        handle: The voice.
        fade: The fade in seconds (as ``SoundHandle.stop``).

    Raises:
        ValueError: For a negative fade, when asked.
    """
    if not fade >= 0.0:
        message = f'fade must be >= 0 seconds, got {fade}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    self._fades_at_next_update.append((handle, fade))

def last_frame_work_by_kind(self) -> dict[str, float]:
    """The last finished frame's audio work in seconds, by kind (the overlay's graph).

    Returns:
        The seconds per kind (empty when the frame did no audio work).

    return work_by_kind

def silenced(self, channel_index: int | None) -> None:
    """A channel (None: every channel) was stopped outside the engine: only it is quiet.

    Its voices go on in the voice table by frame time (``VoiceTable.silenced``), so
    ``is_playing``, voice ends and steals are those of the frames had they not been silenced.

    Args:
        channel_index: The mixer channel ``FrameSilencer`` stopped, or None after
            ``pygame.mixer.stop()``.
    """
    indices = self._partition.library if channel_index is None else (channel_index,)
    for index in indices:
        self._voices.silenced(index)

def snapshot(self) -> AudioDiagnosticsSnapshot:
    """The engine as the debug overlay's Audio panel draws it (ruling R3).

    Returns:
        The snapshot.
    """
    channels = self._voices.snapshot()
    statistics = self.sounds.statistics()
    requests = statistics.hits + statistics.misses
    return AudioDiagnosticsSnapshot(
        cache_mode=self.cache_mode,
        device=_device_description(),
        voices_live=sum(
            1 for channel in channels if channel.group == 'live' and channel.state != 'idle'
        ),
        voices_library=self._voices.voice_count,
        voices_legacy=sum(
            1 for channel in channels if channel.group == 'legacy' and channel.state != 'idle'
        ),
        compiles_last_second=sum(count for _seconds, count in self._compile_window),
        cache_hit_rate=None if requests == 0 else statistics.hits / requests,
        frame_work_by_kind=self.last_frame_work_by_kind(),
        frame_processing_seconds=self._last_processing_seconds,
        channels=channels,
        bus_levels={name: self.buses[name].effective_gain() for name in self.buses.names()},
        muted_buses=frozenset(name for name in self.buses.names() if self.buses[name].mute),
        soloed_buses=frozenset(name for name in self.buses.names() if self.buses[name].solo),
        recently_stolen_channels=self._voices.recently_stolen_channels(),
        compile_log=self.accountant.compile_log,
    )

def update(
    self,
    *,
    dt: float,
    active_scene: object | None,
    previous_scene: object | None,
    active_transitions: Sequence[object | None],
    paused_owners: Sequence[object] = (),
) -> None:
    """Apply the owner rules, then move every voice by the frame's served time.

    The arguments are ``LiveAudio.update``'s (see the module docstring).

    Args:
        dt: The frame's served time (a replay's recorded dt).
        active_scene: The active scene.
        previous_scene: The previous scene; held only while the active scene's
            ``debug_subject`` is it (a pause screen over it).
        active_transitions: The running and the pending transition (either may be None).
        paused_owners: Other owners whose voices pause (a playback scope's).
    """
    fades, self._fades_at_next_update = self._fades_at_next_update, []
    for handle, fade in fades:
        handle.stop(fade=fade)
    playing_owners = [
        SYSTEM_OWNER,
        *(owner for owner in (active_scene, *active_transitions) if owner is not None),
    ]
    # The previous scene is held only behind a pause screen showing it (ruling R33); a scene
    # switched away from directly is cleaned up
    shown_as_paused = getattr(active_scene, 'debug_subject', None) is previous_scene
    held_candidates = (previous_scene, *paused_owners) if shown_as_paused else paused_owners
    held_owners = [
        owner
        for owner in held_candidates
        if owner is not None and not _contains(playing_owners, owner)
    ]
    for owner in list(self._owners):
        if _contains(playing_owners, owner) or _contains(held_owners, owner):
            continue
        self._voices.stop_owner(owner, fade_seconds=SCENE_CLEANUP_FADE_SECONDS)
        self._owners = [kept for kept in self._owners if kept is not owner]
    self._voices.advance(dt=dt, paused_owners=held_owners)
    self._count_compiles(dt=dt)
