def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - mirrors impl spec 8
    self,
    *,
    wave: str | Wave | None = None,
    noise: str | Noise | None = None,
    sources: Mapping[str, Wave | Noise | Source] | None = None,
    envelope: synth.Envelope | EnvelopeSpec | str = 'pluck',
    filter: Filter | None = None,  # ruff: ignore[builtin-argument-shadowing] - impl spec 8
    drive: float = 0.0,
    profile: str = 'hybrid',
    live: bool = False,
    seed: int | None = None,
    normalize: bool = False,
    hard_edges: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Build an instrument.

    Args:
        wave: A wave or a wave name: a single layer.
        noise: A ``Noise`` or a noise kind: a single layer.
        sources: Named layers, one to four, in mix order.
        envelope: A preset name, a ``synth.Envelope`` or an ``EnvelopeSpec``.
        filter: A filter for the whole sound.
        drive: Distortion, 0-20.
        profile: ``hybrid`` (the others are constrained later, M4).
        live: Whether the sound is live (M2).
        seed: The noise seed; None derives it from the sound's name.
        normalize: Normalize the rendered peak.
        hard_edges: Skip the de-click fades.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Unless exactly one of wave, noise and sources is given, on more than
            four sources, on a drive outside 0-20 or an unknown profile or envelope.
    """
    given = [argument for argument in (wave, noise, sources) if argument is not None]
    if len(given) != 1:
        message = 'an instrument takes exactly one of wave, noise or sources'
        raise ValueError(message)
    layers: tuple[tuple[str, Source], ...]
    if sources is not None:
        if not sources:
            message = 'sources cannot be empty'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if len(sources) > MAXIMUM_SOURCES:
            message = f'an instrument has at most {MAXIMUM_SOURCES} sources, got {len(sources)}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        layers = tuple((name, _as_source(entry)) for name, entry in sources.items())
    elif wave is not None:
        layers = ((DEFAULT_SOURCE_NAME, _as_source(wave)),)
    else:
        noise_layer = Noise(noise) if isinstance(noise, str) else noise
        assert noise_layer is not None
        layers = ((DEFAULT_SOURCE_NAME, _as_source(noise_layer)),)
    if not 0.0 <= drive <= DRIVE_HIGHEST:
        message = f'drive must be between 0 and {DRIVE_HIGHEST}, got {drive}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if profile not in PROFILES:
        message = f'unknown profile {profile!r}; use one of {", ".join(PROFILES)}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    self._sources = layers
    self._envelope = _envelope_spec(envelope)
    self._filter = filter.to_spec() if filter is not None else None
    self._drive = drive
    self._profile = profile
    self._live = live
    self._seed = seed
    self._normalize = normalize
    self._hard_edges = hard_edges

def build_spec(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - mirrors the brief's signature
    instrument: Instrument,
    *,
    name: str,
    pitch: PitchLike | None,
    notes: str | Sequence[tuple[PitchLike, float]] | None,
    chord: Sequence[PitchLike] | None,
    length: float | None,
    transpose: float,
    tuning: Tuning,
    sample_rate: int,
    playback_defaults: PlaybackDefaults,
) -> SoundSpec:
    """Turn an instrument and the identity arguments into a ``SoundSpec``.

    Wave names are resolved through the current wave registry here. A single pitch or chord lasts
    ``length`` seconds (default 0.25) before its release. An unpitched instrument given a pitch
    sets ``unpitched_scale`` to ``pitch_hz / 440``. With no pitch, notes or chord the spec's
    ``notes`` is None (the renderer decides), except an unpitched instrument given a ``length``,
    which gets one reference-pitch event carrying it.

    Args:
        instrument: How the sound sounds.
        name: The sound's name (the default seed derives from it).
        pitch: One pitch, or None.
        notes: A melody, or None.
        chord: Pitches played together, or None.
        length: Seconds for a single pitch or chord; None means 0.25.
        transpose: Semitones to shift ``notes`` or ``chord``.
        tuning: The tuning for pitch names.
        sample_rate: The rate to render at.
        playback_defaults: Default playback settings, carried but not part of the identity.

    Returns:
        The spec.
    """
    _refuse_filters_at_or_above_nyquist(instrument, sample_rate=sample_rate)
    events, unpitched_scale = _note_events(
        instrument,
        pitch=pitch,
        notes=notes,
        chord=chord,
        length=length,
        transpose=transpose,
        tuning=tuning,
        sample_rate=sample_rate,
    )
    return SoundSpec(
        name=name,
        sources=tuple(
            _source_spec(source, tuning=tuning, sample_rate=sample_rate)
            for _, source in instrument.sources
        ),
        envelope=instrument.envelope,
        filter=instrument.filter,
        drive=instrument.drive,
        notes=events,
        unpitched_scale=unpitched_scale,
        sample_rate=sample_rate,
        seed=instrument.seed if instrument.seed is not None else default_seed(name),
        normalize=instrument.normalize,
        hard_edges=instrument.hard_edges,
        live=instrument.live,
        tuning_a4=tuning.a4,
        playback_defaults=playback_defaults,
    )

docs.title: instruments
docs.text:
The instrument catalog: ready-made instruments for every family, with their ranges.

Usage

from glitchygames.audio import instruments

violin = instruments.get('violin') # an ordinary Instrument sound = self.scene_manager.audio.sound(violin, notes='G3:0.5 D4:0.5 A4:1') instruments.entry('alto saxophone').playing_range # (Note('Db3'), Note('Ab5')) instruments.names(family=instruments.Family.BRASS) # every brass instrument's name instruments.names(tag=instruments.Tag.MECHANICAL) # every entry carrying a tag instruments.get('slapstick') # an alias: the same instrument as 'whip'

Every entry is an Instrument made from the engine's own parts (waves from overtone series, noise, layered sources with their own envelopes and pitches, filters and drive; see timbres), so it plays, caches and renders offline like any other. The voices come in every range (soprano, mezzo-soprano, alto, treble, countertenor, tenor, baritone, bass, basso profundo) on five vowels, and the families' sizes have their variants (sopranino to contrabass saxophones and recorders, alto to contrabass trombones, piccolo to contrabass flutes, and so on). They are synthesized approximations: there are no recorded samples, vibrato or moving filters in the engine yet, so sustained tones are steady and a vowel is truest mid-range.

Three families hold the instruments that are neither struck bars nor blown: plucked idiophones (kalimba, mbira, music box, sansula), friction instruments (glass harmonica, glass harp, terpodion) and noise makers (whip crack, diaphone, air horn, vehicle horn, party horn). A Tag marks a quality across families (Tag.MECHANICAL, on the music box), so names(tag=...) finds those wherever they sound.

Electromechanical takes the electric pianos (tine electric piano, reed electric piano), the clavinet and the tonewheel organ ... registrations from keyboards and organs, and adds the hohner pianet. Sound effects is a new family (thunder sheet, rain machine, ocean drum, cannon, coconut shells, door slam), each effect playable as a note.

Drums and percussion (237 entries) holds the family's builds in drums.py (hand drums such as daf, dhol, kendang and mridangam, snares, gongs such as agung and jing, cymbals, shakers, clappers, garamut, washboard) and its sound-alikes in drum_sound_alikes.py. A sound-alike is a verified instrument no source sets apart in sound from an existing entry (bamboula and conga): its own entry, listed under its own name, with CatalogEntry.sounds_like naming the parent whose build it shares. CatalogEntry.sound_changes (empty so far) would let one differ by a sourced trait.

Plucked strings (92 entries) holds the family's builds in plucked_strings.py (guitars, basses, ukuleles, banjos, mandolins, lutes such as angelique, zithers such as qanun, tar, ruan and chapman stick) and its sound-alikes in plucked_sound_alikes.py (requinto guitar and classical guitar, liuqin and pipa). The family is pitched, so a pitched sound-alike gives its own sourced range, a requinto's span being its own: it shares its parent's build, not its range.

instruments.ALIASES (read-only, as CATALOG is) maps each other name (slapstick) to its catalog name (whip): another name for the same instrument, where a sound-alike is a different instrument. entry and get resolve aliases, while names and entries list catalog names only.

instruments.get builds each instrument once per process and returns the same (immutable) instrument afterwards. A sound-alike is built under its own name: its instrument is equal by value to its parent's, not the same object.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CatalogEntry:
    """One catalog instrument.

    Attributes:
        name: Its catalog name (``alto saxophone``): lower-case words separated by single spaces.
        title: Its display name (``Alto saxophone``).
        family: Its family.
        lowest: Its lowest sounding note name, or None when it is unpitched.
        highest: Its highest sounding note name, or None when it is unpitched.
        build: Makes the instrument (called once; ``instruments.get`` keeps the result). Every
            entry from ``CATALOG`` / ``instruments.entry()`` has a build: None only in a raw
            table entry for a sound-alike, which the catalog's assembly gives its parent's
            builder.
        tags: Its tags, members of ``Tag`` (empty for most entries).
        sounds_like: The catalog name of the entry this one sounds like (its parent), or None.
            A sound-alike is a distinct instrument, listed under its own name, that no source
            sets apart in sound from its parent: it builds its parent's instrument. It is pitched
            exactly when its parent is, and a pitched one gives its own sourced range (decision 8,
            plans/2026-11-07-instrument-catalog-expansion-design.md, and
            plans/2026-11-09-instrument-catalog-batch-4-implementation.md); another name for the
            same instrument is an alias instead.
        sound_changes: Keyword overrides of the parent's builder (a ``functools.partial``), for
            a sound-alike that a source sets apart by a trait (a smaller head's higher tone)
            while it inherits everything else; empty for most. Each change needs a source,
            cited in the entry's comment, as every other value does. Stored read-only.
    """

    name: str
    title: str
    family: Family
    lowest: str | None
    highest: str | None
    build: Callable[[], Instrument] | None = field(default=None, repr=False, compare=False)
    tags: frozenset[Tag] = field(default=frozenset())
    sounds_like: str | None = None
    # compare=False: a mappingproxy is unhashable and the frozen entry must stay hashable, so
    # equality ignores the changes
    sound_changes: Mapping[str, object] = field(default=MappingProxyType({}), compare=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate the name, the range, the tags and the build, and freeze the sound changes.

        The sound-alike rules that need the whole catalog (the parent exists, is no sound-alike,
        takes the changes) are checked when the catalog is assembled
        (``registry.sound_alikes_from``).

        Raises:
            ValueError: On a name that is not lower-case words separated by single spaces, a range
                with only one end, a note name that does not parse, a lowest note above the
                highest, or neither a build nor a ``sounds_like``.
            TypeError: On a tag that is not a ``Tag`` (a string equal to a tag's value included).
        """
        # A copy, so the caller's dict cannot change the entry afterwards
        object.__setattr__(self, 'sound_changes', MappingProxyType(dict(self.sound_changes)))
        if self.build is None and self.sounds_like is None:
            message = f'{self.name}: give a build, or the entry it sounds like'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if ENTRY_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(self.name) is None:
            message = (
                f'catalog name {self.name!r} must be lower-case words separated by single spaces'
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        if (self.lowest is None) != (self.highest is None):
            message = f'{self.name}: give both ends of the range, or neither (unpitched)'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if (
            self.lowest is not None
            and self.highest is not None
            and Note(self.lowest).midi_number > Note(self.highest).midi_number
        ):
            message = f'{self.name}: lowest {self.lowest} is above highest {self.highest}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        for tag in self.tags:
            if type(tag) is not Tag:
                message = f'{self.name}: tag {tag!r} must be a Tag'
                raise TypeError(message)

    @property
    def pitched(self) -> bool:
        """True when the instrument plays the note's pitch (it has a range)."""
        return self.lowest is not None

    @property
    def playing_range(self) -> tuple[Note, Note] | None:
        """The lowest and highest notes, or None when unpitched."""
        if self.lowest is None or self.highest is None:
            return None
        return Note(self.lowest), Note(self.highest)

    def middle_note(self) -> Note:
        """The note halfway through the range in semitones (A4 when unpitched).

        Returns:
            The note.
        """
        playing_range = self.playing_range
        if playing_range is None:
            return Note('A4')
        lowest, highest = playing_range
        return Note.from_midi_number((lowest.midi_number + highest.midi_number) // 2)

    if playing_range is None:
        return Note('A4')
    lowest, highest = playing_range
    return Note.from_midi_number((lowest.midi_number + highest.midi_number) // 2)

def entry(name: str) -> CatalogEntry:
    """The catalog entry named ``name``, in any case.

    Args:
        name: A catalog name or an alias, e.g. ``'tenor saxophone'`` or ``'slapstick'``
            (``'Tenor Saxophone'`` finds it too: the name is lowercased first).

    Returns:
        The entry.

    Raises:
        KeyError: When no instrument has that name (the message suggests close names).
    """
    lowered = name.lower()
    try:
        return CATALOG[ALIAS_TABLE.get(lowered, lowered)]
    except KeyError:
        # Suggestions come from catalog names and aliases together.
        close = difflib.get_close_matches(lowered, [*CATALOG, *ALIAS_TABLE], n=SUGGESTION_COUNT)
        hint = f'; did you mean {", ".join(close)}?' if close else ''
        message = f'no instrument named {name!r} in the catalog{hint}'
        raise KeyError(message) from None

def names(*, family: Family | str | None = None, tag: Tag | str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Every catalog name, in catalog order, or only one family's and/or one tag's.

    Args:
        family: A family, its name in any case (``'Double Reeds'``), or None for all.
        tag: A tag, its name in any case (``'Mechanical'``), or None for all.

        name
        for name, value in CATALOG.items()
        if (wanted_family is None or value.family == wanted_family)
        and (wanted_tag is None or wanted_tag in value.tags)
    )

docs.title: aliases
docs.text:
Other names for catalog instruments (instruments.entry and get resolve them).

Each key is an alias, lower-case words separated by single spaces, and each value is the catalog name it stands for. registry.aliases_from checks the table when the catalog is assembled: an alias may not be a catalog name, and its target must be one.

docs.title: brass
docs.text:
Brass: trumpets, horns, trombones, tubas, their mutes, and historic and folk lip-reeds.

Ranges are sounding pitch, after the standard orchestration ranges (Adler, The Study of Orchestration); historic and folk instruments' are typical. A brass tone's brightness comes from its bell and bore: a trumpet's harmonics fall slowly, a horn's and a tuba's fast. Each note also starts brighter than it holds (bite: the lips' first buzz), and mutes reshape the spectrum (a straight mute thins the low end, a cup mute darkens, a harmon mute leaves a nasal buzz).

docs.title: catalog
docs.text:
The catalog's entry type, families and tags (the tables are in the family modules).

A CatalogEntry names an instrument, its family and its playing range (sounding pitch, from standard orchestration ranges; folk and world instruments vary by maker and tuning, so theirs are typical). Unpitched entries (drums, cymbals) have no range: their tones are fixed. A Tag marks a quality that cuts across families (Tag.MECHANICAL); the set is closed, so tags cannot drift into synonyms. A sound-alike (sounds_like) is an instrument of its own that no source sets apart in sound from another entry, its parent: it is listed under its own name and builds its parent's instrument, changed only by its sourced sound_changes.

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class CatalogEntry:
    """One catalog instrument.

    Attributes:
        name: Its catalog name (``alto saxophone``): lower-case words separated by single spaces.
        title: Its display name (``Alto saxophone``).
        family: Its family.
        lowest: Its lowest sounding note name, or None when it is unpitched.
        highest: Its highest sounding note name, or None when it is unpitched.
        build: Makes the instrument (called once; ``instruments.get`` keeps the result). Every
            entry from ``CATALOG`` / ``instruments.entry()`` has a build: None only in a raw
            table entry for a sound-alike, which the catalog's assembly gives its parent's
            builder.
        tags: Its tags, members of ``Tag`` (empty for most entries).
        sounds_like: The catalog name of the entry this one sounds like (its parent), or None.
            A sound-alike is a distinct instrument, listed under its own name, that no source
            sets apart in sound from its parent: it builds its parent's instrument. It is pitched
            exactly when its parent is, and a pitched one gives its own sourced range (decision 8,
            plans/2026-11-07-instrument-catalog-expansion-design.md, and
            plans/2026-11-09-instrument-catalog-batch-4-implementation.md); another name for the
            same instrument is an alias instead.
        sound_changes: Keyword overrides of the parent's builder (a ``functools.partial``), for
            a sound-alike that a source sets apart by a trait (a smaller head's higher tone)
            while it inherits everything else; empty for most. Each change needs a source,
            cited in the entry's comment, as every other value does. Stored read-only.
    """

    name: str
    title: str
    family: Family
    lowest: str | None
    highest: str | None
    build: Callable[[], Instrument] | None = field(default=None, repr=False, compare=False)
    tags: frozenset[Tag] = field(default=frozenset())
    sounds_like: str | None = None
    # compare=False: a mappingproxy is unhashable and the frozen entry must stay hashable, so
    # equality ignores the changes
    sound_changes: Mapping[str, object] = field(default=MappingProxyType({}), compare=False)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate the name, the range, the tags and the build, and freeze the sound changes.

        The sound-alike rules that need the whole catalog (the parent exists, is no sound-alike,
        takes the changes) are checked when the catalog is assembled
        (``registry.sound_alikes_from``).

        Raises:
            ValueError: On a name that is not lower-case words separated by single spaces, a range
                with only one end, a note name that does not parse, a lowest note above the
                highest, or neither a build nor a ``sounds_like``.
            TypeError: On a tag that is not a ``Tag`` (a string equal to a tag's value included).
        """
        # A copy, so the caller's dict cannot change the entry afterwards
        object.__setattr__(self, 'sound_changes', MappingProxyType(dict(self.sound_changes)))
        if self.build is None and self.sounds_like is None:
            message = f'{self.name}: give a build, or the entry it sounds like'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if ENTRY_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(self.name) is None:
            message = (
                f'catalog name {self.name!r} must be lower-case words separated by single spaces'
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        if (self.lowest is None) != (self.highest is None):
            message = f'{self.name}: give both ends of the range, or neither (unpitched)'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if (
            self.lowest is not None
            and self.highest is not None
            and Note(self.lowest).midi_number > Note(self.highest).midi_number
        ):
            message = f'{self.name}: lowest {self.lowest} is above highest {self.highest}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        for tag in self.tags:
            if type(tag) is not Tag:
                message = f'{self.name}: tag {tag!r} must be a Tag'
                raise TypeError(message)

    @property
    def pitched(self) -> bool:
        """True when the instrument plays the note's pitch (it has a range)."""
        return self.lowest is not None

    @property
    def playing_range(self) -> tuple[Note, Note] | None:
        """The lowest and highest notes, or None when unpitched."""
        if self.lowest is None or self.highest is None:
            return None
        return Note(self.lowest), Note(self.highest)

    def middle_note(self) -> Note:
        """The note halfway through the range in semitones (A4 when unpitched).

        Returns:
            The note.
        """
        playing_range = self.playing_range
        if playing_range is None:
            return Note('A4')
        lowest, highest = playing_range
        return Note.from_midi_number((lowest.midi_number + highest.midi_number) // 2)

docs.title: drum_sound_alikes
docs.text:
Drums and percussion's sound-alikes: listed instruments that share another entry's build.

A sound-alike is a distinct instrument, verified by its source, that no fetched source sets apart in sound from an existing entry. The owner ruled (2026-11-08) that each is a catalog entry of its own rather than an alias: "could we also consider making them full on instruments that inherit from the parent and change their details? ... I want them to all show up." Each is listed under its own name, so a person finds it by the name they know, and each builds its parent's instrument through sounds_like (assembled in registry.sound_alikes_from). A true alias, another name for the same instrument, stays in aliases.py. The family's builds are in drums.py.

docs.title: drums
docs.text:
Drums and percussion: drums, rattles, scrapers, clappers, cymbals and gongs.

The family holds the Hornbostel-Sachs classes 1 (idiophones: rattles, scrapers, clappers, blocks, cymbals, gongs, bells) and 2 (membranophones: struck and friction drums) whose entries are unpitched or played at one fixed tone (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hornbostel%E2%80%93Sachs). Tuned bars, bells, pans and timpani are tuned percussion (percussion.py). Percussion here is fixed tones and filtered noise: its sounds do not follow the note's pitch, so these entries have no range. The jing, agung, kemanak and the tonic-tuned drums have a definite pitch at a fixed tone, and the pitch a note gives is ignored. Each is built with drum: a struck tone that rings out, a noise band for the stick, hand or snares, and a tail; a ring is cut when the note ends, fading out over the entry's tail. The family's sound-alikes, instruments that share an entry's build (sounds_like), are listed in the sibling module drum_sound_alikes.py; DRUMS_AND_PERCUSSION is this module's builds followed by them.

docs.title: idiophones
docs.text:
Idiophones other than the tuned percussion bars and bells: plucked and rubbed.

An idiophone is an instrument whose own body is the vibrating, sounding part (Hornbostel-Sachs class 1). The Hornbostel-Sachs list of idiophones is at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_idiophones_by_Hornbostel%E2%80%93Sachs_number

Plucked idiophones (Hornbostel-Sachs 12) are a set of metal tongues, or lamellae, each fixed at one end, plucked and left to ring: the kalimba and mbira with a thumb, the music box with the pins of a revolving cylinder. A clamped tine rings at 1 : 6.27 of its fundamental (see percussion.TINE_RATIOS), so each is built as a struck bar with those two partials.

Friction instruments (Hornbostel-Sachs 13) are set singing by rubbing: a wet finger on glass, a rosined cylinder on a rod. The glass harmonica (bowls on a spindle) is built as a blown tone; the glass harp and the terpodion use the rubbed shape (inharmonic partials that swell in and hold).

docs.title: keyboards
docs.text:
Keyboards (pianos, harpsichords, celesta), organs, electromechanical and electronic instruments.

A piano string is struck by a hammer near a seventh of its length, so its seventh harmonic is nearly gone; each note has two or three slightly detuned strings, whose beating is the piano's shimmer. A harpsichord's quill plucks near the end (bright) and has a 4' octave rank. Organs are drawbar registrations (Harmonics.drawbars) or pipe stops: a principal's every harmonic, a flute stop's nearly pure tone, a reed stop's brassy one. The tonewheel organ's percussion is a decaying second or third harmonic. Electromechanical instruments (the electric pianos, the Clavinet, the tonewheel organs) read a mechanical vibration electrically. Ranges are each instrument's keyboard; an organ's are its keys at 8' pitch (a 61-note manual, C2-C7), and a 16' stop or drawbar sounds an octave lower.

docs.title: noise_makers
docs.text:
Noise makers: free aerophones and horns, instruments that make a signal rather than a note.

A free aerophone (Hornbostel-Sachs 41) is set sounding by moving it through the air: whips, bullroarers, sirens. An interruptive or reed free aerophone (412) is a horn: a reed or diaphragm chops a stream of air or current into a buzz. The Hornbostel-Sachs aerophone list is at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_aerophones_by_Hornbostel%E2%80%93Sachs_number

Each one here is unpitched: it ignores the pitch it is given, as a drum does, so each is built with drum. The whip crack is a one-shot that dies away at once; the horns sound for as long as the note is held (their tones have a sustain level) and the diaphone's noise rumble decays.

docs.title: percussion
docs.text:
Tuned percussion: mallets, bells, pans, timpani and gamelan.

Tuned percussion's partials are not harmonics. A free bar (glockenspiel) rings at 1 : 2.76 : 5.40 : 8.93 of its fundamental; marimba and vibraphone bars are cut so the first overtone is the fourth harmonic and the xylophone's the third; a tubular bell's and a carillon bell's partials (hum, prime, tierce and nominal; the weak quint is left out) give the bell's minor-third colour; a tubular bell's struck note is heard an octave below its fourth mode, which with the fifth and sixth rings near 2 : 3 : 4 of that note; steel pans and handpans are tuned to the octave and twelfth; a timpani's head favours 1 : 1.5 : 2 (Rossing, Science of Percussion Instruments; Fletcher and Rossing, The Physics of Musical Instruments). Untuned percussion (drums, cymbals) is the drums and percussion family, in drums.py.

def struck_bar(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - a struck bar's partials
    ratios: tuple[float, ...],
    levels: tuple[float, ...],
    *,
    ring_seconds: float,
    mallet: float = 0.05,
    mallet_low_pass: float = 3000.0,
    overtone_ring: float = 0.25,
) -> Instrument:
    """A struck or plucked bar: a fundamental and its overtones, each ringing out on its own.

    Args:
        ratios: Each partial's frequency as a multiple of the note's.
        levels: Each partial's level, one per ratio.
        ring_seconds: How long the fundamental rings (it is also the release).
        mallet: Seconds of the mallet's noise burst.
        mallet_low_pass: Cutoff in hertz of the mallet's noise.
        overtone_ring: The overtones' ring time as a fraction of the fundamental's, divided by
            the overtone's number.

    Returns:
        The instrument.
    """
    partials = tuple(
        Partial(
            ratio=ratio,
            level=level,
            ring_seconds=ring_seconds if number == 0 else ring_seconds * overtone_ring / number,
        )
        for number, (ratio, level) in enumerate(zip(ratios, levels, strict=True))
    )
    return struck(partials, release=ring_seconds, mallet=mallet, mallet_low_pass=mallet_low_pass)

docs.title: plucked_sound_alikes
docs.text:
Plucked strings' sound-alikes: listed instruments that share another entry's build.

A sound-alike is a distinct instrument, verified by its source, that no fetched source sets apart in sound from an existing entry. The owner ruled (2026-11-08) that each is a catalog entry of its own rather than an alias: "could we also consider making them full on instruments that inherit from the parent and change their details? ... I want them to all show up." Each is listed under its own name, so a person finds it by the name they know, and each builds its parent's instrument through sounds_like (assembled in registry.sound_alikes_from). It gives its own sourced range, since a sound-alike of another size plays another span. A true alias, another name for the same instrument, stays in aliases.py. The family's builds are in plucked_strings.py.

def aliases_from(table: Mapping[str, str], catalog: Mapping[str, CatalogEntry]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """The alias table, checked against the catalog.

    Args:
        table: Alias to catalog name.
        catalog: The catalog the targets must belong to.

    Returns:
        A copy of the table.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When an alias is not lower-case words separated by single spaces, is itself
            a catalog name, or names a target that is not a catalog name.
    """
    for alias, target in table.items():
        if ENTRY_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(alias) is None:
            message = f'alias {alias!r} must be lower-case words separated by single spaces'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if alias in catalog:
            message = f'alias {alias!r} is a catalog name'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if target not in catalog:
            message = f'alias {alias!r} names no instrument: {target!r}'
            raise ValueError(message)
    return dict(table)

    catalog: dict[str, CatalogEntry] = {}

    return catalog

def entry(name: str) -> CatalogEntry:
    """The catalog entry named ``name``, in any case.

    Args:
        name: A catalog name or an alias, e.g. ``'tenor saxophone'`` or ``'slapstick'``
            (``'Tenor Saxophone'`` finds it too: the name is lowercased first).

    Returns:
        The entry.

    Raises:
        KeyError: When no instrument has that name (the message suggests close names).
    """
    lowered = name.lower()
    try:
        return CATALOG[ALIAS_TABLE.get(lowered, lowered)]
    except KeyError:
        # Suggestions come from catalog names and aliases together.
        close = difflib.get_close_matches(lowered, [*CATALOG, *ALIAS_TABLE], n=SUGGESTION_COUNT)
        hint = f'; did you mean {", ".join(close)}?' if close else ''
        message = f'no instrument named {name!r} in the catalog{hint}'
        raise KeyError(message) from None

A sound-alike (an entry with sounds_like) builds its parent's instrument, with its sound_changes replacing the parent builder's keywords.

Parameters:

Name to entry, in the same order, each sound-alike carrying its build.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

Naming the entry, when sound changes come without sounds_like, or a sound-alike has its own build, sounds like itself, an entry that is not in the catalog or another sound-alike, is pitched when its parent is not (or the reverse), or carries changes its parent's builder cannot take.

Source code in src/glitchygames/audio/instruments/registry.py 
def sound_alikes_from(catalog: Mapping[str, CatalogEntry]) -> dict[str, CatalogEntry]:
    """The catalog with every sound-alike given its build, checked against its parent.

    A sound-alike (an entry with ``sounds_like``) builds its parent's instrument, with its
    ``sound_changes`` replacing the parent builder's keywords.

    Args:
        catalog: Name to entry, as ``catalog_from`` assembles it.

    Returns:
        Name to entry, in the same order, each sound-alike carrying its build.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Naming the entry, when sound changes come without ``sounds_like``, or a
            sound-alike has its own build, sounds like itself, an entry that is not in the
            catalog or another sound-alike, is pitched when its parent is not (or the reverse),
            or carries changes its parent's builder cannot take.
    """
    assembled: dict[str, CatalogEntry] = {}
    for name, catalog_entry in catalog.items():
        parent_name = catalog_entry.sounds_like
        if parent_name is None:
            if catalog_entry.sound_changes:
                message = f'{name}: sound changes need the entry it sounds like'
                raise ValueError(message)
            assembled[name] = catalog_entry
            continue
        if catalog_entry.build is not None:
            message = f'{name}: a sound-alike takes the build of {parent_name!r}, not its own'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if parent_name == name:
            message = f'{name}: sounds like itself'
            raise ValueError(message)
        parent = catalog.get(parent_name)
        if parent is None:
            message = f'{name}: sounds like no instrument: {parent_name!r}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if parent.sounds_like is not None:
            message = f'{name}: sounds like {parent_name!r}, itself a sound-alike'
            raise ValueError(message)
        # Decision 8 (plans/2026-11-07-instrument-catalog-expansion-design.md), extended by
        # plans/2026-11-09-instrument-catalog-batch-4-implementation.md: a pitched sound-alike
        # gives its own sourced range, but pitched-ness comes from the parent's build
        if catalog_entry.pitched != parent.pitched:
            message = f'{name}: pitched exactly when {parent_name!r} is'
            raise ValueError(message)
        assembled[name] = dataclasses.replace(
            catalog_entry, build=_sound_alike_build(catalog_entry, parent)
        )
    return assembled

docs.title: sound_effects
docs.text:
Sound effects: theatre and Foley devices that imitate a non-musical sound.

This family is defined by use, not by how the sound is made: a thunder sheet, a rain machine or a pair of coconut shells exists to stand in for thunder, rain or a horse. The Foley craft, the reproduction of everyday sounds for film and stage, is described at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foley_(filmmaking)

Every effect plays as a note, so it can be used in music; each is unpitched and ignores the pitch it is given, as a drum does, so each is built with drum: a noise band with a ring for a one-shot (a thunder sheet's crash), with an attack for a swell (an ocean drum). None of them sustains while held: each dies away after its ring. A ring is also cut when the note ends: it fades out over the entry's tail from the note's end, so a note shorter than the ring sounds shorter than the ring figures in the comments below.

docs.title: strings
docs.text:
Strings: bowed, harps and struck strings (dulcimers).

Plucked strings (guitars, basses, lutes) are in the sibling module plucked_strings.py.

Ranges are sounding pitch (a double bass sounds an octave below written), after the standard orchestration ranges (Adler, The Study of Orchestration) and the common tunings of folk instruments. Timbres: a bowed string is sawtooth-like (the bow's stick-slip motion; Helmholtz) with bow noise.

docs.title: timbres
docs.text:
The building blocks the instrument catalog is made of: overtone series and instrument shapes.

Every catalog instrument is an ordinary Instrument (waves, noise, up to four sources, an envelope, filters and drive), built by one of the shapes here:

  • blown: a sustained tone (flutes, reeds, brass, bowed strings, voices, organs): a wave from an overtone series, optional detuned copies (a chorus or a section), breath or bow noise, an optional bright bite layer that fades after the attack (a brass or reed onset).
  • plucked: a string that is plucked or struck once and rings down (guitars, lutes, harps, pianos): the series shaped by where the string is plucked, optional extra courses (a mandolin's pairs, a twelve-string's octaves) and a pick or hammer noise.
  • struck: a bar, bell, plate or membrane whose partials are not harmonics (mallets, bells, steel pans, timpani): up to four sine partials at their own frequency ratios, each with its own decay, so the high partials die first, as they do in a struck bar.
  • rubbed: a glass, rod or bowl set singing by friction (a wet finger, a rosined cylinder): the struck partials, but swelling in over an attack and holding while the note is held.
  • drum: an unpitched hit: a tone that may glide (a kick's drop) and filtered noise, each decaying on its own.

The overtone shapes: falling_series (each harmonic quieter by a slope in dB per octave; with odd_only the closed-pipe spectrum of a clarinet), plucked_series (a string plucked at a fraction of its length has no harmonics with a node there: the comb of sin(pi n p), standard string acoustics) and formant_series (harmonics weighted by resonance peaks: a voice's vowel, an instrument's body).

def blown(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - each keyword is one physical trait
    levels: Sequence[float],
    *,
    attack: float,
    release: float,
    decay: float = 0.0,
    sustain: float = 1.0,
    breath: float = 0.0,
    breath_low_pass: float = 4000.0,
    low_pass: float | None = None,
    high_pass: float | None = None,
    drive: float = 0.0,
    chorus_cents: float = 0.0,
    bite_levels: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> Instrument:
    """A sustained tone: a wind, a bowed string, an organ pipe or a voice.

    Args:
        levels: The tone's harmonic levels.
        attack: Seconds to full level (a flute speaks slower than a trumpet).
        release: Seconds to silence after the note.
        decay: Seconds from the attack peak down to ``sustain``.
        sustain: The held level.
        breath: Breath or bow noise level (0 for none).
        breath_low_pass: The breath noise's low-pass cutoff.
        low_pass: A low-pass cutoff for the whole instrument (a darker bell or body), or None.
        high_pass: A high-pass cutoff when there is no low-pass (a mute), or None.
        drive: Distortion, 0-20 (a hard-blown reed's grit).
        chorus_cents: When above 0, a second copy of the tone this many cents sharp (two
            players, or a slightly unsteady pitch beating against itself).
        bite_levels: A brighter series that fades after the attack, or None.

    Returns:
        The instrument.
    """
    tone_wave = wave_from_levels(levels)
    sources: dict[str, Source] = {'tone': Source(tone_wave)}
    if chorus_cents > 0.0:
        sources['chorus'] = Source(tone_wave, detune_cents=chorus_cents, level=CHORUS_LEVEL)
    if bite_levels is not None:
        sources['bite'] = Source(
            wave_from_levels(bite_levels),
            level=0.6,
            envelope=envelope(
                attack=attack, decay=BITE_DECAY_SECONDS, sustain=BITE_SUSTAIN, release=release
            ),
        )
    if breath > 0.0:
        sources['breath'] = noise_layer(level=breath, low_pass=breath_low_pass)
    return Instrument(
        sources=sources,
        envelope=envelope(attack=attack, decay=decay, sustain=sustain, release=release),
        filter=_instrument_filter(low_pass=low_pass, high_pass=high_pass),
        drive=drive,
        normalize=True,
    )

def drum(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - each keyword is one physical trait
    *,
    tones: Sequence[Tone] = (),
    noise: float = 0.0,
    noise_ring_seconds: float = 0.1,
    noise_low_pass: float | None = None,
    noise_high_pass: float | None = None,
    tail: float = 0.3,
    attack: float = 0.0,
    drive: float = 0.0,
) -> Instrument:
    """An unpitched hit: fixed tones (they ignore the note's pitch) and filtered noise.

    Args:
        tones: Up to three (four without noise) pitched parts.
        noise: The noise level (0 for none).
        noise_ring_seconds: Seconds the noise takes to die away.
        noise_low_pass: The noise's low-pass cutoff, or None.
        noise_high_pass: The noise's high-pass cutoff when there is no low-pass, or None.
        tail: Seconds the sound may ring after the note ends.
        attack: Seconds to full level (a brush swish, a gong's bloom).
        drive: Distortion, 0-20.

    Returns:
        The instrument.

    Raises:
        ValueError: With nothing to sound, or more parts than the four sources allow.
    """
    room = 3 if noise > 0.0 else 4
    if len(tones) > room or (not tones and noise <= 0.0):
        message = f'a drum takes noise or 1 to {room} tones here, got {len(tones)} tones'
        raise ValueError(message)
    sources: dict[str, Source] = {}
    for number, tone in enumerate(tones, start=1):
        glide = (
            PitchCurve(to=Hz(tone.glide_to), seconds=tone.glide_seconds, easing='ease_out_quad')
            if tone.glide_to is not None
            else None
        )
        sources[f'tone_{number}'] = Source(
            tone.wave,
            pitch=Hz(tone.hertz),
            pitch_curve=glide,
            level=tone.level,
            envelope=envelope(
                attack=attack, decay=tone.ring_seconds, sustain=tone.sustain, release=tail
            ),
        )
    if noise > 0.0:
        sources['noise'] = noise_layer(
            level=noise,
            low_pass=noise_low_pass,
            high_pass=noise_high_pass,
            layer_envelope=envelope(
                attack=attack, decay=noise_ring_seconds, sustain=0.0, release=tail
            ),
        )
    return Instrument(
        sources=sources,
        envelope=envelope(attack=0.0, release=tail),
        drive=drive,
        normalize=True,
    )

A sawtooth falls 6 dB per octave (1/n); a bright brass or double reed falls less, a flute much more.

def falling_series(
    *,
    count: int,
    decibels_per_octave: float,
    odd_only: bool = False,
    even_level: float = 1.0,
) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """Harmonic levels falling by a slope: harmonic n at -slope x log2(n) dB.

    A sawtooth falls 6 dB per octave (1/n); a bright brass or double reed falls less, a flute
    much more.

    Args:
        count: How many harmonics, from the fundamental.
        decibels_per_octave: The slope.
        odd_only: Leave out the even harmonics (a closed pipe: the clarinet, the crumhorn).
        even_level: Scale the even harmonics by this (a clarinet keeps a trace of them).

    Returns:
        The levels, harmonic 1 first.
    """
    levels: list[float] = []
    for harmonic in range(1, count + 1):
        level = decibels_to_level(-decibels_per_octave * math.log2(harmonic))
        if harmonic % 2 == 0:
            level *= 0.0 if odd_only else even_level
        levels.append(level)
    return tuple(levels)

docs.title: formant_series(*, fundamental_hz, formants, source_decibels_per_octave=6.0, floor_decibels=-40.0)
docs.text:
Harmonic levels of a tone at fundamental_hz heard through resonance peaks.

The source-filter model of a voice (Fant, Acoustic Theory of Speech Production): a source whose harmonics fall by source_decibels_per_octave (the glottal pulses fall about 12 dB an octave and the lips' radiation lifts them 6, so 6 net), times the resonances' response at each harmonic. Each resonance responds as a damped resonator does, 1 / sqrt(1 + (2 (f - centre) / bandwidth)^2) scaled by its gain, so its skirts reach far enough that the fundamental is never lost (a gaussian peak left a soprano's "ee" with almost no fundamental: a thin tone whose waveform repeats at a higher octave). The table's harmonics keep their levels at every pitch, so the peaks sit where they belong only near fundamental_hz (pick the middle of the instrument's range) and move with the note elsewhere.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fundamental_hz float

The pitch the peaks are placed for.

required formants Sequence[Formant]

The resonance peaks.

required source_decibels_per_octave float

The source's slope.

6.0 floor_decibels float

The response between peaks.

-40.0

Returns:

Type Description tuple[float, ...]

The levels (as many harmonics as fit below 12 kHz, at most 32), the loudest 1.

Source code in src/glitchygames/audio/instruments/timbres.py 
def formant_series(
    *,
    fundamental_hz: float,
    formants: Sequence[Formant],
    source_decibels_per_octave: float = 6.0,
    floor_decibels: float = -40.0,
) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """Harmonic levels of a tone at ``fundamental_hz`` heard through resonance peaks.

    The source-filter model of a voice (Fant, *Acoustic Theory of Speech Production*): a source
    whose harmonics fall by ``source_decibels_per_octave`` (the glottal pulses fall about 12 dB
    an octave and the lips' radiation lifts them 6, so 6 net), times the resonances' response
    at each harmonic. Each resonance responds as a damped resonator does,
    1 / sqrt(1 + (2 (f - centre) / bandwidth)^2) scaled by its gain, so its skirts reach far
    enough that the fundamental is never lost (a gaussian peak left a soprano's "ee" with almost
    no fundamental: a thin tone whose waveform repeats at a higher octave). The table's
    harmonics keep their levels at every pitch, so the peaks sit where they belong only near
    ``fundamental_hz`` (pick the middle of the instrument's range) and move with the note
    elsewhere.

    Args:
        fundamental_hz: The pitch the peaks are placed for.
        formants: The resonance peaks.
        source_decibels_per_octave: The source's slope.
        floor_decibels: The response between peaks.

    Returns:
        The levels (as many harmonics as fit below 12 kHz, at most 32), the loudest 1.
    """
    count = max(1, min(HIGHEST_HARMONIC, int(12000.0 // fundamental_hz)))
    source = falling_series(count=count, decibels_per_octave=source_decibels_per_octave)
    levels: list[float] = []
    for harmonic, source_level in enumerate(source, start=1):
        frequency = harmonic * fundamental_hz
        response = decibels_to_level(floor_decibels)
        for formant in formants:
            distance = 2.0 * (frequency - formant.hertz) / formant.bandwidth
            response += decibels_to_level(formant.decibels) / math.sqrt(1.0 + distance**2)
        levels.append(source_level * response)
    loudest = max(levels)
    return tuple(level / loudest for level in levels)

def noise_layer(
    *,
    level: float,
    low_pass: float | None = None,
    high_pass: float | None = None,
    layer_envelope: EnvelopeSpec | None = None,
    seed: int | None = None,
) -> Source:
    """White noise with at most one filter (low-pass wins: one filter per source).

    Args:
        level: The layer's level, 0-1.
        low_pass: A low-pass cutoff in hertz, or None.
        high_pass: A high-pass cutoff in hertz, or None.

    return Source(
        Noise('white', level=level, seed=seed), filter=layer_filter, envelope=layer_envelope

def plucked(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - each keyword is one physical trait
    levels: Sequence[float],
    *,
    ring_seconds: float,
    release: float = 0.25,
    attack: float = 0.002,
    sustain: float = 0.0,
    courses: Sequence[Course] = (),
    pick: float = 0.0,
    pick_high_pass: float = 2000.0,
    low_pass: float | None = None,
    high_pass: float | None = None,
    drive: float = 0.0,
) -> Instrument:
    """A string plucked or struck once: it rings down over ``ring_seconds``.

    Args:
        levels: The string's harmonic levels (``plucked_series``).
        ring_seconds: Seconds from the pluck down to ``sustain``.
        release: Seconds to silence once the note is let go (a damped string).
        attack: Seconds to full level.
        sustain: The level it rings down to (above 0 for an amplified, driven guitar).
        courses: Up to two more strings per note (paired courses, octave strings).
        pick: The pick, nail or hammer noise level (0 for none).
        pick_high_pass: The pick noise's high-pass cutoff.
        low_pass: A low-pass cutoff for the instrument, or None.
        high_pass: A high-pass cutoff when there is no low-pass, or None.
        drive: Distortion, 0-20.

    Returns:
        The instrument.

    Raises:
        ValueError: With more than two courses.
    """
    if len(courses) > MAXIMUM_COURSES:
        message = f'a plucked instrument takes at most two extra courses, got {len(courses)}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    string_wave = wave_from_levels(levels)
    sources: dict[str, Source] = {'string': Source(string_wave)}
    for number, course in enumerate(courses, start=1):
        sources[f'course_{number}'] = Source(
            string_wave, semitones=course.semitones, detune_cents=course.cents, level=course.level
        )
    if pick > 0.0:
        sources['pick'] = noise_layer(
            level=pick,
            high_pass=pick_high_pass,
            layer_envelope=envelope(attack=0.0005, decay=0.02, sustain=0.0, release=0.01),
        )
    return Instrument(
        sources=sources,
        envelope=envelope(attack=attack, decay=ring_seconds, sustain=sustain, release=release),
        filter=_instrument_filter(low_pass=low_pass, high_pass=high_pass),
        drive=drive,
        normalize=True,
    )

Harmonic n is scaled by |sin(pi n p)|: a harmonic with a node where the string is plucked is not excited (plucked at a fifth of the length, the fifth, tenth... harmonics are gone). The levels are scaled so the loudest is 1.

Parameters:

How many harmonics.

required decibels_per_octave float

The underlying slope.

required pluck_position float

Where the string is plucked, as a fraction of its length (0-0.5).

def plucked_series(
    *, count: int, decibels_per_octave: float, pluck_position: float
) -> tuple[float, ...]:
    """A string's harmonics when plucked or struck at ``pluck_position`` of its length.

    Harmonic n is scaled by |sin(pi n p)|: a harmonic with a node where the string is plucked
    is not excited (plucked at a fifth of the length, the fifth, tenth... harmonics are gone).
    The levels are scaled so the loudest is 1.

    Args:
        count: How many harmonics.
        decibels_per_octave: The underlying slope.
        pluck_position: Where the string is plucked, as a fraction of its length (0-0.5).

    Returns:
        The levels, harmonic 1 first.
    """
    slope = falling_series(count=count, decibels_per_octave=decibels_per_octave)
    shaped = [
        level * abs(math.sin(math.pi * harmonic * pluck_position))
        for harmonic, level in enumerate(slope, start=1)
    ]
    loudest = max(shaped)
    return tuple(level / loudest for level in shaped)

    Friction feeds the vibration steadily, so the sound swells in over ``attack`` and then

    *,
    release: float,
    mallet: float = 0.0,
    mallet_low_pass: float = 3000.0,
    low_pass: float | None = None,

def with_drones(
    chanter: Instrument, *, drones: Sequence[tuple[float, float]], drone_wave: Wave
) -> Instrument:
    """A chanter with fixed-pitch drones sounding under every note (a bagpipe).

    Args:
        chanter: The chanter: its ``tone`` source and, if any, its ``breath`` are kept.
        drones: (hertz, level) for each drone, at most two with breath, three without.
        drone_wave: The drones' wave.

    Returns:
        The instrument.

    Raises:
        ValueError: With more drones than the four sources allow.
    """
    kept = {name: source for name, source in chanter.sources if name in {'tone', 'breath'}}
    if len(drones) > 4 - len(kept):
        message = f'room for {4 - len(kept)} drones, got {len(drones)}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    sources = dict(kept)
    for number, (hertz, level) in enumerate(drones, start=1):
        sources[f'drone_{number}'] = Source(drone_wave, pitch=Hz(hertz), level=level)
    assert chanter.envelope is not None
    return Instrument(
        sources=sources,
        envelope=chanter.envelope,
        filter=None
        if chanter.filter is None
        else Filter(kind=chanter.filter.kind, cutoff=chanter.filter.cutoff_hz),
        drive=chanter.drive,
        normalize=True,
    )

docs.title: voices
docs.text:
Sung voices: soprano to basso profundo on five vowels, humming, choirs and whistling.

A sung vowel is the voice's harmonics heard through the vocal tract's resonances (formants). The formant frequencies, bandwidths and gains for soprano, alto, countertenor, tenor and bass on a, e, i, o and u are the Csound manual's "Formant Values" table (Csound Reference Manual, Appendix, https://csound.com/docs/manual/MiscFormants.html). Mezzo-soprano uses the alto's, baritone the tenor's and bass's averaged, basso profundo the bass's, treble (a boy soprano) the soprano's. The harmonic levels are computed at the middle of each voice's range; the instrument's harmonics keep those levels at every pitch, so the vowel is truest mid-range (no formant filter moves with the note here). Choirs are three detuned voices; ranges are the usual choral ranges.

docs.title: winds
docs.text:
Woodwinds: flutes, clarinets, saxophones, double reeds, bagpipes and free reeds.

Ranges are sounding pitch (a B-flat clarinet's written C sounds B-flat), after the standard orchestration ranges (Adler, The Study of Orchestration; Vienna Symphonic Library's instrument pages); folk instruments' are typical of the common keys. Timbres follow the instruments' acoustics: a flute is nearly pure with breath, a clarinet (a closed cylinder) favours odd harmonics, saxophones and double reeds (cones) have every harmonic and are brighter, free reeds are bright and buzzy, a bagpipe's chanter sounds over fixed drones.

docs.title: library
docs.text:
The sound library: one-call sound(), the cache modes and compile accounting.

The first request for a sound compiles it, equal requests return the same Sound, and getting a sound never plays it (feature spec 3.1, impl spec 6.2 and 6.4). With cache none getting a sound renders nothing: a Sound holds only what identifies it and what a game may read of it, and every play compiles it anew (compile_for_play), which forces mid-frame rendering for benchmarks; a sound played 5 times compiles 5 times (AUD-MEAS-001). The pieces of work are timed by the library's AudioAccountant (impl spec 11.0).

What a game may read of a sound (length, peak, sample_rate) never depends on the cache, which is replay-local, so a replay under another mode reads the same, bit for bit. Under ram the request's compile sets them, and release() (the memory limit's eviction) keeps them. Under none (Rulings R49 and R50) nothing renders or decodes at request: - a spec's and a version 0 recipe's length is derived the way the compile sizes its samples (render.rendered_frame_count, SoundRecipe.frame_count), and their sample_rate is the rate they compile at; - a recorded file's length and sample_rate are known only by decoding it (a mixer converts it as it loads; a truncated WAV decodes fewer frames than its header claims), so they come from a decode on their first read; - peak likewise comes from a compile on its first read. That compile is counted and attributed like any other, and what it gives is kept. A play's compile gives them too, so a read after a play compiles nothing more.

The engine's own sounds (the CRT power-on's, engine_sound) compile once per process (the owner, 2026-11-02): their compiled samples are kept in ENGINE_SOUND_CACHE, by identity key (impl spec 6.2: the key holds the mixer's rate and the tuning, so a mixer restarted at another rate compiles anew), and every later request, in any library of any engine context, reuses them. The first compile is counted and attributed like any compile, in the library that asked; a reuse is a counted hit. They are outside a library's cache mode and memory limit: under none they stay compiled and their plays compile nothing, the memory limit never evicts them, and bytes_held leaves them out. Each library makes its own Sound of them (its own player and pygame sound) over the shared samples, which are read-only (impl spec 10.1). The cache is a read-only cache in the engine context's sense (plans/2026-10-25-engine-context.md, the audit's read-only rows): values computed only from their keys, never written after they are made.

class EngineSoundCache:
    """The engine's own sounds' compiled samples, one cache per process, by identity key.

    Only the engine's sounds (the CRT power-on's, ``SoundLibrary.engine_sound``) are kept here;
    a game's sounds stay in its context's library. Nothing here is ever evicted: the engine's
    sounds are few and short (the CRT's five or six, about 0.5 MB at 44.1 kHz). ``clear`` exists
    for the test harness, which starts every test with an empty cache.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Start empty."""
        self._compiled: dict[str, CompiledSamples] = {}

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """The number of sounds kept.

        Returns:
            The count.
        """
        return len(self._compiled)

    def compiled(self, identity_key: str) -> CompiledSamples | None:
        """The compiled samples of a sound, if this process compiled it already.

        Args:
            identity_key: The sound's identity key.

        Returns:
            The samples, or None.
        """
        return self._compiled.get(identity_key)

    def keep(self, sound: Sound) -> CompiledSamples:
        """Keep a freshly compiled sound's samples, made read-only, for every later request.

        Args:
            sound: The compiled sound.

        Returns:
            The samples kept.
        """
        assert sound.samples_float is not None
        assert sound.samples_int16 is not None
        # Shared by every context's Sound: nothing may write them in place
        sound.samples_float.flags.writeable = False
        sound.samples_int16.flags.writeable = False
        compiled = CompiledSamples(
            samples_float=sound.samples_float,
            samples_int16=sound.samples_int16,
            peak=sound.peak,
            sample_rate=sound.sample_rate,
        )
        self._compiled[sound.identity_key] = compiled
        return compiled

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Forget every sound (the test harness's reset; the next request compiles)."""
        self._compiled.clear()

class Sound:
    """A sound the library compiled (or, under cache ``none``, will compile at each play).

    Exactly one of ``spec`` (a version 1 sound or an instrument), ``legacy_recipe`` (version 0) and
    ``recorded_file`` says how it is compiled. ``length``, ``peak`` and ``sample_rate`` are what a
    game may read of it, the same under either cache (see the module docstring): a sound got from
    the library gives all three (under ``none`` the ones not derived come from one compile on
    their first read), and ``release()`` keeps them. A sound neither compiled nor got from a
    library reads ``length`` and ``peak`` as 0.0. A sound the memory limit dropped is compiled
    again, in place, by its next request.

    Attributes:
        name: The short name, the path stem, or a generated ``instrument-<digest>`` name.
        is_live: Whether this is a live (M2) sound.
        is_engine_sound: Whether this is one of the engine's own sounds (``engine_sound``).
        identity_key: The cache key.
        playback_defaults: The sound file's playback defaults.
        spec: The spec of a version 1 sound, or None.
        legacy_recipe: The version 0 recipe, or None.
        recorded_file: The WAV/OGG path of a recorded sound, or None.
        samples_float: Mono float64 samples, or None until compiled.
        samples_int16: The same as signed 16-bit PCM, or None until compiled.
    """

    def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - one construction site
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        identity_key: str,
        sample_rate: int,
        playback_defaults: PlaybackDefaults,
        spec: SoundSpec | None = None,
        legacy_recipe: SoundRecipe | None = None,
        recorded_file: Path | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Make an uncompiled sound.

        Args:
            name: The sound's name.
            identity_key: The cache key.
            sample_rate: The rate to compile at.
            playback_defaults: The default playback settings.
            spec: The spec of a version 1 sound.
            legacy_recipe: The version 0 recipe.
            recorded_file: A recorded sound's file.
        """
        self.name = name
        self.identity_key = identity_key
        # The rate to compile at; a recorded file's decode replaces it with the samples' own
        self._sample_rate = sample_rate
        self.playback_defaults = playback_defaults
        self.spec = spec
        self.legacy_recipe = legacy_recipe
        self.recorded_file = recorded_file
        self.is_live = spec.live if spec is not None else False
        # The engine's own sound (engine_sound): compiled once per process, never evicted or
        # compiled again for a play, whatever the cache mode
        self.is_engine_sound = False
        # None until known: a compile sets them, or (cache none) describe_lazily's derivation,
        # or a first read's compile through _compile_for_metadata
        self._length: float | None = None
        self._peak: float | None = None
        self._sample_rate_known = True
        self._compile_for_metadata: Callable[[Sound], Sound] | None = None
        self.samples_float: FloatArray | None = None
        self.samples_int16: Int16Array | None = None
        self._mixer_sound: pygame.mixer.Sound | None = None
        self._mixer_settings: tuple[int, int, int] | None = None
        self._mixer_bytes = 0
        # The audio engine that handed the sound out plays it (attach_player)
        self._player: SoundPlayer | None = None
        self._warned_no_player = False

    def attach_player(self, player: SoundPlayer) -> None:
        """Let ``play()`` go to an audio engine (it attaches itself when it hands the sound out).

        Args:
            player: The engine's play function.
        """
        self._player = player

    def play(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8's playback arguments
        self,
        *,
        volume: float | None = None,
        pan: float | None = None,
        bus: str | None = None,
        priority: int | None = None,
        loop: bool | None = None,
        at_frame: int | None = None,
        persist: bool = False,
        position: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    ) -> SoundHandle:
        """Play the sound; arguments left as None take the sound file's defaults (impl spec 8).

        Args:
            volume: 0-1.
            pan: -1 (left) to 1 (right).
            bus: The bus name.
            priority: 0-100, for voice stealing.
            loop: Whether it loops until stopped or released.
            at_frame: A frame to start on (M2).
            persist: Whether the voice outlives its scene.
            position: A position for positional audio (M4).

        Returns:
            The handle. A sound no audio engine handed out (a bare library's) has no voices: its
            handle answers False, and a warning is logged once per sound.
        """
        if self._player is None:
            if not self._warned_no_player:
                self._warned_no_player = True
                log.warning('%s was not got from an audio engine: its plays are silent', self.name)
            return SoundHandle(slot=-1, generation=-1)
        return self._player(
            self,
            volume=volume,
            pan=pan,
            bus=bus,
            priority=priority,
            loop=loop,
            at_frame=at_frame,
            persist=persist,
            position=position,
        )

    @property
    def length(self) -> float:
        """Seconds, including the release tail (0.0 for a sound neither compiled nor described)."""
        if self._length is None:
            self._compile_for_unknown_metadata()
        return 0.0 if self._length is None else self._length

    @property
    def peak(self) -> float:
        """The loudest sample's magnitude before clipping (0.0 until known, as ``length``)."""
        if self._peak is None:
            self._compile_for_unknown_metadata()
        return 0.0 if self._peak is None else self._peak

    @property
    def sample_rate(self) -> int:
        """The rate of the samples.

        The rate the sound compiles at (the mixer's at request time), except a recorded file's:
        decoded without a mixer it keeps its file's rate, and loaded through a mixer it is
        converted to the mixer's, known once it is decoded.
        """
        if not self._sample_rate_known:
            self._compile_for_unknown_metadata()
        return self._sample_rate

    def describe_lazily(
        self,
        *,
        length: float | None,
        sample_rate_known: bool,
        compile_for_metadata: Callable[[Sound], Sound],
    ) -> None:
        """Hold what cache ``none`` knows of the sound without compiling it.

        Args:
            length: The derived length, or None when only a compile can tell it.
            sample_rate_known: False when only a compile can tell the rate (a recorded file).
            compile_for_metadata: Compiles a copy of the sound (the library's, counted and
                timed); the first read of a value not yet known calls it once.
        """
        self._length = length
        self._sample_rate_known = sample_rate_known
        self._compile_for_metadata = compile_for_metadata

    def adopt_metadata(self, compiled: Sound) -> None:
        """Keep a compiled copy's length, peak and rate where this sound does not know them yet.

        Args:
            compiled: A compiled copy of this sound (a play's, or a first read's).
        """
        if self._length is None:
            self._length = compiled.length
        if self._peak is None:
            self._peak = compiled.peak
        if not self._sample_rate_known:
            self._sample_rate = compiled.sample_rate
            self._sample_rate_known = True

    def _compile_for_unknown_metadata(self) -> None:
        """Compile a copy for what is not yet known, when the library gave a way to (``none``)."""
        if self._compile_for_metadata is not None:
            self.adopt_metadata(self._compile_for_metadata(self))

    @property
    def retained_bytes(self) -> int:
        """Every byte the sound holds: both sample arrays and the pygame sound's buffer."""
        held = self._mixer_bytes
        for samples in (self.samples_float, self.samples_int16):
            if samples is not None:
                held += samples.nbytes
        return held

    @property
    def is_compiled(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the sound holds its samples."""
        return self.samples_int16 is not None

    def fresh_copy(self, *, sample_rate: int | None = None) -> Sound:
        """Make an uncompiled sound that compiles the same way (cache ``none``, each play).

        Args:
            sample_rate: A rate to compile the copy at instead of this sound's (an offline
                render's); a spec is rebuilt at that rate. A recorded file still decodes at its
                own rate (or the mixer's). None keeps this sound's rate.

        Returns:
            The new sound.
        """
        # The rate it compiles at, read without a first-read compile (a recorded file's decode
        # finds its own rate whatever this is)
        rate = self._sample_rate if sample_rate is None else sample_rate
        spec = self.spec
        if spec is not None and spec.sample_rate != rate:
            spec = replace(spec, sample_rate=rate)
        return Sound(
            name=self.name,
            identity_key=self.identity_key,
            sample_rate=rate,
            playback_defaults=self.playback_defaults,
            spec=spec,
            legacy_recipe=self.legacy_recipe,
            recorded_file=self.recorded_file,
        )

    def install(
        self,
        *,
        samples_float: FloatArray,
        samples_int16: Int16Array,
        peak: float,
        sample_rate: int,
        mixer_sound: pygame.mixer.Sound | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Hold the compiled samples.

        Args:
            samples_float: Mono float64 samples.
            samples_int16: The same as signed 16-bit PCM.
            peak: The loudest magnitude before clipping.
            sample_rate: The rate of the samples.
            mixer_sound: A pygame sound already made from them (a recorded file's), or None.
        """
        self.samples_float = samples_float
        self.samples_int16 = samples_int16
        self._peak = peak
        self._sample_rate = sample_rate
        self._sample_rate_known = True
        self._length = len(samples_int16) / sample_rate
        self._mixer_sound = mixer_sound
        self._mixer_settings = pygame.mixer.get_init() if mixer_sound is not None else None
        self._mixer_bytes = len(mixer_sound.get_raw()) if mixer_sound is not None else 0

    def release(self) -> None:
        """Drop the samples and the pygame sound (the memory limit's eviction; cache ``none``).

        ``length``, ``peak`` and ``sample_rate`` stay: a game may read them whatever the cache.
        """
        self.samples_float = None
        self.samples_int16 = None
        self._mixer_sound = None
        self._mixer_settings = None
        self._mixer_bytes = 0

    def mixer_sound(self) -> pygame.mixer.Sound | None:
        """The pygame sound for the running mixer, built on first use.

        A sound compiled before the mixer started gets its pygame sound here once there is a
        mixer. If the mixer's rate differs from the sound's, the samples are resampled (linearly)
        so the sound keeps its pitch and length; a two-channel mixer gets the mono samples on both
        channels.

        Returns:
            The sound, or None without a mixer or before the sound is compiled.

        Raises:
            AudioUnavailableError: If the mixer is not signed 16-bit.
        """
        settings = pygame.mixer.get_init()
        if settings is None or self.samples_int16 is None:
            return None
        if self._mixer_sound is not None and self._mixer_settings == settings:
            return self._mixer_sound
        rate, sample_format, channel_count = settings
        if sample_format != SIGNED_16_BIT_FORMAT:
            message = f'mixer format {sample_format} is not signed 16-bit'
            raise AudioUnavailableError(message)
        samples = self.samples_int16
        if rate != self.sample_rate:
            samples = _resample(samples, from_rate=self.sample_rate, to_rate=rate)
        frames = (
            samples
            if channel_count == 1
            else np.repeat(samples[:, np.newaxis], channel_count, axis=1)
        )
        # pygame.sndarray.make_sound has incomplete type stubs for its ndarray parameter
        self._mixer_sound = pygame.sndarray.make_sound(np.ascontiguousarray(frames))
        self._mixer_settings = settings
        self._mixer_bytes = int(frames.nbytes)
        return self._mixer_sound

def fresh_copy(self, *, sample_rate: int | None = None) -> Sound:
    """Make an uncompiled sound that compiles the same way (cache ``none``, each play).

    Args:
        sample_rate: A rate to compile the copy at instead of this sound's (an offline
            render's); a spec is rebuilt at that rate. A recorded file still decodes at its
            own rate (or the mixer's). None keeps this sound's rate.

    Returns:
        The new sound.
    """
    # The rate it compiles at, read without a first-read compile (a recorded file's decode
    # finds its own rate whatever this is)
    rate = self._sample_rate if sample_rate is None else sample_rate
    spec = self.spec
    if spec is not None and spec.sample_rate != rate:
        spec = replace(spec, sample_rate=rate)
    return Sound(
        name=self.name,
        identity_key=self.identity_key,
        sample_rate=rate,
        playback_defaults=self.playback_defaults,
        spec=spec,
        legacy_recipe=self.legacy_recipe,
        recorded_file=self.recorded_file,
    )

A sound compiled before the mixer started gets its pygame sound here once there is a mixer. If the mixer's rate differs from the sound's, the samples are resampled (linearly) so the sound keeps its pitch and length; a two-channel mixer gets the mono samples on both channels.

def mixer_sound(self) -> pygame.mixer.Sound | None:
    """The pygame sound for the running mixer, built on first use.

    A sound compiled before the mixer started gets its pygame sound here once there is a
    mixer. If the mixer's rate differs from the sound's, the samples are resampled (linearly)
    so the sound keeps its pitch and length; a two-channel mixer gets the mono samples on both
    channels.

    Returns:
        The sound, or None without a mixer or before the sound is compiled.

    Raises:
        AudioUnavailableError: If the mixer is not signed 16-bit.
    """
    settings = pygame.mixer.get_init()
    if settings is None or self.samples_int16 is None:
        return None
    if self._mixer_sound is not None and self._mixer_settings == settings:
        return self._mixer_sound
    rate, sample_format, channel_count = settings
    if sample_format != SIGNED_16_BIT_FORMAT:
        message = f'mixer format {sample_format} is not signed 16-bit'
        raise AudioUnavailableError(message)
    samples = self.samples_int16
    if rate != self.sample_rate:
        samples = _resample(samples, from_rate=self.sample_rate, to_rate=rate)
    frames = (
        samples
        if channel_count == 1
        else np.repeat(samples[:, np.newaxis], channel_count, axis=1)
    )
    # pygame.sndarray.make_sound has incomplete type stubs for its ndarray parameter
    self._mixer_sound = pygame.sndarray.make_sound(np.ascontiguousarray(frames))
    self._mixer_settings = settings
    self._mixer_bytes = int(frames.nbytes)
    return self._mixer_sound

def play(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8's playback arguments
    self,
    *,
    volume: float | None = None,
    pan: float | None = None,
    bus: str | None = None,
    priority: int | None = None,
    loop: bool | None = None,
    at_frame: int | None = None,
    persist: bool = False,
    position: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
) -> SoundHandle:
    """Play the sound; arguments left as None take the sound file's defaults (impl spec 8).

    Args:
        volume: 0-1.
        pan: -1 (left) to 1 (right).
        bus: The bus name.
        priority: 0-100, for voice stealing.
        loop: Whether it loops until stopped or released.
        at_frame: A frame to start on (M2).
        persist: Whether the voice outlives its scene.
        position: A position for positional audio (M4).

    Returns:
        The handle. A sound no audio engine handed out (a bare library's) has no voices: its
        handle answers False, and a warning is logged once per sound.
    """
    if self._player is None:
        if not self._warned_no_player:
            self._warned_no_player = True
            log.warning('%s was not got from an audio engine: its plays are silent', self.name)
        return SoundHandle(slot=-1, generation=-1)
    return self._player(
        self,
        volume=volume,
        pan=pan,
        bus=bus,
        priority=priority,
        loop=loop,
        at_frame=at_frame,
        persist=persist,
        position=position,
    )
