class SoundLibrary:
    """Resolves, compiles and caches sounds (the engine's ``audio.sound`` lives here).

    The memory limit counts every byte a compiled sound retains (``Sound.retained_bytes``).
    """

    def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - mirrors the brief's signature
        self,
        *,
        cache: CacheMode,
        accountant: AudioAccountant,
        waves: WaveRegistry,
        tuning_source: Callable[[], Tuning],
        memory_limit_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES,
        is_playing: Callable[[Sound], bool] = _nothing_plays,
    ) -> None:
        """Make a library.

        Args:
            cache: The cache mode.
            accountant: Where compile and decode times go.
            waves: The registry the wave tables of loaded sound files are registered in; it must
                be the current context's (``build_spec`` looks waves up there).
            tuning_source: Gives the tuning at each request.
            memory_limit_bytes: The bytes compiled sounds may retain (both sample arrays and the
                pygame sound) before the least recently played idle sounds go.
            is_playing: Says whether a sound is playing, so eviction spares it; the mixer
                supplies it. The default says nothing is playing.

        Raises:
            ValueError: For cache ``disk``, which arrives in M3.
        """
        if cache is CacheMode.DISK:
            raise ValueError(DISK_CACHE_MESSAGE)
        self._cache = cache
        self._accountant = accountant
        self._waves = waves
        self._tuning_source = tuning_source
        self._memory_limit_bytes = memory_limit_bytes
        self._is_playing = is_playing
        self._recipes: dict[str, SoundRecipe] = {}
        self._indexes: dict[tuple[Path, Path | None], ShortNameIndex] = {}
        # request -> identity key, so a repeated request is a dictionary hit (impl spec 6.2).
        # A sound file edited after its first request is not re-read: hot reload is M4.
        self._memo: dict[tuple[object, ...], str] = {}
        self._sounds: dict[str, Sound] = {}
        # The engine's own sounds this library handed out, by request (engine_sound)
        self._engine_sounds: dict[tuple[object, ...], Sound] = {}
        # Compiled sounds, least recently played first
        self._play_order: OrderedDict[str, Sound] = OrderedDict()
        self._hits = 0
        self._misses = 0
        self._compiles = 0

    def add_recipes(self, recipes: Iterable[SoundRecipe]) -> None:
        """Add version 0 recipes by name; they are looked up before the sound directory.

        Args:
            recipes: The recipes.
        """
        for recipe in recipes:
            self._recipes[recipe.name] = recipe

    def names(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        """The names of the added recipes and of every sound requested so far.

        Returns:
            The names, sorted.
        """
        known = set(self._recipes)
        known.update(sound.name for sound in self._sounds.values())
        return tuple(sorted(known))

    def statistics(self) -> CacheStatistics:
        """What the cache has done so far.

        Returns:
            The counters.
        """
        return CacheStatistics(
            hits=self._hits,
            misses=self._misses,
            compiles=self._compiles,
            bytes_held=self._bytes_held(),
        )

    def sound(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8
        self,
        source: str | Instrument,
        *,
        scene_sound_directory: Path | None,
        package_root: Path | None = None,
        pitch: PitchLike | None = None,
        notes: str | Sequence[tuple[PitchLike, float]] | None = None,
        chord: Sequence[PitchLike] | None = None,
        length: float | None = None,
        transpose: float = 0.0,
        parameters: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    ) -> Sound:
        """Get a sound; the first request for an identity compiles it. Getting never plays.

        Arguments given here replace the sound file entry's own: a ``pitch``, ``notes`` or
        ``chord`` replaces all three of the entry's, ``length`` replaces its length, and
        ``transpose`` is added to its transpose. A recorded or version 0 sound takes none of them.

        Args:
            source: A short name, a path (``'sounds/pickups.toml#coin'``, ``'sounds/slap.wav'``;
                relative to ``package_root``), or an ``Instrument``.
            scene_sound_directory: Where short names are looked up, or None.
            package_root: The game package's directory (paths and file references stay inside it).
            pitch: A pitch.
            notes: A melody.
            chord: Pitches played together.
            length: Seconds per note or chord before release.
            transpose: Semitones to shift notes or a chord.
            parameters: Live parameters; they identify the request but a baked sound ignores them
                (live sounds arrive in M2).

        Returns:
            The sound. Under cache ``none`` it holds no samples and nothing was rendered or
            decoded: what is not derived comes from one compile on its first read (see the
            module docstring).
        """
        request = SoundRequest(
            source=source,
            scene_sound_directory=scene_sound_directory,
            package_root=package_root,
            pitch=pitch,
            notes=notes,
            chord=chord,
            length=length,
            transpose=transpose,
            parameters=parameters,
        )
        sound, known = self._lookup(request)
        self._ensure_compiled(sound, known=known)
        return sound

    def compile_for_play(self, sound: Sound) -> Sound:
        """The sound to play: the same one under ``ram``, a fresh compile under ``none``.

        Under ``ram`` a sound the memory limit dropped is compiled again, in place, and counted.
        Playing makes a ``ram`` sound the most recently played.

        Args:
            sound: A sound from ``sound()``.

        The engine's own sounds (``engine_sound``) are always compiled: they play as they are.

        Returns:
            The compiled sound.
        """
        if sound.is_engine_sound:
            return sound
        if self._cache is CacheMode.NONE:
            fresh = self._compiled_copy(sound)
            # A later read of what the sound did not know yet reuses this play's compile
            sound.adopt_metadata(fresh)
            return fresh
        if not sound.is_compiled:
            self._misses += 1
            self._compile(sound)
            self._hold(sound)
        else:
            self._play_order.move_to_end(sound.identity_key)
        return sound

    def engine_sound(
        self, instrument: Instrument, *, pitch: PitchLike | None, length: float | None
    ) -> Sound:
        """Get one of the engine's own sounds (the CRT power-on's): compiled once per process.

        The first request in the process compiles it here, counted, timed and attributed like
        any compile (a miss); every later one, in this library or any other context's, reuses
        the process's compiled samples (a hit) and compiles nothing. The cache mode and the
        memory limit do not apply (see the module docstring).

        Args:
            instrument: The instrument.
            pitch: Its pitch, or None for a noise.
            length: Seconds before the release.

        Returns:
            The library's own ``Sound`` over the shared samples, compiled.
        """
        sample_rate = mixer_sample_rate()
        tuning = self._tuning_source()
        request_key = (instrument, _freeze(pitch), length, sample_rate, tuning)
        handed_out = self._engine_sounds.get(request_key)
        if handed_out is not None:
            self._hits += 1
            return handed_out
        request = SoundRequest(
            source=instrument, scene_sound_directory=None, pitch=pitch, length=length
        )
        sound = self._build(request, sample_rate=sample_rate, tuning=tuning)
        sound.is_engine_sound = True
        compiled = ENGINE_SOUND_CACHE.compiled(sound.identity_key)
        if compiled is None:
            self._misses += 1
            self._compile(sound)
            ENGINE_SOUND_CACHE.keep(sound)
        else:
            self._hits += 1
            sound.install(
                samples_float=compiled.samples_float,
                samples_int16=compiled.samples_int16,
                peak=compiled.peak,
                sample_rate=compiled.sample_rate,
            )
        self._engine_sounds[request_key] = sound
        return sound

    def warm(self, requests: Sequence[SoundRequest], *, budget_ms: float | None = None) -> float:
        """Compile as many of the requests as fit in a time budget (for a loading scene).

        At least one request compiles per call. It uses the same compile path as ``sound()``.

        Args:
            requests: The ``sound()`` argument sets to have compiled.
            budget_ms: The milliseconds to spend this call, or None for no limit.

        Returns:
            Progress from 0 to 1: the share of requests that are compiled.
        """
        if not requests:
            return 1.0
        started = clock.raw_counter_ns()
        compiled_this_call = 0
        done = 0
        for request in requests:
            sound, known = self._lookup(request)
            if self._cache is CacheMode.RAM and not sound.is_compiled:
                elapsed_ms = (clock.raw_counter_ns() - started) / 1_000_000
                if budget_ms is not None and compiled_this_call > 0 and elapsed_ms >= budget_ms:
                    continue
                compiled_this_call += 1
            self._ensure_compiled(sound, known=known)
            done += 1
        return done / len(requests)

    def _ensure_compiled(self, sound: Sound, *, known: bool) -> None:
        """Count the request and, under ``ram``, compile the sound unless it is already.

        Under ``none`` a new sound is described without rendering (``_describe``).
        """
        if self._cache is CacheMode.NONE:
            if known:
                self._hits += 1
            else:
                self._misses += 1
                self._describe(sound)
            return
        if sound.is_compiled:
            self._hits += 1
            return
        self._misses += 1
        self._compile(sound)
        self._hold(sound)

    def _describe(self, sound: Sound) -> None:
        """Give a new cache ``none`` sound what can be known of it without compiling.

        ``length`` is the compile's frame count over the rate it compiles at, the same division
        ``Sound.install`` makes, so it is ``ram``'s bit for bit: a spec's from
        ``rendered_frame_count`` (the renderer's own buffer size), a version 0 recipe's from
        ``SoundRecipe.frame_count`` (``mix``'s own). A recorded file's length and rate are known
        only by decoding it, and every peak only by compiling: those come from
        ``_compiled_copy`` on their first read.
        """
        compile_rate = sound.sample_rate  # known for every sound until it is described
        if sound.spec is not None:
            length = rendered_frame_count(sound.spec) / compile_rate
        elif sound.legacy_recipe is not None:
            length = sound.legacy_recipe.frame_count(sample_rate=compile_rate) / compile_rate
        else:
            length = None
        sound.describe_lazily(
            length=length,
            sample_rate_known=sound.recorded_file is None,
            compile_for_metadata=self._compiled_copy,
        )

    def _compiled_copy(self, sound: Sound) -> Sound:
        """Compile a copy of a cache ``none`` sound (timed and counted).

        Returns:
            The compiled copy.
        """
        copy = sound.fresh_copy()
        self._compile(copy)
        return copy

    def _hold(self, sound: Sound) -> None:
        """Keep a compiled sound in memory; over the limit, drop the least recently played."""
        assert sound.samples_int16 is not None
        self._play_order[sound.identity_key] = sound
        self._play_order.move_to_end(sound.identity_key)
        if self._bytes_held() <= self._memory_limit_bytes:
            return
        for candidate in list(self._play_order.values()):
            # The sound just asked for stays, and so does anything that is playing
            if candidate is sound or self._is_playing(candidate):
                continue
            del self._play_order[candidate.identity_key]
            candidate.release()
            if self._bytes_held() <= self._memory_limit_bytes:
                break

    def _bytes_held(self) -> int:
        """Every byte the held sounds retain (a pygame sound built after compiling counts).

        Returns:
            The byte count.
        """
        return sum(held.retained_bytes for held in self._play_order.values())

    def _compile(self, sound: Sound) -> None:
        """Compile a sound into itself, timed and counted."""
        kind = 'decode' if sound.recorded_file is not None else 'compile'
        with self._accountant.measure(kind, sound.name):
            compile_sound(sound)
        self._compiles += 1

    def _lookup(self, request: SoundRequest) -> tuple[Sound, bool]:
        """Find the sound for a request, making (not compiling) it if it is new.

        Returns:
            The sound, and whether it was known already.
        """
        sample_rate = mixer_sample_rate()
        tuning = self._tuning_source()
        source = request.source
        source_key: object = (
            ('instrument', source)
            if isinstance(source, Instrument)
            else ('name', source, request.scene_sound_directory, request.package_root)
        )
        memo_key = (
            source_key,
            _freeze(request.pitch),
            _freeze(request.notes),
            _freeze(request.chord),
            request.length,
            request.transpose,
            _freeze(request.parameters),
            sample_rate,
            tuning,
        )
        remembered = self._memo.get(memo_key)
        if remembered is not None:
            return self._sounds[remembered], True
        sound = self._build(request, sample_rate=sample_rate, tuning=tuning)
        existing = self._sounds.get(sound.identity_key)
        if existing is not None:
            self._memo[memo_key] = existing.identity_key
            return existing, True
        self._sounds[sound.identity_key] = sound
        self._memo[memo_key] = sound.identity_key
        return sound, False

    def _build(self, request: SoundRequest, *, sample_rate: int, tuning: Tuning) -> Sound:
        """Resolve a request to an uncompiled sound.

        Returns:
            The sound.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When a recorded or version 0 sound is given a pitch, notes, chord, length
                or transpose.
        """
        if isinstance(request.source, Instrument):
            return self._instrument_sound(
                request.source,
                name=None,
                request=request,
                defaults=PlaybackDefaults(),
                sample_rate=sample_rate,
                tuning=tuning,
            )
        entry = self._resolve_entry(request)
        if (entry.legacy_recipe is not None or entry.file is not None) and _names_identity(request):
            message = (
                f'{entry.name!r} is a recorded or version 0 sound: it takes no pitch, notes, '
                f'chord, length or transpose'
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        if entry.legacy_recipe is not None:
            return Sound(
                name=entry.name,
                identity_key=_digest({
                    'legacy_recipe': entry.legacy_recipe.to_dict(),
                    'name': entry.name,
                    'sample_rate': sample_rate,
                    'render_version': AUDIO_RENDER_VERSION,
                    'numpy_version': np.__version__,
                    'platform': sysconfig.get_platform(),
                }),
                sample_rate=sample_rate,
                playback_defaults=entry.playback_defaults,
                legacy_recipe=entry.legacy_recipe,
            )
        if entry.file is not None:
            path = require_recorded_file(entry)
            status = path.stat()
            return Sound(
                name=entry.name,
                identity_key=_digest({
                    'recorded_file': str(path.resolve()),
                    'modification_time_ns': status.st_mtime_ns,
                    'size': status.st_size,
                    'sample_rate': sample_rate,
                }),
                sample_rate=sample_rate,
                playback_defaults=entry.playback_defaults,
                recorded_file=path,
            )
        assert entry.instrument is not None
        return self._instrument_sound(
            entry.instrument,
            name=entry.name,
            request=request,
            defaults=entry.playback_defaults,
            sample_rate=sample_rate,
            tuning=tuning,
            entry=entry,
        )

    def _instrument_sound(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - one construction site
        self,
        instrument: Instrument,
        *,
        name: str | None,
        request: SoundRequest,
        defaults: PlaybackDefaults,
        sample_rate: int,
        tuning: Tuning,
        entry: SoundEntry | None = None,
    ) -> Sound:
        """Build the sound of an instrument (given directly, or named by a sound file entry).

        Returns:
            The uncompiled sound.

        Raises:
            SoundRenderError: For a live instrument, which has no baked audio in M1.
        """
        pitch, notes, chord = request.pitch, request.notes, request.chord
        length, transpose = request.length, request.transpose
        if entry is not None:
            if pitch is None and notes is None and chord is None:
                pitch, notes, chord = entry.pitch, entry.notes, entry.chord
            if length is None:
                length = entry.length
            transpose += entry.transpose

        def spec_named(spec_name: str) -> SoundSpec:
            return build_spec(
                instrument,
                name=spec_name,
                pitch=pitch,
                notes=notes,
                chord=chord,
                length=length,
                transpose=transpose,
                tuning=tuning,
                sample_rate=sample_rate,
                playback_defaults=defaults,
            )

        if name is None:
            # The seed derives from the name, so the generated name must be the same in every
            # process: a digest of the spec built under a fixed name, never a hash() or an id()
            digest = identity_key(spec_named(GENERATED_NAME_PREFIX))
            name = f'{GENERATED_NAME_PREFIX}-{digest[:GENERATED_NAME_DIGITS]}'
        spec = spec_named(name)
        if spec.live:
            message = f'{name!r} is a live sound; live sounds arrive in M2'
            raise SoundRenderError(message)
        return Sound(
            name=name,
            identity_key=identity_key(spec),
            sample_rate=sample_rate,
            playback_defaults=defaults,
            spec=spec,
        )

    def _resolve_entry(self, request: SoundRequest) -> SoundEntry:
        """Find the sound file entry a string names.

        Returns:
            The entry (a recorded file gets one made for it).

        Raises:
            KeyError: For a short name with no sound directory. (Other failures come from the
                helpers: ``SoundAssetError`` for a name in both ``add_recipes`` and the
                directory or a bad path, ``KeyError`` for an unknown name.)
        """
        source = request.source
        assert isinstance(source, str)
        directory = request.scene_sound_directory
        package_root = request.package_root
        if is_path_reference(source):
            return self._path_entry(source, package_root=package_root)
        if source in self._recipes:
            self._refuse_name_in_both(source, directory=directory, package_root=package_root)
            return SoundEntry(name=source, legacy_recipe=self._recipes[source])
        if directory is None:
            message = f'no sound named {source!r}: the scene has no sound directory'
            raise KeyError(message)
        index = self._index_for(directory, package_root=package_root)
        location = index.resolve(source)
        if location.is_recorded_file:
            return SoundEntry(
                name=location.path.stem, file=location.path, source_path=location.path
            )
        return self._entry_in(index.load(location), location.table_name)

    def _refuse_name_in_both(
        self, name: str, *, directory: Path | None, package_root: Path | None
    ) -> None:
        """Refuse a recipe name the sound directory also defines (Ruling R2).

        Raises:
            SoundAssetError: Naming add_recipes and the directory's file.
        """
        if directory is None:
            return
        try:
            location = self._index_for(directory, package_root=package_root).resolve(name)
        except KeyError:
            return
        message = (
            f'the sound name {name!r} is defined in add_recipes and in {location.path}; rename one'
        )
        raise SoundAssetError(message)

    def _index_for(self, directory: Path, *, package_root: Path | None) -> ShortNameIndex:
        key = (directory, package_root)
        if key not in self._indexes:
            self._indexes[key] = ShortNameIndex(directory, package_root=package_root)
        return self._indexes[key]

    def _path_entry(self, source: str, *, package_root: Path | None) -> SoundEntry:
        """The entry a path reference names.

        Returns:
            The entry.

        Raises:
            SoundAssetError: For a TOML path without a sound name, a ``#`` on a recorded file, or
                a file that is neither a sound file nor a WAV/OGG.
        """
        file_part, _, table_name = source.partition(INSTRUMENT_SEPARATOR)
        path = Path(file_part)
        if package_root is not None and not path.is_absolute():
            path = package_root / path
        suffix = path.suffix.lower()
        if suffix == SOUND_FILE_SUFFIX:
            if not table_name:
                message = f'{source!r}: name a sound in the file, as {file_part}#<sound>'
                raise SoundAssetError(message)
            return self._entry_in(load_sound_file(path, package_root=package_root), table_name)
        if suffix in RECORDED_SOUND_SUFFIXES and not table_name:
            return SoundEntry(name=path.stem, file=path, source_path=path)
        message = (
            f'{source!r}: a sound path is a {SOUND_FILE_SUFFIX} sound file followed by '
            f'#<sound>, or a {" or ".join(RECORDED_SOUND_SUFFIXES)} file'
        )
        raise SoundAssetError(message)

    def _entry_in(self, sound_file: SoundFile, table_name: str | None) -> SoundEntry:
        """Register a loaded file's waves and take one of its sounds.

        Returns:
            The entry.

        Raises:
            KeyError: When the file defines no such sound. (Registering its waves can raise
                ``SoundAssetError``.)
        """
        self._register_waves(sound_file)
        assert table_name is not None
        if table_name not in sound_file.sounds:
            known = ', '.join(sound_file.sounds) or 'none'
            message = f'{sound_file.path} has no sound {table_name!r} (it defines: {known})'
            raise KeyError(message)
        return sound_file.sounds[table_name]

    def _register_waves(self, sound_file: SoundFile) -> None:
        """Register a file's ``[waves.*]`` before its instruments' specs are built.

        Registering an equal wave under a name again changes nothing.

        Raises:
            SoundAssetError: When a different wave is registered under the name already.
        """
        for wave_name, file_wave in sound_file.waves.items():
            if wave_name in self._waves:
                if self._waves[wave_name] == file_wave:
                    continue
                message = (
                    f'{sound_file.path}: waves.{wave_name}: a different wave is already '
                    f'registered under this name'
                )
                raise SoundAssetError(message)
            self._waves.register(wave_name, file_wave)

def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - mirrors the brief's signature
    self,
    *,
    cache: CacheMode,
    accountant: AudioAccountant,
    waves: WaveRegistry,
    tuning_source: Callable[[], Tuning],
    memory_limit_bytes: int = DEFAULT_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES,
    is_playing: Callable[[Sound], bool] = _nothing_plays,
) -> None:
    """Make a library.

    Args:
        cache: The cache mode.
        accountant: Where compile and decode times go.
        waves: The registry the wave tables of loaded sound files are registered in; it must
            be the current context's (``build_spec`` looks waves up there).
        tuning_source: Gives the tuning at each request.
        memory_limit_bytes: The bytes compiled sounds may retain (both sample arrays and the
            pygame sound) before the least recently played idle sounds go.
        is_playing: Says whether a sound is playing, so eviction spares it; the mixer
            supplies it. The default says nothing is playing.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For cache ``disk``, which arrives in M3.
    """
    if cache is CacheMode.DISK:
        raise ValueError(DISK_CACHE_MESSAGE)
    self._cache = cache
    self._accountant = accountant
    self._waves = waves
    self._tuning_source = tuning_source
    self._memory_limit_bytes = memory_limit_bytes
    self._is_playing = is_playing
    self._recipes: dict[str, SoundRecipe] = {}
    self._indexes: dict[tuple[Path, Path | None], ShortNameIndex] = {}
    # request -> identity key, so a repeated request is a dictionary hit (impl spec 6.2).
    # A sound file edited after its first request is not re-read: hot reload is M4.
    self._memo: dict[tuple[object, ...], str] = {}
    self._sounds: dict[str, Sound] = {}
    # The engine's own sounds this library handed out, by request (engine_sound)
    self._engine_sounds: dict[tuple[object, ...], Sound] = {}
    # Compiled sounds, least recently played first
    self._play_order: OrderedDict[str, Sound] = OrderedDict()
    self._hits = 0
    self._misses = 0
    self._compiles = 0

def compile_for_play(self, sound: Sound) -> Sound:
    """The sound to play: the same one under ``ram``, a fresh compile under ``none``.

    Under ``ram`` a sound the memory limit dropped is compiled again, in place, and counted.
    Playing makes a ``ram`` sound the most recently played.

    Args:
        sound: A sound from ``sound()``.

    The engine's own sounds (``engine_sound``) are always compiled: they play as they are.

    Returns:
        The compiled sound.
    """
    if sound.is_engine_sound:
        return sound
    if self._cache is CacheMode.NONE:
        fresh = self._compiled_copy(sound)
        # A later read of what the sound did not know yet reuses this play's compile
        sound.adopt_metadata(fresh)
        return fresh
    if not sound.is_compiled:
        self._misses += 1
        self._compile(sound)
        self._hold(sound)
    else:
        self._play_order.move_to_end(sound.identity_key)
    return sound

def engine_sound(
    self, instrument: Instrument, *, pitch: PitchLike | None, length: float | None
) -> Sound:
    """Get one of the engine's own sounds (the CRT power-on's): compiled once per process.

    The first request in the process compiles it here, counted, timed and attributed like
    any compile (a miss); every later one, in this library or any other context's, reuses
    the process's compiled samples (a hit) and compiles nothing. The cache mode and the
    memory limit do not apply (see the module docstring).

    Args:
        instrument: The instrument.
        pitch: Its pitch, or None for a noise.
        length: Seconds before the release.

    Returns:
        The library's own ``Sound`` over the shared samples, compiled.
    """
    sample_rate = mixer_sample_rate()
    tuning = self._tuning_source()
    request_key = (instrument, _freeze(pitch), length, sample_rate, tuning)
    handed_out = self._engine_sounds.get(request_key)
    if handed_out is not None:
        self._hits += 1
        return handed_out
    request = SoundRequest(
        source=instrument, scene_sound_directory=None, pitch=pitch, length=length
    )
    sound = self._build(request, sample_rate=sample_rate, tuning=tuning)
    sound.is_engine_sound = True
    compiled = ENGINE_SOUND_CACHE.compiled(sound.identity_key)
    if compiled is None:
        self._misses += 1
        self._compile(sound)
        ENGINE_SOUND_CACHE.keep(sound)
    else:
        self._hits += 1
        sound.install(
            samples_float=compiled.samples_float,
            samples_int16=compiled.samples_int16,
            peak=compiled.peak,
            sample_rate=compiled.sample_rate,
        )
    self._engine_sounds[request_key] = sound
    return sound

def sound(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8
    self,
    source: str | Instrument,
    *,
    scene_sound_directory: Path | None,
    package_root: Path | None = None,
    pitch: PitchLike | None = None,
    notes: str | Sequence[tuple[PitchLike, float]] | None = None,
    chord: Sequence[PitchLike] | None = None,
    length: float | None = None,
    transpose: float = 0.0,
    parameters: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
) -> Sound:
    """Get a sound; the first request for an identity compiles it. Getting never plays.

    Arguments given here replace the sound file entry's own: a ``pitch``, ``notes`` or
    ``chord`` replaces all three of the entry's, ``length`` replaces its length, and
    ``transpose`` is added to its transpose. A recorded or version 0 sound takes none of them.

    Args:
        source: A short name, a path (``'sounds/pickups.toml#coin'``, ``'sounds/slap.wav'``;
            relative to ``package_root``), or an ``Instrument``.
        scene_sound_directory: Where short names are looked up, or None.
        package_root: The game package's directory (paths and file references stay inside it).
        pitch: A pitch.
        notes: A melody.
        chord: Pitches played together.
        length: Seconds per note or chord before release.
        transpose: Semitones to shift notes or a chord.
        parameters: Live parameters; they identify the request but a baked sound ignores them
            (live sounds arrive in M2).

    Returns:
        The sound. Under cache ``none`` it holds no samples and nothing was rendered or
        decoded: what is not derived comes from one compile on its first read (see the
        module docstring).
    """
    request = SoundRequest(
        source=source,
        scene_sound_directory=scene_sound_directory,
        package_root=package_root,
        pitch=pitch,
        notes=notes,
        chord=chord,
        length=length,
        transpose=transpose,
        parameters=parameters,
    )
    sound, known = self._lookup(request)
    self._ensure_compiled(sound, known=known)
    return sound

Compile as many of the requests as fit in a time budget (for a loading scene).

At least one request compiles per call. It uses the same compile path as sound().

def warm(self, requests: Sequence[SoundRequest], *, budget_ms: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Compile as many of the requests as fit in a time budget (for a loading scene).

    At least one request compiles per call. It uses the same compile path as ``sound()``.

    Args:
        requests: The ``sound()`` argument sets to have compiled.
        budget_ms: The milliseconds to spend this call, or None for no limit.

    Returns:
        Progress from 0 to 1: the share of requests that are compiled.
    """
    if not requests:
        return 1.0
    started = clock.raw_counter_ns()
    compiled_this_call = 0
    done = 0
    for request in requests:
        sound, known = self._lookup(request)
        if self._cache is CacheMode.RAM and not sound.is_compiled:
            elapsed_ms = (clock.raw_counter_ns() - started) / 1_000_000
            if budget_ms is not None and compiled_this_call > 0 and elapsed_ms >= budget_ms:
                continue
            compiled_this_call += 1
        self._ensure_compiled(sound, known=known)
        done += 1
    return done / len(requests)

Compile a sound into itself: the one compile path (the library's, and offline renders').

A version 1 sound or instrument renders its spec, a version 0 recipe renders through today's renderer, and a recorded file is decoded. Nothing is timed or counted here: that is the caller's (SoundLibrary._compile).

Name Type Description Default sound Sound

def compile_sound(sound: Sound) -> None:
    """Compile a sound into itself: the one compile path (the library's, and offline renders').

    A version 1 sound or instrument renders its spec, a version 0 recipe renders through today's
    renderer, and a recorded file is decoded. Nothing is timed or counted here: that is the
    caller's (``SoundLibrary._compile``).

    Args:
        sound: The sound, compiled or not; its samples are replaced.
    """
    if sound.recorded_file is not None:
        _decode_recorded_file(sound)
    elif sound.spec is not None:
        rendered = render_sound(sound.spec)
        sound.install(
            samples_float=rendered.samples,
            samples_int16=to_pcm16(rendered.samples),
            peak=rendered.peak,
            sample_rate=sound.sample_rate,
        )
    else:
        assert sound.legacy_recipe is not None
        # Version 0 recipes compile through today's renderer, unchanged (impl spec 10.4)
        samples = sound.legacy_recipe.render(sample_rate=sound.sample_rate)
        sound.install(
            samples_float=samples,
            samples_int16=to_pcm16(samples),
            peak=float(np.max(np.abs(samples))) if len(samples) else 0.0,
            sample_rate=sound.sample_rate,
        )

docs.title: live
docs.text:
Real-time synth voices streamed through reserved mixer channels.

pygame has no audio callback, so each voice renders short chunks from the game loop and keeps one chunk queued behind the one playing (pygame holds one queued Sound per channel). The safety margin is the rest of the playing chunk minus one device buffer: about 88 ms at 44100 Hz with a 512-sample buffer and 100 ms chunks. A longer frame underruns; the voice restarts next update.

Channel facts this module relies on (pygame-ce 2.5.8): Channel.stop() and Channel.fadeout() start the queued sound, so fades are rendered into the samples and stop_now() calls stop() twice; set_reserved(n) reserves channels 0..n-1; set_num_channels(smaller) stops sounds on the removed channels, so the pool is reserved once at startup and never resized.

class LiveAudio:
    """Owns the live voice pool and applies the owner rules every frame."""

    def __init__(self, *, channel_indices: Sequence[int]) -> None:
        """Use the channels reserved by reserve_live_voice_pool()."""
        self._pool_size = len(channel_indices)
        self._free_channel_indices = list(channel_indices)
        self._voice_channels: dict[int, int] = {}  # id(voice) -> channel index
        self._voices: list[LiveVoice] = []
        self._unavailable_logged = False

    def create_voice(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments]
        self,
        *,
        owner: object,
        waveform: Waveform,
        frequency: float,
        volume: float = 0.5,
        low_pass_cutoff: float | None = None,
        tremolo: Tremolo | None = None,
        chunk_duration: float = DEFAULT_CHUNK_DURATION,
    ) -> LiveVoice:
        """Create a stopped voice on a free pool channel.

        Without a mixer the voice is a silent no-op (logged once). The channel returns to the
        pool once the voice has drained or been stopped (see update()).

        Returns:
            The voice; call start() to hear it.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If every pool channel is in use.

        """
        if pygame.mixer.get_init() is None:
            if not self._unavailable_logged:
                log.warning('Audio unavailable; live voices are silent')
                self._unavailable_logged = True
            return LiveVoice(
                channel=None,
                owner=owner,
                waveform=waveform,
                frequency=frequency,
                volume=volume,
                low_pass_cutoff=low_pass_cutoff,
                tremolo=tremolo,
                chunk_duration=chunk_duration,
                sample_rate=mixer_sample_rate(),
            )
        if not self._free_channel_indices:
            message = (
                f'All {self._pool_size} live voice channels are in use; raise --live-voice-pool'
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        channel_index = self._free_channel_indices.pop(0)
        voice = LiveVoice(
            channel=pygame.mixer.Channel(channel_index),
            owner=owner,
            waveform=waveform,
            frequency=frequency,
            volume=volume,
            low_pass_cutoff=low_pass_cutoff,
            tremolo=tremolo,
            chunk_duration=chunk_duration,
            sample_rate=mixer_sample_rate(),
        )
        self._voice_channels[id(voice)] = channel_index
        self._voices.append(voice)
        return voice

    @property
    def playing_voice_count(self) -> int:
        """Number of pool voices currently playing (see LiveVoice.is_playing)."""
        return sum(1 for voice in self._voices if voice.is_playing)

    def release_voice(self, voice: LiveVoice) -> None:
        """Silence a voice and return its channel to the pool."""
        voice.stop_now()
        if voice in self._voices:
            self._voices.remove(voice)
            self._free_channel_indices.append(self._voice_channels.pop(id(voice)))

    def update(
        self,
        *,
        active_scene: object | None,
        previous_scene: object | None,
        active_transitions: Sequence[object | None],
        paused_owners: Sequence[object] = (),
    ) -> None:
        """Play voices of active owners, pause the paused scenes', release the rest.

        Voices that are stopped, or faded out and drained, give their channel back first. A
        fading or draining voice keeps updating even when its owner is paused: stopping wins
        over pausing, so the fade is rendered instead of cut off.

        Args:
            active_scene: SceneManager.active_scene.
            previous_scene: SceneManager.previous_scene (what a PauseScene returns to).
            active_transitions: The running transition and the pending one (either may be
                None); a voice created for a ride is owned by its transition.
            paused_owners: Other owners whose voices pause rather than end: the live scene a
                playback scope stashed, the scene it returns to and the previous scene as it
                began (the game behind a pause screen; glitchygames/replay/playback.py), so
                their voices play on after it.

        """
        live_transitions = [transition for transition in active_transitions if transition]
        for voice in list(self._voices):
            if voice.is_finished:
                self.release_voice(voice)
                continue
            owner = voice.owner
            owner_is_live_transition = any(
                owner is live_transition for live_transition in live_transitions
            )
            if owner is active_scene or owner_is_live_transition:
                voice.resume()
                voice.update()
            elif owner is previous_scene or any(owner is paused for paused in paused_owners):
                if voice.state in {VoiceState.FADING, VoiceState.DRAINING}:
                    voice.update()
                else:
                    voice.pause()
            else:
                self.release_voice(voice)

            low_pass_cutoff=low_pass_cutoff,
            tremolo=tremolo,

    channel_index = self._free_channel_indices.pop(0)

class LiveVoice:
    """An oscillator whose parameters can change every frame."""

    def __init__(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments]
        self,
        *,
        channel: pygame.mixer.Channel | None,
        owner: object,
        waveform: Waveform,
        frequency: float,
        volume: float,
        low_pass_cutoff: float | None = None,
        tremolo: Tremolo | None = None,
        chunk_duration: float = DEFAULT_CHUNK_DURATION,
        sample_rate: int,
        random_source: np.random.Generator | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Create a stopped voice; channel None makes a silent no-op voice."""
        self._channel = channel
        self.owner = owner
        self._waveform = waveform
        self._sample_rate = sample_rate
        self._chunk_samples = sample_count(chunk_duration, sample_rate)
        self._random_source = (
            random_source if random_source is not None else numpy_stream(LIVE_RANDOM_STREAM)
        )
        self._target_frequency = frequency
        self._rendered_frequency = frequency
        self._target_volume = volume
        self._rendered_volume = volume
        self._target_cutoff = low_pass_cutoff
        self._rendered_cutoff = low_pass_cutoff
        self._tremolo = tremolo
        self._oscillator_phase = 0.0
        self._tremolo_phase = 0.0
        self._filter_history = np.zeros(DEFAULT_FILTER_TAPS - 1)
        self._fade_total_samples = 0
        self._fade_remaining_samples = 0
        self._state = VoiceState.IDLE

    # --- Parameters (ignored once the voice is stopping or stopped) ---

    @property
    def frequency(self) -> float:
        """Target frequency in Hz."""
        return self._target_frequency

    @frequency.setter
    def frequency(self, value: float) -> None:
        if self._accepts_changes:
            self._target_frequency = value

    @property
    def volume(self) -> float:
        """Target volume 0.0-1.0."""
        return self._target_volume

    @volume.setter
    def volume(self, value: float) -> None:
        if self._accepts_changes:
            self._target_volume = value

    @property
    def low_pass_cutoff(self) -> float | None:
        """Target low-pass cutoff in Hz (None: unfiltered)."""
        return self._target_cutoff

    @low_pass_cutoff.setter
    def low_pass_cutoff(self, value: float | None) -> None:
        if self._accepts_changes:
            self._target_cutoff = value

    @property
    def tremolo(self) -> Tremolo | None:
        """Tremolo settings (None: off)."""
        return self._tremolo

    @tremolo.setter
    def tremolo(self, value: Tremolo | None) -> None:
        if self._accepts_changes:
            self._tremolo = value

    @property
    def _accepts_changes(self) -> bool:
        return self._state in {VoiceState.IDLE, VoiceState.PLAYING, VoiceState.PAUSED}

    @property
    def state(self) -> VoiceState:
        """Current lifecycle state."""
        return self._state

    @property
    def is_playing(self) -> bool:
        """True from start() until the channel has drained (paused counts as playing)."""
        if self._channel is None:
            return False
        if self._state in {VoiceState.PLAYING, VoiceState.PAUSED, VoiceState.FADING}:
            return True
        return self._state is VoiceState.DRAINING and bool(self._channel.get_busy())

    @property
    def is_finished(self) -> bool:
        """True once the voice was stopped, or has faded out and its channel has drained."""
        if self._state is VoiceState.STOPPED:
            return True
        return (
            self._state is VoiceState.DRAINING
            and self._channel is not None
            and not self._channel.get_busy()
        )

    # --- Lifecycle ---

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Start playing (renders and plays the first chunk)."""
        if self._channel is None or self._state is not VoiceState.IDLE:
            return
        self._state = VoiceState.PLAYING
        self._channel.play(to_sound(self._render_chunk(), volume=1.0))

    def update(self) -> None:
        """Keep one chunk queued; call once per frame."""
        if self._channel is None or self._state not in {VoiceState.PLAYING, VoiceState.FADING}:
            return
        if not self._channel.get_busy():
            log.debug('Live voice underrun; restarting')
            self._channel.play(to_sound(self._render_chunk(), volume=1.0))
            return
        if self._channel.get_queue() is None:
            self._channel.queue(to_sound(self._render_chunk(), volume=1.0))

    def stop(self, *, fade_out: float = DEFAULT_FADE_OUT) -> None:
        """Fade to silence over fade_out seconds of rendered audio, then drain.

        LiveAudio.update() keeps rendering the fade and returns the channel to the pool once
        the voice has drained.
        """
        if self._channel is None or self._state not in {VoiceState.PLAYING, VoiceState.PAUSED}:
            return
        if self._state is VoiceState.PAUSED:
            self._channel.unpause()
        self._fade_total_samples = max(1, sample_count(fade_out, self._sample_rate))
        self._fade_remaining_samples = self._fade_total_samples
        self._state = VoiceState.FADING

    def stop_now(self) -> None:
        """Silence immediately: the first stop() starts the queued chunk, the second stops it."""
        if self._channel is not None and self._state is not VoiceState.STOPPED:
            self._channel.stop()
            self._channel.stop()
        self._state = VoiceState.STOPPED

    def pause(self) -> None:
        """Pause; the queued chunk is kept."""
        if self._channel is not None and self._state is VoiceState.PLAYING:
            self._channel.pause()
            self._state = VoiceState.PAUSED

    def resume(self) -> None:
        """Resume after pause()."""
        if self._channel is not None and self._state is VoiceState.PAUSED:
            self._channel.unpause()
            self._state = VoiceState.PLAYING

    # --- Rendering ---

    def _render_chunk(self) -> FloatArray:
        count = self._chunk_samples
        ramp = np.arange(1, count + 1) / count  # Reaches the target on the last sample
        frequencies = (
            self._rendered_frequency + (self._target_frequency - self._rendered_frequency) * ramp
        )
        volumes = self._rendered_volume + (self._target_volume - self._rendered_volume) * ramp
        self._rendered_frequency = self._target_frequency
        self._rendered_volume = self._target_volume

        raw, self._oscillator_phase = oscillator(
            self._waveform,
            frequencies,
            count / self._sample_rate,
            sample_rate=self._sample_rate,
            phase=self._oscillator_phase,
            random_source=self._random_source,
        )
        samples = self._filtered(raw=raw, ramp=ramp)
        self._filter_history = np.concatenate((self._filter_history, raw))[
            -(DEFAULT_FILTER_TAPS - 1) :
        ]
        if self._tremolo is not None:
            samples, self._tremolo_phase = tremolo(
                samples,
                self._tremolo.rate_hz,
                self._tremolo.depth,
                sample_rate=self._sample_rate,
                phase=self._tremolo_phase,
            )
        samples *= volumes
        if self._state is VoiceState.FADING:
            samples *= self._fade_gains(count)
        return samples

    def _filtered(self, *, raw: FloatArray, ramp: FloatArray) -> FloatArray:
        """Apply the low-pass, crossfading old and new outputs when the cutoff changes.

        Returns:
            The filtered chunk.

        """
        old_output = self._apply_cutoff(raw=raw, cutoff=self._rendered_cutoff)
        if self._target_cutoff == self._rendered_cutoff:
            return old_output
        new_output = self._apply_cutoff(raw=raw, cutoff=self._target_cutoff)
        self._rendered_cutoff = self._target_cutoff
        return old_output * (1.0 - ramp) + new_output * ramp

    def _apply_cutoff(self, *, raw: FloatArray, cutoff: float | None) -> FloatArray:
        if cutoff is None:
            return raw
        kernel = filter_kernel(
            cutoff,
            sample_rate=self._sample_rate,
            taps=DEFAULT_FILTER_TAPS,
            high_pass=False,
        )
        return apply_kernel(raw, kernel, history=self._filter_history)

    def _fade_gains(self, count: int) -> FloatArray:
        positions = self._fade_remaining_samples - np.arange(1, count + 1)
        gains = np.clip(positions / self._fade_total_samples, 0.0, 1.0)
        self._fade_remaining_samples -= count
        if self._fade_remaining_samples <= 0:
            self._state = VoiceState.DRAINING
        return gains

def reserve_live_voice_pool(pool_size: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Reserve channels for live voices; call once at startup before any sound plays.

    Grows the mixer by pool_size channels, then reserves channels 0..pool_size-1. Nothing is
    playing yet, so those channels are idle, and one-shot sounds keep the original count. A
    wrapper over ``voices.reserve_channels`` (no library channels) until the engine reserves
    the whole partition itself (impl spec 7.1; removed in M2).

    Returns:
        The reserved channel indices (empty without a mixer or with pool_size 0).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If pool_size is negative.

    """
    if pool_size < 0:
        message = f'pool_size must be >= 0, got {pool_size}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if pool_size == 0 or pygame.mixer.get_init() is None:
        return ()
    # A second engine in one process (a test run, a launcher) finds the pool it grew already
    # there: growing again would add channels per engine, and every set_num_channels reallocates
    # pygame's channel table while the audio thread may still finish a sound on it (BUGS.md
    # #145). So when a partition (this pool's, or reserve_channels' with library channels)
    # already reserves at least the pool, every reserved channel stays reserved and nothing
    # grows: lowering the reservation would hand the library's channels to Sound.play(). A
    # restarted mixer has no partition, so it grows again.
    channel_count = pygame.mixer.get_num_channels()
    already_reserved = reserved_channel_count()
    if already_reserved >= pool_size:
        library_channels = already_reserved - pool_size
        legacy_channels = channel_count - already_reserved
    else:
        library_channels = 0
        legacy_channels = channel_count
    partition = reserve_channels(
        live_pool=pool_size, library_channels=library_channels, legacy_channels=legacy_channels
    )
    return partition.live

Offline rendering: a sound, or a mix of sounds, written to a WAV file with no audio device.

render_to_file (impl spec 8 and 9; feature spec W9, 10 and AUD-FUNC-008) mixes compiled float buffers the way the device path plays them, but at exact sample offsets, and writes the result as a 16-bit PCM or 32-bit float WAV file. It never opens or touches the mixer: a sound not compiled yet (cache none) is compiled on a copy through the library's one compile path (library.compile_sound), so the render is the compiled buffer itself.

The rules:

  • Parity: a sound rendered alone (loops=1, no events) at its own rate is written exactly as its compiled int16 buffer: the mix of one event at offset 0 and volume 1 is its float buffer, converted as the library converts it (synth.to_pcm16).
  • Events: each OfflineEvent adds its sound's float buffer at round(seconds x rate), times its volume. The output is stereo when any event pans or stems is asked for, and then every event (the sound itself included, at the centre) takes the voices' constant-power pan law (voices.constant_power_gains, impl spec 7.2); otherwise it is mono.
  • Loops: the sound plays loops times back to back, as the device replays a baked buffer.
  • Tail (R37): a sound rendered alone (no events, any loops) is never cut: its nominal end is its buffer's end, so the file is the compiled buffer bit for bit for every sound (AUD-FUNC-008). In a mix with events, each buffer's nominal end is an instrument sound's last note release (where its held part ends) or any other sound's buffer end, and the render stops once the output has stayed below -90 dBFS for 100 ms after the last of them, keeping those 100 ms, or tail_seconds after it if that is sooner. A quiet stretch the buffers end before 100 ms stops nothing: the whole mix is written.
  • Clipping: the report gives the peak and the number of samples beyond full scale. A float32 file keeps them; an int16 file clips them (never silently: they are counted).
  • Stems: with stems=True each bus's events (by the sound's playback bus) are also written to <stem>.<bus><suffix> beside the mix, the same length and format.

Live sounds (and so parameter_timeline) arrive in M2.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OfflineEvent:
    """A sound placed in an offline mix.

    Attributes:
        seconds: When it starts, from the mix's start (at ``round(seconds x rate)``).
        sound: The sound (compiled or not).
        volume: Its gain, 0 or more (not the sound file's playback default: given here).
        pan: -1 (left) to 1 (right); any pan but 0 makes the output stereo.
    """

    seconds: float
    sound: Sound
    volume: float = 1.0
    pan: float = 0.0

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Refuse a time before the start, a negative volume or a pan outside -1..1.

        Raises:
            ValueError: Naming the value.
        """
        if not (math.isfinite(self.seconds) and self.seconds >= 0.0):
            message = f'an event starts at 0 seconds or later, got {self.seconds}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if not self.volume >= 0.0:
            message = f'an event volume is 0 or more, got {self.volume}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if not PAN_LOWEST <= self.pan <= PAN_HIGHEST:
            message = f'pan must be between {PAN_LOWEST} and {PAN_HIGHEST}, got {self.pan}'
            raise ValueError(message)

def render_to_file(  # ruff: ignore[too-many-arguments] - impl spec 8's signature
    sound: Sound,
    path: Path | str,
    *,
    sample_rate: int | None = None,
    sample_format: str = 'int16',
    loops: int = 1,
    tail_seconds: float | None = None,
    stems: bool = False,
    parameter_timeline: Mapping[str, Sequence[tuple[float, float]]] | None = None,
    events: Sequence[OfflineEvent] = (),
) -> RenderReport:
    """Render a sound (and any events) to a WAV file, opening no audio device.

    Args:
        sound: The sound, at offset 0, centred, at volume 1.
        path: The WAV file to write (written aside, then moved into place).
        sample_rate: The rate to render at (default: the sound's). Sounds at another rate are
            compiled at this one (a recorded file is resampled linearly).
        sample_format: ``'int16'`` (PCM) or ``'float32'`` (IEEE float, overs kept).
        loops: How many times the sound plays, back to back.
        tail_seconds: The most the render runs past the last nominal end, or None for the
            -90 dBFS rule alone (alone, a sound's nominal end is its buffer's end, so neither
            cuts it).
        stems: Also write each bus's events to a file of its own (the output is then stereo).
        parameter_timeline: Live parameters over time; must be None until live sounds (M2).
        events: More sounds placed in the mix.

    Returns:
        What was written.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For a parameter timeline (live sounds arrive in M2) or an argument out of
            its range; nothing is written. An unwritable path raises ``OSError`` (no partial file
            is left behind).
    """
    if parameter_timeline is not None:
        raise ValueError(LIVE_SOUNDS_MESSAGE)
    _check_arguments(
        sample_rate=sample_rate, sample_format=sample_format, loops=loops, tail_seconds=tail_seconds
    )
    destination = Path(path)
    rate = sound.sample_rate if sample_rate is None else sample_rate
    placed = _placed_buffers(sound, rate=rate, loops=loops, events=events)
    stereo = stems or any(abs(event.pan) > 0.0 for event in events)
    total = max(entry.offset + len(entry.samples) for entry in placed)
    mix = _mixed(placed, total=total, stereo=stereo)
    end = _render_end(
        mix,
        nominal_end=max(entry.nominal_end for entry in placed),
        sample_rate=rate,
        tail_seconds=tail_seconds,
    )
    mix = mix[:end]
    _write_wave(destination, mix, sample_rate=rate, sample_format=sample_format)
    stem_paths: list[Path] = []
    if stems:
        for bus in sorted({entry.bus for entry in placed}):
            stem_path = destination.with_name(f'{destination.stem}.{bus}{destination.suffix}')
            on_the_bus = [entry for entry in placed if entry.bus == bus]
            stem = _mixed(on_the_bus, total=total, stereo=True)[:end]
            _write_wave(stem_path, stem, sample_rate=rate, sample_format=sample_format)
            stem_paths.append(stem_path)
    return RenderReport(
        path=destination,
        frames=len(mix),
        peak=float(np.max(np.abs(mix), initial=0.0)),
        clip_count=int(np.count_nonzero(np.abs(mix) > FULL_SCALE)),
        stem_paths=tuple(stem_paths),
    )

docs.title: pitch
docs.text:
Pitch types: notes, hertz, MIDI numbers and scale steps, and the one conversion to hertz.

Three explicit types name a pitch (Note('A4'), Hz(440.0), Midi(69)), so a bare int is never guessed at: 60 could mean middle C or a 60 Hz hum. Anywhere a pitch is accepted, a string is a note name and a float is hertz. resolve_pitch is the single point that turns any of them into hertz.

Twelve-tone equal temperament is used: frequency = a4 * 2 ** ((midi_number - 69) / 12), the standard MIDI tuning relation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MIDI_tuning_standard).

class Hz(float):
    """A frequency in hertz."""

    __slots__ = ()

    def times(self, ratio: float) -> Hz:
        """Multiply the frequency by a ratio.

        Args:
            ratio: The factor; 1.5 is a perfect fifth in just intonation.

        Returns:
            The scaled frequency.

        """
        return Hz(float(self) * ratio)

    def octave_up(self, octaves: int = 1) -> Hz:
        """Raise the frequency by whole octaves.

        Args:
            octaves: The number of octaves.

        Returns:
            The frequency, doubled once per octave.

        """
        return self.times(2.0**octaves)

    def octave_down(self, octaves: int = 1) -> Hz:
        """Lower the frequency by whole octaves.

        Args:
            octaves: The number of octaves.

        Returns:
            The frequency, halved once per octave.

        """
        return self.times(2.0**-octaves)

class Midi(int):
    """A MIDI note number from 0 to 127; 60 is middle C and 69 is A4."""

    __slots__ = ()

    def __new__(cls, number: int) -> Self:
        """Create a MIDI note number.

        Args:
            number: The note number, 0 to 127.

        Returns:
            The validated MIDI note number.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the number is not an int or is outside 0 to 127.

        """
        if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, int):  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance] - callers may pass anything at runtime
            message = f'Midi needs an int from 0 to 127, got {number!r}'
            raise ValueError(message)  # ruff: ignore[type-check-without-type-error] - contract is ValueError
        if not MIDI_LOWEST <= number <= MIDI_HIGHEST:
            message = f'Midi must be from {MIDI_LOWEST} to {MIDI_HIGHEST}, got {number}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        return super().__new__(cls, number)

    def to_hz(self, *, tuning: Tuning | None = None) -> Hz:
        """Convert to hertz.

        Args:
            tuning: The tuning to use; A4 = 440 Hz when omitted.

        Returns:
            The frequency in hertz.

        """
        return (tuning or Tuning()).hertz_for_midi_number(int(self))

docs.text:
A note name such as 'C4', 'F#4' or 'Bb3', optionally shifted by cents.

C4 is middle C and A4 is 440 Hz (at the default tuning). Shifts made by up, down and detune stay symbolic: the tuning is applied only when the note is converted to hertz, so a detuned note follows the engine's tuning. Notes compare and hash by pitch and offset, so 'Bb3' equals 'A#3'.

class Note:
    """A note name such as 'C4', 'F#4' or 'Bb3', optionally shifted by cents.

    C4 is middle C and A4 is 440 Hz (at the default tuning). Shifts made by up, down and
    detune stay symbolic: the tuning is applied only when the note is converted to hertz, so
    a detuned note follows the engine's tuning. Notes compare and hash by pitch and offset, so
    'Bb3' equals 'A#3'.
    """

    __slots__ = ('_cents', '_midi_number', '_name')

    def __init__(self, name: str, *, cents: float = 0.0) -> None:
        """Parse a note name.

        Args:
            name: A letter A-G, an optional '#' or 'b', then an octave digit (optionally
                negative, so 'C-1' is MIDI 0).
            cents: An offset from the named note in hundredths of a semitone.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the name is not a valid note name or cents is not finite.

        """
        match = NOTE_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(name) if isinstance(name, str) else None  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance] - callers may pass anything at runtime
        if match is None:
            message = f"Invalid note name {name!r}; expected e.g. 'C4', 'F#4' or 'Bb3'"
            raise ValueError(message)
        if not math.isfinite(cents):
            message = f'Note cents must be finite, got {cents!r}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        letter, accidental, octave = match.groups()
        self._name: str = name
        self._cents: float = float(cents)
        self._midi_number: int = (
            SEMITONES_PER_OCTAVE * (int(octave) + 1)
            + LETTER_SEMITONES[letter]
            + ACCIDENTAL_SEMITONES[accidental]
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_midi_number(cls, midi_number: int, *, cents: float = 0.0) -> Note:
        """Build the note (spelled with sharps) for a MIDI note number.

        Args:
            midi_number: The note number; 60 is C4. It may lie outside 0 to 127, as long as
                the octave stays a single digit.
            cents: An offset from the note in hundredths of a semitone.

        Returns:
            The note.

        """
        octave, pitch_class = divmod(midi_number, SEMITONES_PER_OCTAVE)
        return cls(f'{SHARP_NAMES[pitch_class]}{octave - 1}', cents=cents)

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The name this note was created with."""
        return self._name

    @property
    def midi_number(self) -> int:
        """The MIDI note number of the named note, before any cents offset."""
        return self._midi_number

    @property
    def cents(self) -> float:
        """The offset from the named note in cents; 0.0 for a plain note."""
        return self._cents

    def up(self, *, semitones: float = 0.0, cents: float = 0.0) -> Note:
        """Move up in pitch, staying relative to whatever tuning is applied later.

        Args:
            semitones: Semitones to move up.
            cents: Hundredths of a semitone to move up.

        Returns:
            A note; a plain named note when the total shift is a whole number of semitones,
            otherwise the nearest named note carrying the remaining cents offset.

        """
        total_cents = self._cents + semitones * CENTS_PER_SEMITONE + cents
        whole_semitones = round(total_cents / CENTS_PER_SEMITONE)
        remaining_cents = total_cents - whole_semitones * CENTS_PER_SEMITONE
        if math.isclose(remaining_cents, 0.0, abs_tol=CENTS_TOLERANCE):
            remaining_cents = 0.0
        return Note.from_midi_number(
            self._midi_number + whole_semitones,
            cents=remaining_cents,
        )

    def down(self, *, semitones: float = 0.0, cents: float = 0.0) -> Note:
        """Move down in pitch.

        Args:
            semitones: Semitones to move down.
            cents: Hundredths of a semitone to move down.

        Returns:
            The lowered note; see up.

        """
        return self.up(semitones=-semitones, cents=-cents)

    def detune(self, *, cents: float) -> Note:
        """Shift slightly sharp (positive) or flat (negative).

        Args:
            cents: Hundredths of a semitone.

        Returns:
            The detuned note; see up.

        """
        return self.up(cents=cents)

    def to_hz(self, *, tuning: Tuning | None = None) -> Hz:
        """Convert to hertz: the tuning is applied first, then the cents offset.

        Args:
            tuning: The tuning to use; A4 = 440 Hz when omitted.

        Returns:
            The frequency in hertz.

        """
        return (tuning or Tuning()).hertz_for_midi_number(
            self._midi_number + self._cents / CENTS_PER_SEMITONE,
        )

    @override
    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        """Compare by pitch and cents offset.

        Returns:
            True if other is a Note of the same pitch and offset.

        """
        if not isinstance(other, Note):
            return NotImplemented
        return (self._midi_number, self._cents) == (other._midi_number, other._cents)

    @override
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        """Hash by pitch and cents offset.

        Returns:
            The hash of the MIDI note number and offset.

        """
        return hash(('Note', self._midi_number, self._cents))

    @override
    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """Return a constructor-style representation.

        Returns:
            The representation.

        """
        if self._cents:
            return f'Note({self._name!r}, cents={self._cents!r})'
        return f'Note({self._name!r})'

    match = NOTE_NAME_PATTERN.fullmatch(name) if isinstance(name, str) else None  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance] - callers may pass anything at runtime
    if match is None:
        message = f"Invalid note name {name!r}; expected e.g. 'C4', 'F#4' or 'Bb3'"
        raise ValueError(message)
    if not math.isfinite(cents):
        message = f'Note cents must be finite, got {cents!r}'
        raise ValueError(message)
    letter, accidental, octave = match.groups()
    self._name: str = name
    self._cents: float = float(cents)
    self._midi_number: int = (
        SEMITONES_PER_OCTAVE * (int(octave) + 1)
        + LETTER_SEMITONES[letter]
        + ACCIDENTAL_SEMITONES[accidental]
    )

def up(self, *, semitones: float = 0.0, cents: float = 0.0) -> Note:
    """Move up in pitch, staying relative to whatever tuning is applied later.

    Args:
        semitones: Semitones to move up.
        cents: Hundredths of a semitone to move up.

    Returns:
        A note; a plain named note when the total shift is a whole number of semitones,
        otherwise the nearest named note carrying the remaining cents offset.

    """
    total_cents = self._cents + semitones * CENTS_PER_SEMITONE + cents
    whole_semitones = round(total_cents / CENTS_PER_SEMITONE)
    remaining_cents = total_cents - whole_semitones * CENTS_PER_SEMITONE
    if math.isclose(remaining_cents, 0.0, abs_tol=CENTS_TOLERANCE):
        remaining_cents = 0.0
    return Note.from_midi_number(
        self._midi_number + whole_semitones,
        cents=remaining_cents,
    )

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scale:
    """A scale from a root pitch class, played in numbered steps.

    Step 0 is the root in octave 4, and a step past the top wraps into the next octave.

    Attributes:
        root: The root pitch class, e.g. 'C', 'F#' or 'Bb'.
        kind: One of the names in SCALE_INTERVALS.

    """

    root: str
    kind: str

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate the root and kind.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the root or the kind is not recognised.

        """
        if not isinstance(self.root, str) or PITCH_CLASS_PATTERN.fullmatch(self.root) is None:  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance] - callers may pass anything at runtime
            message = f"Invalid scale root {self.root!r}; expected e.g. 'C', 'F#' or 'Bb'"
            raise ValueError(message)
        if self.kind not in SCALE_INTERVALS:
            message = f'Unknown scale {self.kind!r}; expected one of {sorted(SCALE_INTERVALS)}'
            raise ValueError(message)

    def step(self, number: int) -> Note:
        """Return the note at a numbered step.

        Args:
            number: The step; 0 is the root, negative steps go below it.

        Returns:
            The note.

        """
        intervals = SCALE_INTERVALS[self.kind]
        octaves, index = divmod(number, len(intervals))
        root_note = Note(f'{self.root}{DEFAULT_SCALE_ROOT_OCTAVE}')
        return Note.from_midi_number(
            root_note.midi_number + SEMITONES_PER_OCTAVE * octaves + intervals[index],
        )

def resolve_pitch(pitch: PitchLike, *, tuning: Tuning, sample_rate: int = 44100) -> Hz:
    """Convert any pitch to hertz; the one conversion point.

    Args:
        pitch: A Note, Hz, Midi, ScaleStep, a note-name string, or a float (hertz).
        tuning: The tuning for note names, MIDI numbers and scale steps.
        sample_rate: The sample rate, for the Nyquist check.

    Returns:
        The frequency in hertz.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For a bare int (use Midi or Hz), a bad note name, or a frequency that is
            not finite, is negative or is above Nyquist.
        TypeError: For any other type.

    """
    if isinstance(pitch, bool) or (isinstance(pitch, int) and not isinstance(pitch, Midi)):
        message = (
            f'A bare int is ambiguous: {pitch!r} could be a MIDI note or a frequency. '
            f'Use Midi({pitch}) or Hz({pitch}).'
        )
        raise ValueError(message)  # ruff: ignore[type-check-without-type-error] - contract is ValueError
    if isinstance(pitch, ScaleStep):
        pitch = pitch.to_note()
    if isinstance(pitch, str):
        pitch = Note(pitch)
    if isinstance(pitch, Note | Midi):
        return _validated_hertz(pitch.to_hz(tuning=tuning), sample_rate=sample_rate)
    if isinstance(pitch, float):  # pyright: ignore[reportUnnecessaryIsInstance] - callers may pass anything at runtime
        return _validated_hertz(float(pitch), sample_rate=sample_rate)
    message = f'Cannot use {pitch!r} of type {type(pitch).__name__} as a pitch'
    raise TypeError(message)

class SoundBank:
    """Plays recipes by name, rendering each on first use."""

    def __init__(self, recipes: Iterable[SoundRecipe]) -> None:
        """Index the recipes by name.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If two recipes share a name.

        """
        self._recipes: dict[str, SoundRecipe] = {}
        for recipe in recipes:
            if recipe.name in self._recipes:
                message = f'duplicate sound recipe name {recipe.name!r}'
                raise ValueError(message)
            self._recipes[recipe.name] = recipe
        self._sounds: dict[tuple[str, int], pygame.mixer.Sound] = {}
        self._unavailable_logged = False

    def play(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Play a sound; a no-op (logged once) when audio is unavailable.

        Raises:
            KeyError: If no recipe has this name.

        """
        recipe = self._recipes.get(name)
        if recipe is None:
            message = f'no sound recipe named {name!r}'
            raise KeyError(message)
        sound = self._render_cached(recipe)
        if sound is None:
            return
        # The pygame stub types Sound.play() as returning a Channel, but at runtime it returns
        # None when no unreserved channel is free. A Channel is always truthy, so test truthiness.
        if not sound.play():
            log.debug('No free mixer channel for sound %r', name)

    def prerender(self) -> None:
        """Render and cache every recipe at the mixer rate, so no sound renders mid-frame.

        A no-op (logged once, like play) when audio is unavailable.
        """
        for recipe in self._recipes.values():
            if self._render_cached(recipe) is None:
                return

    def _render_cached(self, recipe: SoundRecipe) -> pygame.mixer.Sound | None:
        """Return the recipe's Sound for the current mixer rate, rendering it on first use.

        Returns:
            The cached Sound, or None when audio is unavailable (logged once).

        """
        cache_key = (recipe.name, mixer_sample_rate())
        if cache_key not in self._sounds:
            try:
                self._sounds[cache_key] = to_sound(recipe.render(), volume=recipe.volume)
            except AudioUnavailableError:
                if not self._unavailable_logged:
                    log.warning('Audio unavailable; sound effects are silent')
                    self._unavailable_logged = True
                return None
        return self._sounds[cache_key]

@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class SoundRecipe:
    """A named sound made of tones."""

    name: str
    tones: tuple[Tone, ...]
    volume: float = 0.5
    peak: float = 0.9

    def frame_count(self, *, sample_rate: int) -> int:
        """How many frames ``render`` gives at a rate, without rendering (cache ``none``'s length).

        ``mix`` sizes its result with ``mixed_frame_count`` from each tone's start
        (``sample_count(offset)``) and length (``Tone.frame_count``); normalizing keeps it.

        Returns:
            The frame count.
        """
        return mixed_frame_count(
            (sample_count(tone.offset, sample_rate), tone.frame_count(sample_rate=sample_rate))
            for tone in self.tones
        )

    def render(self, *, sample_rate: int | None = None) -> FloatArray:
        """Mix every tone at its offset and normalize to peak.

        Returns:
            The sound's samples.

        """
        rate = mixer_sample_rate() if sample_rate is None else sample_rate
        layers = [(tone.render(sample_rate=rate), tone.offset) for tone in self.tones]
        return normalize(mix(*layers, sample_rate=rate), peak=self.peak)

    def to_sound(self) -> pygame.mixer.Sound:
        """Render at the mixer's rate and wrap as a pygame Sound.

        Returns:
            The sound.

        """
        return to_sound(self.render(), volume=self.volume)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Serialize to plain data (TOML/JSON friendly).

        Returns:
            The recipe as a dict (without its name, which is the key it is stored under).

        """
        return {
            'volume': self.volume,
            'peak': self.peak,
            'tones': [_tone_to_dict(tone) for tone in self.tones],
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, name: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> SoundRecipe:
        """Build a recipe from to_dict() output.

        Returns:
            The recipe.

        Raises:
            SoundRecipeError: Naming the recipe and field that is invalid.

        """
        tones: list[Tone] = []

@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tone:
    """One layer of a sound."""

    waveform: Waveform
    start_frequency: float
    duration: float
    envelope: Envelope
    end_frequency: float | None = None  # None: constant pitch
    easing: str = 'linear'
    volume: float = 1.0
    offset: float = 0.0
    low_pass_cutoff: float | None = None
    high_pass_cutoff: float | None = None
    distortion: float | None = None
    tremolo: Tremolo | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Validate the settings.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If duration is not positive or offset/volume are negative.

        """
        if self.duration <= 0.0:
            message = f'duration must be > 0, got {self.duration}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if self.offset < 0.0:
            message = f'offset must be >= 0, got {self.offset}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if self.volume < 0.0:
            message = f'volume must be >= 0, got {self.volume}'
            raise ValueError(message)

    def frame_count(self, *, sample_rate: int) -> int:
        """How many frames ``render`` gives, without rendering.

        The oscillator makes ``sample_count(duration)`` frames, and every later stage
        (distortion, filters, tremolo, envelope, volume) keeps the count.

        Returns:
            The frame count.
        """
        return sample_count(self.duration, sample_rate)

    def render(self, *, sample_rate: int) -> FloatArray:
        """Render this tone (without its offset).

        Returns:
            The tone's samples.

        """
        if self.waveform is Waveform.NOISE or self.end_frequency is None:
            frequency: float | FloatArray = self.start_frequency
        else:
            frequency = frequency_curve(
                self.start_frequency,
                self.end_frequency,
                self.duration,
                easing=self.easing,
                sample_rate=sample_rate,
            )
        samples, _ = oscillator(
            self.waveform,
            frequency,
            self.duration,
            sample_rate=sample_rate,
            random_source=np.random.default_rng(RECIPE_NOISE_SEED),
        )
        if self.distortion is not None:
            samples = distort(samples, self.distortion)
        if self.low_pass_cutoff is not None:
            samples = low_pass(samples, self.low_pass_cutoff, sample_rate=sample_rate)
        if self.high_pass_cutoff is not None:
            samples = high_pass(samples, self.high_pass_cutoff, sample_rate=sample_rate)
        if self.tremolo is not None:
            samples, _ = tremolo(
                samples,
                self.tremolo.rate_hz,
                self.tremolo.depth,
                sample_rate=sample_rate,
            )
        return apply_envelope(samples, self.envelope, sample_rate=sample_rate) * self.volume

docs.title: render
docs.text:
The M1 renderer: a SoundSpec in, mono float64 samples out (impl spec 5).

render_sound is pure: the same spec always gives the same samples, and it reads no mixer, clock or engine random stream (noise is seeded from the spec, impl spec 6.3).

Each note is rendered on its own: every source renders its oscillator or noise for the note's held length plus the amplifier's release, then its own filter, its own envelope and its level; the sources are summed; then come the sound's filter, the amplifier envelope and drive. Notes are summed at round(start_seconds * sample_rate). Then the sum must be finite, and last come the boundary de-click fades, the optional normalization to -1 dBFS and the clip to full scale, with the peak reported.

Filters and the 2x anti-alias kernel are applied centred (zero phase): a compiled sound is rendered whole, so the kernels' delay is taken back and nothing is shifted in time.
