@classmethod
def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Add font options to the argument parser.

    Args:
        parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

    Returns:
        argparse.ArgumentParser

    """
    group = parser.add_argument_group('Font Options')

    group.add_argument(
        '--font-name',
        default=DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
        help=(
            f'Font to use (default: the bundled {DEFAULT_FONT_NAME}; the bundled variants are '
            "Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any other name is looked up among the system's "
            'fonts)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-size',
        type=int,
        default=14,
        help=(
            'size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own '
            '(default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    # The style options apply to every font the manager loads, unless the font's own
    # configuration gives a value (BUGS.md #210)
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-bold',
        action='store_true',
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_bold'],
        help='draw text bold',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-italic',
        action='store_true',
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_italic'],
        help='draw text italic',
    )
    # On by default (pygame.freetype's own default), so --no-font-antialias turns it off
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-antialias',
        action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_antialias'],
        # Every text the engine, its games and its tools draw follows it, except the
        # channel 3 screen's digit (backgrounds.py), hard-edged on purpose
        help='antialias text (default: %(default)s)',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-dpi',
        type=int,
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_dpi'],
        help=(
            'the resolution, in dots per inch, font sizes are scaled at (a size is in pixels '
            f'at {BASE_FONT_DPI}) (default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-system',
        choices=['pygame', 'freetype'],
        default='freetype',
        help='Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)',
    )

    return parser

@classmethod
def compare_font_systems(
    cls,
    text: str = 'Hello World',
    size: int = 24,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Compare both font systems side by side.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to render for comparison.
        size (int): Font size for comparison.

    Returns:
        dict: Information about both font systems.

    """
    config: dict[str, Any] = {'font_size': size}

    # Get pygame.font. Its render takes (text, antialias, color) positionally, not
    # freetype's fgcolor keyword (which raised TypeError on a real pygame.font.Font).
    pygame_font = cast('pygame.font.Font', cls.get_font('pygame', config))
    pygame_surface: pygame.Surface = pygame_font.render(text, cls.antialias(), (255, 255, 255))

    # Get pygame.freetype
    freetype_font = cls.get_font('freetype', config)
    freetype_render_result = freetype_font.render(text, fgcolor=(255, 255, 255))
    freetype_surface: pygame.Surface = (
        freetype_render_result[0]
        if isinstance(freetype_render_result, tuple)
        else freetype_render_result
    )

    return {
        'pygame': {
            'font': pygame_font,
            'surface': pygame_surface,
            'size': pygame_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.font.Font',
        },
        'freetype': {
            'font': freetype_font,
            'surface': freetype_surface,
            'size': freetype_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.freetype.Font',

    }

@classmethod
def font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
    """Return a font object.

    If the font requested can't be found then bitstream_vera will be loaded instead.

    Note that if you are trying to package your game with pyinstaller, you'll need to bundle
    your game's fonts with the pyinstaller invocation.  Make sure you have distribution
    rights to the fonts you're including with your game.

    bitstream_vera is a permissively licensed font that can be used with your game.

    Args:
        font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

    Returns:
        GameFont

    """
    settings = cls.font_settings(font_config)
    cache_key = settings.cache_key

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    log.info('Loading Font: %s', settings.name)
    log.info('Font Size: %s', settings.size)

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=settings.name)
    if font_path is not None:
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
            'GameFont', _styled_freetype_font(font_path=font_path, settings=settings)
        )
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        # SysFont picks a bold or italic face when the system has one and asks the
        # constructor to embolden or slant only when it has none
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.SysFont(
                name=settings.name,
                size=settings.size,
                bold=settings.bold,
                italic=settings.italic,
                constructor=_freetype_font_constructor(settings=settings),
            ),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Note: Not sure why but pygame.freetype.SysFont doesn't
        # seem to work with pyinstaller packaged games.
        log.info('Loading Font: Built-In')

        # BUG: pygame's documentation claims that passing None as the font name
        # will load the default font, but this raises TypeError ("not a file object")
        # in PyInstaller-packaged games. Load the bundled Vera.ttf instead.
        # (BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY says where bitmappy.spec bundles it.) The fallback keeps
        # the requested size (it used to load at 12 whatever was asked for).
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            _styled_freetype_font(
                font_path=BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES['vera'],
                settings=settings,
            ),
        )

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def font_settings(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> FontSettings:
    """Return the settings a font configuration asks for, without changing the configuration.

    An empty or missing configuration asks for the engine's default font (the current
    context's font options). A name or size the configuration leaves out gets
    DEFAULT_FONT_NAME or DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE; a style option it leaves out gets the engine's
    option, then FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS, so --font-bold and the rest reach every font.

    Args:
        font_config: The font configuration.

    Returns:
        The font's settings.

    """
    font_options = _font_options()
    source = font_config or font_options

    def option(key: str, *, default: bool | int) -> bool | int:
        for options in (source, font_options):
            value = options.get(key)
            if value is not None:
                return value
        return default

    return FontSettings(
        name=source.get('font_name') or DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
        size=source.get('font_size') or DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE,
        bold=bool(option('font_bold', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_bold'])),
        italic=bool(option('font_italic', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_italic'])),
        antialias=bool(option('font_antialias', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_antialias'])),
        dpi=int(option('font_dpi', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_dpi'])),
    )

@classmethod
def get_font(
    cls,
    font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype'] | None = None,
    font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> GameFont:
    """Get a font object, choosing between pygame.font and pygame.freetype.

    Args:
        font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype". If None, use the default preference.
        font_config: The font configuration.

    Returns:
        pygame.font.Font | pygame.freetype.Font: The requested font object.

    """
    if font_system is None:
        # Default to freetype
        use_freetype: bool = bool(_font_options().get('use_freetype', True))
    else:
        use_freetype = font_system == 'freetype'

    # Try freetype first, fall back to pygame if it fails
    if use_freetype:
        try:
            return cls.font(font_config)
        except (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) as e:
            log.info('Freetype font failed, falling back to pygame: %s', e)
            return cls.pygame_font(font_config)
    else:
        return cls.pygame_font(font_config)

@classmethod
def pygame_font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
    """Return a regular pygame font object for compatibility with UI components.

    Args:
        font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

    Returns:
        GameFont: A regular pygame font object.

    """
    settings = cls.font_settings(font_config)
    cache_key = f'pygame_{settings.cache_key}'

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=settings.name)
    if font_path is not None:
        pygame_font = pygame.font.Font(font_path, settings.pygame_font_size)
        pygame_font.set_bold(settings.bold)
        pygame_font.set_italic(settings.italic)
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast('GameFont', pygame_font)
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        # SysFont picks a bold or italic face when the system has one, and emboldens or
        # slants the font itself when it has none
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.font.SysFont(
                settings.name,
                settings.pygame_font_size,
                bold=settings.bold,
                italic=settings.italic,
            ),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Fall back to default font
        fallback_font = pygame.font.Font(None, settings.pygame_font_size)
        fallback_font.set_bold(settings.bold)
        fallback_font.set_italic(settings.italic)
        loaded_font = cast('GameFont', fallback_font)

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def release_shared_instances(cls) -> None:
    """Forget this context's shared instances, so each class's next construction is new.

    ``GameEngine`` calls it before it makes its event managers: a new engine run builds
    managers of its own (opening devices through its own doors), not the earlier run's. It
    releases this context's only: a game in another engine context keeps its managers.
    """
    current_context().value(slot=SHARED_INSTANCES_SLOT).clear()

class FontManager(ResourceManager, metaclass=ReadOnlyViews):
    """A font manager for handling fonts in the game.

    Supports both pygame.font and pygame.freetype font systems:

    Examples:
        # Use default font system (pygame.font)
        font = FontManager.get_font()

        # Force pygame.font
        font = FontManager.get_font(font_system='pygame')

        # Force pygame.freetype
        font = FontManager.get_font(font_system='freetype')

        # Change the current engine context's default system
        FontManager.set_font_system(font_system='freetype')
        font = FontManager.get_font()  # Now uses freetype by default

        # Check current system
        system = FontManager.get_font_system()  # Returns "pygame" or "freetype"

    """

    # The current context's font options (audit C13), read on the class or on a manager; a
    # read-only view of the context's dict, which readers may change in place
    OPTIONS = ReadOnlyView[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]](
        read_current=lambda _owner: _font_options(),
        read_own=lambda _manager: _font_options(),
        write_instead=(
            "the current context's font options in place (FontManager.OPTIONS.update(...)) "
            'or FontManager.set_font_system(...)'
        ),
    )
    RENDER_CACHE: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {}
    _font_cache: ClassVar[dict[str, GameFont]] = {}

    class FontProxy(FontEvents, ResourceManager):
        """A font proxy."""

        # A proxy belongs to its manager: each construction is a new one (ResourceManager)
        SHARES_INSTANCE: ClassVar[bool] = False

        def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
            """Initialize the font proxy.

            Args:
                game (object): The game object.

            """
            super().__init__(game=game)
            self.game: Any = game
            self.proxies: list[Any] = [self.game, pygame.freetype]

        @override
        def on_font_changed_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
            """Handle font changed event.

            Args:
                event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

            """
            self.game.on_font_changed_event(event)

    def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
        """Initialize the font manager.

        Args:
            game (object): The game object (the scene manager): its ``engine_options`` give
                the default font options.

        """
        super().__init__(game=game)
        self.game: Any = game

        # Register pygame.freetype (imported at module top, so always available)
        pygame.freetype.init()
        log.info('Freetype Font Cache Size: %s', pygame.freetype.get_cache_size())
        log.info(
            'Freetype Font Default Resolution: %s',
            pygame.freetype.get_default_resolution(),
        )

        # Set up the default options: this context's (audit C13)
        font_options = _font_options()
        font_options['font_name'] = self.game.engine_options['font_name']
        font_options['font_size'] = self.game.engine_options['font_size']
        # A style option the game's options leave out gets the engine's default (antialiasing
        # on), so options not built by the engine's parser still load fonts
        for style_option, default_value in FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS.items():
            font_options[style_option] = self.game.engine_options.get(style_option, default_value)

        # Set font system based on command line argument
        font_system: str = self.game.engine_options.get('font_system', 'freetype')
        font_options['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
        log.info('Font system initialized: %s', font_system)

        # pygame's one default resolution per process, not this context's: the last
        # FontManager made sets it (audit S8, plans/2026-10-25-engine-context.md)
        pygame.freetype.set_default_resolution(font_options['font_dpi'])

        # Ideas:
        #
        # Pre-generate font cache based on settings that are provided.
        # Indexed by the letter they represent.
        # a -> <font name>
        # What about bold, italic, bold + italic, anti-aliased?
        # Maybe we can generate all combinations?
        # Allow caller to pass in a font settings blob and generate.
        # A progress bar class that integrates with tqdm?

        # Ideally, I'd like to support both modes.
        #
        # https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/font.html
        # To use the pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading
        # and rendering computer fonts based pygame.ftfont as pygame.fontpygame
        # module for loading and rendering fonts define the environment variable
        # PYGAME_FREETYPE before the first import of pygamethe top level pygame
        # package. Module pygame.ftfont is a pygame.fontpygame module for loading
        # and rendering fonts compatible module that passes all but one of the font
        # module unit tests: it does not have the UCS-2 limitation of the SDL_ttf
        # based font module, so fails to raise an exception for a code point greater
        # than 'uFFFF'. If pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading and
        # rendering computer fonts is unavailable then the SDL_ttf font module
        # will be loaded instead.

        # Set up proxies: the font proxy first, then pygame.freetype
        self.proxies: list[Any] = [FontManager.FontProxy(game=game), pygame.freetype]

    @classmethod
    def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
        """Add font options to the argument parser.

        Args:
            parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

        Returns:
            argparse.ArgumentParser

        """
        group = parser.add_argument_group('Font Options')

        group.add_argument(
            '--font-name',
            default=DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
            help=(
                f'Font to use (default: the bundled {DEFAULT_FONT_NAME}; the bundled variants are '
                "Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any other name is looked up among the system's "
                'fonts)'
            ),
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-size',
            type=int,
            default=14,
            help=(
                'size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own '
                '(default: %(default)s)'
            ),
        )
        # The style options apply to every font the manager loads, unless the font's own
        # configuration gives a value (BUGS.md #210)
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-bold',
            action='store_true',
            default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_bold'],
            help='draw text bold',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-italic',
            action='store_true',
            default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_italic'],
            help='draw text italic',
        )
        # On by default (pygame.freetype's own default), so --no-font-antialias turns it off
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-antialias',
            action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
            default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_antialias'],
            # Every text the engine, its games and its tools draw follows it, except the
            # channel 3 screen's digit (backgrounds.py), hard-edged on purpose
            help='antialias text (default: %(default)s)',
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-dpi',
            type=int,
            default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_dpi'],
            help=(
                'the resolution, in dots per inch, font sizes are scaled at (a size is in pixels '
                f'at {BASE_FONT_DPI}) (default: %(default)s)'
            ),
        )
        group.add_argument(
            '--font-system',
            choices=['pygame', 'freetype'],
            default='freetype',
            help='Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)',
        )

        return parser

    # PyInstaller-compiled games fall back to the bundled Vera.ttf font
    # since system font paths are not available in frozen environments.
    @classmethod
    def font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
        """Return a font object.

        If the font requested can't be found then bitstream_vera will be loaded instead.

        Note that if you are trying to package your game with pyinstaller, you'll need to bundle
        your game's fonts with the pyinstaller invocation.  Make sure you have distribution
        rights to the fonts you're including with your game.

        bitstream_vera is a permissively licensed font that can be used with your game.

        Args:
            font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

        Returns:
            GameFont

        """
        settings = cls.font_settings(font_config)
        cache_key = settings.cache_key

        # Check cache first
        if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
            return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

        log.info('Loading Font: %s', settings.name)
        log.info('Font Size: %s', settings.size)

        # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
        font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=settings.name)
        if font_path is not None:
            loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
                'GameFont', _styled_freetype_font(font_path=font_path, settings=settings)
            )
            FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
            return loaded_font

        try:
            # SysFont picks a bold or italic face when the system has one and asks the
            # constructor to embolden or slant only when it has none
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.freetype.SysFont(
                    name=settings.name,
                    size=settings.size,
                    bold=settings.bold,
                    italic=settings.italic,
                    constructor=_freetype_font_constructor(settings=settings),
                ),
            )
        except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
            # Note: Not sure why but pygame.freetype.SysFont doesn't
            # seem to work with pyinstaller packaged games.
            log.info('Loading Font: Built-In')

            # BUG: pygame's documentation claims that passing None as the font name
            # will load the default font, but this raises TypeError ("not a file object")
            # in PyInstaller-packaged games. Load the bundled Vera.ttf instead.
            # (BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY says where bitmappy.spec bundles it.) The fallback keeps
            # the requested size (it used to load at 12 whatever was asked for).
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                _styled_freetype_font(
                    font_path=BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES['vera'],
                    settings=settings,
                ),
            )

        # Cache the result
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    @classmethod
    def pygame_font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
        """Return a regular pygame font object for compatibility with UI components.

        Args:
            font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

        Returns:
            GameFont: A regular pygame font object.

        """
        settings = cls.font_settings(font_config)
        cache_key = f'pygame_{settings.cache_key}'

        # Check cache first
        if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
            return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

        # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
        font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=settings.name)
        if font_path is not None:
            pygame_font = pygame.font.Font(font_path, settings.pygame_font_size)
            pygame_font.set_bold(settings.bold)
            pygame_font.set_italic(settings.italic)
            loaded_font: GameFont = cast('GameFont', pygame_font)
            FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
            return loaded_font

        try:
            # SysFont picks a bold or italic face when the system has one, and emboldens or
            # slants the font itself when it has none
            loaded_font = cast(
                'GameFont',
                pygame.font.SysFont(
                    settings.name,
                    settings.pygame_font_size,
                    bold=settings.bold,
                    italic=settings.italic,
                ),
            )
        except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
            # Fall back to default font
            fallback_font = pygame.font.Font(None, settings.pygame_font_size)
            fallback_font.set_bold(settings.bold)
            fallback_font.set_italic(settings.italic)
            loaded_font = cast('GameFont', fallback_font)

        # Cache the result
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    @classmethod
    def antialias(cls) -> bool:
        """Return whether text is antialiased: --font-antialias, on unless turned off.

        pygame.font chooses antialiasing on each render call, so every caller that draws
        with a pygame.font font passes this (freetype fonts carry it themselves). Text that
        must stay hard-edged whatever the setting passes False with a comment saying why.

        Returns:
            The engine's antialias setting (True when no engine has set the options).

        """
        return cls.font_settings().antialias

    @classmethod
    def font_settings(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> FontSettings:
        """Return the settings a font configuration asks for, without changing the configuration.

        An empty or missing configuration asks for the engine's default font (the current
        context's font options). A name or size the configuration leaves out gets
        DEFAULT_FONT_NAME or DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE; a style option it leaves out gets the engine's
        option, then FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS, so --font-bold and the rest reach every font.

        Args:
            font_config: The font configuration.

        Returns:
            The font's settings.

        """
        font_options = _font_options()
        source = font_config or font_options

        def option(key: str, *, default: bool | int) -> bool | int:
            for options in (source, font_options):
                value = options.get(key)
                if value is not None:
                    return value
            return default

        return FontSettings(
            name=source.get('font_name') or DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
            size=source.get('font_size') or DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE,
            bold=bool(option('font_bold', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_bold'])),
            italic=bool(option('font_italic', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_italic'])),
            antialias=bool(option('font_antialias', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_antialias'])),
            dpi=int(option('font_dpi', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_dpi'])),
        )

    @classmethod
    def get_font(
        cls,
        font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype'] | None = None,
        font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    ) -> GameFont:
        """Get a font object, choosing between pygame.font and pygame.freetype.

        Args:
            font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype". If None, use the default preference.
            font_config: The font configuration.

        Returns:
            pygame.font.Font | pygame.freetype.Font: The requested font object.

        """
        if font_system is None:
            # Default to freetype
            use_freetype: bool = bool(_font_options().get('use_freetype', True))
        else:
            use_freetype = font_system == 'freetype'

        # Try freetype first, fall back to pygame if it fails
        if use_freetype:
            try:
                return cls.font(font_config)
            except (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) as e:
                log.info('Freetype font failed, falling back to pygame: %s', e)
                return cls.pygame_font(font_config)
        else:
            return cls.pygame_font(font_config)

    @classmethod
    def set_font_system(cls, font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype']) -> None:
        """Set the default font system preference.

        Args:
            font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype" to specify the font system.

        """
        _font_options()['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
        log.info('Font system set to: %s', font_system)

    @classmethod
    def get_font_system(cls) -> str:
        """Get the current font system preference.

        Returns:
            str: "freetype" or "pygame" indicating the current font system.

        """
        return 'freetype' if _font_options().get('use_freetype', False) else 'pygame'

    @classmethod
    def compare_font_systems(
        cls,
        text: str = 'Hello World',
        size: int = 24,
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Compare both font systems side by side.

        Args:
            text (str): Text to render for comparison.
            size (int): Font size for comparison.

        Returns:
            dict: Information about both font systems.

        """
        config: dict[str, Any] = {'font_size': size}

        # Get pygame.font. Its render takes (text, antialias, color) positionally, not
        # freetype's fgcolor keyword (which raised TypeError on a real pygame.font.Font).
        pygame_font = cast('pygame.font.Font', cls.get_font('pygame', config))
        pygame_surface: pygame.Surface = pygame_font.render(text, cls.antialias(), (255, 255, 255))

        # Get pygame.freetype
        freetype_font = cls.get_font('freetype', config)
        freetype_render_result = freetype_font.render(text, fgcolor=(255, 255, 255))
        freetype_surface: pygame.Surface = (
            freetype_render_result[0]
            if isinstance(freetype_render_result, tuple)
            else freetype_render_result
        )

        return {
            'pygame': {
                'font': pygame_font,
                'surface': pygame_surface,
                'size': pygame_surface.get_size(),
                'type': 'pygame.font.Font',
            },
            'freetype': {
                'font': freetype_font,
                'surface': freetype_surface,
                'size': freetype_surface.get_size(),
                'type': 'pygame.freetype.Font',
            },
        }

def __getattr__(self: Self, attr: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Get an attribute from the first proxy that has it.

    This method is called when an attribute is not found.

    Args:
        attr: The attribute to get.

    Returns:
        The attribute.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If no proxy has the attribute (or there are no proxies yet).

    """
    # The proxies themselves are an instance attribute: before __init__ sets them there are
    # none to try (looking them up here would recurse)
    if attr == 'proxies':
        raise AttributeError(MISSING_ATTRIBUTE_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

    # Try each proxy in turn (BUGS.md #198: the lookup returned or raised on the first)
    for proxy in self.proxies:
        try:
            return getattr(proxy, attr)
        except AttributeError:
            continue

    if self.proxies:
        self.log.error('No proxies for %s.%s', type(self), attr)
    raise AttributeError(NO_PROXIES_MSG.format(cls=type(self), attr=attr))

def __new__(cls: type[Self], *_args: Any, **_kwargs: Any) -> Self:
    """Return the class's shared instance, or a new instance for an unshared class.

    Args:
        cls: The class.
        *_args: The positional arguments (``__init__`` takes them).
        **_kwargs: The keyword arguments (``__init__`` takes them).

    Returns:
        The shared instance (made now if there is none yet), or a new instance.

    """
    if not cls.SHARES_INSTANCE:
        return object.__new__(cls)
    shared_instances = current_context().value(slot=SHARED_INSTANCES_SLOT)
    if cls not in shared_instances:
        shared_instances[cls] = object.__new__(cls)
        LOG.debug('Created Resource Manager: %s', cls)

    return shared_instances[cls]

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def release_shared_instances(cls) -> None:
    """Forget this context's shared instances, so each class's next construction is new.

    ``GameEngine`` calls it before it makes its event managers: a new engine run builds

def __init__(self: Self, game: object = None) -> None:
    """Initialize the font manager.

    Args:
        game (object): The game object (the scene manager): its ``engine_options`` give
            the default font options.

    """
    super().__init__(game=game)
    self.game: Any = game

    # Register pygame.freetype (imported at module top, so always available)
    pygame.freetype.init()
    log.info('Freetype Font Cache Size: %s', pygame.freetype.get_cache_size())
    log.info(
        'Freetype Font Default Resolution: %s',
        pygame.freetype.get_default_resolution(),
    )

    # Set up the default options: this context's (audit C13)
    font_options = _font_options()
    font_options['font_name'] = self.game.engine_options['font_name']
    font_options['font_size'] = self.game.engine_options['font_size']
    # A style option the game's options leave out gets the engine's default (antialiasing
    # on), so options not built by the engine's parser still load fonts
    for style_option, default_value in FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS.items():
        font_options[style_option] = self.game.engine_options.get(style_option, default_value)

    # Set font system based on command line argument
    font_system: str = self.game.engine_options.get('font_system', 'freetype')
    font_options['use_freetype'] = font_system == 'freetype'
    log.info('Font system initialized: %s', font_system)

    # pygame's one default resolution per process, not this context's: the last
    # FontManager made sets it (audit S8, plans/2026-10-25-engine-context.md)
    pygame.freetype.set_default_resolution(font_options['font_dpi'])

    # Ideas:
    #
    # Pre-generate font cache based on settings that are provided.
    # Indexed by the letter they represent.
    # a -> <font name>
    # What about bold, italic, bold + italic, anti-aliased?
    # Maybe we can generate all combinations?
    # Allow caller to pass in a font settings blob and generate.
    # A progress bar class that integrates with tqdm?

    # Ideally, I'd like to support both modes.
    #
    # https://www.pygame.org/docs/ref/font.html
    # To use the pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading
    # and rendering computer fonts based pygame.ftfont as pygame.fontpygame
    # module for loading and rendering fonts define the environment variable
    # PYGAME_FREETYPE before the first import of pygamethe top level pygame
    # package. Module pygame.ftfont is a pygame.fontpygame module for loading
    # and rendering fonts compatible module that passes all but one of the font
    # module unit tests: it does not have the UCS-2 limitation of the SDL_ttf
    # based font module, so fails to raise an exception for a code point greater
    # than 'uFFFF'. If pygame.freetypeEnhanced pygame module for loading and
    # rendering computer fonts is unavailable then the SDL_ttf font module
    # will be loaded instead.

    # Set up proxies: the font proxy first, then pygame.freetype
    self.proxies: list[Any] = [FontManager.FontProxy(game=game), pygame.freetype]

@classmethod
def args(cls, parser: argparse.ArgumentParser) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Add font options to the argument parser.

    Args:
        parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser.

    Returns:
        argparse.ArgumentParser

    """
    group = parser.add_argument_group('Font Options')

    group.add_argument(
        '--font-name',
        default=DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
        help=(
            f'Font to use (default: the bundled {DEFAULT_FONT_NAME}; the bundled variants are '
            "Vera, VeraBd, VeraIt and VeraBI; any other name is looked up among the system's "
            'fonts)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-size',
        type=int,
        default=14,
        help=(
            'size of the default font, used by text that asks for no font of its own '
            '(default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    # The style options apply to every font the manager loads, unless the font's own
    # configuration gives a value (BUGS.md #210)
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-bold',
        action='store_true',
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_bold'],
        help='draw text bold',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-italic',
        action='store_true',
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_italic'],
        help='draw text italic',
    )
    # On by default (pygame.freetype's own default), so --no-font-antialias turns it off
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-antialias',
        action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_antialias'],
        # Every text the engine, its games and its tools draw follows it, except the
        # channel 3 screen's digit (backgrounds.py), hard-edged on purpose
        help='antialias text (default: %(default)s)',
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-dpi',
        type=int,
        default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_dpi'],
        help=(
            'the resolution, in dots per inch, font sizes are scaled at (a size is in pixels '
            f'at {BASE_FONT_DPI}) (default: %(default)s)'
        ),
    )
    group.add_argument(
        '--font-system',
        choices=['pygame', 'freetype'],
        default='freetype',
        help='Font system to use: freetype (enhanced, default) or pygame (built-in)',
    )

    return parser

@classmethod
def compare_font_systems(
    cls,
    text: str = 'Hello World',
    size: int = 24,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    """Compare both font systems side by side.

    Args:
        text (str): Text to render for comparison.
        size (int): Font size for comparison.

    Returns:
        dict: Information about both font systems.

    """
    config: dict[str, Any] = {'font_size': size}

    # Get pygame.font. Its render takes (text, antialias, color) positionally, not
    # freetype's fgcolor keyword (which raised TypeError on a real pygame.font.Font).
    pygame_font = cast('pygame.font.Font', cls.get_font('pygame', config))
    pygame_surface: pygame.Surface = pygame_font.render(text, cls.antialias(), (255, 255, 255))

    # Get pygame.freetype
    freetype_font = cls.get_font('freetype', config)
    freetype_render_result = freetype_font.render(text, fgcolor=(255, 255, 255))
    freetype_surface: pygame.Surface = (
        freetype_render_result[0]
        if isinstance(freetype_render_result, tuple)
        else freetype_render_result
    )

    return {
        'pygame': {
            'font': pygame_font,
            'surface': pygame_surface,
            'size': pygame_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.font.Font',
        },
        'freetype': {
            'font': freetype_font,
            'surface': freetype_surface,
            'size': freetype_surface.get_size(),
            'type': 'pygame.freetype.Font',
        },
    }

@classmethod
def font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
    """Return a font object.

    If the font requested can't be found then bitstream_vera will be loaded instead.

    Note that if you are trying to package your game with pyinstaller, you'll need to bundle
    your game's fonts with the pyinstaller invocation.  Make sure you have distribution
    rights to the fonts you're including with your game.

    bitstream_vera is a permissively licensed font that can be used with your game.

    Args:
        font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

    Returns:
        GameFont

    """
    settings = cls.font_settings(font_config)
    cache_key = settings.cache_key

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    log.info('Loading Font: %s', settings.name)
    log.info('Font Size: %s', settings.size)

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=settings.name)
    if font_path is not None:
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast(
            'GameFont', _styled_freetype_font(font_path=font_path, settings=settings)
        )
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        # SysFont picks a bold or italic face when the system has one and asks the
        # constructor to embolden or slant only when it has none
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.freetype.SysFont(
                name=settings.name,
                size=settings.size,
                bold=settings.bold,
                italic=settings.italic,
                constructor=_freetype_font_constructor(settings=settings),
            ),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Note: Not sure why but pygame.freetype.SysFont doesn't
        # seem to work with pyinstaller packaged games.
        log.info('Loading Font: Built-In')

        # BUG: pygame's documentation claims that passing None as the font name
        # will load the default font, but this raises TypeError ("not a file object")
        # in PyInstaller-packaged games. Load the bundled Vera.ttf instead.
        # (BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY says where bitmappy.spec bundles it.) The fallback keeps
        # the requested size (it used to load at 12 whatever was asked for).
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            _styled_freetype_font(
                font_path=BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES['vera'],
                settings=settings,
            ),
        )

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def font_settings(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> FontSettings:
    """Return the settings a font configuration asks for, without changing the configuration.

    An empty or missing configuration asks for the engine's default font (the current
    context's font options). A name or size the configuration leaves out gets
    DEFAULT_FONT_NAME or DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE; a style option it leaves out gets the engine's
    option, then FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS, so --font-bold and the rest reach every font.

    Args:
        font_config: The font configuration.

    Returns:
        The font's settings.

    """
    font_options = _font_options()
    source = font_config or font_options

    def option(key: str, *, default: bool | int) -> bool | int:
        for options in (source, font_options):
            value = options.get(key)
            if value is not None:
                return value
        return default

    return FontSettings(
        name=source.get('font_name') or DEFAULT_FONT_NAME,
        size=source.get('font_size') or DEFAULT_FONT_SIZE,
        bold=bool(option('font_bold', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_bold'])),
        italic=bool(option('font_italic', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_italic'])),
        antialias=bool(option('font_antialias', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_antialias'])),
        dpi=int(option('font_dpi', default=FONT_STYLE_DEFAULTS['font_dpi'])),
    )

@classmethod
def get_font(
    cls,
    font_system: Literal['pygame', 'freetype'] | None = None,
    font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> GameFont:
    """Get a font object, choosing between pygame.font and pygame.freetype.

    Args:
        font_system: Either "pygame" or "freetype". If None, use the default preference.
        font_config: The font configuration.

    Returns:
        pygame.font.Font | pygame.freetype.Font: The requested font object.

    """
    if font_system is None:
        # Default to freetype
        use_freetype: bool = bool(_font_options().get('use_freetype', True))
    else:
        use_freetype = font_system == 'freetype'

    # Try freetype first, fall back to pygame if it fails
    if use_freetype:
        try:
            return cls.font(font_config)
        except (TypeError, FileNotFoundError, OSError) as e:
            log.info('Freetype font failed, falling back to pygame: %s', e)
            return cls.pygame_font(font_config)
    else:
        return cls.pygame_font(font_config)

@classmethod
def pygame_font(cls, font_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> GameFont:
    """Return a regular pygame font object for compatibility with UI components.

    Args:
        font_config (dict | None): The font configuration.

    Returns:
        GameFont: A regular pygame font object.

    """
    settings = cls.font_settings(font_config)
    cache_key = f'pygame_{settings.cache_key}'

    # Check cache first
    if cache_key in FontManager._font_cache:
        return FontManager._font_cache[cache_key]

    # A bundled font loads from its file: no system font scan (BUGS.md #156).
    font_path = bundled_font_path(font_name=settings.name)
    if font_path is not None:
        pygame_font = pygame.font.Font(font_path, settings.pygame_font_size)
        pygame_font.set_bold(settings.bold)
        pygame_font.set_italic(settings.italic)
        loaded_font: GameFont = cast('GameFont', pygame_font)
        FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
        return loaded_font

    try:
        # SysFont picks a bold or italic face when the system has one, and emboldens or
        # slants the font itself when it has none
        loaded_font = cast(
            'GameFont',
            pygame.font.SysFont(
                settings.name,
                settings.pygame_font_size,
                bold=settings.bold,
                italic=settings.italic,
            ),
        )
    except TypeError, FileNotFoundError:
        # Fall back to default font
        fallback_font = pygame.font.Font(None, settings.pygame_font_size)
        fallback_font.set_bold(settings.bold)
        fallback_font.set_italic(settings.italic)
        loaded_font = cast('GameFont', fallback_font)

    # Cache the result
    FontManager._font_cache[cache_key] = loaded_font
    return loaded_font

@classmethod
def release_shared_instance(cls) -> None:
    """Forget this class's shared instance, so its next construction makes a new one.

    Only this engine context's instance is forgotten (audit C12). A playback scope that
    made a controller manager the live game has none of releases it as the scope ends
    (``GameEngine.exit_playback_devices``).
    """
    current_context().value(slot=SHARED_INSTANCES_SLOT).pop(cls, None)

@classmethod
def release_shared_instances(cls) -> None:
    """Forget this context's shared instances, so each class's next construction is new.

    ``GameEngine`` calls it before it makes its event managers: a new engine run builds
    managers of its own (opening devices through its own doors), not the earlier run's. It
    releases this context's only: a game in another engine context keeps its managers.
    """
    current_context().value(slot=SHARED_INSTANCES_SLOT).clear()

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FontSettings:
    """Everything a loaded font depends on: its name, size and style.

    Attributes:
        name: The font's name (a bundled font or a system font).
        size: The size in points (pixels at BASE_FONT_DPI).
        bold: Drawn bold (pygame.freetype's strong, pygame.font's set_bold).
        italic: Drawn italic (pygame.freetype's oblique, pygame.font's set_italic).
        antialias: pygame.freetype's antialiased; pygame.font antialiases per render call,
            so its callers pass FontManager.antialias().
        dpi: The resolution sizes are scaled at.

    """

    name: str
    size: int
    bold: bool
    italic: bool
    antialias: bool
    dpi: int

    @property
    def cache_key(self) -> str:
        """The font cache key: two configurations share a font only if all fields match.

        Returns:
            The key (without the font system's prefix).

        """
        return (
            f'{self.name}_{self.size}_bold{int(self.bold)}_italic{int(self.italic)}'
            f'_antialias{int(self.antialias)}_dpi{self.dpi}'
        )

    @property
    def pygame_font_size(self) -> int:
        """The size to give pygame.font, which has no resolution of its own.

        Returns:
            The size scaled by dpi / BASE_FONT_DPI (at least 1).

        """
        return max(1, round(self.size * self.dpi / BASE_FONT_DPI))

def bundled_font_path(*, font_name: str) -> Path | None:
    """Return the file of a bundled font, or None when the name is not a bundled font.

    Args:
        font_name: A font name, in any case (e.g. 'Vera', 'VeraBd').

    Returns:
        The bundled font's file, or None for any other name (a system font).

    """
    file_name = BUNDLED_FONT_FILE_NAMES.get(font_name.lower())
    if file_name is None:
        return None
    return BUNDLED_FONT_DIRECTORY / file_name

class BallSpawnMode:
    """Bitwise flags for ball spawn behavior."""

    NONE = 0

    # Spawn triggers
    ON_PADDLE_COLLISION = 1 << 0
    ON_WALL_BOUNCE = 1 << 1
    ON_BALL_COLLISION = 1 << 2
    ON_SCORE = 1 << 3

    # Spawn conditions
    SPEED_CHECK_ENABLED = 1 << 4  # Only spawn if ball speed is reasonable
    COOLDOWN_ENABLED = 1 << 5  # Respect cooldown between spawns
    RANDOM_POSITION = 1 << 6  # Spawn at random position vs fixed
    RANDOM_SPEED = 1 << 7  # Random initial speed vs fixed
    RANDOM_COLOR = 1 << 8  # Random color vs default

    # Spawn frequency controls
    FREQUENT = 1 << 9  # Short cooldown (0.5s)
    NORMAL = 1 << 10  # Normal cooldown (2.0s)
    RARE = 1 << 11  # Long cooldown (5.0s)

    # Convenience combinations
    PADDLE_ONLY = (
        ON_PADDLE_COLLISION
        | SPEED_CHECK_ENABLED
        | COOLDOWN_ENABLED
        | RANDOM_POSITION
        | RANDOM_SPEED
        | RANDOM_COLOR
        | NORMAL
    )
    WALL_ONLY = (
        ON_WALL_BOUNCE
        | SPEED_CHECK_ENABLED
        | COOLDOWN_ENABLED
        | RANDOM_POSITION
        | RANDOM_SPEED
        | RANDOM_COLOR
        | NORMAL
    )
    BALL_ONLY = (
        ON_BALL_COLLISION
        | SPEED_CHECK_ENABLED
        | COOLDOWN_ENABLED
        | RANDOM_POSITION
        | RANDOM_SPEED
        | RANDOM_COLOR
        | NORMAL
    )
    ALL_TRIGGERS = ON_PADDLE_COLLISION | ON_WALL_BOUNCE | ON_BALL_COLLISION | ON_SCORE
    FREQUENT_SPAWNING = (
        ALL_TRIGGERS
        | SPEED_CHECK_ENABLED
        | COOLDOWN_ENABLED
        | RANDOM_POSITION
        | RANDOM_SPEED
        | RANDOM_COLOR
        | FREQUENT
    )
    NO_SPAWNING = NONE

Ball Sprite.

The ball moves and bounces off walls itself; paddle hits are resolved by the caller: a CollisionManager overlap check pairs balls with paddles and calls handle_paddle_collision (PaddleSlap does this).

The ball is a world sprite: its position is world_x/world_y, and the engine writes rect from them (snapped with the ball's own pixel_snap_mode) before each render (glitchygames/world.py). Under an identity camera, as in PaddleSlap, screen and world coordinates are the same. Game logic should read the world position or the collision rect, never rect, which holds where the ball was last drawn.
