class BallSprite(Sprite):
    """Ball Sprite.

    The ball moves and bounces off walls itself; paddle hits are resolved by the caller:
    a CollisionManager overlap check pairs balls with paddles and calls
    handle_paddle_collision (PaddleSlap does this).

    The ball is a world sprite: its position is world_x/world_y, and the engine writes rect
    from them (snapped with the ball's own pixel_snap_mode) before each render
    (glitchygames/world.py). Under an identity camera, as in PaddleSlap, screen and world
    coordinates are the same. Game logic should read the world position or the collision
    rect, never rect, which holds where the ball was last drawn.
    """

    COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        x: int = 0,
        y: int = 0,
        width: int = 20,
        height: int = 20,
        radius: int = 5,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None = None,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
        collision_sound: str | None = None,
        bounce_top_bottom: bool = True,
        bounce_left_right: bool = False,
        speed_up_settings: SpeedUpSettings | None = None,
        serve_settings: ServeSettings | None = None,
        pixel_snap_mode: PixelSnapMode = PixelSnapMode.NEAREST_HALF_UP,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the ball sprite.

        Args:
            x (int): The x position of the ball.
            y (int): The y position of the ball.
            width (int): The width of the ball's image (the visible ball is the circle).
            height (int): The height of the ball's image.
            radius (int): The radius of the circle drawn centred in the image: the visible ball,
                whose pixels are its hitbox (BUGS.md #172: it was always 5 whatever the size).
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.
            collision_sound (str | None): The sound to play on collision.
            bounce_top_bottom (bool): Whether to bounce off top and bottom boundaries.
            bounce_left_right (bool): Whether to bounce off left and right boundaries.
            speed_up_settings (SpeedUpSettings | None): How and when the ball speeds up;
                None means SpeedUpSettings() (no automatic speed-ups).
            serve_settings (ServeSettings | None): How reset() and serve() serve the
                ball; None means ServeSettings() (Pong-style diagonal serves).
            pixel_snap_mode (PixelSnapMode): How the sub-pixel world position is rounded
                to the rect position the ball is drawn at.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the circle does not fit in the image (it would be clipped silently),
                or its radius is not positive.

        """
        if radius <= 0 or 2 * radius > min(width, height):
            message = f'A radius-{radius} ball does not fit a {width}x{height} image'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()  # type: ignore[type-arg]

        super().__init__(x=x, y=y, width=width, height=height, groups=groups)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        self.use_gfxdraw = True
        # Sprite.__init__ created the image after the display was set, so it already has the
        # display's pixel format (convert() would return an equivalent copy)
        self.image.set_colorkey(0)
        self.radius = radius
        self.direction = 0
        self.speed = Speed(250.0, 125.0)  # 250 pixels/second horizontal, 125 pixels/second vertical

        # Sub-pixel position tracking (floats for accurate physics). The engine writes rect,
        # the snapped whole-pixel position the ball is drawn at, from world_x/world_y before
        # each render, so code should move the ball via world_x/world_y.
        self._pixel_snap_mode = pixel_snap_mode
        self.world_x = float(x)
        self.world_y = float(y)
        if collision_sound:
            self.snd = game_objects.load_sound(collision_sound)
        self.color = WHITE

        # Configure boundary bouncing behavior
        self.bounce_top_bottom = bounce_top_bottom
        self.bounce_left_right = bounce_left_right

        # Configure serve and speed-up behavior
        self.serve_settings = serve_settings or ServeSettings()
        self.speed_up_settings = speed_up_settings or SpeedUpSettings()
        self.speed_up_count = 0  # Speed-ups applied since the last reset (curve step n)
        self._continuous_elapsed_time = 0.0  # Game seconds toward the next CONTINUOUS step
        # The dt of the last dt_tick, so handle_paddle_collision can tell where the ball was
        # before this frame's move (0.0 until the first tick: no move to undo)
        self._last_tick_dt = 0.0
        # Where the last dt_tick started (world_x, world_y), so a game can follow the ball's
        # path through the frame (PaddleSlap's swept ball-ball check, BUGS.md #174); None until
        # the first tick
        self.frame_start_world_position: tuple[float, float] | None = None

        # Collision tracking (set by callers like PaddleSlap)
        self.collision_cooldowns: dict[str, float] = {}
        self.on_paddle_collision: Callable[[BallSprite], None] | None = None
        # Called with the ball after each wall bounce (one call per bounce, corners included)
        self.on_wall_bounce: Callable[[BallSprite], None] | None = None

        # Trajectory history (PaddleSlap fills it only while DEBUG logging is on)
        self._trajectory: list[tuple[float, float, float, float]] = []

        self.reset()

        # The ball always needs refreshing.
        # This saves us a set on dirty every update.
        self.dirty = 2

    @property
    def trajectory(self: Self) -> tuple[tuple[float, float, float, float], ...]:
        """The recorded trajectory points, oldest first.

        Returns:
            A read-only snapshot of (x, y, speed x, speed y) per recorded point.

        """
        return tuple(self._trajectory)

    def record_trajectory_point(
        self: Self,
        *,
        x: float,
        y: float,
        speed_x: float,
        speed_y: float,
        limit: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Append a point to the trajectory, dropping the oldest beyond limit.

        Args:
            x: The x position to record.
            y: The y position to record.
            speed_x: The horizontal speed to record.
            speed_y: The vertical speed to record.
            limit: The most points to keep.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If limit is below 1.

        """
        if limit < 1:
            msg = f'The trajectory limit must be at least 1, got {limit}'
            raise ValueError(msg)
        self._trajectory.append((x, y, speed_x, speed_y))
        del self._trajectory[:-limit]

    @property
    def world_x(self: Self) -> float:
        """The ball's sub-pixel x position."""
        return self._world_x

    @world_x.setter
    def world_x(self: Self, value: float) -> None:
        """Set the sub-pixel x position (the engine places rect from it before rendering)."""
        self._world_x = value

    @property
    def world_y(self: Self) -> float:
        """The ball's sub-pixel y position."""
        return self._world_y

    @world_y.setter
    def world_y(self: Self, value: float) -> None:
        """Set the sub-pixel y position (the engine places rect from it before rendering)."""
        self._world_y = value

    @property
    def pixel_snap_mode(self: Self) -> PixelSnapMode:
        """How the sub-pixel world position is rounded to the drawn rect position."""
        return self._pixel_snap_mode

    @pixel_snap_mode.setter
    def pixel_snap_mode(self: Self, mode: PixelSnapMode) -> None:
        """Change the snap mode; collision uses it at once, drawing from the next positioning."""
        self._pixel_snap_mode = mode

    def drawn_center(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Return the centre of the ball's image at its current snapped world position.

        This is where the engine's next positioning draws the ball (under an identity camera,
        as in PaddleSlap; with a moving camera it is the drawn centre in world pixels). Unlike
        rect.center it is current during dt_tick, before the engine has positioned the ball.

        Returns:
            tuple[int, int]: The centre, as rect.center reads after positioning.

        """
        drawn_rect = pygame.Rect(
            snapped_world_position(self, self.world_x, self.world_y), self.rect.size
        )
        return drawn_rect.center

    @property
    def color(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        """The color of the ball.

        Returns:
            tuple[int, int, int]: The color of the ball.

        """
        return self._color

    @color.setter
    def color(self: Self, new_color: tuple[int, int, int]) -> None:
        """Set the color of the ball.

        Args:
            new_color (tuple): The new color of the ball.

        """
        self._color = new_color
        pygame.draw.circle(
            self.image, self._color, (self.width // 2, self.height // 2), self.radius, 0
        )

    def reset(self: Self, serve_toward: ServeHorizontalDirection | None = None) -> None:
        """Start a new serve: random position within the spawn margin, then serve().

        Also restarts the speed-up curve and the continuous speed-up timer.

        Args:
            serve_toward (ServeHorizontalDirection | None): Override the horizontal
                direction for this serve (e.g. toward the player who lost the point).

        """
        self.speed_up_count = 0
        self._continuous_elapsed_time = 0.0

        # The margin is measured from the visible circle (the collision rect) to each edge
        margin = self.serve_settings.spawn_margin
        visible_rect = self._visible_rect()
        self.world_x = float(
            self._random_spawn_coordinate(int(self.screen_width - visible_rect.width), margin)
            - visible_rect.offset_x
        )
        self.world_y = float(
            self._random_spawn_coordinate(int(self.screen_height - visible_rect.height), margin)
            - visible_rect.offset_y
        )
        self.serve(serve_toward=serve_toward)

    @staticmethod
    def _random_spawn_coordinate(maximum_position: int, margin: int) -> int:
        """Pick a visible-edge coordinate in [margin, maximum_position - margin], or center.

        Returns:
            int: The coordinate (never negative).

        """
        lowest = margin
        highest = maximum_position - margin
        if lowest > highest:
            return max(maximum_position // 2, 0)
        return random_stream(SERVE_RANDOM_STREAM).randint(lowest, highest)

    def serve(self: Self, serve_toward: ServeHorizontalDirection | None = None) -> None:
        """Set a serve velocity from serve_settings without moving the ball.

        Args:
            serve_toward (ServeHorizontalDirection | None): Override the horizontal
                direction for this serve.

        """
        settings = self.serve_settings
        serve_random = random_stream(SERVE_RANDOM_STREAM)
        horizontal = serve_toward or settings.horizontal
        if horizontal is ServeHorizontalDirection.EITHER:
            horizontal = serve_random.choice((
                ServeHorizontalDirection.LEFT,
                ServeHorizontalDirection.RIGHT,
            ))
        vertical = settings.vertical
        if vertical is ServeVerticalDirection.EITHER:
            vertical = serve_random.choice((
                ServeVerticalDirection.UP,
                ServeVerticalDirection.DOWN,
            ))

        angle_radians = math.radians(
            serve_random.uniform(settings.minimum_angle_degrees, settings.maximum_angle_degrees)
        )
        horizontal_sign = 1.0 if horizontal is ServeHorizontalDirection.RIGHT else -1.0
        vertical_sign = 1.0 if vertical is ServeVerticalDirection.DOWN else -1.0
        self.speed.x = horizontal_sign * settings.speed * math.cos(angle_radians)
        self.speed.y = vertical_sign * settings.speed * math.sin(angle_radians)
        # Heading in degrees, 0 = right, 90 = down (kept for debugging and display)
        self.direction = math.degrees(math.atan2(self.speed.y, self.speed.x)) % 360

    def speed_up(self: Self) -> None:
        """Apply one speed-up step according to speed_up_settings.

        Scales the configured axes by the curve's next step ratio, then applies
        max_speed. Changes made to speed between steps (collisions) are kept.
        """
        settings = self.speed_up_settings
        ratio = speed_up_step_ratio(settings.curve, settings.multiplier, self.speed_up_count)
        self.speed_up_count += 1
        if settings.axes is not SpeedUpAxes.Y_ONLY:
            self.speed.x *= ratio
        if settings.axes is not SpeedUpAxes.X_ONLY:
            self.speed.y *= ratio
        self._clamp_to_max_speed()

    def _clamp_to_max_speed(self: Self) -> None:
        """Limit the configured axes to speed_up_settings.max_speed, if one is set."""
        settings = self.speed_up_settings
        if settings.max_speed is None:
            return
        match settings.axes:
            case SpeedUpAxes.BOTH:
                speed_magnitude = math.hypot(self.speed.x, self.speed.y)
                if speed_magnitude > settings.max_speed:
                    scale_factor = settings.max_speed / speed_magnitude
                    self.speed.x *= scale_factor
                    self.speed.y *= scale_factor
            case SpeedUpAxes.X_ONLY:
                if abs(self.speed.x) > settings.max_speed:
                    self.speed.x = math.copysign(settings.max_speed, self.speed.x)
            case SpeedUpAxes.Y_ONLY:
                if abs(self.speed.y) > settings.max_speed:
                    self.speed.y = math.copysign(settings.max_speed, self.speed.y)
            case _:  # pragma: no cover - every SpeedUpAxes is matched above
                assert_never(settings.axes)

    def _advance_continuous_speed_up(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Advance the CONTINUOUS speed-up timer by dt seconds of game time.

        Args:
            dt (float): Game time elapsed this frame, in seconds.

        """
        settings = self.speed_up_settings
        if SpeedUpTrigger.CONTINUOUS not in settings.triggers:
            return
        self._continuous_elapsed_time += dt
        intervals_due = math.floor(
            (self._continuous_elapsed_time + CONTINUOUS_SPEED_UP_TIME_TOLERANCE) / settings.interval
        )
        if intervals_due < 1:
            return
        match settings.schedule:
            case SpeedUpSchedule.FIXED_RATE:
                self.speed_up()
                self._continuous_elapsed_time -= intervals_due * settings.interval
            case SpeedUpSchedule.CATCH_UP:
                for _ in range(intervals_due):
                    self.speed_up()
                self._continuous_elapsed_time -= intervals_due * settings.interval
            case SpeedUpSchedule.MINIMUM_GAP:
                self.speed_up()
                self._continuous_elapsed_time = 0.0
            case _:  # pragma: no cover - every SpeedUpSchedule is matched above
                assert_never(settings.schedule)
        # The tolerance can leave a tiny negative remainder
        self._continuous_elapsed_time = max(self._continuous_elapsed_time, 0.0)

    def _apply_triggered_speed_up(self: Self, trigger: SpeedUpTrigger) -> None:
        """Speed up if the given event is one of the configured triggers.

        Args:
            trigger (SpeedUpTrigger): The event that just happened.

        """
        if trigger in self.speed_up_settings.triggers:
            self.speed_up()

    def on_paddle_bounce(self: Self) -> None:
        """Speed up for a paddle hit if PADDLE_BOUNCE is a configured trigger."""
        self._apply_triggered_speed_up(SpeedUpTrigger.PADDLE_BOUNCE)

    @override
    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Update the ball with delta time.

        Args:
            dt (float): The delta time.

        """
        self._last_tick_dt = dt
        self.frame_start_world_position = (self.world_x, self.world_y)

        # Check for continuous speed-up
        self._advance_continuous_speed_up(dt)

        # Apply velocity to sub-pixel position (the engine places rect before rendering)
        self.world_x += self.speed.x * dt
        self.world_y += self.speed.y * dt

        # Ensure the ball is marked as dirty for redrawing
        self.dirty = 1

        # Paddle hits are found by the game's CollisionManager after the balls move and
        # resolved by handle_paddle_collision() (see PaddleSlap's Game.dt_tick, which resolves
        # them after every sprite moved).

        self._do_bounce()

        # Only kill ball once its visible circle is fully off screen and left/right
        # bouncing is disabled
        if not self.bounce_left_right:
            visible_rect = self._visible_rect()
            if visible_rect.left > self.screen_width or visible_rect.right < 0:
                # Mark ball for deletion instead of resetting
                self.kill()

        # Vertical boundaries are handled by bounce(), not reset.

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the ball."""
        # Movement is now handled in dt_tick() for frame-rate independence
        # This method is kept for compatibility but no longer moves the ball

    def _do_bounce(self: Self) -> None:
        """Enhanced ball boundary physics with improved collision response."""
        # Every ball checks every frame: read the eight arguments only when DEBUG is on
        if log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
            log.debug(
                'BALL BOUNCE CHECK: pos=(%.1f,%.1f) '
                'speed=(%.3f,%.3f) '
                'screen=(%s,%s) '
                'bounce_top_bottom=%s '
                'bounce_left_right=%s',
                self.world_x,
                self.world_y,
                self.speed.x,
                self.speed.y,
                self.screen_width,
                self.screen_height,
                self.bounce_top_bottom,
                self.bounce_left_right,
            )

        # Enhanced boundary checking with proper physics
        self._handle_boundary_collisions(log)

    def _handle_boundary_collisions(self: Self, log: logging.Logger) -> None:
        """Bounce off any wall the ball is touching while moving toward it.

        A frame that hits one wall, or two at a corner, is a single bounce: one sound
        and at most one WALL_BOUNCE speed-up, then one on_wall_bounce call. A ball
        touching a wall while already moving away from it (e.g. the frame after a bounce)
        does not bounce again.

        Args:
            log (logging.Logger): Logger instance for debug output

        """
        hit_horizontal_wall = False  # top or bottom
        hit_vertical_wall = False  # left or right

        # Contact is on the visible circle's box at the snapped (drawn) position
        visible_rect = self._visible_rect()

        if self.bounce_top_bottom:
            if visible_rect.top <= 0 and self.speed.y < 0:
                self._handle_top_collision(log)
                hit_horizontal_wall = True
            elif visible_rect.bottom >= self.screen_height and self.speed.y > 0:
                self._handle_bottom_collision(log)
                hit_horizontal_wall = True

        if self.bounce_left_right:
            if visible_rect.left <= 0 and self.speed.x < 0:
                self._handle_left_collision(log)
                hit_vertical_wall = True
            elif visible_rect.right >= self.screen_width and self.speed.x > 0:
                self._handle_right_collision(log)
                hit_vertical_wall = True

        if hit_horizontal_wall and hit_vertical_wall:
            self._handle_corner_collision(log)

        if hit_horizontal_wall or hit_vertical_wall:
            self._finish_wall_bounce()

        self._keep_inside_playfield()

    def _finish_wall_bounce(self: Self) -> None:
        """Play the bounce sound, apply any WALL_BOUNCE speed-up, then call on_wall_bounce."""
        if hasattr(self, 'snd') and self.snd is not None:  # type: ignore[reportUnnecessaryComparison]
            self.snd.play()
        self._apply_triggered_speed_up(SpeedUpTrigger.WALL_BOUNCE)
        if self.on_wall_bounce is not None:
            self.on_wall_bounce(self)

    def _keep_inside_playfield(self: Self) -> None:
        """Mirror any overshoot past a bouncing wall back inside the playfield.

        Runs whether or not the ball bounced this frame, so a ball found past a wall
        while moving away from it (or not moving) is still put back inside. The limits
        are where the visible circle's edges meet the walls.
        """
        visible_rect = self._visible_rect()
        if self.bounce_top_bottom:
            self.world_y = self._mirrored_inside(
                self.world_y,
                minimum=float(-visible_rect.offset_y),
                maximum=float(self.screen_height - visible_rect.height - visible_rect.offset_y),
            )
        if self.bounce_left_right:
            self.world_x = self._mirrored_inside(
                self.world_x,
                minimum=float(-visible_rect.offset_x),
                maximum=float(self.screen_width - visible_rect.width - visible_rect.offset_x),
            )

    @staticmethod
    def _mirrored_inside(position: float, *, minimum: float, maximum: float) -> float:
        """Mirror a position that overshot [minimum, maximum] back inside, clamping huge ones.

        Returns:
            float: The position within [minimum, maximum].

        """
        if position < minimum:
            position = 2.0 * minimum - position
        elif position > maximum:
            position = 2.0 * maximum - position
        return min(max(position, minimum), maximum)

    def _visible_rect(self: Self) -> VisibleRect:
        """Return the ball's visible collision rect and its offset from the drawn position.

        The rect is the same one collision checks use (get_collision_rect: the visible
        pixels of the image at the snapped world position), so walls, paddles and other
        balls all meet the circle players see.

        Returns:
            VisibleRect: The rect plus its offset from the snapped world position.

        """
        collision_rect = get_collision_rect(self, self.world_x, self.world_y)
        snapped_world_x, snapped_world_y = snapped_world_position(self, self.world_x, self.world_y)
        return VisibleRect(
            left=collision_rect.left,
            top=collision_rect.top,
            width=collision_rect.width,
            height=collision_rect.height,
            offset_x=collision_rect.x - snapped_world_x,
            offset_y=collision_rect.y - snapped_world_y,
        )

    def _handle_top_collision(self: Self, log: logging.Logger) -> None:
        """Reflect the velocity off the top wall.

        Position is corrected afterwards by _keep_inside_playfield(), which mirrors
        only a real overshoot (contact is detected on the snapped rect, so the world
        position may already be just inside the wall).

        Args:
            log (logging.Logger): Logger instance for debug output

        """
        self.speed.y = abs(self.speed.y)  # ensure downward
        self._add_collision_visual_feedback('top', log)

    def _handle_bottom_collision(self: Self, log: logging.Logger) -> None:
        """Reflect the velocity off the bottom wall (see _handle_top_collision).

        Args:
            log (logging.Logger): Logger instance for debug output

        """
        self.speed.y = -abs(self.speed.y)  # ensure upward
        self._add_collision_visual_feedback('bottom', log)

    def _handle_left_collision(self: Self, log: logging.Logger) -> None:
        """Reflect the velocity off the left wall (see _handle_top_collision).

        Args:
            log (logging.Logger): Logger instance for debug output

        """
        self.speed.x = abs(self.speed.x)  # ensure rightward
        self._add_collision_visual_feedback('left', log)

    def _handle_right_collision(self: Self, log: logging.Logger) -> None:
        """Reflect the velocity off the right wall (see _handle_top_collision).

        Args:
            log (logging.Logger): Logger instance for debug output

        """
        self.speed.x = -abs(self.speed.x)  # ensure leftward
        self._add_collision_visual_feedback('right', log)

    def _handle_corner_collision(self: Self, log: logging.Logger) -> None:
        """Give visual feedback for a bounce that hit two walls in the same frame.

        The edge handlers have already reflected both velocity components, and
        _keep_inside_playfield() corrects position, so this must not change either.

        Args:
            log (logging.Logger): Logger instance for debug output

        """
        log.debug(
            'BALL CORNER COLLISION: pos=(%.1f, %.1f) speed=(%.3f, %.3f)',
            self.world_x,
            self.world_y,
            self.speed.x,
            self.speed.y,
        )
        self._add_collision_visual_feedback('corner', log)

    def _add_collision_visual_feedback(
        self: Self,
        collision_type: str,
        log: logging.Logger,
    ) -> None:
        """Add visual feedback for collision points and bounce directions.

        Args:
            collision_type (str): Type of collision ("top", "bottom", "left", "right", "corner")
            log (logging.Logger): Logger instance for debug output

        """
        # Visual feedback implementation
        # This could include:
        # - Particle effects at collision point
        # - Screen shake
        # - Color changes
        # - Trail effects showing bounce direction

        # For now, we'll add debug logging and prepare for future visual effects
        log.debug(
            'BALL COLLISION VISUAL FEEDBACK: %s at (%.1f, %.1f)',
            collision_type,
            self.world_x,
            self.world_y,
        )

        # Future implementation could include:
        # - Particle system for collision sparks
        # - Screen shake effect
        # - Ball color change on collision
        # - Trail effect showing bounce direction
        # - Sound effect variations based on collision type

        # Mark ball as needing visual update
        self.dirty = 2  # Force full redraw for visual effects

    def _entered_paddle_from_left(
        self: Self, *, ball_rect: VisibleRect, paddle_rect: pygame.Rect
    ) -> bool:
        """Decide which face of a paddle the touching ball is pushed out of.

        The same rule as the platformers' _entered_wall_from_left: look at where the visible
        rect was before this frame's move (speed.x * the last tick's dt back). If it was clear
        of the paddle on one side, the ball came in from that side, even when a long frame
        (30 fps, a hitch) carried its centre past the paddle's centre. If it already
        overlapped (e.g. resting on the paddle's top or bottom edge, or not moving), the side
        of the paddle's centre the ball's centre is on decides, so it is pushed out on its own
        side rather than through the paddle.

        Args:
            ball_rect (VisibleRect): The ball's visible rect at its current position.
            paddle_rect (pygame.Rect): The paddle's collision rect.

        Returns:
            bool: True to push the ball out of the paddle's left face, False its right face.

        """
        return entered_from_left(
            mover_left=ball_rect.left,
            mover_right=ball_rect.right,
            displacement_x=self.speed.x * self._last_tick_dt,
            solid_left=paddle_rect.left,
            solid_right=paddle_rect.right,
            mover_center_x=ball_rect.left + ball_rect.width / 2,
            solid_center_x=paddle_rect.x + paddle_rect.width / 2,
        )

    def handle_paddle_collision(self: Self, paddle: Sprite) -> bool:
        """Bounce off a paddle if the ball's visible circle touches it.

        Meant as the fine check after a CollisionManager broad-phase overlap. The ball is
        the circle inscribed in its collision rect (its visible pixels); the paddle is its
        collision rect. Touching counts. On a hit the ball is placed with its visible edge
        flush against the face it came in through (see _entered_paddle_from_left), its
        horizontal speed points away from the paddle, the paddle's sound plays, a
        PADDLE_BOUNCE speed-up and the max_speed clamp are applied, and on_paddle_collision
        is called.

        Args:
            paddle (Sprite): The paddle the broad phase paired with this ball.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the ball hit the paddle and bounced; False (with no side effects)
            otherwise.

        """
        ball_rect = self._visible_rect()
        paddle_rect = get_sprite_collision_rect(paddle)

        radius = ball_rect.width / 2
        ball_center_x = ball_rect.left + ball_rect.width / 2
        ball_center_y = ball_rect.top + ball_rect.height / 2
        closest_x = min(max(ball_center_x, paddle_rect.left), paddle_rect.right)
        closest_y = min(max(ball_center_y, paddle_rect.top), paddle_rect.bottom)
        distance_squared = (ball_center_x - closest_x) ** 2 + (ball_center_y - closest_y) ** 2
        if distance_squared > radius * radius:
            return False

        visible_offset_x = ball_rect.offset_x

        if self._entered_paddle_from_left(ball_rect=ball_rect, paddle_rect=paddle_rect):
            # Ball hits the paddle's left face - visible right edge on the left face
            self.world_x = float(paddle_rect.left - (visible_offset_x + ball_rect.width))
            self.speed.x = -abs(self.speed.x)
        else:
            # Ball hits the paddle's right face - visible left edge on the right face
            self.world_x = float(paddle_rect.right - visible_offset_x)
            self.speed.x = abs(self.speed.x)

        # Play collision sound if paddle has one
        paddle_sound = getattr(paddle, 'snd', None)
        if paddle_sound is not None:
            paddle_sound.play()

        # Speed-up on paddle collision (speed_up() applies max_speed itself). Clamp
        # again in case the ball arrived above max_speed with no speed-up triggered.
        self._apply_triggered_speed_up(SpeedUpTrigger.PADDLE_BOUNCE)
        self._clamp_to_max_speed()

        # Notify the game that a paddle collision occurred (for ball spawn)
        collision_callback = getattr(self, 'on_paddle_collision', None)
        if callable(collision_callback):
            collision_callback(self)

        # Mark ball as dirty for redraw
        self.dirty = 2
        return True

def __init__(
    self: Self,
    *,
    x: int = 0,
    y: int = 0,
    width: int = 20,
    height: int = 20,
    radius: int = 5,
    groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None = None,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
    collision_sound: str | None = None,
    bounce_top_bottom: bool = True,
    bounce_left_right: bool = False,
    speed_up_settings: SpeedUpSettings | None = None,
    serve_settings: ServeSettings | None = None,
    pixel_snap_mode: PixelSnapMode = PixelSnapMode.NEAREST_HALF_UP,
) -> None:
    """Initialize the ball sprite.

    Args:
        x (int): The x position of the ball.
        y (int): The y position of the ball.
        width (int): The width of the ball's image (the visible ball is the circle).
        height (int): The height of the ball's image.
        radius (int): The radius of the circle drawn centred in the image: the visible ball,
            whose pixels are its hitbox (BUGS.md #172: it was always 5 whatever the size).
        groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.
        collision_sound (str | None): The sound to play on collision.
        bounce_top_bottom (bool): Whether to bounce off top and bottom boundaries.
        bounce_left_right (bool): Whether to bounce off left and right boundaries.
        speed_up_settings (SpeedUpSettings | None): How and when the ball speeds up;
            None means SpeedUpSettings() (no automatic speed-ups).
        serve_settings (ServeSettings | None): How reset() and serve() serve the
            ball; None means ServeSettings() (Pong-style diagonal serves).
        pixel_snap_mode (PixelSnapMode): How the sub-pixel world position is rounded
            to the rect position the ball is drawn at.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the circle does not fit in the image (it would be clipped silently),
            or its radius is not positive.

    """
    if radius <= 0 or 2 * radius > min(width, height):
        message = f'A radius-{radius} ball does not fit a {width}x{height} image'
        raise ValueError(message)
    if groups is None:
        groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()  # type: ignore[type-arg]

    super().__init__(x=x, y=y, width=width, height=height, groups=groups)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    self.use_gfxdraw = True
    # Sprite.__init__ created the image after the display was set, so it already has the
    # display's pixel format (convert() would return an equivalent copy)
    self.image.set_colorkey(0)
    self.radius = radius
    self.direction = 0
    self.speed = Speed(250.0, 125.0)  # 250 pixels/second horizontal, 125 pixels/second vertical

    # Sub-pixel position tracking (floats for accurate physics). The engine writes rect,
    # the snapped whole-pixel position the ball is drawn at, from world_x/world_y before
    # each render, so code should move the ball via world_x/world_y.
    self._pixel_snap_mode = pixel_snap_mode
    self.world_x = float(x)
    self.world_y = float(y)
    if collision_sound:
        self.snd = game_objects.load_sound(collision_sound)
    self.color = WHITE

    # Configure boundary bouncing behavior
    self.bounce_top_bottom = bounce_top_bottom
    self.bounce_left_right = bounce_left_right

    # Configure serve and speed-up behavior
    self.serve_settings = serve_settings or ServeSettings()
    self.speed_up_settings = speed_up_settings or SpeedUpSettings()
    self.speed_up_count = 0  # Speed-ups applied since the last reset (curve step n)
    self._continuous_elapsed_time = 0.0  # Game seconds toward the next CONTINUOUS step
    # The dt of the last dt_tick, so handle_paddle_collision can tell where the ball was
    # before this frame's move (0.0 until the first tick: no move to undo)
    self._last_tick_dt = 0.0
    # Where the last dt_tick started (world_x, world_y), so a game can follow the ball's
    # path through the frame (PaddleSlap's swept ball-ball check, BUGS.md #174); None until
    # the first tick
    self.frame_start_world_position: tuple[float, float] | None = None

    # Collision tracking (set by callers like PaddleSlap)
    self.collision_cooldowns: dict[str, float] = {}
    self.on_paddle_collision: Callable[[BallSprite], None] | None = None
    # Called with the ball after each wall bounce (one call per bounce, corners included)
    self.on_wall_bounce: Callable[[BallSprite], None] | None = None

    # Trajectory history (PaddleSlap fills it only while DEBUG logging is on)
    self._trajectory: list[tuple[float, float, float, float]] = []

    self.reset()

    # The ball always needs refreshing.
    # This saves us a set on dirty every update.
    self.dirty = 2

docs.text:
Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 
@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

@classmethod
def break_when(cls: type[Sprite], sprite_type: object | None = None) -> None:
    """Register a breakpoint for a sprite type.

    Args:
        sprite_type (object | None): The sprite type to break on.
            None means break on any sprite.

    """
    # The current context's breakpoints: None means disabled, [] means any
    counters = sprite_counters()
    if counters.breakpoints is None:
        counters.breakpoints = []

    # If none, break always.
    if sprite_type is not None:
        # Register the type asked for (not cls): __init__ compares str(type(self)) with it
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==%s', sprite_type)
        counters.breakpoints.append(str(sprite_type))
    else:
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==<any>')

def drawn_center(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """Return the centre of the ball's image at its current snapped world position.

    This is where the engine's next positioning draws the ball (under an identity camera,
    as in PaddleSlap; with a moving camera it is the drawn centre in world pixels). Unlike
    rect.center it is current during dt_tick, before the engine has positioned the ball.

    Returns:
        tuple[int, int]: The centre, as rect.center reads after positioning.

    """
    drawn_rect = pygame.Rect(
        snapped_world_position(self, self.world_x, self.world_y), self.rect.size
    )
    return drawn_rect.center

@override
def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
    """Update the ball with delta time.

    Args:
        dt (float): The delta time.

    """
    self._last_tick_dt = dt
    self.frame_start_world_position = (self.world_x, self.world_y)

    # Check for continuous speed-up
    self._advance_continuous_speed_up(dt)

    # Apply velocity to sub-pixel position (the engine places rect before rendering)
    self.world_x += self.speed.x * dt
    self.world_y += self.speed.y * dt

    # Ensure the ball is marked as dirty for redrawing
    self.dirty = 1

    # Paddle hits are found by the game's CollisionManager after the balls move and
    # resolved by handle_paddle_collision() (see PaddleSlap's Game.dt_tick, which resolves
    # them after every sprite moved).

    self._do_bounce()

    # Only kill ball once its visible circle is fully off screen and left/right
    # bouncing is disabled
    if not self.bounce_left_right:
        visible_rect = self._visible_rect()
        if visible_rect.left > self.screen_width or visible_rect.right < 0:
            # Mark ball for deletion instead of resetting
            self.kill()

Bounce off a paddle if the ball's visible circle touches it.

Meant as the fine check after a CollisionManager broad-phase overlap. The ball is the circle inscribed in its collision rect (its visible pixels); the paddle is its collision rect. Touching counts. On a hit the ball is placed with its visible edge flush against the face it came in through (see _entered_paddle_from_left), its horizontal speed points away from the paddle, the paddle's sound plays, a PADDLE_BOUNCE speed-up and the max_speed clamp are applied, and on_paddle_collision is called.

def handle_paddle_collision(self: Self, paddle: Sprite) -> bool:
    """Bounce off a paddle if the ball's visible circle touches it.

    Meant as the fine check after a CollisionManager broad-phase overlap. The ball is
    the circle inscribed in its collision rect (its visible pixels); the paddle is its
    collision rect. Touching counts. On a hit the ball is placed with its visible edge
    flush against the face it came in through (see _entered_paddle_from_left), its
    horizontal speed points away from the paddle, the paddle's sound plays, a
    PADDLE_BOUNCE speed-up and the max_speed clamp are applied, and on_paddle_collision
    is called.

    Args:
        paddle (Sprite): The paddle the broad phase paired with this ball.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the ball hit the paddle and bounced; False (with no side effects)
        otherwise.

    """
    ball_rect = self._visible_rect()
    paddle_rect = get_sprite_collision_rect(paddle)

    radius = ball_rect.width / 2
    ball_center_x = ball_rect.left + ball_rect.width / 2
    ball_center_y = ball_rect.top + ball_rect.height / 2
    closest_x = min(max(ball_center_x, paddle_rect.left), paddle_rect.right)
    closest_y = min(max(ball_center_y, paddle_rect.top), paddle_rect.bottom)
    distance_squared = (ball_center_x - closest_x) ** 2 + (ball_center_y - closest_y) ** 2
    if distance_squared > radius * radius:
        return False

    visible_offset_x = ball_rect.offset_x

    if self._entered_paddle_from_left(ball_rect=ball_rect, paddle_rect=paddle_rect):
        # Ball hits the paddle's left face - visible right edge on the left face
        self.world_x = float(paddle_rect.left - (visible_offset_x + ball_rect.width))
        self.speed.x = -abs(self.speed.x)
    else:
        # Ball hits the paddle's right face - visible left edge on the right face
        self.world_x = float(paddle_rect.right - visible_offset_x)
        self.speed.x = abs(self.speed.x)

    # Play collision sound if paddle has one
    paddle_sound = getattr(paddle, 'snd', None)
    if paddle_sound is not None:
        paddle_sound.play()

    # Speed-up on paddle collision (speed_up() applies max_speed itself). Clamp
    # again in case the ball arrived above max_speed with no speed-up triggered.
    self._apply_triggered_speed_up(SpeedUpTrigger.PADDLE_BOUNCE)
    self._clamp_to_max_speed()

    # Notify the game that a paddle collision occurred (for ball spawn)
    collision_callback = getattr(self, 'on_paddle_collision', None)
    if callable(collision_callback):
        collision_callback(self)

    # Mark ball as dirty for redraw
    self.dirty = 2
    return True

def record_trajectory_point(
    self: Self,
    *,
    x: float,
    y: float,
    speed_x: float,
    speed_y: float,
    limit: int,
) -> None:
    """Append a point to the trajectory, dropping the oldest beyond limit.

    Args:
        x: The x position to record.
        y: The y position to record.
        speed_x: The horizontal speed to record.
        speed_y: The vertical speed to record.
        limit: The most points to keep.

    Raises:

    """
    if limit < 1:
        msg = f'The trajectory limit must be at least 1, got {limit}'
        raise ValueError(msg)
    self._trajectory.append((x, y, speed_x, speed_y))
    del self._trajectory[:-limit]

def reset(self: Self, serve_toward: ServeHorizontalDirection | None = None) -> None:
    """Start a new serve: random position within the spawn margin, then serve().

    Also restarts the speed-up curve and the continuous speed-up timer.

    Args:
        serve_toward (ServeHorizontalDirection | None): Override the horizontal
            direction for this serve (e.g. toward the player who lost the point).

    """
    self.speed_up_count = 0
    self._continuous_elapsed_time = 0.0

    # The margin is measured from the visible circle (the collision rect) to each edge
    margin = self.serve_settings.spawn_margin
    visible_rect = self._visible_rect()
    self.world_x = float(
        self._random_spawn_coordinate(int(self.screen_width - visible_rect.width), margin)
        - visible_rect.offset_x
    )
    self.world_y = float(
        self._random_spawn_coordinate(int(self.screen_height - visible_rect.height), margin)
        - visible_rect.offset_y
    )
    self.serve(serve_toward=serve_toward)

docs.text:

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default serve_toward ServeHorizontalDirection | None

def serve(self: Self, serve_toward: ServeHorizontalDirection | None = None) -> None:
    """Set a serve velocity from serve_settings without moving the ball.

    Args:
        serve_toward (ServeHorizontalDirection | None): Override the horizontal
            direction for this serve.

    """
    settings = self.serve_settings
    serve_random = random_stream(SERVE_RANDOM_STREAM)
    horizontal = serve_toward or settings.horizontal
    if horizontal is ServeHorizontalDirection.EITHER:
        horizontal = serve_random.choice((
            ServeHorizontalDirection.LEFT,
            ServeHorizontalDirection.RIGHT,
        ))
    vertical = settings.vertical
    if vertical is ServeVerticalDirection.EITHER:
        vertical = serve_random.choice((
            ServeVerticalDirection.UP,
            ServeVerticalDirection.DOWN,
        ))

    angle_radians = math.radians(
        serve_random.uniform(settings.minimum_angle_degrees, settings.maximum_angle_degrees)
    )
    horizontal_sign = 1.0 if horizontal is ServeHorizontalDirection.RIGHT else -1.0
    vertical_sign = 1.0 if vertical is ServeVerticalDirection.DOWN else -1.0
    self.speed.x = horizontal_sign * settings.speed * math.cos(angle_radians)
    self.speed.y = vertical_sign * settings.speed * math.sin(angle_radians)
    # Heading in degrees, 0 = right, 90 = down (kept for debugging and display)
    self.direction = math.degrees(math.atan2(self.speed.y, self.speed.x)) % 360

def speed_up(self: Self) -> None:
    """Apply one speed-up step according to speed_up_settings.

    Scales the configured axes by the curve's next step ratio, then applies
    max_speed. Changes made to speed between steps (collisions) are kept.
    """
    settings = self.speed_up_settings
    ratio = speed_up_step_ratio(settings.curve, settings.multiplier, self.speed_up_count)
    self.speed_up_count += 1
    if settings.axes is not SpeedUpAxes.Y_ONLY:
        self.speed.x *= ratio
    if settings.axes is not SpeedUpAxes.X_ONLY:
        self.speed.y *= ratio
    self._clamp_to_max_speed()

docs.title: PixelSnapMode
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

How a sub-pixel world position is converted to the whole pixel a sprite is drawn at.

NEAREST_HALF_UP suits smooth-motion games (Pong, PaddleSlap): the drawn position tracks the true position as closely as possible with even steps at half pixels. FLOOR suits retro, top-down, and platformer games: like SNES-era fixed-point positions, only the whole-pixel part is drawn, and it behaves the same on both sides of zero.

Source code in src/glitchygames/pixel_snap.py 
class PixelSnapMode(Enum):
    """How a sub-pixel world position is converted to the whole pixel a sprite is drawn at.

    NEAREST_HALF_UP suits smooth-motion games (Pong, PaddleSlap): the drawn position
    tracks the true position as closely as possible with even steps at half pixels.
    FLOOR suits retro, top-down, and platformer games: like SNES-era fixed-point
    positions, only the whole-pixel part is drawn, and it behaves the same on both
    sides of zero.
    """

    NEAREST_HALF_UP = 'nearest_half_up'  # Halves round toward +infinity: 2.5 -> 3, -2.5 -> -2
    NEAREST_EVEN = 'nearest_even'  # Python round(): halves go to the even pixel: 2.5 -> 2
    FLOOR = 'floor'  # Toward -infinity: 2.9 -> 2, -0.5 -> -1
    CEIL = 'ceil'  # Toward +infinity: 2.1 -> 3, -2.9 -> -2
    TRUNCATE = 'truncate'  # Toward zero: -0.5 and 0.5 both -> 0

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ServeSettings:
    """Where and how a ball is served by reset() and serve().

    The defaults suit Pong-style games: a diagonal serve 15-60 degrees above or below
    horizontal, toward either side. For Breakout-style serves use vertical=UP and a
    steeper band; for a fixed serve set both angles equal and pick single directions.

    Attributes:
        minimum_angle_degrees: Smallest serve angle from horizontal (0-90).
        maximum_angle_degrees: Largest serve angle from horizontal (0-90).
        horizontal: Horizontal direction of the serve.
        vertical: Vertical direction of the serve.
        speed: Serve speed in px/s.
        spawn_margin: Minimum distance in px between a served ball's visible circle
            (its collision rect) and each screen edge; on screens too small for it the
            ball is centered.

    """

    minimum_angle_degrees: float = 15.0
    maximum_angle_degrees: float = 60.0
    horizontal: ServeHorizontalDirection = ServeHorizontalDirection.EITHER
    vertical: ServeVerticalDirection = ServeVerticalDirection.EITHER
    speed: float = 250.0
    spawn_margin: int = 50

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Reject serve settings outside their valid ranges.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a field is outside its valid range.

        """
        for field_name in ('minimum_angle_degrees', 'maximum_angle_degrees'):
            angle = getattr(self, field_name)
            if not (math.isfinite(angle) and 0.0 <= angle <= MAXIMUM_SERVE_ANGLE_DEGREES):
                msg = f'{field_name} must be between 0 and 90 degrees, got {angle}'
                raise ValueError(msg)
        if self.minimum_angle_degrees > self.maximum_angle_degrees:
            msg = (
                f'serve angle band is inverted: minimum {self.minimum_angle_degrees} > '
                f'maximum {self.maximum_angle_degrees}'
            )
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if not (math.isfinite(self.speed) and self.speed > 0.0):

class SpeedUpSchedule(Enum):
    """How CONTINUOUS speed-ups are scheduled against elapsed game time.

    All schedules count game time (the dt passed to dt_tick), so pausing pauses them.
    """

    # Every interval of game time; leftover time carries over so the rate does not
    # depend on frame rate. After a long frame, one speed-up is applied and the extra
    # whole intervals are skipped (no burst). The sane default for most games.
    FIXED_RATE = 'fixed_rate'
    # Every elapsed interval, applying several speed-ups in one frame after a long
    # frame. For deterministic simulations or replays that must match elapsed time.
    CATCH_UP = 'catch_up'
    # The next interval starts when a speed-up fires; leftover time is discarded, so
    # speed-ups are never closer than interval but arrive later at lower frame rates.
    MINIMUM_GAP = 'minimum_gap'

class SpeedUpSettings:
    """How and when a ball speeds up.

    Attributes:
        triggers: Events that cause a speed-up (NONE disables automatic speed-ups).
        curve: How speed grows over successive speed-ups.
        axes: Which velocity components are scaled.
        multiplier: Growth per speed-up (>= 1.0); its meaning depends on curve.
        interval: Seconds of game time between CONTINUOUS speed-ups.
        schedule: How CONTINUOUS speed-ups are scheduled (see SpeedUpSchedule).
        max_speed: Cap in px/s on the scaled speed (magnitude for BOTH, the single
            component otherwise), or None for no cap.

    """

    triggers: SpeedUpTrigger = SpeedUpTrigger.NONE
    curve: SpeedUpCurve = SpeedUpCurve.EXPONENTIAL
    axes: SpeedUpAxes = SpeedUpAxes.BOTH
    multiplier: float = 1.1
    interval: float = 1.0
    schedule: SpeedUpSchedule = SpeedUpSchedule.FIXED_RATE
    max_speed: float | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Reject settings that would stop, reverse, or break the ball.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a field is outside its valid range.

        """
        if not (math.isfinite(self.multiplier) and self.multiplier >= 1.0):
            msg = f'speed-up multiplier must be a finite number >= 1.0, got {self.multiplier}'
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if not (math.isfinite(self.interval) and self.interval > 0.0):
            msg = f'speed-up interval must be a positive number of seconds, got {self.interval}'
            raise ValueError(msg)
        if self.max_speed is not None and not (
            math.isfinite(self.max_speed) and self.max_speed > 0.0
        ):
            msg = f'max_speed must be None or a positive number, got {self.max_speed}'
            raise ValueError(msg)

def snap_to_pixel(value: float, mode: PixelSnapMode) -> int:
    """Convert a sub-pixel coordinate to a whole pixel using the given snap mode.

    Args:
        value: The sub-pixel coordinate.
        mode: The rounding rule to apply.

    Returns:
        int: The whole-pixel coordinate.

    """
    match mode:
        case PixelSnapMode.NEAREST_HALF_UP:
            # Not math.floor(value + 0.5): the addition itself rounds at float boundaries,
            # e.g. 0.49999999999999994 + 0.5 == 1.0, and above 2**52 a whole number plus
            # 0.5 rounds to an even neighbor. Subtracting the floor is exact, so compare
            # the fractional part directly.
            whole_pixel = math.floor(value)
            return whole_pixel + 1 if value - whole_pixel >= HALF_PIXEL else whole_pixel
        case PixelSnapMode.NEAREST_EVEN:
            return round(value)
        case PixelSnapMode.FLOOR:
            return math.floor(value)
        case PixelSnapMode.CEIL:
            return math.ceil(value)
        case PixelSnapMode.TRUNCATE:
            return math.trunc(value)
        case _:  # pragma: no cover - every PixelSnapMode is matched above
            assert_never(mode)

def speed_up_step_ratio(curve: SpeedUpCurve, multiplier: float, completed_steps: int) -> float:
    """Return the factor that advances speed from step n to step n + 1 of a curve.

    Applying ratios to the current speed (rather than setting speed from the curve
    directly) keeps changes from collisions between speed-ups, while following the
    curve exactly when nothing else changes the speed.

    Args:
        curve: The growth curve.
        multiplier: Growth per speed-up (>= 1.0).
        completed_steps: Speed-ups already applied (n).

    Returns:
        float: f(n + 1) / f(n) for the curve.

    """
    growth = multiplier - 1.0
    match curve:
        case SpeedUpCurve.LINEAR:
            return (1.0 + (completed_steps + 1) * growth) / (1.0 + completed_steps * growth)
        case SpeedUpCurve.EXPONENTIAL:
            return multiplier
        case SpeedUpCurve.LOGARITHMIC:
            return (1.0 + growth * math.log1p(completed_steps + 1)) / (
                1.0 + growth * math.log1p(completed_steps)
            )
        case _:  # pragma: no cover - every SpeedUpCurve is matched above
            assert_never(curve)

class BasePaddle(Sprite):
    """Base Paddle class."""

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        axis: type[Horizontal | Vertical],
        speed: int,
        name: str,
        color: tuple[int, int, int],
        *,
        x: int,
        y: int,
        width: int,
        height: int,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None = None,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
        collision_sound: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the paddle.

        Args:
            axis (type[Horizontal] | type[Vertical]): The axis to move on.
            speed (int): The speed to move at.
            name (str): The name of the paddle.
            color (tuple[int, int, int]): The color of the paddle.
            x (int): The x position of the paddle.
            y (int): The y position of the paddle.
            width (int): The width of the paddle.
            height (int): The height of the paddle.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.
            collision_sound (str | None): The sound to play on collision.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()  # type: ignore[type-arg]

        super().__init__(name=name, x=x, y=y, width=width, height=height, groups=groups)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

        self.use_gfxdraw = True
        self.moving = False

        # Sprite.__init__ created the image after the display was set, so it already has the
        # display's pixel format (convert() would return an equivalent copy)
        draw.rect(self.image, color, (0, 0, self.width, self.height))
        if collision_sound:
            self.snd = load_sound(collision_sound)
        # Create Speed object based on axis type
        speed_obj = Speed(speed, 0) if axis is Horizontal else Speed(0, speed)
        self._move: Horizontal | Vertical = axis(speed_obj)

        # Sub-pixel position accumulator to prevent rounding loss at high frame rates.
        # Without this, round(speed * tiny_dt) loses fractional pixels each frame,
        # causing paddles to move slower as FPS increases.
        self._sub_pixel_x: float = float(x)
        self._sub_pixel_y: float = float(y)

        self.dirty = 1

    def move_horizontal(self: Self) -> None:
        """Move the paddle horizontally."""
        self.rect.x += self._move.current_speed
        self.dirty = 1

    def move_vertical(self: Self) -> None:
        """Move the paddle vertically."""
        self.rect.y += self._move.current_speed
        self.dirty = 1

    def is_at_bottom_of_screen(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Check if the paddle is at the bottom of the screen.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the paddle is at the bottom of the screen, False otherwise.

        """
        return self.rect.bottom >= self.screen_height

    def is_at_top_of_screen(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Check if the paddle is at the top of the screen.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the paddle is at the top of the screen, False otherwise.

        """
        return self.rect.top <= 0

    def is_at_left_of_screen(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Check if the paddle is at the left of the screen.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the paddle is at the left of the screen, False otherwise.

        """
        assert self.screen is not None

        screen_rect = self.screen.get_rect()
        return self.rect.left + self._move.current_speed < screen_rect.left

    def is_at_right_of_screen(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Check if the paddle is at the right of the screen.

        Returns:
            bool: True if the paddle is at the right of the screen, False otherwise.

        """
        assert self.screen is not None

        screen_rect = self.screen.get_rect()
        return self.rect.right + self._move.current_speed > screen_rect.right

docs.text:
Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Name Type Description bool bool

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

@classmethod
def break_when(cls: type[Sprite], sprite_type: object | None = None) -> None:
    """Register a breakpoint for a sprite type.

    Args:
        sprite_type (object | None): The sprite type to break on.
            None means break on any sprite.

    """
    # The current context's breakpoints: None means disabled, [] means any
    counters = sprite_counters()
    if counters.breakpoints is None:
        counters.breakpoints = []

    # If none, break always.
    if sprite_type is not None:
        # Register the type asked for (not cls): __init__ compares str(type(self)) with it
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==%s', sprite_type)
        counters.breakpoints.append(str(sprite_type))
    else:
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==<any>')

def on_quit_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Handle a quit event.

    Args:
        event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

    """
    # QUIT             none
    self.log.debug('%s: %s', type(self), event)
    # terminate() exists on scenes (SceneInterface), not on Sprite: a sprite that also
    # mixes in a scene's interface ends it here. Cast to Any to allow dynamic dispatch.
    game: Any = self
    game.terminate()

class HorizontalPaddle(BasePaddle):
    """Horizontal Paddle."""

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        name: str,
        size: tuple[int, int],
        position: tuple[int, int],
        color: tuple[int, int, int],
        speed: int,
        *,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None = None,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
        collision_sound: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the horizontal paddle.

        Args:
            name (str): The name of the paddle.
            size (tuple[int, int]): The size of the paddle.
            position (tuple[int, int]): The position of the paddle.
            color (tuple[int, int, int]): The color of the paddle.
            speed (int): The speed to move at.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.
            collision_sound (str | None): The sound to play on collision.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()  # type: ignore[type-arg]
        super().__init__(  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            Horizontal,
            speed,
            name,
            color,
            x=position[0],
            y=position[1],
            width=size[0],
            height=size[1],
            groups=groups,
            collision_sound=collision_sound,
        )

    def _clamp_to_screen(self: Self) -> None:
        """Keep the paddle on screen, stopping it at an edge (so it does not bounce)."""
        assert self.screen is not None
        screen_rect = self.screen.get_rect()
        if self.rect.x < 0:
            self.rect.x = 0
            self._sub_pixel_x = 0.0
            self.stop()
        elif self.rect.x + self.rect.width > screen_rect.right:
            self.rect.x = screen_rect.right - self.rect.width
            self._sub_pixel_x = float(self.rect.x)
            self.stop()

    def left(self: Self) -> None:
        """Move left."""
        assert isinstance(self._move, Horizontal)
        self._move.left()
        self.dirty = 1

    def right(self: Self) -> None:
        """Move right."""
        assert isinstance(self._move, Horizontal)
        self._move.right()
        self.dirty = 1

    def stop(self: Self) -> None:
        """Stop moving."""
        self._move.stop()
        self.dirty = 1

    def speed_up(self: Self) -> None:
        """Speed up."""
        self._move.speed.speed_up_horizontal()
        self._move.current_speed = self._move.speed.x

    @override
    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Update the horizontal paddle with delta time.

        Args:
            dt (float): The delta time.

        """
        # Sub-pixel tracking: accumulate float, round for rect
        movement = self._move.get_movement_with_dt(dt)
        self._sub_pixel_x += movement
        self.rect.x = round(self._sub_pixel_x)
        # Clamped here, in game logic, so the frame's collision sees the paddle on screen
        # (update() runs in the render phase, after collision: the pose rule, CLAUDE.md)
        self._clamp_to_screen()
        self.dirty = 1

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

@classmethod
def break_when(cls: type[Sprite], sprite_type: object | None = None) -> None:
    """Register a breakpoint for a sprite type.

    Args:
        sprite_type (object | None): The sprite type to break on.
            None means break on any sprite.

    """
    # The current context's breakpoints: None means disabled, [] means any
    counters = sprite_counters()
    if counters.breakpoints is None:
        counters.breakpoints = []

    # If none, break always.
    if sprite_type is not None:
        # Register the type asked for (not cls): __init__ compares str(type(self)) with it
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==%s', sprite_type)
        counters.breakpoints.append(str(sprite_type))
    else:
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==<any>')

class VerticalPaddle(BasePaddle):
    """Vertical Paddle."""

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        name: str,
        size: tuple[int, int],
        position: tuple[int, int],
        color: tuple[int, int, int],
        speed: int,
        *,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None = None,  # type: ignore[type-arg]
        collision_sound: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the vertical paddle.

        Args:
            name (str): The name of the paddle.
            size (tuple[int, int]): The size of the paddle.
            position (tuple[int, int]): The position of the paddle.
            color (tuple[int, int, int]): The color of the paddle.
            speed (int): The speed to move at.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.
            collision_sound (str | None): The sound to play on collision.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()  # type: ignore[type-arg]

        super().__init__(  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            Vertical,
            speed,
            name,
            color,
            x=position[0],
            y=position[1],
            width=size[0],
            height=size[1],
            groups=groups,
            collision_sound=collision_sound,
        )

    def _clamp_to_screen(self: Self) -> None:
        """Keep the paddle on screen, stopping it at an edge (so it does not bounce)."""
        if self.rect.y < 0:
            self.rect.y = 0
            self._sub_pixel_y = 0.0
            self.stop()
        elif self.rect.y + self.rect.height > self.screen_height:
            self.rect.y = self.screen_height - self.rect.height
            self._sub_pixel_y = float(self.rect.y)
            self.stop()

    def up(self: Self) -> None:
        """Move up."""
        assert isinstance(self._move, Vertical)
        self._move.up()
        self.dirty = 1

    def down(self: Self) -> None:
        """Move down."""
        assert isinstance(self._move, Vertical)
        self._move.down()
        self.dirty = 1

    def stop(self: Self) -> None:
        """Stop moving."""
        self._move.stop()
        self.dirty = 1

    def speed_up(self: Self) -> None:
        """Speed up."""
        self._move.speed.speed_up_vertical()
        self._move.current_speed = self._move.speed.y

    @override
    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Update the vertical paddle with delta time.

        Args:
            dt (float): The delta time.

        """
        # Sub-pixel tracking: accumulate float, round for rect
        movement = self._move.get_movement_with_dt(dt)
        self._sub_pixel_y += movement
        self.rect.y = round(self._sub_pixel_y)
        # Clamped here, in game logic, so the frame's collision sees the paddle on screen
        # (update() runs in the render phase, after collision: the pose rule, CLAUDE.md)
        self._clamp_to_screen()
        self.dirty = 1

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. @classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

@classmethod
def break_when(cls: type[Sprite], sprite_type: object | None = None) -> None:
    """Register a breakpoint for a sprite type.

    Args:
        sprite_type (object | None): The sprite type to break on.
            None means break on any sprite.

    """
    # The current context's breakpoints: None means disabled, [] means any
    counters = sprite_counters()
    if counters.breakpoints is None:
        counters.breakpoints = []

    # If none, break always.
    if sprite_type is not None:
        # Register the type asked for (not cls): __init__ compares str(type(self)) with it
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==%s', sprite_type)
        counters.breakpoints.append(str(sprite_type))
    else:
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==<any>')

def on_quit_event(self: Self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Handle a quit event.

    Args:
        event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

    """
    # QUIT             none
    self.log.debug('%s: %s', type(self), event)
    # terminate() exists on scenes (SceneInterface), not on Sprite: a sprite that also
    # mixes in a scene's interface ends it here. Cast to Any to allow dynamic dispatch.
    game: Any = self
    game.terminate()

def load_sound(snd_file: str, volume: float = 0.25) -> pygame.mixer.Sound:
    """Load a sound file.

    Args:
        snd_file (str): The sound file to load.
        volume (float): The volume to set the sound to.

    Returns:
        pygame.mixer.Sound: The sound object.

    """
    path: Path = Path(__file__).parent / 'snd_files' / snd_file
    sound = pygame.mixer.Sound(path)
    sound.set_volume(volume)
    return sound
