def print_system_info(self: Self) -> None:
    """Print system information."""
    # General Info
    self.log.info('Pygame Version: %s', pygame.version.ver)
    self.log.info('CPU Count: %s', multiprocessing.cpu_count())
    self.log.info('System: %s', platform.system())
    self.log.info('Machine: %s', platform.machine())
    self.log.info('Platform: %s', platform.platform())
    self.log.info('Platform (Terse): %s', platform.platform(aliased=False, terse=True))
    self.log.info('Processor: %s', platform.processor())
    self.log.info('Release: %s', platform.release())

    # Set up a display mode.
    # Note: pygame.display.init() isn't necessary here
    # because we've already called pygame.init() which
    # initializes all available modules.
    #
    # Let's do a sanity check and make sure we're initialized.
    self.log.info('Display inited: %s', pygame.display.get_init())

    # Display some configuration information.
    self.log.info('SDL Version: %s', pygame.get_sdl_version())
    self.log.info('SDL Byte Order: %s', pygame.get_sdl_byteorder())

    # Dump a bit more info about the configured mode.
    self.log.info('Display Driver: %s', pygame.display.get_driver())
    # Formatted here, not by logging: LogRecord checks isinstance(args[0], Mapping), and
    # pygame-ce's VidInfo raises AttributeError for __class__, which CPython 3.14.2
    # (Pyodide 314's) lets through isinstance (fixed in the pygame-ce fork; see
    # plans/2026-10-23-game-host-and-browser-runner.md)
    self.log.info('Display Info: %s', str(self.display_info))  # ruff: ignore[logging-eager-conversion] - VidInfo breaks LogRecord's isinstance (above)
    self.log.info('Initial Resolution: %s', self.initial_resolution)
    self.log.info('8-bit Modes: %s', pygame.display.list_modes(8))
    self.log.info('16-bit Modes: %s', pygame.display.list_modes(16))
    self.log.info('24-bit Modes: %s', pygame.display.list_modes(24))
    self.log.info('32-bit Modes: %s', pygame.display.list_modes(32))
    self.log.info(
        'Best Color Depth: %s (%s)',
        (pygame.display.mode_ok(self.initial_resolution), self.mode_flags),
        self.mode_flags,
    )
    self.log.info('Window Manager Info: %s', pygame.display.get_wm_info())
    self.log.info('Platform Timer Resolution: %s', pygame.TIMER_RESOLUTION)

def process_controller_event(self: Self, event: events.HashableEvent) -> bool:
    """Process a controller event.

    Args:
        event (events.HashableEvent): The event.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the event was handled, False otherwise.

    """
    if self.controller_manager is None:
        return False

    # Each device's input events come from one layer only: a controller event of a device
    # the game does not see on its controller layer is dropped (handled: deliberately not
    # dispatched; glitchygames/input/input_devices.py, rules 1 and 2)
    if not self.input_devices.dispatches(
        event_type=event.type, instance_id=self._device_event_instance_id(event=event)
    ):
        return True

    # Matched by class (the type's class from events.EVENT_CLASSES, which every event of
    # the type is, however it was built) and then by type where a class covers several
    manager = self.controller_manager
    match event:
        case events.ControllerAxisEvent():
            manager.on_controller_axis_motion_event(event)
        case events.ControllerTouchpadEvent(type=pygame.CONTROLLERTOUCHPADMOTION):
            manager.on_controller_touchpad_motion_event(event)
        case events.ControllerButtonEvent(type=pygame.CONTROLLERBUTTONDOWN):
            manager.on_controller_button_down_event(event)
        case events.ControllerButtonEvent(type=pygame.CONTROLLERBUTTONUP):
            manager.on_controller_button_up_event(event)
        case events.ControllerTouchpadEvent(type=pygame.CONTROLLERTOUCHPADDOWN):
            manager.on_controller_touchpad_down_event(event)
        case events.ControllerTouchpadEvent(type=pygame.CONTROLLERTOUCHPADUP):
            manager.on_controller_touchpad_up_event(event)
        case events.HashableEvent(type=pygame.CONTROLLERSENSORUPDATE):
            manager.on_controller_sensor_update_event(event)
        case _:
            return self._process_controller_device_event(manager=manager, event=event)
    return True

def process_events(
    self: Self, *, should_discard: Callable[[pygame.event.Event], bool] | None = None
) -> bool:
    """Process every event queued this frame.

    ``pygame.event.get()`` removes the whole batch from SDL's queue at once, so every event
    of the batch is handled here: none may be dropped. Each event is judged on its own; an
    event whose type has no entry in ``event_handlers``, or whose handler did not handle
    it, goes to ``process_unimplemented_event``.

    Args:
        should_discard: Returns True for an event to remove from the batch without
            processing it (not counted as unhandled). SceneManager passes
            ``is_discarded_during_transition`` during a transition.

    Returns:
        bool: True if at least one event was dispatched and every dispatched event was
        handled (a raw-event scene's ``process_event`` counts as handled). False if any
        dispatched event was unhandled, or if nothing was dispatched: an empty batch, or
        one whose events were all discarded.

    """
    raw_events = self._pump_events()
    # Polled input is read once per frame, right after the pump, so it agrees with this
    # frame's events; it stays fixed until the next frame's pump, so dt_tick (which runs
    # before this) reads the previous frame's snapshot (glitchygames/input/state.py)
    set_current_input(snapshot=active_sources().input_snapshot())
    dispatched_event_count = 0
    every_event_was_handled = True
    for pygame_event in raw_events:
        if should_discard is not None and should_discard(pygame_event):
            continue
        dispatched_event_count += 1

        # Support scenes processing pygame raw events, bypassing
        # the glitchygames.engine event processing altogether
        if hasattr(self._active_scene, 'process_event'):
            self._active_scene.process_event(pygame_event)  # type: ignore[union-attr] # ty: ignore[call-non-callable]
            continue

        event = events.HashableEvent.from_pygame(pygame_event)

        # Decided per event: a type missing from the map is unhandled
        event_was_handled = False
        if event.type in self.event_handlers:
            event_was_handled = bool(self.event_handlers[event.type](event))

        # If an event is not in the event handler map, or the function
        # called didn't handle the event in question, we'll process it
        # as an unimplemented event
        if not event_was_handled:
            self.process_unimplemented_event(event)
            every_event_was_handled = False

    return dispatched_event_count > 0 and every_event_was_handled

def process_game_event(self: Self, event: events.HashableEvent) -> bool:  # ruff: ignore[too-many-return-statements]
    """Process a game event.

    Args:
        event (events.HashableEvent): The event.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the event was handled, False otherwise.

    """
    # Game events are listed in the order they're most
    # likely to occur in; matched by class (the type's class from events.EVENT_CLASSES),
    # or by type for the types without a class of their own
    match event:
        case events.FpsEvent():
            # FPSEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 1
            self.game_manager.on_fps_event(event)
            return True

        case events.GameEvent():
            # GAMEEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 2
            self.game_manager.on_game_event(event)
            return True

        case events.HashableEvent(type=events.MENUEVENT):
            # MENUEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 3
            self.game_manager.on_menu_item_event(event)
            return True

        case events.ActiveEvent():
            # ACTIVEEVENT      gain, state
            self.game_manager.on_active_event(event)
            return True

        case events.HashableEvent(type=pygame.USEREVENT):
            # USEREVENT        code
            self.game_manager.on_user_event(event)
            return True

        case events.VideoResizeEvent():
            # VIDEORESIZE      size, w, h
            self.game_manager.on_video_resize_event(event)
            return True

        case events.HashableEvent(type=pygame.VIDEOEXPOSE):
            # VIDEOEXPOSE      none
            self.game_manager.on_video_expose_event(event)
            return True

        case events.HashableEvent(type=pygame.SYSWMEVENT):
            # SYSWMEVENT
            self.game_manager.on_sys_wm_event(event)
            return True

        case events.HashableEvent(type=pygame.QUIT):
            # QUIT             none
            self.game_manager.on_quit_event(event)
            return True

        case _:
            pass

    return False

    """Process a joystick event.

    Args:
        event (events.HashableEvent): The event.

    Returns:
        bool: True if the event was handled, False otherwise.

    # Each device's input events come from one layer only: a mapped pad's joystick-layer
    # events are dropped (handled: deliberately not dispatched), as are the events of a
    # device the game does not see (glitchygames/input/input_devices.py, rules 1 and 2)
    if not self.input_devices.dispatches(
        event_type=event.type, instance_id=self._device_event_instance_id(event=event)
    ):
        return True

    # Matched by class (the type's class from events.EVENT_CLASSES), then by type for
    # the button class's two types
    match event:
        case events.JoyAxisEvent():
            # JOYAXISMOTION    instance_id, axis, value
            self.joystick_manager.on_joy_axis_motion_event(event)
        case events.JoyBallEvent():
            # JOYBALLMOTION    instance_id, ball, rel
            self.joystick_manager.on_joy_ball_motion_event(event)
        case events.JoyHatEvent():
            # JOYHATMOTION     instance_id, hat, value
            self.joystick_manager.on_joy_hat_motion_event(event)
        case events.JoyButtonEvent(type=pygame.JOYBUTTONUP):
            # JOYBUTTONUP      instance_id, button
            self.joystick_manager.on_joy_button_up_event(event)
        case events.JoyButtonEvent(type=pygame.JOYBUTTONDOWN):
            # JOYBUTTONDOWN    instance_id, button
            self.joystick_manager.on_joy_button_down_event(event)
        case events.JoyDeviceAddedEvent():
            self.joystick_manager.on_joy_device_added_event(event)
            self._synchronize_input_devices()
        case events.JoyDeviceRemovedEvent():
            self.joystick_manager.on_joy_device_removed_event(event)
            self._synchronize_input_devices()
        case _:
            return False
    return True

def process_unimplemented_event(self: Self, event: events.HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Process an unimplemented event.

    Args:
        event (events.HashableEvent): The event.

    """
    self._record_unhandled_event(event)

    # Debug: Special handling for event type 1543
    if event.type == UNKNOWN_SDL2_EVENT_TYPE_1543:
        event_name = pygame.event.event_name(event.type)
        LOG.debug(
            'process_unimplemented_event received event type %s (%s): %s',
            event.type,
            event_name,
            event,
        )
        LOG.debug('Event dict contents: %s', dict(event))
        LOG.debug(
            'Event attributes: %s',
            [attr for attr in dir(event) if not attr.startswith('_')],
        )

        # Check if this might be a controller event by looking at controller count
        # (through the devices door, glitchygames/input/devices.py)
        try:
            current_controller_count: int = active_sources().devices().controller_count()
            LOG.debug(
                'Current controller count when event 1543 received: %s',
                current_controller_count,
            )
        except pygame.error:
            LOG.debug('Controller system not initialized — skipping controller count check')

        # Check if this event has any controller-related attributes
        LOG.debug('Event has device_index: %s', hasattr(event, 'device_index'))
        LOG.debug('Event has guid: %s', hasattr(event, 'guid'))
        LOG.debug('Event has instance_id: %s', hasattr(event, 'instance_id'))

        # Try to get the raw event object if possible
        LOG.debug('Event type: %s', type(event))
        LOG.debug('Event repr: %r', event)
        LOG.debug(
            'pygame.event.event_name(event.type): %s',
            pygame.event.event_name(event.type),
        )

    if event.type not in self.unimplemented_events:
        self.log.debug(
            '(UNIMPLEMENTED) %s: %s',
            pygame.event.event_name(event.type).upper(),
            event,
        )
        self.unimplemented_events.append(event.type)

    """
    dispatch: dict[int, Callable[..., Any]] = self._build_window_event_dispatch()
    handler = dispatch.get(event.type)
    if handler:
        handler(event)
        return True

    return False

The live voices' pool (--live-voice-pool), the sound library's channels (--sound-channels), then the legacy rest for Sound.play() callers. Reserved as the event managers are made, or earlier, when the game's construction asks for audio (SceneManager.audio), so the audio engine always plays on this run's partition.

def reserved_channel_partition(self: Self) -> ChannelPartition:
    """Partition the mixer's channels once per run, and return the partition (impl 7.1).

    The live voices' pool (``--live-voice-pool``), the sound library's channels
    (``--sound-channels``), then the legacy rest for ``Sound.play()`` callers. Reserved as
    the event managers are made, or earlier, when the game's construction asks for audio
    (``SceneManager.audio``), so the audio engine always plays on this run's partition.

    Only a partition made on a running mixer is kept (ruling R35): without a mixer the
    empty partition is returned, and a later call (once the mixer runs) reserves.

    Returns:
        The partition (empty without a mixer).

    """
    if self.channel_partition is not None:
        return self.channel_partition
    from glitchygames.audio.engine import DEFAULT_LIBRARY_CHANNELS, LEGACY_CHANNELS
    from glitchygames.audio.voices import reserve_channels

    partition = reserve_channels(
        live_pool=int(self.options.get('live_voice_pool', DEFAULT_LIVE_VOICE_POOL)),
        library_channels=int(self.options.get('sound_channels', DEFAULT_LIBRARY_CHANNELS)),
        legacy_channels=LEGACY_CHANNELS,
    )
    self.live_voice_channels = partition.live
    if pygame.mixer.get_init() is not None:
        self.channel_partition = partition
    return partition

@staticmethod
def resolve_target_fps(
    *,
    command_line_target_fps: float | None,
    game: type[Scene] | Scene,
) -> float:
    """Resolve the effective target FPS.

    Order: explicit command line value (0 = uncapped) > the game's TARGET_FPS
    (when not None) > DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS.

    Args:
        command_line_target_fps: The --target-fps value, or None if it was not passed.
        game: The game scene class or instance, which may declare TARGET_FPS.

    Returns:
        float: The effective target FPS (0 means uncapped).

    Raises:
        TypeError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is neither None nor a (non-bool) number.
        ValueError: If the game's TARGET_FPS is negative, NaN or infinite.

    """
    if command_line_target_fps is not None:
        return float(command_line_target_fps)

    # Looked up by name: TARGET_FPS is optional on a game (Scene does not declare it)
    game_target_fps = getattr(game, 'TARGET_FPS', None)
    if game_target_fps is None:
        return DEFAULT_TARGET_FPS

    scene_class = scene_class_of(game)
    # bool is a subclass of int, so it must be rejected explicitly.
    if isinstance(game_target_fps, bool) or not isinstance(game_target_fps, (int, float)):
        message = (
            f'{scene_class.__name__}.TARGET_FPS must be a number or None, '
            f'got {game_target_fps!r}'
        )
        raise TypeError(message)
    if not math.isfinite(game_target_fps) or game_target_fps < 0:
        message = (
            f'{scene_class.__name__}.TARGET_FPS must be a finite number >= 0 '
            f'(0 = uncapped), got {game_target_fps!r}'
        )
        raise ValueError(message)

    return float(game_target_fps)

@classmethod
def set_cursor(
    cls,
    cursor: list[str] | None,
    cursor_black: str = '.',
    cursor_white: str = 'X',
    cursor_xor: str = 'o',
) -> list[str]:
    """Set the cursor.

    Args:
        cursor (list[str]): The cursor.
        cursor_black (str): The black cursor.
        cursor_white (str): The white cursor.
        cursor_xor (str): The xor cursor.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The cursor.

    """
    if not cursor:
        # Cursor setup.
        # Cursor width/height must be a multiple of 8
        cursor = [
            'XX                      ',
            'XXX                     ',
            'XXXX                    ',
            'XX.XX                   ',
            'XX..XX                  ',
            'XX...XX                 ',
            'XX....XX                ',
            'XX.....XX               ',
            'XX......XX              ',
            'XX.......XX             ',
            'XX........XX            ',
            'XX........XXX           ',
            'XX......XXXXX           ',
            'XX.XXX..XX              ',
            'XXXX XX..XX             ',
            'XX   XX..XX             ',
            '     XX..XX             ',
            '      XX..XX            ',
            '      XX..XX            ',
            '       XXXX             ',
            '       XX               ',
            '                        ',
            '                        ',
            '                        ',
        ]

    cursor_width: int = len(cursor[0])
    cursor_height: int = len(cursor)

    # Compile our cursor so we can draw it to the screen.
    cursor_data, cursor_mask = pygame.cursors.compile(
        cursor,
        black=cursor_black,
        white=cursor_white,
        xor=cursor_xor,
    )

    # Now set the cursor as the active cursor.
    pygame.mouse.set_cursor((cursor_width, cursor_height), (0, 0), cursor_data, cursor_mask)

    return cursor

docs.title: start()
docs.text:
Start the game engine.

However the run ends, the teardown (_shutdown: recordings closed) runs first; if the teardown itself raises, the run exits ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR (both errors logged). An exception raised before start(), in __init__, is not mapped: it exits with Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap; see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay (--replay-trace) that ends normally exits with its own code (ReplayResult.exit_code under its exit policy), watched or headless.

How it ends (_begin_start and _crash_boundary raise these): RuntimeError if the game is not initialized; SystemExit with ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR after an uncaught exception (logged with its traceback), ExitCode.INTERRUPTED after Ctrl-C (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay short (ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code (ExitCode.SUCCESS, ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED or ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT for a truncated recording).

def start(self: Self) -> None:
    """Start the game engine.

    However the run ends, the teardown (``_shutdown``: recordings closed) runs first; if the
    teardown itself raises, the run exits ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` (both errors logged).
    An exception raised before start(), in ``__init__``, is not mapped: it exits with
    Python's default 1 (each game has its own entry point, so there is no one place to wrap;
    see glitchygames/exit_codes.py). A replay (``--replay-trace``) that ends normally exits
    with its own code (``ReplayResult.exit_code`` under its exit policy), watched or
    headless.

    How it ends (``_begin_start`` and ``_crash_boundary`` raise these): RuntimeError if the
    game is not initialized; SystemExit with ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` after an uncaught
    exception (logged with its traceback), ``ExitCode.INTERRUPTED`` after Ctrl-C
    (KeyboardInterrupt), or whatever status a SystemExit raised during the run carries (a
    signal handler's, a game's own), except a game's own successful exit that cuts a replay
    short (``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED``; a rebaseline ends normally then, with what the game
    ran); at the normal end of a replay, with the replay's exit code (``ExitCode.SUCCESS``,
    ``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED`` or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for a truncated recording).
    """
    profiler = self._begin_start()
    with self._crash_boundary(profiler=profiler):
        self._run_game()

For a host that must not block (a browser: glitchygames/host.py). The run is start()'s, inside the same crash boundary (the same teardown and exit codes), but its frames are driven by one awaited wait_for_tick() per outer tick: a live game's by GameHost.run_async (an inner frame on the ticks TickPacer picks for the target FPS), a watched replay's by its viewer (run_watched_replay_async: the tick's inner frames, then the viewer's outer frame).

Raises:

If the run is a headless replay (it never holds between frames, so it would never give control back), or (from _begin_start) the game is not initialized.

--compare-trace is refused before anything starts, exiting (exit_with) with ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED: OLD is replayed by a child process, which a browser page (the host start_async is for) cannot start (_refuse_a_comparison_in_a_browser).

Source code in src/glitchygames/engine/game_engine.py 
async def start_async(self: Self, *, wait_for_tick: Callable[[], Awaitable[float]]) -> None:
    """Start the game engine, giving control back to the caller between frames.

    For a host that must not block (a browser: glitchygames/host.py). The run is
    ``start()``'s, inside the same crash boundary (the same teardown and exit codes), but
    its frames are driven by one awaited ``wait_for_tick()`` per outer tick: a live game's
    by ``GameHost.run_async`` (an inner frame on the ticks ``TickPacer`` picks for the
    target FPS), a watched replay's by its viewer (``run_watched_replay_async``: the tick's
    inner frames, then the viewer's outer frame).

    Args:
        wait_for_tick: Waits for the next outer tick (a browser animation frame) and
            returns its timestamp in seconds.

    It ends as ``start()`` does (see there).

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the run is a headless replay (it never holds between frames, so
            it would never give control back), or (from ``_begin_start``) the game is not
            initialized.

    ``--compare-trace`` is refused before anything starts, exiting (``exit_with``) with
    ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED``: OLD is replayed by a child process, which a browser page
    (the host start_async is for) cannot start (``_refuse_a_comparison_in_a_browser``).

    """
    self._refuse_a_comparison_in_a_browser()
    # Chosen first (a run start_async cannot drive is refused before anything starts), but
    # called inside the boundary
    run_frames: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]
    if self.host is not None:
        run_frames = functools.partial(
            self.host.run_async, scene_manager=self.scene_manager, wait_for_tick=wait_for_tick
        )
    elif self.replay_sources is not None and not self.replay_sources.options.headless:
        run_frames = functools.partial(
            run_watched_replay_async,
            scene_manager=self.scene_manager,
            viewer=self.replay_sources.viewer,
            wait_for_tick=wait_for_tick,
        )
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(ASYNC_RUN_NEEDS_HOST_MSG)
    profiler = self._begin_start()
    with self._crash_boundary(profiler=profiler):
        if self._begin_run():
            if self._power_on_plays():
                sound_cues = self._power_on_sound_cues()
                self._hand_back_power_on(
                    outcome=await play_power_on_async(
                        screen=self.screen,
                        sources=active_sources(),
                        wait_for_tick=wait_for_tick,
                        sound_cues=sound_cues,
                    ),
                    sound_cues=sound_cues,
                )
            self._build_game(paced_by_timer=False)
            await run_frames()

Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame).

The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of every save store the doors opened (saves), the descriptors of devices opened (devices) and the enumeration answers given (device_enumeration). Then RecordingSources are installed around the active doors and record every frame from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown (exit_on_signal, installed by start), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt). stop_trace_recording (called by _shutdown) closes the file.

Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises SourcesAlreadyRunningError (from install_sources; glitchygames/sources.py).

def start_trace_recording(self: Self, *, path: Path) -> GameplayRecorder:
    """Start recording the session to a trace file (before the first frame).

    The header also holds what the run took in before recording started: a snapshot of
    every save store the doors opened (``saves``), the descriptors of devices opened
    (``devices``) and the enumeration answers given (``device_enumeration``). Then
    ``RecordingSources`` are installed around the active doors and record every frame
    from what passes through them (glitchygames/recording.py). SIGTERM (and SIGHUP on
    Unix, SIGBREAK on Windows) ends a started run through the normal teardown
    (``exit_on_signal``, installed by ``start``), and so does SIGINT (KeyboardInterrupt).
    ``stop_trace_recording`` (called by ``_shutdown``) closes the file.

    Recording must start before the first frame: afterwards installing its doors raises
    ``SourcesAlreadyRunningError`` (from ``install_sources``; glitchygames/sources.py).

    Args:
        path: The recording's file.

    Returns:
        The recorder.

    Raises:
        TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError: If this engine is already recording.

    """
    if self.trace_recorder is not None:
        message = (
            f'start_trace_recording() was called while recording to '
            f'{self.trace_recorder.path}; one run records once'
        )
        raise TraceRecordingAlreadyStartedError(message)
    inner = active_sources()
    registry = inner.devices()
    # A store a run started with --record-trace opened before recording started is in the
    # header as first opened: the first scene's setup() may have written to it since, and
    # the replay runs that setup() again (LiveSources.first_open_save_snapshots, read
    # through the host's doors in a hosted run)
    first_open_snapshots: Mapping[str, dict[str, Any]] = (
        inner.first_open_save_snapshots if isinstance(inner, LiveSources | HostSources) else {}
    )
    # A rebaseline copies these fields from the replayed recording instead (rebaseline.py)
    header = {
        **self.trace_recording_header(),
        SAVES_HEADER_FIELD: {
            namespace: (
                first_open_snapshots[namespace]
                if namespace in first_open_snapshots
                else save_namespace_snapshot(saves=store)
            )
            for namespace, store in inner.opened_save_namespaces.items()
        },
        DEVICES_HEADER_FIELD: [
            descriptor.to_json() for descriptor in registry.take_opened_descriptors()
        ],
        DEVICE_ENUMERATION_FIELD: [
            answer.to_json() for answer in registry.take_enumeration_answers()
        ],
    }
    recorder = GameplayRecorder(path=path, header=header)
    install_sources(sources=RecordingSources(inner=inner, recorder=recorder))
    self.trace_recorder = recorder
    self.log.info('Recording gameplay to %s (random seed %s)', path, self.random_seed)
    return recorder

def stop_trace_recording(self: Self) -> None:
    """Close the recording, if one is running.

    The ``RecordingSources`` stay installed (the run is ending); with the recorder closed
    they only delegate.
    """
    recorder = self.trace_recorder
    if recorder is None:
        return
    self.trace_recorder = None
    recorder.close()
    if recorder.write_failed:
        self.recording_write_failed = True

def trace_recording_header(self: Self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the header of a --record-trace recording.

    Returns:
        The game and scene class names, engine, pygame and Python versions, the screen
        size, every command-line option (JSON-safe), the start time and the random seed.

    """
    active_scene = self.scene_manager.active_scene
    engine_version = installed_engine_version()
    # The running game's scene (_build_game built it before any recording starts)
    game: Scene = self.running_game.instance
    game_class = type(game)
    return {
        'game_class': game_class.__name__,
        # With the class name, tells apart two games whose classes share a name
        'game_module': game_class.__module__,
        # The game's logical name, which replays compare (glitchygames/logical_names.py):
        # unchanged when the game's code moves
        GAME_HEADER_FIELD: logical_name(scene_class=game_class),
        'scene_class': None if active_scene is None else type(active_scene).__name__,
        'engine_version': engine_version,
        'pygame_version': pygame.version.ver,
        'python_version': platform.python_version(),
        'screen_size': [self.screen_width, self.screen_height],
        # Path options relative to the project root (stored_options)
        'options': {
            str(name): json_safe_value(value)
            for name, value in stored_options(options=self.options).items()
        },
        # The origin of the run's wall clock from here on, recorded and replayed alike:
        # recorded_at plus the frame clock (RecordingSources.wall_clock_time; rule 9 of
        # glitchygames/replay/driver.py), so game code reading it replays exactly
        RECORDED_AT_HEADER_FIELD: clock.raw_wall_clock_time().isoformat(),
        'random_seed': self.random_seed,
        # The engine's custom event ids this run allocated: a replay in a process that
        # allocated them otherwise moves the recorded events to its own (BUGS.md #211.1)
        CUSTOM_EVENT_TYPES_HEADER_FIELD: custom_event_types_header(),
        # Each run's provenance, newest first (glitchygames/recording_history.py): this one
        # paces its frames when it has a target FPS (0 is uncapped)
        MEASUREMENT_RUNS_HEADER_FIELD: [
            self.measurement_run(
                game=game_class,
                processing_paced=self.scene_manager.target_fps > 0,
                rebaselined_from=None,
            ).to_json()
        ],
    }

def unhandled_event_report(self: Self) -> list[str]:
    """Describe every unhandled event type, most frequent first.

    Each line names the type (pygame's event name and its number, so custom and unknown
    types still show), its count, when it was first seen and the first event's attribute
    names, e.g. ``JOYDEVICEADDED (1541) x1, first at 0.3 s, attributes: device_index, guid``.

    Returns:
        One line per type; empty when every event was handled.

    """
    records = sorted(
        self.unhandled_events.items(),
        key=lambda item: item[1].count,
        reverse=True,
    )
    return [
        f'{pygame.event.event_name(event_type).upper()} ({event_type}) x{record.count}, '
        f'first at {record.first_seen_seconds:.1f} s, '

class GoldenTraceSceneManager(SceneManager):
    """The engine's SceneManager plus a frame step without pacing, timing or FPS events.

    It adds methods only, so a game runs exactly as it does under SceneManager.start().
    """

    @classmethod
    def install(cls) -> GoldenTraceSceneManager:
        """Make a fresh instance the SceneManager singleton (GameEngine then adopts it).

        Returns:
            The new scene manager.

        """
        SceneManager._reset()
        cls._reset()
        manager = cls()
        # Stored as the current engine context's entry for SceneManager in the scene managers
        # slot, so a plain SceneManager() call answers with it too
        current_context().value(slot=SCENE_MANAGERS_SLOT)[SceneManager] = manager
        return manager

    @classmethod
    def uninstall(cls) -> None:
        """Clear the singleton so the next game starts from a fresh scene manager."""
        SceneManager._reset()
        cls._reset()

    def run_frame(self) -> None:
        """Run one frame the way SceneManager.start() does, without pacing or timing."""
        self._run_frame()

class EventProxy:
    """Proxy for events."""

    log: logging.Logger = LOG

    def __init__(self: Self, event_source: object) -> None:
        """Initialize the event proxy.

        Args:
            event_source: The event source.

        """
        super().__init__()
        # No proxies for the root class.
        self.proxies: list[Any] = []

        # This is used for leave objects which
        # don't have their own proxies.
        #
        # Subclassed managers that set their own proxy
        # will not have this.
        self.event_source = event_source

    def unhandled_event(self: Self, *_args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Handle unhandled events.

        Args:
            *_args: Additional positional arguments (unused).
            **kwargs: The keyword arguments.

        """
        # inspect.stack()[1] is the call frame above us, so this should be reasonable.
        event_handler = inspect.stack()[1].function

        event = kwargs.get('event')

        event_trigger: dict[str, Any] | None = kwargs.get('trigger')

        self.log.debug(
            'Unhandled Event %s: %s->%s Event Trigger: %s',
            event_handler,
            self.event_source,
            event,
            event_trigger,
        )

    def __getattr__(self: Self, attr: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
        """Get an attribute.

        This method is called when an attribute is not found.

        Args:
            attr: The attribute to get.

        Returns:
            The attribute.

        """
        return self.unhandled_event

def __getattr__(self: Self, attr: str) -> Callable[..., Any]:
    """Proxy calls to the active scene.

    Args:
        attr (str): The attribute to proxy.

    Returns:
        Callable[..., Any]: The callable object.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If the attribute is not an on_*_event method.

    """
    # Attempt to proxy the call to the active scene.
    if attr.startswith('on_') and attr.endswith('_event'):
        try:
            # Pass it to the active scene for handling
            return getattr(self.active_scene, attr)
        except AttributeError:
            # Pass it to the game engine for suppression
            return getattr(self.game_engine, attr)
    else:
        message = f"'{type(self)}' object has no attribute '{attr}'"
        raise AttributeError(message)

def __init__(self: Self) -> None:
    """Initialize the scene manager."""
    # Prevent re-initialization of singleton
    if self._initialized:
        return

    super().__init__()

    # None until the display is initialized (set later); get_surface() never raises
    self.screen = pygame.display.get_surface()
    self.update_type: str = 'update'
    # The engine's options (the game_engine setter sets them: the engine's own dict);
    # empty until an engine is set
    self.engine_options: dict[str, Any] = {}
    self.fps_log_interval_ms: int = 1000
    self.target_fps: float = 0.0
    self.dt: float = 0.0
    # The last frame's measured start-to-start time (dt is what the frame-time door made of
    # it); only the performance statistics read it (_performance_frame_seconds)
    self._measured_frame_seconds: float = 0.0
    self.timer: Any = 0
    self._game_engine: GameEngine | None = None
    self.active_scene: Scene | None = None
    self.next_scene: Scene | None = self.active_scene
    self.previous_scene: Scene | None = self.active_scene
    self.quit_requested: bool = False
    # Frames finished this run; the doors' end_frame receives each frame's number
    self.frame_number: int = 0
    # Whether the last run_frame_step was a hold (the doors presented the latest frame again,
    # a watched replay's outer tick) rather than a frame
    self.last_step_was_held: bool = False
    self._initialize_supervision()

    # Scene transition support
    self._active_transition: Transition | None = None  # Transition object during effect
    # The requested switch, as its next scene and its transition
    self._pending_transition: tuple[Scene | None, Transition] | None = None

    self.pacing_fallback_clock: pygame.time.Clock = pygame.time.Clock()

    # SCREEN shake lives here (not on a scene) so it outlives scene switches
    self.screen_shake: ScreenShake = ScreenShake()
    # The display no longer shows what the surface holds (a shaken or overlaid frame was
    # presented, frames ran unpresented, or a playback scope ended): the next presented
    # frame updates the whole display (_show_frame)
    self._display_is_stale: bool = False
    # The time this frame spent presenting (_present_frame): left out of its processing time
    self._frame_present_seconds: float = 0.0
    self.debug_overlay: DebugOverlay = DebugOverlay()
    self.rumble: RumbleController = RumbleController()

    self._live_rumble_behind_scope: RumbleController | None = None
    self._live_audio: LiveAudio | None = None
    # This context's performance manager (glitchygames.performance.adaptive_clamping): the
    # scene manager and it are both per engine context, so it is looked up once here and
    # every frame's tracking skips the slot read (AdaptiveClamping() is a slot read)
    from glitchygames.performance import AdaptiveClamping

    self.performance_manager: AdaptiveClamping = AdaptiveClamping()

    # Jitter tracking attributes
    self._jitter_samples: list[int] = []
    self._jitter_last_log_ns: int = 0
    self._jitter_interval_start_ns: int = 0
    self._jitter_late_frames: int = 0
    self._timer_prev_deadline_ns: int | None = None
    # When the last FPS event was posted (frame-clock seconds); start() sets it
    self._previous_fps_event_seconds: float = 0.0
    # In-game playback (glitchygames/replay/playback.py): the scope requested for the next
    # frame, the scope in progress, and how the last one went
    self._requested_playback: PlaybackRequest | None = None

    self._playback_requesting_scene: Scene | None = None

    # an audio engine made then counts its compiles as setup (sound engine impl 6.5)

    self._last_playback_result: ReplayResult | None = None

def __init_subclass__(cls, **keyword_arguments: Any) -> None:
    """Wrap the subclass's own ``__init__`` so its shared instance is initialized once.

    Args:
        **keyword_arguments: Passed on to ``object.__init_subclass__``.

    """
    super().__init_subclass__(**keyword_arguments)
    own_initializer = cls.__dict__.get('__init__')
    if own_initializer is not None:
        # Through type.__setattr__: the subclass's __init__ is replaced by its wrapper, whose
        # signature a type checker cannot match to the base __init__ it overrides
        type.__setattr__(cls, '__init__', _initialize_once(own_initializer))

def __new__(cls) -> Self:
    """Return this engine context's scene manager of this class, made on first use."""
    instance = _scene_manager_for_class(scene_manager_class=cls)
    if instance is None:
        instance = super().__new__(cls)
        current_context().value(slot=SCENE_MANAGERS_SLOT)[cls] = instance
    # Not always a cls: a subclass asked after its base was made gets the base's manager
    # (_scene_manager_for_class walks the MRO). The cast keeps the subclass type callers expect
    return cast('Self', instance)

def add_supervisor(self: Self, *, supervisor: Supervisor) -> None:
    """Call ``supervisor`` once per frame at the supervisor slot (supervision.py).

    One the scope's code adds while a playback scope plays (the rebuilt scene's setup() or
    cleanup(), its event handlers) belongs to the scope and is removed when it ends

def audio_for(self: Self, *, game_engine: GameEngine | None) -> AudioEngine:
    """The engine context's audio engine, made on first use from ``game_engine``.

    ``audio`` with the game engine given rather than read from ``game_engine``, which
    ``GameEngine`` sets only as it builds the game: the CRT power-on asks before that
    (rulings R34, R35), and the engine it makes is the one ``audio`` returns afterwards.

    Args:
        game_engine: The game engine whose partition and sound options the audio engine is
            made from, or None for the default partition with cache ``ram``.

    Returns:
        The audio engine (the existing one, whatever ``game_engine`` is given, once made).
    """
    from glitchygames.audio.engine import (
        BYTES_PER_MEGABYTE,
        DEFAULT_CACHE_MEMORY_MEGABYTES,
        AudioEngine,
        default_channel_partition,
        install_audio_engine,
    )
    from glitchygames.audio.library import CacheMode

    audio_engine = _existing_audio_engine()
    if audio_engine is not None:
        return audio_engine
    partition = (
        default_channel_partition()
        if game_engine is None
        else game_engine.reserved_channel_partition()
    )
    options: Mapping[str, Any] = {} if game_engine is None else game_engine.options
    return install_audio_engine(
        engine=AudioEngine(
            partition=partition,
            cache=CacheMode(options.get('sound_cache', CacheMode.RAM.value)),
            memory_limit_bytes=int(
                options.get('sound_cache_memory', DEFAULT_CACHE_MEMORY_MEGABYTES)
            )
            * BYTES_PER_MEGABYTE,
            scene_source=self._scene_for_audio,
            frame_number=self.frame_number,
            # Made in gameplay (a first audio call in dt_tick), its compiles are the frame's
            setup_mode=self._scene_in_setup is not None or self._awaiting_first_logic_frame,
        )
    )

def begin_frames(self: Self) -> float:
    """Begin the run's frames: the frame clock's first reading and the first frame's dt.

    Returns:
        The perf_counter() reading the first frame starts at.

    """
    frame_start_seconds: float = clock.raw_counter_seconds()

    # above, as before (a replay's frame-time door returns the recorded first dt)
    self._set_frame_time(measured=clock.raw_counter_seconds() - frame_start_seconds)
    mark_frames_started()
    return frame_start_seconds

docs.title: end_playback()
docs.text:
End the playback scope in progress (a demo, an instant replay); the game goes on.

Honoured from a supervisor (add_supervisor; the scope then ends once that frame ended, so the frame is played and compared whole) and between frames (at once). Its outcome's reason is 'ended_by_game'. Asked anywhere else in a frame, it is ignored (logged at DEBUG): inside a scope the only scene code running is the played scene's, whose call did nothing in its original run (no scope was playing then), as recorded_playback_answer keeps a playback request's answer. A control event handler's call (add_control_event_handler) is honoured only when a supervisor's own record_control_event ran it, inside the slot; the handlers of a frame's re-applied control events (a replayed breakpoint) run before the supervisors, outside the slot, so their call is ignored. Nothing when no scope is in progress (a requested one still begins).

The player's presses reach no scene during an instant replay; a supervisor reads the player's polled input from playback_player_input to decide when to end it.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/scene.py 
def end_playback(self: Self) -> None:
    """End the playback scope in progress (a demo, an instant replay); the game goes on.

    Honoured from a supervisor (``add_supervisor``; the scope then ends once that frame
    ended, so the frame is played and compared whole) and between frames (at once). Its
    outcome's reason is ``'ended_by_game'``. Asked anywhere else in a frame, it is ignored
    (logged at DEBUG): inside a scope the only scene code running is the played scene's,
    whose call did nothing in its original run (no scope was playing then), as
    ``recorded_playback_answer`` keeps a playback request's answer. A control event
    handler's call (``add_control_event_handler``) is honoured only when a supervisor's own
    ``record_control_event`` ran it, inside the slot; the handlers of a frame's re-applied
    control events (a replayed breakpoint) run before the supervisors, outside the slot, so
    their call is ignored. Nothing when no scope is in progress (a requested one still
    begins).

    The player's presses reach no scene during an instant replay; a supervisor reads the
    player's polled input from ``playback_player_input`` to decide when to end it.
    """
    session = self._playback_session
    if session is None:
        return
    if not self._frame_in_progress:
        self._exit_playback(reason='ended_by_game')
        return
    if not self._in_supervisor_slot:
        LOG.debug('end_playback() asked by the played scene is ignored: it did nothing live')
        return
    sources = session.sources
    # First reason found wins, as PlaybackSources._note_end keeps it (the class has no
    # room for a public method that would do this)
    if sources.end_reason is None:
        sources.end_reason = 'ended_by_game'

def handle_event(self, event: events.HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Handle pygame events.

    Args:
        event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

    """
    # Check for focused sprites first
    if self.active_scene and self.active_scene.all_sprites:
        focused_sprites = [
            sprite
            for sprite in self.active_scene.all_sprites
            if hasattr(sprite, 'is_active') and sprite.is_active
        ]

        if focused_sprites and event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            # Scene does not expose a handle_event() method; focused sprites
            # receive key events through the normal event dispatch pipeline.
            return

    # Only process other events if no focused sprites handled it
    if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
        self.log.info('POSTING QUIT EVENT')
        self.quit_requested = True

def instant_replay(self: Self) -> bool:
    """Show the active scene's last ``INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS``, then go on where it was.

    The scene is rebuilt from its start in a playback scope from the start of the next
    frame and plays its instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py): the frames
    before the last ``INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS`` of frame time run unseen, unpaced and silent,
    the rest are shown at the game's pace, then the live scene, never touched, goes on
    exactly where it was (glitchygames/replay/playback.py, rules 6 and 7). The player's
    presses do not end it; the game may, with ``end_playback``. How it ended:
    ``last_playback_outcome``.

    Returns:
        True when the instant replay will begin. False (logged; nothing happens) when the
        active scene keeps no journal (its class sets no ``INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS``, or
        its first logic frame has not run), the journal is past the scene's
        ``MAX_INSTANT_REPLAY_FAST_FORWARD_SECONDS``, or a playback is already starting or
        playing. Inside a playback of the journal, what the recorded scene was answered
        (nothing is requested: scopes do not nest).

def journal_pumped_events(
    self: Self,
    *,
    raw_events: list[pygame.event.Event],
    posts_before_pump: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
    origins: list[str] | None,
    redelivered_events: list[RedeliveredEvent],
) -> None:
    """Hand one pump's batch to the instant-replay journal (``GameEngine._pump_events``).

    Nothing while no journal is kept or a playback scope serves the frame (its scene is
    not the live session's).

    Args:

        raw_events=raw_events,
        posts_before_pump=posts_before_pump,
        origins=origins,

def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> None:
    """Handle the debug overlay keys, then forward key-down events as the proxy would.

    F3 toggles the overlay and F4 cycles its panels, unless a sprite in the active scene has
    keyboard focus (is_active), so typing into text fields is never intercepted. Every other
    key goes to the active scene (every Scene has the handler, and records the press first),
    or to the game engine when there is no active scene.

    Args:
        event (KeyEvent): The key-down event.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If there is no active scene and the game engine has no handler.

    """
    if event.key in OVERLAY_KEYS and not self._active_scene_has_focused_sprite():
        self.debug_overlay.handle_key(key=event.key)
        return
    if self.active_scene is not None:
        # Recorded before dispatch, so a quit-key release knows this scene saw the press
        self.active_scene.record_key_press(key=event.key)
        self.active_scene.on_key_down_event(event)
    elif self.game_engine is not None and hasattr(self.game_engine, 'on_key_down_event'):
        self.game_engine.on_key_down_event(event)
    else:
        message = (
            f"'{type(self)}' object has no attribute 'on_key_down_event': neither the "
            'active scene nor the game engine provides it'
        )
        raise AttributeError(message)

Play a recording as an attract-mode demo, then return to then.

The demo plays in a playback scope (glitchygames/replay/playback.py) from the start of the next frame, at the game's speed, and ends at the recording's end, at the first key or button press (exit_on_input), at a divergence (logged at WARNING, demo diverged: <description>) or at the recording's own quit. A recording cut off part way plays to its last complete frame and ends as truncated. A recording that cannot be played (missing, unreadable, of another game, with no scene start to begin at) is logged at WARNING, naming the demo and the reason, and nothing starts; so is a request while another playback is starting or playing. How it ended: last_playback_outcome.

required then Scene

def play_recording(self: Self, *, path: Path, then: Scene) -> None:
    """Play a recording as an attract-mode demo, then return to ``then``.

    The demo plays in a playback scope (glitchygames/replay/playback.py) from the start of
    the next frame, at the game's speed, and ends at the recording's end, at the first key
    or button press (``exit_on_input``), at a divergence (logged at WARNING, ``demo
    diverged: <description>``) or at the recording's own quit. A recording cut off part
    way plays to its last complete frame and ends as ``truncated``. A recording that
    cannot be played (missing, unreadable, of another game, with no scene start to
    begin at) is logged at WARNING, naming the demo and the reason, and nothing starts;
    so is a request while another playback is starting or playing. How it ended:
    ``last_playback_outcome``.

    Args:
        path: The recording.
        then: The scene to make active when the demo ends (usually the scene asking).

    """
    # Function-level import, for layering: glitchygames.replay.playback imports
    # glitchygames.scenes (it needs Scene), and scenes must not import replay at runtime, so
    # a module-level import here would be a cycle.
    from glitchygames.replay.playback import (
        DEMO_PLAYBACK,
        PlaybackOptions,
        start_playback_from_recording,
    )

    start_playback_from_recording(
        manager=self,
        path=path,
        then=then,
        options=PlaybackOptions(exit_on_input=True, kind=DEMO_PLAYBACK),
    )

docs.text:
Record a supervisor action in this frame and hand it to its handlers.

The event is recorded (with a read-only copy of data) before any handler runs. Every handler for kind runs, in registration order, even when an earlier one raises; then the first handler exception is re-raised, and any later ones are logged, so a broken handler fails loudly without silently skipping the others.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/scene.py 
def record_control_event(self: Self, *, kind: str, data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Record a supervisor action in this frame and hand it to its handlers.

    The event is recorded (with a read-only copy of ``data``) before any handler runs.
    Every handler for ``kind`` runs, in registration order, even when an earlier one
    raises; then the first handler exception is re-raised, and any later ones are logged,
    so a broken handler fails loudly without silently skipping the others.
    """
    control_event = ControlEvent(kind=kind, data=data)
    self._frame_control_events.append(control_event)
    first_error: Exception | None = None
    scope_handlers = [
        scope_handler
        for scope_kind, scope_handler in self._scope_control_event_handlers
        if scope_kind == kind
    ]
    for handler in list(self._control_event_handlers.get(kind, [])):
        try:
            self._run_live_or_scope_code(
                is_scope_code=handler in scope_handlers,
                call=lambda handler=handler: handler(control_event),
            )
        except Exception as error:
            if first_error is None:
                first_error = error
            else:
                LOG.exception('Another %r control event handler failed', kind)
    if first_error is not None:
        raise first_error

def recorded_playback_answer(self: Self) -> bool | None:
    """Return what a playback request got in the frame being played, inside a scope.

    A scene played back from its instant-replay journal asks for playbacks where the live
    scene did (an instant replay after every goal): each request is answered with the next
    answer that frame recorded, and nothing is requested (scopes do not nest;
    glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 8). ``start_playback`` asks this first.

    Returns:
        The recorded answer; None outside a scope, or when the frame recorded none left.

    """
    session = self._playback_session
    if session is None:
        return None
    answers = session.sources.replay.recorded_playback_answers
    return answers.popleft() if answers else None

def request_playback(self: Self, *, request: PlaybackRequest) -> bool:
    """Enter a playback scope at the start of the next frame (glitchygames/replay/playback.py).

    A scope begins between frames, so the rebuilt scene's first frame is a whole frame, as
    the recorded one was, and the frame that asked runs to its end on the live doors. If
    the active scene changed by then (a ``next_scene`` switch at the end of the frame that
    asked), the request is dropped (logged): the scene to return to has gone.

    Args:
        request: The scope to enter (``start_playback`` builds it).

    Returns:
        False (logged) when a scope is already requested or in progress: scopes do not
        nest. True otherwise.

    """
    if self._requested_playback is not None or self.in_playback_scope:
        LOG.warning('A playback is already starting or playing; %s not started', request.kind)
        return False
    self._requested_playback = request
    # A scene asking from its setup() (a title screen starting the next demo as a demo
    # returns to it) is the one active from then on
    self._playback_requesting_scene = (
        self._scene_in_setup if self._scene_in_setup is not None else self.active_scene
    )
    return True

def run_frame_step(self: Self, *, frame_start_seconds: float, paced: bool = True) -> float:
    """Run one step of the frame loop: one frame, or a held frame presented again.

    Args:
        frame_start_seconds: The perf_counter() reading this frame starts at (the previous
            step's return value, or ``begin_frames``').
        paced: True (``start``) paces the frame as always: the timer backend's deadline,
            else the pygame clock, or the doors' pacing. False (an outer driver that waits
            for its own tick, ``GameHost.run_async``) never waits or calibrates a timer:
            the wait for the next tick is the pacing, and is measured into the next
            frame's start-to-start dt like a pacing sleep.

    Returns:
        The perf_counter() reading the next frame starts at.

    """
    # The doors may hold the loop between frames (a paused watched replay): no frame
    # runs, the last one is presented again with the doors' overlay
    self.last_step_was_held = active_sources().hold_frame()
    if self.last_step_was_held:
        # Unless the hold ended the run (the viewer quit): nothing more to show
        if not active_sources().stop_requested:
            self._present_held_frame()
        # The hold is not part of the next frame's measured time
        return clock.raw_counter_seconds()

    # Frame pacing using timer backend when available
    # None without an engine (a bare SceneManager) or before the engine made its timer
    game_engine = self.game_engine
    timer = game_engine.timer if game_engine is not None and paced else None
    # The doors may pace the frame themselves (0.0: not at all, in a headless replay);
    # an unpaced step is never paced here
    paced_seconds = active_sources().paced_frame_seconds() if paced else 0.0
    period_ns = 0
    if timer is not None:
        period_ns = (
            timer.start_frame(self.target_fps)
            if paced_seconds is None
            else round(paced_seconds * 1_000_000_000)
        )

    # The frame's work starts here. A paced frame starts where the last one closed (after
    # its pacing sleep); an unpaced one now: the outer driver's wait since the last step's
    # closing reading is this frame's pacing, in its dt but never in its processing time
    work_start_seconds = frame_start_seconds if paced else clock.raw_counter_seconds()
    self._run_frame()

    # The frame's processing time: its work, without the pacing sleep that follows
    processing_seconds = clock.raw_counter_seconds() - work_start_seconds

    return self._finish_frame(
        frame_start_seconds=frame_start_seconds,
        timer=timer,
        period_ns=period_ns,
        paced_seconds=paced_seconds,
        processing_seconds=processing_seconds,
    )

Start the scene manager.

Each frame starts at the previous frame's closing perf_counter() reading and ends in _finish_frame, which sets self.dt once, to that frame's start-to-start period, so logic in frame N receives the time frame N-1 took (engine audit #15).

The blocking frame loop: begin_frames, then run_frame_step while should_run_frames, then end_frames. An outer driver that must give control back between frames (a browser; glitchygames/host.py GameHost.run_async) runs the same steps itself, one per tick, unpaced.

def start(self: Self) -> None:
    """Start the scene manager.

    Each frame starts at the previous frame's closing perf_counter() reading and ends in
    _finish_frame, which sets ``self.dt`` once, to that frame's start-to-start period, so
    logic in frame N receives the time frame N-1 took (engine audit #15).

    The blocking frame loop: ``begin_frames``, then ``run_frame_step`` while
    ``should_run_frames``, then ``end_frames``. An outer driver that must give control back
    between frames (a browser; glitchygames/host.py ``GameHost.run_async``) runs the same
    steps itself, one per tick, unpaced.
    """
    frame_start_seconds = self.begin_frames()
    while self.should_run_frames():
        frame_start_seconds = self.run_frame_step(frame_start_seconds=frame_start_seconds)
    self.end_frames()

@dataclass
class InputScript:
    """Scripted input for one game.

    Attributes:
        key_events: Frame number -> key events posted before that frame runs.
        placements: Frame number -> callables that adjust the active scene before that frame
            runs (used to put the player somewhere a short script cannot walk to).
        per_frame: Optional callable run before every frame; it returns extra events to post
            (a paddle tracking the ball).

    """

    key_events: dict[int, list[pygame.event.Event]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    placements: dict[int, list[Callable[[Scene], None]]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    per_frame: Callable[[Scene], list[pygame.event.Event]] | None = None

    def at(self, frame_number: int, *events: pygame.event.Event) -> None:
        """Post events before a frame.

        Args:
            frame_number: The frame the events are posted before.
            *events: The events to post.

        """
        self.key_events.setdefault(frame_number, []).extend(events)

    def tap(self, frame_number: int, key: int, *, held_frames: int) -> None:
        """Press a key before one frame and release it a number of frames later.

        Args:
            frame_number: The frame the key is pressed before.
            key: The pygame key code.
            held_frames: How many frames the key stays down.

        """
        self.at(frame_number, press(key))
        self.at(frame_number + held_frames, release(key))

    def place(self, frame_number: int, placement: Callable[[Scene], None]) -> None:
        """Adjust the active scene before a frame.

        Args:
            frame_number: The frame the placement runs before.
            placement: The callable that adjusts the scene.

        """
        self.placements.setdefault(frame_number, []).append(placement)

@contextlib.contextmanager
def deterministic_environment(*, save_root: Path) -> Generator[None]:
    """Replace the save directory, then restore it.

    Randomness needs no replacement: ``_start_game`` passes ``--random-seed`` when given one.
    Clocks need none either: a game clock read from Scene.game_time is driven by the harness's
    fixed dt.

    Args:
        save_root: Directory the games' save files go to.

    Yields:
        None, while the replacements are in place.

    """

    def temporary_save_directory(app_name: str) -> Path:
        return save_root / app_name

    replacements: list[tuple[object, str, object]] = [
        (save_manager_module, 'get_save_directory', temporary_save_directory),
    ]
    originals = [(owner, name, getattr(owner, name)) for owner, name, _ in replacements]
    try:
        for owner, name, replacement in replacements:
            setattr(owner, name, replacement)
        yield
    finally:
        for owner, name, original in originals:
            setattr(owner, name, original)

def discard_environment_events() -> None:
    """Drop events the host environment posted; keep the rest in order.

    ``pygame.event.get(eventtype=...)`` does not return pygame-ce's window events (they are
    split out of SDL's single window event only by an unfiltered get), so the whole queue is
    drained and every non-environment event is posted again.
    """
    kept_events = [
        event for event in pygame.event.get() if event.type not in ENVIRONMENT_EVENT_TYPES
    ]
    for event in kept_events:
        pygame.event.post(event)

@contextlib.contextmanager
def golden_game(
    *,
    scene_class: type[Scene],
    random_seed: int | None,
    extra_arguments: list[str] | None = None,
) -> Generator[GoldenTraceSceneManager]:
    """Start a game in the harness with temporary saves; tear it all down afterwards.

    Args:
        scene_class: The game's scene class.
        random_seed: The run's master seed (``--random-seed``), or None (``seed_arguments``).
        extra_arguments: More command-line arguments (``--replay-trace PATH``).

    Yields:
        The scene manager with the game scene active.

    """
    with (
        tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='golden-trace-saves-') as save_directory,
        deterministic_environment(save_root=Path(save_directory)),
    ):
        manager = _start_game(
            scene_class=scene_class, random_seed=random_seed, extra_arguments=extra_arguments
        )
        try:
            yield manager
        finally:
            engine = manager.game_engine
            if engine is not None:
                engine.stop_trace_recording()
            pygame.event.clear()
            GoldenTraceSceneManager.uninstall()

Build the input script a MODULE:NAME reference names (--input-script).

The contract: NAME is a callable in module MODULE that takes no arguments and returns a fresh InputScript (as each of our games' builders in scripts/golden_inputs.py does: a script holds state, such as the keys a per-frame input holds, so each run builds its own). MODULE is imported with the current directory searched first, as python -m and python -c search it, so a project's own module (scripts.golden_inputs, run from the repository root) is found from its console script too.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default reference str

required

Returns:

Type Description InputScript

The input script it builds.

Raises:

Type Description InputScriptError

If the reference is not MODULE:NAME, its module does not import, it has no such name, the name is not callable, or the call returns something other than an InputScript.

Source code in src/glitchygames/replay/tools/golden_traces.py 
def load_input_script(*, reference: str) -> InputScript:
    """Build the input script a ``MODULE:NAME`` reference names (``--input-script``).

    The contract: ``NAME`` is a callable in module ``MODULE`` that takes no arguments and
    returns a fresh ``InputScript`` (as each of our games' builders in scripts/golden_inputs.py
    does: a script holds state, such as the keys a per-frame input holds, so each run builds its
    own). ``MODULE`` is imported with the current directory searched first, as ``python -m``
    and ``python -c`` search it, so a project's own module (``scripts.golden_inputs``, run from
    the repository root) is found from its console script too.

    Args:
        reference: ``MODULE:NAME``.

    Returns:
        The input script it builds.

    Raises:
        InputScriptError: If the reference is not ``MODULE:NAME``, its module does not import,
            it has no such name, the name is not callable, or the call returns something other
            than an ``InputScript``.

    """
    module_name, separator, name = reference.partition(REFERENCE_SEPARATOR)
    if not separator or not module_name or not name:
        message = f'{reference!r} is not MODULE:NAME'
        raise InputScriptError(message)
    current_directory = str(Path.cwd())
    searched_first = current_directory not in sys.path
    if searched_first:
        sys.path.insert(0, current_directory)
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module(module_name)
    except ImportError as error:
        message = f'{reference!r}: module {module_name!r} does not import ({error})'
        raise InputScriptError(message) from error
    finally:
        if searched_first:
            sys.path.remove(current_directory)
    builder: object = getattr(module, name, None)
    if not callable(builder):
        message = f'{reference!r}: {module_name} has no callable {name!r}'
        raise InputScriptError(message)
    script: object = builder()
    if not isinstance(script, InputScript):
        message = f'{reference!r} returned a {type(script).__name__}, not an InputScript'
        raise InputScriptError(message)
    return script

def record_trace(
    *,
    scene_class: type[Scene],
    script: InputScript,
    frame_count: int,
    recording_path: Path | None = None,
    random_seed: int | None = None,
    **hooks: Unpack[RecordTraceHooks],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a game headless with its scripted input and record every sprite each frame.

    Args:
        scene_class: The game's scene class.
        script: Its input script (a fresh one: a per-frame input holds state across frames).
        frame_count: How many frames to run.
        recording_path: If given, the engine also records the run there as ``--record-trace``
            would (GameEngine.start_trace_recording), for checking recordings against the
            harness's own frames.
        random_seed: The run's master seed, passed as ``--random-seed``; None rolls one, as
            any run does (our golden traces pass ``RANDOM_SEED``).
        **hooks: Optional callbacks into the run, by keyword (``RecordTraceHooks``).

    Returns:
        The trace: the game (the scene class's logical name,
        ``glitchygames.logical_names.logical_name``), frame seconds and one record per frame;
        with no ``random_seed`` given, the seed the run rolled too (``random_seed``, decision
        17's row 1: a golden is compared by running it again under its seed). A trace under a
        given seed names none, so ours keep their bytes. A caller that names its games otherwise
        sets ``game`` itself (our golden traces name theirs by game key:
        scripts/record_golden_traces.py).

    """
    frame_observer = hooks.get('frame_observer')
    before_recording = hooks.get('before_recording')
    frames: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    sprite_ids = StableSpriteIds()
    with golden_game(scene_class=scene_class, random_seed=random_seed) as manager:
        engine = manager.game_engine
        assert engine is not None
        rolled_seed = (
            {} if random_seed is not None else {RANDOM_SEED_HEADER_FIELD: engine.random_seed}
        )
        if before_recording is not None:
            assert manager.active_scene is not None
            before_recording(manager.active_scene)
        if recording_path is not None:
            engine.start_trace_recording(path=recording_path)
        for frame_number in range(frame_count):
            manager.dt = FRAME_SECONDS
            discard_environment_events()
            assert manager.active_scene is not None
            for placement in script.placements.get(frame_number, []):
                placement(manager.active_scene)
            if script.per_frame is not None:
                for event in script.per_frame(manager.active_scene):
                    pygame.event.post(event)
            for event in script.key_events.get(frame_number, []):
                pygame.event.post(event)
            manager.run_frame()
            frames.append(
                sample_scene_frame(
                    frame_number=frame_number,
                    scene=manager.active_scene,
                    sprite_ids=sprite_ids,
                )
            )
            if frame_observer is not None:
                frame_observer(
                    frame_number=frame_number,
                    scene=manager.active_scene,
                    sprite_ids=sprite_ids,
                )
    return {
        'game': logical_name(scene_class=scene_class),
        'frame_seconds': FRAME_SECONDS,
        **rolled_seed,
        'frames': frames,
    }

docs.text:
Replay a recording made by record_trace(recording_path=...) through the harness.

Key events and per-frame input come from the recording (the replay's event pump), so they are not posted again. The script's placements are not input: they move sprites directly, like a supervisor, so they are applied again on the same frames, before the frame runs, as record_trace applies them. (A placement that posts events, such as a key release before a pause, posts real events the replay drops: the recording serves them.)

The result is settled as GameEngine._shutdown settles it (finish_run): a harness that stops before the recording's last frame reports a length divergence.

    are not posted again. The script's placements are not input: they move sprites directly,
    like a supervisor, so they are applied again on the same frames, before the frame runs, as
    record_trace applies them. (A placement that posts events, such as a key release before a
    pause, posts real events the replay drops: the recording serves them.)

    The result is settled as GameEngine._shutdown settles it (``finish_run``): a harness that
    stops before the recording's last frame reports a length divergence.

    Args:
        scene_class: The game's scene class.
        script: The input script the recording was made with (its placements are applied).
        path: The recording.
        frame_limit: Stop after this many frames even if the replay goes on (None: run until
            the replay stops).

    Returns:
        The replay's result.

    """
    # Headless: a watched replay would pause at its end (or divergence) instead of stopping
    # No seed: a replay runs under its recording's (another is refused)
    with golden_game(
        scene_class=scene_class,
        random_seed=None,
        extra_arguments=['--replay-trace', str(path), '--headless'],
    ) as manager:
        engine = manager.game_engine
        assert engine is not None
        sources = engine.replay_sources
        assert sources is not None
        frame_number = 0
        while (
            not sources.stop_requested
            and manager.active_scene is not None
            and (frame_limit is None or frame_number < frame_limit)
        ):
            # The harness steps frames without start()/_finish_frame, so it asks the frame-time
            # door itself: the first call returns frame 0's dt, each later call the next frame's
            manager.dt = sources.frame_seconds(measured=FRAME_SECONDS)
            for placement in script.placements.get(frame_number, []):
                placement(manager.active_scene)
            manager.run_frame()
            frame_number += 1
        sources.finish_run()
    return sources.result

docs.title: identity
docs.text:
A game's identity, read from the game object alone: its package, directory and console script.

The game passes itself to the engine (GameEngine(game=Game)) and declares nothing else (stage D's decision 13); the tools find what they need about it from that object:

  • package: the top-level package of the scene class's module (paddleslap for paddleslap.game; __main__ for a game run as a script);
  • package directory: where that package is, from importlib.util.find_spec (looked up, never imported), or the loaded module's file when the import system can't find it (a script's __main__);
  • console script: the installed console script whose entry point (module:function) is in that package and starts the game's module (children.console_script_for_game_module);
  • distribution: the installed distribution that holds the package (importlib.metadata.packages_distributions), else the console script's distribution (an editable install's metadata lists no packages, only its .pth file); looked up when first read, never as the identity is made: the lookup scans every installed file (0.6 s here, and far more on a loaded machine), and no tool reads it;
  • source revision (game_source_revision): the package directory's commit, looked up as the engine's own is; each run records it beside the engine's, and a ledger row names it.

Whatever isn't found is None: a game no console script starts, or one no distribution holds, still has an identity.

@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class GameIdentity:
    """What the tools know about a game from its scene class.

    Attributes:
        package: The top-level package of the scene class's module.
        package_directory: Where that package is, or None when it can't be found.
        console_script: The installed console script that starts the game, or None.
        find_distribution: How to find ``distribution`` when it is first read (not compared:
            two identities of one game are equal however each finds it).

    """

    package: str
    package_directory: Path | None
    console_script: str | None
    find_distribution: Callable[[], str | None] = dataclasses.field(
        default=no_distribution, compare=False, repr=False, kw_only=True

    def distribution(self) -> str | None:
        """The installed distribution holding the package, or None (found when first read).

        Returns:
            What ``find_distribution`` finds, then the same answer for every later read.

        """
        return self.find_distribution()

def console_script_identity(*, console_script: str) -> GameIdentity:
    """Return the identity of the game an installed console script starts, without importing it.

    What the ``glitchygames`` command knows of a game it names by its console script and does
    not run (``unmeasured``): its package is the top-level package of the console script's entry
    point (``paddleslap`` for ``paddleslap:main``), the package a game's scene is in for every
    game a console script starts here (Brave Adventurer's launcher: ``brave_adventurer_modes``,
    its title scene's). The distribution is the console script's own (the one that installs
    it), not looked up through ``importlib.metadata.packages_distributions``: that scans every
    installed file (most of a second per game), and a console script is installed with the
    package it starts. A console script no installed package has is ``game_entry_point``'s
    ``KeyError``.

    Args:
        console_script: The console script's name (``[project.scripts]``).

    Returns:
        The identity (``package_directory`` None when the package isn't found).

    """
    entry_point = game_entry_point(console_script=console_script)
    package = entry_point.value.partition(ENTRY_POINT_SEPARATOR)[0].partition('.')[0]
    return GameIdentity(
        package=package,
        package_directory=package_directory_of(package=package),
        console_script=console_script,
        find_distribution=functools.partial(console_script_distribution, entry_point=entry_point),
    )

def distribution_of(*, package: str, entry_point: EntryPoint | None) -> str | None:
    """Return the installed distribution holding a package.

    Returns:
        The first distribution the metadata lists the package in, else the starting console
        script's distribution (an editable install lists only its ``.pth`` file), else None.

    """
    listed = importlib.metadata.packages_distributions().get(package)
    if listed:
        return listed[0]
    return None if entry_point is None or entry_point.dist is None else entry_point.dist.name
