def game_identity(*, game: type[Scene] | Scene) -> GameIdentity:
    """Return a game's identity from its scene class (or a scene of that class).

    Args:
        game: The game's scene class, as passed to ``GameEngine(game=...)``, or a scene.

    Returns:
        Its package, package directory, console script and distribution (see the module
        docstring); each of the last three is None when not found. The distribution is looked
        up when first read (``GameIdentity.distribution``), with the import path as it is then.

    """
    scene_class = game if isinstance(game, type) else type(game)
    game_module = scene_class.__module__
    package = game_module.partition('.')[0]
    entry_point = starting_entry_point(package=package, game_module=game_module)
    return GameIdentity(
        package=package,
        package_directory=package_directory_of(package=package),
        console_script=None if entry_point is None else entry_point.name,
        find_distribution=functools.partial(
            distribution_of, package=package, entry_point=entry_point
        ),
    )

def game_source_revision(*, game: type[Scene] | Scene) -> SourceRevision | None:
    """Return the source revision of a game's package: the commit a ledger row names.

    Looked up in the game's package directory (``GameIdentity.package_directory``) as the
    engine's is in its own (``glitchygames.build_info.package_source_revision``: a checkout
    that tracks the package, then an archive, then a build stamp, else unknown), so a game
    outside this repository names its own commit. Only the directory is looked up here, with
    the function ``game_identity`` uses for it: the console script and distribution lookups
    scan every installed distribution (a third of a second), and a run looks this up as it
    starts.

    Args:
        game: The game's scene class, as passed to ``GameEngine(game=...)``, or a scene.

    Returns:
        The revision (``UNKNOWN_REVISION`` when none answered), or None when the game's package
        directory can't be found: the run then names only the engine's.

    """
    scene_class = game if isinstance(game, type) else type(game)
    package_directory = package_directory_of(package=scene_class.__module__.partition('.')[0])
    if package_directory is None:
        return None
    return package_source_revision(package_directory=package_directory)

Return where a top-level package (or module) is.

The import system's spec first: a package's directory, or a single module's file's directory. A game run as a script (__main__) is not looked up there (under python -m, __main__'s spec names the module that was run, not this game): its loaded module's file is used, as for any module the import system can't find.

Returns:

Type Description Path | None

Source code in src/glitchygames/replay/tools/identity.py 
def package_directory_of(*, package: str) -> Path | None:
    """Return where a top-level package (or module) is.

    The import system's spec first: a package's directory, or a single module's file's
    directory. A game run as a script (``__main__``) is not looked up there (under
    ``python -m``, ``__main__``'s spec names the module that was run, not this game): its
    loaded module's file is used, as for any module the import system can't find.

    Returns:
        The directory, or None when neither finds a file.

    """
    specification = None if package == SCRIPT_MODULE else _specification(package=package)
    if specification is not None and specification.submodule_search_locations:
        return Path(next(iter(specification.submodule_search_locations)))
    if specification is not None and specification.has_location and specification.origin:
        return Path(specification.origin).parent
    loaded = sys.modules.get(package)
    module_file = None if loaded is None else getattr(loaded, '__file__', None)
    return None if module_file is None else Path(module_file).parent

Source code in src/glitchygames/replay/tools/identity.py 
def starting_entry_point(*, package: str, game_module: str) -> EntryPoint | None:
    """Return the installed console script in a package that starts a game module.

    Returns:
        Its entry point, or None when none or more than one does.

    """
    in_package = [
        entry_point
        for entry_point in installed_console_scripts()
        if entry_point.value.partition(ENTRY_POINT_SEPARATOR)[0].partition('.')[0] == package
    ]
    try:
        name = console_script_for_game_module(entry_points=in_package, game_module=game_module)
    except KeyError:
        return None
    return next(entry_point for entry_point in in_package if entry_point.name == name)

docs.title: measure
docs.text:
The measure, unmeasured and clear-published tools: recordings in the run ledger.

Design: plans/2026-10-23-recording-metrics-1-frame-performance-history.md (Part 1 of plans/2026-10-23-recording-metrics.md); moved here from scripts/replay_metrics.py (Part 3, Stage D, Task D6). The run ledger keeps one row per recording per run (glitchygames.recording_metrics.LedgerRow) beyond the ten runs a recording holds. A project may publish it ([tool.glitchygames] published-ledger: ours, with the docs site on gh-pages); rows measured here wait in the pending ledger (pending-ledger) until a publish takes them, or go into the ledger directory as row files (--rows-directory: our pre-commit hook, scripts/measure_staged_replays.py).

measure (nox -s replay-metrics; nox -s docs-deploy runs it first):

  1. refuses a game whose commit is unknown, and one with uncommitted changes, unless --allow-dirty (the rows say so; such a trial never counts as measuring its commit) or --skip-dirty (measure nothing and succeed: what docs-deploy passes). The revision is the game's (identity.game_source_revision; the engine's for a game whose package isn't found), the commit a ledger row names (Task D3), so a game outside the engine's checkout is judged by its own;
  2. for each of the game's recordings (recordings.game_recordings: its goldens in the project and its bundled demos; or the PATHs given) not already measured for this commit on this machine (published, pending or a row file; --force measures again): rebaselines it headless into a temporary file through the game's console script (children.rebaseline_recording_headless), so the run measures every frame's processing time and records its provenance. Each replays under its own recorded seed (Stage D's decision 17): --random-seed is refused, as verify refuses it;
  3. appends the rebaselined recording's rows (ledger_rows_from_rebaseline: the measurement, then each run the recording held, unless already in the ledger) to the pending ledger. A run the recording held is written (to the pending file, or with --rows-directory as row files) only if it landed (rows_to_write: measured on a commit that is on the project's landed-ref without uncommitted changes; none at all without that ref, said once when a run would have been judged; LandedCommits asks git once per commit). "Already in the ledger" compares rows with a moved recording's old path resolved to its new one (LedgerRow.held_key, by the project's recording-renames).

The children must run the game's own package (an editable install, as uv run gives), or they cannot name its commit: a row whose commit is not the game's is a failure.

unmeasured lists the recordings measure would measure (without --force): one ledger name per line on standard output, then a summary on standard error. clear-published (after a publish succeeded) removes the pending rows the published ledger now holds; the rest stay pending.

The front ends (glitchygames/replay/tools/registry.py):

  • On the game: --measure [PATH ...] (measure_on_the_game), --unmeasured and --clear-published run from GameEngine.__init__, before the engine starts pygame: the game is neither built nor shown. With no PATHs, --measure measures the game's own recordings, as --unmeasured lists them.
  • The command: glitchygames measure [PATH ...] [--game GAME ...] (measure_command) starts each game (--game, else the project's [tool.glitchygames] games) as a child with --measure and combines their exit codes (combined_exit_code); with PATHs, each is measured by the game its header names, or by the one --game. When the games come from the settings, a golden none of them replays is a failure, named with why (a workspace member that is not installed: uv sync --all-packages). glitchygames unmeasured [--game GAME ...] reads the recordings and the ledger itself, without starting a game it can name by its console script; glitchygames clear-published is the game flag's work.

Every tool finds the project as verify does (verify.verify_project_root: the nearest directory with [tool.glitchygames], else the nearest pyproject.toml) and reads its settings from there; a pending ledger or rows directory in the project's local directory (.glitchygames/) is created through settings.ensure_local_directory.

Exit codes: SUCCESS; OPTIONS_REFUSED for an unknown commit or uncommitted changes (and for a seed, --allow-dirty with --skip-dirty, a game no console script starts given PATHs, or a GAME that names nothing); UNUSABLE_INPUT for settings that can't be read, or a pending ledger that exists but can't be read (no permission, not UTF-8: UnreadableLedgerError, naming it, as performance-pages says it); INTERNAL_ERROR when a recording could not be measured (the others are still measured).

docs.title: LandedCommits
docs.text:
Which commits are on a repository's landed ref, each asked of git once per measurement.

The answer for a commit cannot change while one measurement runs, and every recording's history repeats the same few commits, so rows_to_write asks this instead of git. Whether the landed ref exists is looked up on the first question, and a missing one is said then, once: a measurement with no history run to judge says nothing about it.

Source code in src/glitchygames/replay/tools/measure.py 
class LandedCommits:
    """Which commits are on a repository's landed ref, each asked of git once per measurement.

    The answer for a commit cannot change while one measurement runs, and every recording's
    history repeats the same few commits, so ``rows_to_write`` asks this instead of git. Whether
    the landed ref exists is looked up on the first question, and a missing one is said then, once:
    a measurement with no history run to judge says nothing about it.
    """

    def __init__(self, *, repository: Path, landed_ref: str) -> None:
        """Answer for ``repository``'s ``landed_ref`` (``[tool.glitchygames]`` ``landed-ref``)."""
        self.repository = repository
        self.landed_ref = landed_ref
        self._landed_ref_present: bool | None = None
        self._landed_by_commit: dict[str, bool] = {}

    def has_landed(self, *, commit: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether ``commit`` is on the landed ref (False for every commit without one).

        Returns:
            True when the commit is the landed ref or one of its ancestors.

        """
        if self._landed_ref_present is None:
            self._landed_ref_present = landed_ref_exists(
                repository=self.repository, landed_ref=self.landed_ref
            )
            if not self._landed_ref_present:
                sys.stdout.write(
                    f'No {self.landed_ref} in this repository: no history rows written (earlier '
                    'runs count as landed only on that branch)\n'
                )
        if not self._landed_ref_present:
            return False
        if commit not in self._landed_by_commit:
            self._landed_by_commit[commit] = commit_has_landed(
                repository=self.repository, commit=commit, landed_ref=self.landed_ref
            )
        return self._landed_by_commit[commit]

def child_unmeasured(
    *, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game: str, launch: GameLaunch
) -> tuple[int, int, list[str]]:
    """List a game's unmeasured recordings by starting it with ``--unmeasured``, and read it back.

    For a game the command can't read without starting it (a script path, ``MODULE:CALLABLE``,
    a module). The child's standard output (its listing) is captured and returned, so it joins
    the command's own listing (which the pre-commit hook reads, redirected in its own process),
    and its summary's count joins the command's; its standard error is passed on. pygame's
    banner is hidden in the child, so its standard output is the listing alone.

    Args:
        tool: The unmeasured tool.
        arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.
        game: The game, as named.
        launch: How to start it.

    Returns:
        The child's exit status, how many recordings it looked at (its summary's count, else
        how many it listed), and the ledger names it listed.

    """
    say(tool=tool, message=f'running {game} ({FORM_DESCRIPTIONS[launch.form]})')
    finished = run_command(
        command=[*launch.command, *tool.child_arguments(arguments=arguments)],
        environment={**os.environ, PYGAME_BANNER_VARIABLE: '1'},
        timeout_seconds=None,
        capture_output=OutputCapture.APART,
        working_directory=arguments.project_root,
    )
    error = finished.stderr or ''
    sys.stderr.write(error)
    listed = [line for line in (finished.stdout or '').splitlines() if line.strip()]
    total = unmeasured_total(text=error)
    return finished.returncode, len(listed) if total is None else total, listed

def clear_published(*, pending_path: Path, published_text: str) -> None:
    """Remove the pending rows the published ledger holds (a publish took them).

    Args:
        pending_path: The pending ledger (removed when no row is left).
        published_text: The published ledger's text (after the publish).

    A pending ledger that exists but can't be read raises ``read_pending_ledger``'s
    ``UnreadableLedgerError``, before anything is changed.

    """
    pending = read_pending_ledger(path=pending_path)
    if not pending:
        sys.stdout.write(f'No pending rows in {pending_path}\n')
        return
    published_keys = {row.key for row in parse_ledger(text=published_text).rows}
    remaining = [row for row in pending if row.key not in published_keys]
    if remaining:
        pending_path.write_text(ledger_text(rows=remaining), encoding='utf-8')
    else:
        pending_path.unlink()
    removed = len(pending) - len(remaining)
    sys.stdout.write(
        f'{removed} published row{"" if removed == 1 else "s"} removed, '
        f'{len(remaining)} still pending in {pending_path}\n'
    )

def clear_published_in(*, project_root: Path, pending: str | None, prefix: str) -> ExitCode:
    """Remove the pending rows the project's published ledger holds.

    Args:
        project_root: The project.
        pending: ``--pending``'s value, or None (the project's ``pending-ledger``).
        prefix: What starts a line about the settings (the tool's).

    Returns:
        ``ExitCode.SUCCESS``, or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for settings or a pending ledger
        that can't be read (said on standard error).

    """
    try:
        settings = read_settings(project_root=project_root, prefix=prefix)
    except ProjectSettingsError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{prefix} {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    try:
        clear_published(
            pending_path=pending_path_of(
                given=pending, settings=settings, project_root=project_root
            ),
            published_text=published_ledger_text(
                project_root=project_root, published_ledger=settings.published_ledger
            ),
        )
    except UnreadableLedgerError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{prefix} {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

def combined_exit_code(*, statuses: Sequence[int]) -> ExitCode:
    """Return how a run over several games (or recordings) exits, from each one's exit status.

    Args:
        statuses: The exit statuses, in the order they ran.

    Returns:
        ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` when every one succeeded (or there was none); otherwise the first
        failure's own code, or ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` for a status that is no ``ExitCode``
        (a child killed by a signal).

    """
    for status in statuses:
        if status == ExitCode.SUCCESS:
            continue
        try:
            return ExitCode(status)
        except ValueError:
            return ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

def describe_measurement(*, row: LedgerRow, seconds: float, pending_rows: int) -> str:
    """Describe one recording's measurement on one line.

    Args:
        row: Its measurement's row.
        seconds: How long the rebaseline took.
        pending_rows: How many rows it added to the pending ledger.

    Returns:
        ``RECORDING: N frames in S s, processing p50 ..., p99 ..., max ..., headroom avg ...
        fps (5% low ..., 5% high ...), K frames changed behaviour, R rows pending`` (the
        headroom FPS of the unpaced replay's processing times:
        ``recording_metrics.describe_processing_fps``; left out for a summary without its
        slice means).

    """
    summary = row.summary
    timing = 'no processing times'
    if summary is not None:
        timing = (
            f'processing p50 {_milliseconds(summary.p50_processing_seconds)}, p99 '
            f'{_milliseconds(summary.p99_processing_seconds)}, max '
            f'{_milliseconds(summary.max_processing_seconds)}'
        )
        headroom = describe_processing_fps(summary=summary)
        if headroom is not None:
            timing = f'{timing}, headroom {headroom}'
    return (
        f'{row.recording}: {row.frame_count} frames in {seconds:.1f} s, {timing}, '
        f'{row.frames_changed} frames changed behaviour, {pending_rows} rows pending'
    )

def game_package(*, game: str) -> str | None:
    """Return the top-level import package of a game, in any of the forms GAME takes.

    As ``children.resolve_game`` reads them: a script path (the package it is in, if any), an
    entry point ``MODULE:CALLABLE`` (its module's), an installed console script
    (``identity.console_script_identity``'s), else a module (its own top-level package).

    Args:
        game: The game, as ``[tool.glitchygames] games`` or ``--game`` names it.

    Returns:
        The package, or None for a script in no package.

    """
    if SCRIPT_PATH_SEPARATOR in game or game.endswith(SCRIPT_SUFFIX):
        return top_level_package_of_script(script=Path(game))
    if ENTRY_POINT_SEPARATOR in game:
        return game.partition(ENTRY_POINT_SEPARATOR)[0].partition('.')[0]
    try:
        return console_script_identity(console_script=game).package
    except KeyError:
        return game.partition('.')[0]

def git_listed_files(*, project_root: Path) -> list[Path] | None:
    """Return the files git keeps in a checkout: tracked, and untracked but not ignored.

    The browser bundles' rule (``git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard``,
    scripts/git_checkout.py), so ignored trees (``build/``, ``dist/``, other checkouts inside
    the repository) are none of the project's.

    Args:
        project_root: The project.

    Returns:
        The files (absolute), or None when the project is not in a git checkout (or git is
        missing, or does not answer within ``GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS``): the caller then walks the
        project (``walked_files``).

    """
    try:
        listed = run_command(
            command=['git', 'ls-files', '-z', '--cached', '--others', '--exclude-standard'],
            environment=os.environ,
            timeout_seconds=GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            capture_output=OutputCapture.APART,
            working_directory=project_root,
        )
    except OSError, TimeoutExpired:
        return None
    if listed.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return [project_root / name for name in (listed.stdout or '').split('\0') if name]

    as ``glitchygames.bundled_demos`` finds them in an installed package; bookmarked copies are
    not demos.

    Args:
        path: The file.

    Returns:
        True for a bundled demo; False for a path that is no file (a tracked demo deleted only
        from the working tree, which git still lists).

    """
    package = path.parent.parent
    return (
        path.is_file()
        and path.parent.name == BUNDLED_DEMO_DIRECTORY_NAME
        and path.name.endswith(DEMO_SUFFIX)
        and (package / PACKAGE_MARKER).is_file()
        and not (package.parent / PACKAGE_MARKER).is_file()
        and not is_bookmarked_copy(path=path)
    )

def is_measured_here(
    *,
    rows: Iterable[LedgerRow],
    recording: str,
    code_tree: str | None,
    commit: str | None,
    machine: str,
) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a recording was measured for this code on this machine already.

    By code tree when one is given (the hook's): any row of that tree, recording and machine.
    Else by commit (``is_measured``); a commit that is unknown is never measured (each trial
    measures again).

    Args:
        rows: The rows known (published, pending and row files).
        recording: The recording's ledger name.
        code_tree: The code tree measured, or None.
        commit: The game's commit, or None when unknown.
        machine: This machine's label.

    Returns:
        True when it is measured.

    """
    if code_tree is not None:
        return any(
            row.code_tree == code_tree and row.recording == recording and row.machine == machine
            for row in rows
        )
    if commit is None:
        return False
    return is_measured(rows=rows, recording=recording, commit=commit, machine=machine)

def measure(
    *,
    settings: MeasureSettings,
    recordings: Sequence[tuple[str, Path]],
    published_text: str,
) -> MeasureResult:
    """Measure recordings and append their rows to the pending ledger (see the docstring).

    Args:
        settings: The measurement's settings.
        recordings: ``(console script, path)`` pairs to measure.
        published_text: The published ledger's text.

    Returns:
        What was measured, skipped and failed; ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` and nothing measured
        when the pending ledger exists but can't be read (said on standard error).

    """
    refusal = _refusal(revision=settings.revision, allow_dirty=settings.allow_dirty)
    if refusal is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{refusal}\n')
        return MeasureResult(exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
    commit = settings.revision.commit
    machine = this_machine()
    try:
        known = known_rows(
            published_text=published_text,
            pending_path=settings.pending_path,
            rows_directory=settings.rows_directory,
        )
    except UnreadableLedgerError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{MEASURE_PREFIX} {error}\n')
        return MeasureResult(exit_code=ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT)
    landed_commits = LandedCommits(
        repository=settings.project_root, landed_ref=settings.project_settings.landed_ref
    )
    measured_code = measured_code_label(commit=commit, code_tree=settings.code_tree)
    measured: list[str] = []
    skipped: list[str] = []
    failures: list[str] = []
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='replay-metrics-') as temporary_name:
        for index, (console_script, path) in enumerate(recordings):
            try:
                recording = recording_ledger_name(
                    path=path,
                    project_root=settings.project_root,
                    demo_packages=settings.demo_packages,
                )
            except ValueError as error:
                # A PATH given outside the project: it has no ledger name
                _failure(recording=path.as_posix(), message=str(error.args[0]))
                failures.append(path.as_posix())
                continue
            if not settings.force and _already_measured(
                settings=settings, rows=known, recording=recording, commit=commit, machine=machine
            ):
                sys.stdout.write(f'{recording}: already measured at {measured_code} on {machine}\n')
                skipped.append(recording)
                continue
            started = clock.raw_counter_seconds()
            rows = measure_recording(
                settings=settings,
                console_script=console_script,
                path=path,
                new_path=Path(temporary_name) / f'{index}-{path.name}',
            )
            if rows is None:
                failures.append(recording)
                continue
            if settings.code_tree is not None:
                # The run just measured (the newest) measured the code tree; the recording's
                # own earlier runs are history and keep naming their commits
                rows = [rows[0].model_copy(update={'code_tree': settings.code_tree}), *rows[1:]]
            new_rows = _write_new_rows(
                settings=settings,
                rows=rows,
                held_keys={
                    row.held_key(recording_renames=settings.project_settings.recording_renames)
                    for row in known
                },
                landed_commits=landed_commits,
            )
            known.extend(new_rows)
            measured.append(recording)
            sys.stdout.write(
                describe_measurement(
                    row=rows[0],
                    seconds=clock.raw_counter_seconds() - started,
                    pending_rows=len(new_rows),
                )
                + '\n'
            )
    count = len(measured)
    sys.stdout.write(
        f'Measured {count} recording{"" if count == 1 else "s"} at {measured_code} on {machine} '
        f'({len(skipped)} already measured, {len(failures)} failed) into '
        f'{settings.pending_path if settings.rows_directory is None else settings.rows_directory}\n'
    )
    return MeasureResult(
        exit_code=ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR if failures else ExitCode.SUCCESS,
        measured=tuple(measured),
        skipped=tuple(skipped),
        failures=tuple(failures),
    )

def measure_command(*, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game_arguments: list[str]) -> int:
    """Run ``glitchygames measure [PATH ...] [options] [--game GAME ...]``.

    Args:
        tool: The measure tool.
        arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.
        game_arguments: The arguments after a bare ``--``, for each game started.

    Returns:
        ``measure_named_recordings``' exit code with PATHs, ``measure_each_game``'s without;
        ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` for a seed or both dirty flags (nothing is started).

    """
    if arguments.random_seed is not None or seed_given(arguments=game_arguments):
        say(tool=tool, message=seed_refusal())
        return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
    if arguments.allow_dirty and arguments.skip_dirty:
        say(tool=tool, message=dirty_flags_refusal())
        return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
    # One project for everything below, found as the game finds it
    arguments.project_root = verify_project_root(given=arguments.project_root)
    if arguments.measure:
        return measure_named_recordings(
            tool=tool, arguments=arguments, game_arguments=game_arguments
        )
    return measure_each_game(tool=tool, arguments=arguments, game_arguments=game_arguments)

def measure_each_game(
    *, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game_arguments: list[str]
) -> int:
    """Run ``glitchygames measure``: each game started with ``--measure``, measuring its own.

    When the games come from the settings, the project's goldens none of them replays are
    failures first (``unclaimed_goldens``), named with why.

    Args:
        tool: The measure tool.
        arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.
        game_arguments: The arguments after a bare ``--``, for each game.

    Returns:
        ``combined_exit_code`` of the statuses (``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` for an unclaimed
        golden or a game stopped at the project's ``game-timeout-seconds``,
        ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` for a game that names nothing; the other games still run),
        or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` when the settings can't be read.

    """
    found = games_to_run(tool=tool, arguments=arguments)
    if isinstance(found, ExitCode):
        return found
    games, settings, from_settings = found
    root: Path = arguments.project_root
    statuses: list[int] = []
    if from_settings:
        only: str | None = arguments.only
        for unclaimed in unclaimed_recordings(games=games, settings=settings, project_root=root):
            name = recording_ledger_name(path=unclaimed.path, project_root=root, demo_packages=())
            if only is not None and only not in name:
                continue
            _failure(recording=name, message=unclaimed.reason)
            statuses.append(ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR)
    if not games:
        say(
            tool=tool,
            message=(
                'no games to measure: the project names none in [tool.glitchygames] games (or '
                '[project.scripts]), and no --game was given'
            ),
        )
    for game in games:
        try:
            launch = resolve_named_game(tool=tool, game=game, arguments=arguments)
        except UnknownGameError:
            statuses.append(ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
            continue
        statuses.append(
            run_game_with_tool(
                tool=tool,
                arguments=arguments,
                game_arguments=game_arguments,
                game=game,
                launch=dataclasses.replace(launch, timeout_seconds=settings.game_timeout_seconds),
            )
        )
    return combined_exit_code(statuses=statuses)

def measure_named_recordings(
    *, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game_arguments: list[str]
) -> int:
    """Run ``glitchygames measure PATH ...``: each recording measured by its game.

    Its game is the one ``--game`` names, else the one its header names (``find_recorded_game``,
    as ``replay-trace`` finds it); the recordings of one game are measured by one child, given
    them as PATHs, and stopped if it is still running after the project's
    ``game-timeout-seconds``.

    Args:
        tool: The measure tool.
        arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.
        game_arguments: The arguments after a bare ``--``, for each game.

    Returns:
        ``combined_exit_code`` of the children's and the refusals' statuses (a child stopped at
        its timeout: ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR``), ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` for more than
        one ``--game`` or one that names nothing, or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` when the
        settings can't be read.

    """
    games: list[str] | None = arguments.game
    root: Path = arguments.project_root
    try:
        settings = read_settings(project_root=root, prefix=f'{tool.name}:')
    except ProjectSettingsError as error:
        say(tool=tool, message=str(error))
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    paths = [Path(path).absolute() for path in arguments.measure]
    targets: list[tuple[str, GameLaunch, Path]] = []
    statuses: list[int] = []
    if games is not None:
        if len(games) > 1:
            say(
                tool=tool,
                message=(
                    'with PATHs, one --game at most: it names the game that measures them '
                    f'({len(games)} were given)'
                ),
            )
            return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
        (game,) = games
        try:
            launch = resolve_named_game(tool=tool, game=game, arguments=arguments)
        except UnknownGameError:
            return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
        targets = [(game, launch, path) for path in paths]
    else:
        for path in paths:
            found = find_recorded_game(recording=path, project_root=root)
            if isinstance(found, RecordedGameRefusal):
                _failure(
                    recording=path.as_posix(),
                    message=found.reason.removeprefix(f'{path.as_posix()}: '),
                )
                statuses.append(found.exit_code)
                continue
            name, launch = found
            targets.append((name, launch, path))
    for game, group in groupby(targets, key=operator.itemgetter(0)):
        members = list(group)
        launch = members[0][1]
        statuses.append(
            run_game_with_tool(
                tool=tool,
                arguments=argparse.Namespace(**{
                    **vars(arguments),
                    'measure': [str(path) for _, _, path in members],
                }),
                game_arguments=game_arguments,
                game=game,
                launch=dataclasses.replace(launch, timeout_seconds=settings.game_timeout_seconds),
            )
        )
    return combined_exit_code(statuses=statuses)

def measure_on_the_game(*, options: dict[str, Any], game: type[Scene] | Scene) -> ExitCode:
    """Run ``--measure [PATH ...]`` on a game: rebaseline its recordings into the ledger.

    Runs in place of the game's run (``run_game_flag_tool``, from ``GameEngine.__init__``): the
    game is never built. Each recording is rebaselined through the game's console script, with
    the game's arguments other than measure's own (``registry.tool_free_arguments``), as the
    command passes those after ``--``.

    Args:
        options: The game's parsed options (``measure``: the PATHs given; ``force``,
            ``allow_dirty``, ``skip_dirty``, ``only``, ``code_tree``, ``rows_directory``,
            ``pending``).
        game: The game (its class, or a scene the game passed in).

    Returns:
        ``measure``'s exit code; ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` for ``--skip-dirty`` on a trial;
        ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` for a seed, both dirty flags, or PATHs for a game no
        console script starts; ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for settings or a pending ledger
        that can't be read.

    """
    # Imported here: the tool table imports this module
    from glitchygames.replay.tools.registry import tool_free_arguments, tool_named

    if options.get('random_seed') is not None:
        return refused(message=f'--measure: {seed_refusal()}', exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
    if options.get('allow_dirty') and options.get('skip_dirty'):
        return refused(
            message=f'--measure: {dirty_flags_refusal()}', exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
        )
    root = verify_project_root(given=None)
    try:
        project_settings = read_settings(project_root=root, prefix=MEASURE_PREFIX)
    except ProjectSettingsError as error:
        return refused(message=f'--measure: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT)
    revision = game_revision(game=game)
    if options.get('skip_dirty') and is_trial(revision=revision):
        sys.stdout.write(
            "Not measuring the replays: the game's checkout has uncommitted changes, or its "
            'commit is unknown\n'
        )
        return ExitCode.SUCCESS
    identity = game_identity(game=game)
    console_script = identity.console_script
    given: list[str] = options['measure']
    if console_script is None:
        if given:
            return refused(
                message=(
                    '--measure: no console script starts this game, and a ledger row names the '
                    'console script that replays its recording (install the game with one in '
                    '[project.scripts])'
                ),
                exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED,
            )
        paths: list[Path] = []
    elif given:
        paths = [Path(path).absolute() for path in given]
    else:
        paths = [
            recording.path
            for recording in game_recordings(
                identity=identity, settings=project_settings, project_root=root
            )
        ]
    only: str | None = options.get('only')
    demo_packages = (identity.package,)
    settings = MeasureSettings(
        project_root=root,
        project_settings=project_settings,
        pending_path=pending_path_of(
            given=options.get('pending'), settings=project_settings, project_root=root
        ),
        revision=revision,
        force=bool(options.get('force')),
        allow_dirty=bool(options.get('allow_dirty')),
        code_tree=options.get('code_tree'),
        rows_directory=(
            None if options.get('rows_directory') is None else Path(options['rows_directory'])
        ),
        demo_packages=demo_packages,
        game_arguments=tuple(
            tool_free_arguments(arguments=sys.argv[1:], tool=tool_named(name='measure'))
        ),
    )
    return measure(
        settings=settings,
        recordings=[
            (console_script, path)
            for path in paths
            if console_script is not None
            and selected(path=path, only=only, project_root=root, demo_packages=demo_packages)
        ],
        published_text=published_ledger_text(
            project_root=root, published_ledger=project_settings.published_ledger
        ),
    ).exit_code

def measure_recording(
    *, settings: MeasureSettings, console_script: str, path: Path, new_path: Path
) -> list[LedgerRow] | None:
    """Rebaseline one recording into ``new_path`` and return its ledger rows.

    Args:
        settings: The measurement's settings.
        console_script: The game's console script.
        path: The recording.
        new_path: Where the rebaselined recording goes (a temporary file).

    Returns:
        Its rows (``ledger_rows_from_rebaseline``), or None when it could not be measured (the
        reason is written to standard error).

    """
    recording = recording_ledger_name(
        path=path, project_root=settings.project_root, demo_packages=settings.demo_packages
    )
    completed = rebaseline_recording_headless(
        console_script=console_script,
        path=path,
        new_path=new_path,
        game_arguments=settings.game_arguments,
    )
    if completed.returncode not in MEASURED_EXIT_CODES:
        output = '\n'.join((completed.stdout or '').splitlines()[-FAILURE_OUTPUT_LINES:])
        _failure(
            recording=recording,
            message=(
                f'the rebaseline exited {ExitCode.describe_status(completed.returncode)}\n{output}'
            ),
        )
        return None
    rows = ledger_rows_from_rebaseline(
        recording=recording,
        console_script=console_script,
        trace=read_trace(path=new_path),
        rebaseline_exit=ExitCode.describe_status(completed.returncode),
        # A trial: uncommitted changes, or an unknown commit, measured under --allow-dirty
        allowed_uncommitted_changes=settings.allow_dirty and is_trial(revision=settings.revision),
    )
    measured_commit = rows[0].commit
    if measured_commit != settings.revision.commit:
        _failure(
            recording=recording,
            message=(
                f"the replay measured commit {measured_commit}, not the game's "
                f'{settings.revision.commit} (is the game installed from its checkout? run '
                'through uv run)'
            ),
        )
        return None
    return rows

def recording_ledger_name(*, path: Path, project_root: Path, demo_packages: Sequence[str]) -> str:
    """Return the name the ledger gives a recording.

    A recording in the project is named by its path relative to the project
    (``src/games/paddleslap/src/paddleslap/demos/rally.jsonl.gz``: what a development install,
    which is editable, finds). One outside it (a bundled demo of a built install, in
    ``site-packages``) is named by its bundled demo record's install name
    (``paddleslap/demos/rally.jsonl.gz``, ``glitchygames.bundled_demos.BundledDemo.install_name``),
    so the record is the name's one source.

    Args:
        path: The recording.
        project_root: The project.
        demo_packages: The import packages whose bundled demos may hold a recording outside the
            project (the game's own).

    Returns:
        The name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the recording is neither in the project nor a bundled demo of one of
            those packages.

    """
    resolved = path.resolve()
    root = project_root.resolve()
    if resolved.is_relative_to(root):
        return resolved.relative_to(root).as_posix()
    for demo in bundled_demos(packages=tuple(demo_packages)):
        if demo.path.resolve() == resolved:
            return demo.install_name
    message = f'{path}: neither in the project {project_root} nor an installed bundled demo'
    raise ValueError(message)

docs.text:
Return the rows of a rebaselined recording that a measurement writes.

The newest run (rows[0], the one just measured) is written unless held. A history row (a run the recording held) is written only when no row holds it, and its run was measured on a commit that is on the project's landed-ref (landed_commits.landed_ref: ours is origin/main) with no uncommitted changes: a run of code that never landed would be published unconditionally (it names no code tree). With no landed ref to compare with, none is written. "Held" compares keys with the recording at its current path (LedgerRow.held_key with the project's recording-renames), so a moved recording's earlier runs are not written again.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default rows Sequence[LedgerRow]

The recording's rows, newest first (ledger_rows_from_rebaseline).

required held_keys set[str]

The held_key of every row already held.

required landed_commits LandedCommits

Which commits landed, shared by the measurement's recordings.

required settings ProjectSettings

The project's settings (recording-renames).

required

Returns:

Type Description list[LedgerRow]

The rows to write, in order.

Source code in src/glitchygames/replay/tools/measure.py 
def rows_to_write(
    *,
    rows: Sequence[LedgerRow],
    held_keys: set[str],
    landed_commits: LandedCommits,
    settings: ProjectSettings,
) -> list[LedgerRow]:
    """Return the rows of a rebaselined recording that a measurement writes.

    The newest run (``rows[0]``, the one just measured) is written unless held. A history row (a
    run the recording held) is written only when no row holds it, and its run was measured on a
    commit that is on the project's ``landed-ref`` (``landed_commits.landed_ref``: ours is
    ``origin/main``) with no uncommitted changes: a run of code that never landed would be
    published unconditionally (it names no code tree). With no landed ref to compare with, none
    is written. "Held" compares keys with the recording at its current path
    (``LedgerRow.held_key`` with the project's ``recording-renames``), so a moved recording's
    earlier runs are not written again.

    Args:
        rows: The recording's rows, newest first (``ledger_rows_from_rebaseline``).
        held_keys: The ``held_key`` of every row already held.
        landed_commits: Which commits landed, shared by the measurement's recordings.
        settings: The project's settings (``recording-renames``).

    Returns:
        The rows to write, in order.

    """
    renames = settings.recording_renames
    newest, *history = rows
    written = [] if newest.held_key(recording_renames=renames) in held_keys else [newest]
    for row in history:
        commit = row.commit
        if (
            row.held_key(recording_renames=renames) in held_keys
            or commit is None
            or row.measured_uncommitted_changes
            or not landed_commits.has_landed(commit=commit)
        ):
            continue
        written.append(row)
    return written

def unclaimed_goldens(
    *, games: Sequence[str], settings: ProjectSettings, project_root: Path
) -> list[UnreplayableRecording]:
    """Return the project's goldens that none of its games replays, each with why.

    What measuring every game would silently leave out: a golden of a workspace member that is
    not installed (a plain ``uv sync``), or one whose game is not among the games measured.

    Args:
        games: The games measured (``[tool.glitchygames] games``).
        settings: The project's settings (``golden-globs``).
        project_root: The project.

    Returns:
        The goldens, by path, with the reason each is not measured.

    """
    unclaimed: list[UnreplayableRecording] = []
    for path in golden_paths(settings=settings, project_root=project_root):
        try:
            console_script = recording_console_script(path=path)
        except KeyError as error:
            # The refusal's message (not KeyError's quoted repr), without the path it starts
            # with: the failure line names the recording
            reason = str(error.args[0]).removeprefix(f'{path.as_posix()}: ')
            unclaimed.append(UnreplayableRecording(path=path, reason=reason))
            continue
        if console_script not in games:
            unclaimed.append(
                UnreplayableRecording(
                    path=path,
                    reason=(
                        f'replayed by {console_script}, which is not one of the games measured '
                        '([tool.glitchygames] games)'
                    ),
                )
            )
    return unclaimed

def unmeasured_command(
    *, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game_arguments: list[str]
) -> int:
    """Run ``glitchygames unmeasured [options] [--game GAME ...]``.

    A game named by its installed console script is read here, without starting it
    (``console_script_unmeasured``). A game in another form is started as a child with
    ``--unmeasured``, which lists its own. When the games come from the settings, a golden none
    of them replays is listed too (it is never measured; ``measure`` reports it as a failure),
    its reason on standard error.

    Args:
        tool: The unmeasured tool.
        arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.
        game_arguments: Always empty (the tool runs no game: the command refuses ``--``).

    Returns:
        ``combined_exit_code`` of the games' statuses (``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` for a game
        that names nothing or isn't installed), or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` when the
        settings or the pending ledger can't be read.

    """
    # The tool runs no game, so the command refuses arguments after --: always empty
    del game_arguments
    arguments.project_root = verify_project_root(given=arguments.project_root)
    root: Path = arguments.project_root
    found = games_to_run(tool=tool, arguments=arguments)
    if isinstance(found, ExitCode):
        return found
    games, settings, from_settings = found
    code_tree: str | None = arguments.code_tree
    try:
        known = known_rows(
            published_text=published_ledger_text(
                project_root=root, published_ledger=settings.published_ledger
            ),
            pending_path=pending_path_of(
                given=arguments.pending, settings=settings, project_root=root
            ),
            # A path option's value is the text given (registry.KIND_SETTINGS)
            rows_directory=(
                None if arguments.rows_directory is None else Path(arguments.rows_directory)
            ),
        )
    except UnreadableLedgerError as error:
        say(tool=tool, message=str(error))
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    statuses: list[int] = []
    missing: list[str] = []
    total = 0
    for game in games:
        try:
            launch = resolve_named_game(tool=tool, game=game, arguments=arguments)
        except UnknownGameError:
            statuses.append(ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
            continue
        if launch.form != CONSOLE_SCRIPT_FORM:
            status, count, unmeasured = child_unmeasured(
                tool=tool, arguments=arguments, game=game, launch=launch
            )
            statuses.append(status)
            total += count
            missing.extend(unmeasured)
            continue
        count, unmeasured = console_script_unmeasured(
            console_script=game,
            settings=settings,
            project_root=root,
            known=known,
            code_tree=code_tree,
        )
        total += count
        missing.extend(unmeasured)
    if from_settings:
        for unclaimed in unclaimed_recordings(games=games, settings=settings, project_root=root):
            name = recording_ledger_name(path=unclaimed.path, project_root=root, demo_packages=())
            say(tool=tool, message=f'{name}: {unclaimed.reason}')
            missing.append(name)
            total += 1
    report_unmeasured(
        missing=missing,
        total=total,
        code_tree=code_tree,
        machine=this_machine(),
        prefix=f'glitchygames {tool.name}:',
    )
    return combined_exit_code(statuses=statuses)

def unmeasured_on_the_game(*, options: dict[str, Any], game: type[Scene] | Scene) -> ExitCode:
    """Run ``--unmeasured`` on a game: list its recordings ``--measure`` would measure.

    Runs in place of the game's run, which never starts.

    Args:
        options: The game's parsed options (``code_tree``, ``rows_directory``, ``pending``).
        game: The game (its class, or a scene the game passed in).

    Returns:
        ``ExitCode.SUCCESS``, or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` for settings or a pending ledger
        that can't be read.

    """
    root = verify_project_root(given=None)
    try:
        settings = read_settings(project_root=root, prefix=UNMEASURED_PREFIX)
    except ProjectSettingsError as error:
        return refused(message=f'--unmeasured: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT)
    names = ledger_names(identity=game_identity(game=game), settings=settings, project_root=root)
    machine = this_machine()
    code_tree: str | None = options.get('code_tree')
    try:
        known = known_rows(
            published_text=published_ledger_text(
                project_root=root, published_ledger=settings.published_ledger
            ),
            pending_path=pending_path_of(
                given=options.get('pending'), settings=settings, project_root=root
            ),
            rows_directory=(
                None if options.get('rows_directory') is None else Path(options['rows_directory'])
            ),
        )
    except UnreadableLedgerError as error:
        return refused(message=f'--unmeasured: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT)
    missing = missing_measurements(
        rows=known,
        recordings=names,
        code_tree=code_tree,
        machine=machine,
        commit=game_revision(game=game).commit,
    )
    report_unmeasured(
        missing=missing,
        total=len(names),
        code_tree=code_tree,
        machine=machine,
        prefix=UNMEASURED_PREFIX,
    )
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

def walked_files(*, project_root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """Return the files of a project that is no git checkout, but its hidden trees and environments.

    Hidden directories, virtual environments (``pyvenv.cfg``), caches and installed copies are
    not entered.

    Args:
        project_root: The project.

    Returns:
        The files.

    """
    found: list[Path] = []
    for directory, subdirectories, files in os.walk(project_root):
        here = Path(directory)
        subdirectories[:] = sorted(
            name
            for name in subdirectories
            if not name.startswith('.')
            and name not in SKIPPED_DIRECTORY_NAMES
            and not (here / name / VIRTUAL_ENVIRONMENT_MARKER).exists()
        )
        found.extend(here / name for name in files)
    return found

docs.title: performance_pages
docs.text:
The performance-pages tool: the run ledger's graph pages, one per recording.

Design: plans/2026-10-23-recording-metrics-1-frame-performance-history.md; moved here from scripts/generate_performance_graphs.py (Part 3, Stage D, Task D7), which keeps only our docs site's paths and the snippet its page includes, and calls this module:

  1. merged_ledger: the project's ledger rows from every source, each row once (glitchygames.recording_metrics.merge_ledgers), driven by its [tool.glitchygames] settings (passed in, never read here from any one project): the row files in its ledger-directory (labelled with the commit their code landed in: landed_rows, by the git history of the measured-paths), the ledger it publishes (published-ledger, git show REF:PATH of the local ref; nothing is fetched) and its pending-ledger. Rows measured on uncommitted changes (LedgerRow.from_uncommitted_changes), and row files whose code never landed, are left out of a build that is published (include_uncommitted_changes False) and shown, labelled, in a local one;
  2. write_performance_pages: the merged ledger as one file (ledger_file_name: the published ledger's name, so a deploy publishes it where it is read back), then one graph page per recording (<console-script>-<name>.html): processing time per frame (p50, p99 and max) by commit, frames over budget by commit, and the live runs' frame times (how steady pacing was), one line per machine and kind of run (performance_series: times compare only on one machine, and paced frames process slower than replayed ones); FPS by commit (fps_charts: live runs' achieved FPS solid, replays' headroom FPS dashed, each point the average with its 5% low and 5% high as an error bar, and a line at the target FPS from budget_seconds); and the machines view (machines_chart: each machine's latest replay as a bar of average headroom FPS with its 5% low and high, CI machines marked). FPS is read from the rows' seconds with fps_from_seconds; rows from before the slice means (2026-10-28) have no FPS point. The x axis is the commits in commit-date order, labelled with their short hash; plotly.js comes from jsDelivr (PLOTLY_JS_URL), so rendering imports nothing beyond the engine's own dependencies. Then a frame x commit heatmap per machine from the rows' per-frame profiles (FrameProfile: each bucket's slowest frame); rows without one (older rows, a recording's own runs) have no heatmap line.

A file is rewritten only when its text changed (write_if_changed), and graph pages of recordings no longer in the ledger are removed.

build_performance_pages is one build, local or published: the tool and our docs site's mkdocs hook (scripts/generate_performance_graphs.py: published for gh-deploy) both build through it, so a deploy's pages are the tool's --published ones.

The front ends (glitchygames/replay/tools/registry.py) write the project's pages into DIRECTORY: a local build (rows from uncommitted changes shown, labelled), or with --published what a deploy publishes. They run no game:

  • On the game: mygame --performance-pages DIRECTORY [--published] (performance_pages_on_the_game) runs from GameEngine.__init__, before the engine starts pygame: the game is neither built nor shown.
  • The command: glitchygames performance-pages DIRECTORY [--published] (performance_pages_command).

Both find the project as verify does (verify.verify_project_root) and read its settings from there; a DIRECTORY in the project's local directory (.glitchygames/) is made through settings.ensure_local_directory (measure.ensure_directory).

Exit codes: SUCCESS; UNUSABLE_INPUT for settings that can't be read, a pending ledger that can't be read (no permission, not UTF-8: UnreadableLedgerError, naming it), or row files git can't date (no repository); CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT when DIRECTORY can't be written.

def build_performance_pages(
    *,
    project_root: Path,
    settings: ProjectSettings,
    directory: Path,
    pending_path: Path,
    published: bool,
) -> PerformancePagesBuild:
    """Merge the project's ledger and write its pages: one build, local or published.

    The tool (``--published`` or not) and our docs site's mkdocs hook (published for
    ``gh-deploy``, local for ``build`` and ``serve``: scripts/generate_performance_graphs.py)
    both build through this, so a deploy's pages are the tool's published ones. A pending
    ledger that can't be read raises ``merged_ledger``'s ``UnreadableLedgerError`` before
    anything is written.

    Args:
        project_root: The project.
        settings: Its settings.
        directory: Where the pages go (created when missing, after the rows are read).
        pending_path: Its pending ledger (``pending-ledger``, unless a caller says otherwise).
        published: Build what a deploy publishes: leave out rows measured on uncommitted
            changes and row files whose code has not landed (``merged_ledger``'s
            ``include_uncommitted_changes`` False). Otherwise a local build shows them, labelled.

    Returns:
        The merged rows and the pages written.

    """
    sources = merged_ledger(
        project_root=project_root,
        settings=settings,
        pending_path=pending_path,
        include_uncommitted_changes=not published,
    )
    # Made once the rows are read, so a build that can't read them writes nothing; one in the
    # project's local directory (.glitchygames/) gets its .gitignore
    ensure_directory(directory=directory, project_root=project_root)
    pages = write_performance_pages(rows=sources.rows, directory=directory, settings=settings)
    return PerformancePagesBuild(sources=sources, pages=pages)

def fps_point(*, row: LedgerRow, paced: bool) -> FpsPoint | None:
    """Return a row's FPS: achieved (a paced live run's frame times) or headroom (a replay's).

    A paced run's processing times are no headroom (the processor slows between paced frames:
    glitchygames/replay/processing.py), so a paced row gives its frame times and an unpaced
    one its processing times, each read as FPS with ``fps_from_seconds``.

    Args:
        row: The row.
        paced: Whether its series paced its frames.

    Returns:
        The point, or None when the row lacks the figures (a row from before the slice means, a
        paced row without frame times) or a time is zero.

    """
    summary = row.summary
    if summary is None:
        return None
    if paced:
        frame_time = summary.frame_time
        if frame_time is None:
            return None
        mean, slowest, fastest = (
            frame_time.mean_seconds,
            frame_time.slowest_5_percent_mean_seconds,
            frame_time.fastest_5_percent_mean_seconds,
        )
    else:
        mean, slowest, fastest = (
            summary.mean_processing_seconds,
            summary.slowest_5_percent_mean_processing_seconds,
            summary.fastest_5_percent_mean_processing_seconds,
        )
    average, low, high = _rounded_fps(mean), _rounded_fps(slowest), _rounded_fps(fastest)
    if average is None or low is None or high is None:
        return None
    return FpsPoint(average=average, low=low, high=high)

def machines_chart(*, series_list: Sequence[PerformanceSeries]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Return the machines view: each machine's latest replay as a bar of headroom FPS.

    Replays only (unpaced series): paced runs' times include the wait for the frame deadline.
    Each machine's latest row in commit order that has the figures (``fps_point``) is one bar of
    its average headroom FPS, with an error bar from its 5% low to its 5% high, so machines
    compare at a glance. A machine that measured in CI is marked (``machine_name``).

    Args:
        series_list: The recording's series.

    Returns:
        One plotly bar trace (``meta``: each bar's series slot, for its color), or None when no
        replay row has the figures.

    """
    bars: list[tuple[int, LedgerRow, FpsPoint]] = []
    for slot, series in enumerate(series_list):
        if series.paced:
            continue
        measured = [
            (row, point)
            for row in series.rows
            if (point := fps_point(row=row, paced=False)) is not None
        ]
        if measured:
            row, point = measured[-1]
            bars.append((slot, row, point))
    if not bars:
        return None
    return {
        'type': 'bar',
        'name': 'headroom FPS, latest replay',
        'x': [machine_name(row=row) for _, row, _ in bars],
        'y': [point.average for _, _, point in bars],
        'customdata': [
            f'{_slices_hover(point=point)}<br>commit {row_label(row=row)}, {_hover_detail(row=row)}'
            for _, row, point in bars
        ],
        'error_y': _error_bars(points=[point for _, _, point in bars], width=6),
        'meta': [slot for slot, _, _ in bars],
        'marker': {},
        'hovertemplate': '%{x}: avg %{y} fps, %{customdata}<extra></extra>',
    }

def merged_ledger(
    *,
    project_root: Path,
    settings: ProjectSettings,
    pending_path: Path,
    include_uncommitted_changes: bool,
) -> LedgerSources:
    """Merge the project's row files, published ledger and pending rows, each row once.

    Args:
        project_root: The project (a git repository when it has row files; its published ref
            holds the published ledger).
        settings: The project's settings (``ledger-directory``, ``measured-paths``,
            ``published-ledger``).
        pending_path: The pending rows.
        include_uncommitted_changes: Keep rows that measured other code than their commit
            (``LedgerRow.from_uncommitted_changes``) and row files whose code has not landed,
            labelled: a local build. False for a build that is published: they leave the ledger
            file and every graph.

    Returns:
        The rows and how many each source gave.

    Raises:
        UnreadableLedgerError: If the pending ledger exists but can't be read.

    """
    repository = read_row_files_by_name(directory=project_root / settings.ledger_directory)
    landed = (
        # Only when there are rows: a project without any needs no git
        landed_rows(
            row_files=repository,
            landed=landed_row_files(
                repository=project_root,
                ledger_directory=settings.ledger_directory,
                paths=settings.code_tree_paths,
            ),
            keep_unlanded=include_uncommitted_changes,
        )
        if repository
        else []
    )
    published = parse_ledger(
        text=published_ledger_text(
            project_root=project_root, published_ledger=settings.published_ledger
        )
    )
    try:
        pending = read_ledger_file(path=pending_path)
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:
        raise UnreadableLedgerError(path=pending_path, cause=error) from error
    rows = merge_ledgers(ledgers=[landed, published.rows, pending.rows])
    if not include_uncommitted_changes:
        rows = publishable_rows(rows=rows)
    unreadable_lines = published.unreadable_lines + pending.unreadable_lines
    if unreadable_lines:
        LOG.warning('Skipped %d unreadable ledger lines', unreadable_lines)
    return LedgerSources(
        rows=tuple(rows),
        repository_rows=len(repository),
        published_rows=len(published.rows),
        pending_rows=len(pending.rows),
        unreadable_lines=unreadable_lines,
    )

def performance_pages_in(
    *, project_root: Path, directory: Path, published: bool, prefix: str
) -> ExitCode:
    """Write the project's performance pages into a directory (``build_performance_pages``).

    Args:
        project_root: The project.
        directory: Where the pages go.
        published: Build what a deploy publishes (``--published``), not a local build.
        prefix: What starts a line about a failure (the tool's).

    Returns:
        The exit code (see the module docstring).

    """
    try:
        settings = read_settings(project_root=project_root, prefix=prefix)
    except ProjectSettingsError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{prefix} {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    try:
        build = build_performance_pages(
            project_root=project_root,
            settings=settings,
            directory=directory,
            pending_path=pending_path_of(given=None, settings=settings, project_root=project_root),
            published=published,
        )
    except UnreadableLedgerError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{prefix} {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    except RuntimeError as error:
        # git could not date the row files (landed_row_files): no repository, or a broken one
        sys.stderr.write(f'{prefix} {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    except OSError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{prefix} could not write the performance pages: {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT
    sources = build.sources
    sys.stdout.write(
        f'Graphed {len(build.pages.pages)} recordings from {len(sources.rows)} ledger rows '
        f'({sources.repository_rows} in the repository, {sources.published_rows} published, '
        f'{sources.pending_rows} pending) into {directory}\n'
    )
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

def profile_heatmap(*, series: PerformanceSeries) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    """Return a series' frame x commit heatmap (each bucket's slowest frame, by commit).

    Args:
        series: One recording on one machine, in commit order.

    Returns:
        A plotly heatmap trace (``y``: the commits whose row has a profile; ``x``: bucket
        positions; ``z``: milliseconds, None where untimed or past a shorter profile), or None
        when no row has a profile.

    """
    profiled = [(row_label(row=row), row.profile) for row in series.rows if row.profile is not None]
    if not profiled:
        return None
    width = max(len(profile.max_microseconds) for _, profile in profiled)
    values: list[list[float | None]] = []
    hovers: list[list[str]] = []
    for _, profile in profiled:
        buckets = len(profile.max_microseconds)
        values.append([
            _bucket_milliseconds(profile=profile, bucket=bucket) for bucket in range(width)
        ])
        hovers.append([
            _bucket_hover(profile=profile, bucket=bucket) if bucket < buckets else ''
            for bucket in range(width)
        ])
    return {
        'type': 'heatmap',
        'name': series.label,
        'x': list(range(width)),
        'y': [label for label, _ in profiled],
        'z': values,
        'customdata': hovers,
        'hoverongaps': False,
        'hovertemplate': '%{y}: %{customdata}<extra></extra>',
        'colorbar': {'title': {'text': 'ms'}},
    }

def recording_charts(*, series_list: Sequence[PerformanceSeries]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return a recording's charts as plotly traces, and the commits' order.

    Args:
        series_list: The recording's series.

    Returns:
        ``commits`` (short hashes, commit-date order), ``processing``, ``over_budget`` and
        ``frame_time`` trace lists (``frame_time`` empty when no live run has a commit),
        ``fps`` (``fps_charts``), ``machines`` (``machines_chart``, or None), ``target_fps``
        (``target_fps``, or None) and ``heatmaps`` (``profile_heatmap``, one per series with a
        profiled row).

    """
    commits: list[str] = []
    processing: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    over_budget: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    frame_time: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    ordered_rows = merge_ledgers(ledgers=[[row for series in series_list for row in series.rows]])
    for row in ordered_rows:
        label = row_label(row=row)
        if label and label not in commits:
            commits.append(label)
    for slot, series in enumerate(series_list):
        rows = [(row_label(row=row), row) for row in series.rows]
        summaries = [(label, row, row.summary) for label, row in rows if row.summary is not None]
        for statistic, field in (
            ('p50', 'p50_processing_seconds'),
            ('p99', 'p99_processing_seconds'),
            ('max', 'max_processing_seconds'),
        ):
            points = [
                (label, _milliseconds(getattr(summary, field)), _hover_detail(row=row))
                for label, row, summary in summaries
            ]
            processing.append(_trace(series=series, slot=slot, statistic=statistic, points=points))
        budget_points = [
            (label, float(summary.frames_over_budget), _hover_detail(row=row))
            for label, row, summary in summaries
            if summary.frames_over_budget is not None
        ]
        if budget_points:
            over_budget.append(_trace(series=series, slot=slot, statistic='', points=budget_points))
        timed = [
            (label, row, summary.frame_time)
            for label, row, summary in summaries
            if summary.frame_time is not None
        ]
        if not timed:
            continue
        for statistic, field in (
            ('p50', 'p50_seconds'),
            ('p99', 'p99_seconds'),
            ('max', 'max_seconds'),
        ):
            points = [
                (label, _milliseconds(getattr(times, field)), _hover_detail(row=row))
                for label, row, times in timed
            ]
            frame_time.append(_trace(series=series, slot=slot, statistic=statistic, points=points))
    return {
        'commits': commits,
        'processing': processing,
        'over_budget': over_budget,
        'frame_time': frame_time,
        'fps': fps_charts(series_list=series_list),
        'machines': machines_chart(series_list=series_list),
        'target_fps': target_fps(series_list=series_list),
        'heatmaps': [
            heatmap
            for series in series_list
            if (heatmap := profile_heatmap(series=series)) is not None
        ],
    }

def write_performance_pages(
    *, rows: Sequence[LedgerRow], directory: Path, settings: ProjectSettings
) -> WrittenPages:
    """Write the ledger file and a graph page per recording; remove stale graph pages.

    Args:
        rows: The ledger rows (``merged_ledger``'s).
        directory: Where the files go (created when missing).
        settings: The project's settings (``recording-renames``: a moved recording is one
            series; ``published-ledger``: the ledger file's name).

    Returns:
        What was written and removed.

    """
    series_list = performance_series(rows=rows, recording_renames=settings.recording_renames)
    by_recording: dict[str, list[PerformanceSeries]] = {}
    for series in series_list:
        by_recording.setdefault(series.recording, []).append(series)
    pages = {
        recording: graph_page_name(recording=recording, console_script=series[0].console_script)
        for recording, series in by_recording.items()
    }
    files = {ledger_file_name(settings=settings): ledger_text(rows=rows)}
    for recording, name in pages.items():
        files[name] = graph_page_html(recording=recording, series_list=by_recording[recording])
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    removed = [
        stale.name
        for stale in sorted(directory.glob(f'*{GRAPH_PAGE_SUFFIX}'))
        if stale.name not in files
    ]
    for name in removed:
        (directory / name).unlink()
    written = tuple(
        name for name, text in files.items() if write_if_changed(path=directory / name, text=text)
    )
    return WrittenPages(
        series=tuple(series_list), pages=pages, written=written, removed=tuple(removed)
    )

A game's own recordings: its goldens in the project and the demos bundled in its package.

What --verify with no paths replays (glitchygames/replay/tools/verify.py), found from the game alone (its GameIdentity) and the project's settings, so a game the engine has never seen finds its recordings with nothing declared:

A golden another game replays, or one whose console script can't be told, is not this game's;
  • demos: <package>/demos/*.jsonl.gz in the game's own installed package (glitchygames.bundled_demos.bundled_demos, given that one package).

Bookmarked copies (glitchygames.tracing.is_bookmarked_copy) are neither. A game no console script starts has no recordings found this way: no golden can be told to be its, and none could be replayed by name.

def game_recordings(
    *, identity: GameIdentity, settings: ProjectSettings, project_root: Path
) -> list[Recording]:
    """Return a game's own recordings: its goldens in the project, then its bundled demos.

    Args:
        identity: The game's identity (``identity.game_identity``).
        settings: The project's settings (``golden-globs``).
        project_root: The project the globs are read in.

    Returns:
        The goldens this game's console script replays (sorted by path), then the demos in its
        package (sorted by path); none for a game no console script starts.

    """
    console_script = identity.console_script
    if console_script is None:
        return []
    goldens = [
        Recording(console_script=console_script, path=path, kind='golden')
        for path in golden_paths(settings=settings, project_root=project_root)
        if replaying_console_script(path=path) == console_script
    ]
    demos = [
        Recording(console_script=console_script, path=demo.path, kind='demo')
        for demo in bundled_demos(packages=(identity.package,))
    ]
    return [*goldens, *demos]

docs.title: registry
docs.text:
The table of the engine's tools (TOOLS) and the two front ends built from it.

Every recording, replay and measurement tool is described once, as a Tool with its ToolOption s, and both front ends are generated from that description, so a tool's name, options, defaults and help can't differ between them (tests/replay/tools/test_registry.py walks the table to check):

  • On the game (add_game_flags): GameEngine.args adds each tool to the game's own command line as --<name> (with the tool's options as flags of their own), so any game the engine runs has them without declaring anything. A tool with a game handler runs in place of the game's own run (run_game_flag_tool, from GameEngine.__init__, before the engine starts pygame): one that runs no game, or one that runs the game in a harness of its own (--record-golden-trace, --record-session). A tool without one is the game's run, which the engine already handles (--record-trace, --replay-trace).
  • As the glitchygames command (build_command_parser, glitchygames/replay/tools/ command.py): each tool is a subcommand with the same name and options, plus the command's own arguments (the game to run, --project-root). A subcommand whose tool runs the game starts it as a child process with the tool's flag (glitchygames/replay/tools/children.py).

An option may be listed under several tools (the same ToolOption: --headless is record-trace's and replay-trace's); it is one flag on the game and an option of each tool's subcommand. The engine's general flags that no tool lists (--resolution, ...) stay in GameEngine.args; the command passes them to the game after a bare --. Only one tool runs at a time: a game given two tool flags is refused (run_game_flag_tool).

@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tool:
    """One tool: ``--<name>`` on every game and ``glitchygames <name>``.

    Attributes:
        name: Its name, the same on both front ends (``replay-trace``).
        help: Its help text: the game flag's and the subcommand's.
        options: Its options, the same on both front ends, in order.
        runs_game: Whether the game runs for it (``--replay-trace``) or not (``--report``).
        game_handler: What runs it given as a game flag, in place of the game; None for a tool
            the game's own run handles (``runs_game``). A tool that runs no game must have one
            (refused when it is made: the game would otherwise run in its place).
        command_handler: What runs ``glitchygames <name>``.
        value_kind: What its own flag takes (``ToolValueKind``).
        value_metavar: That value's name in the help (``PATH``).
        value_help: That value's help as the command's positional argument.
        command_arguments: The command's arguments that the game flag has no need of (the game
            to run: ``GAME``, ``--game``): positional ones go before the value, the others after
            the options.
        project_root_use: What its subcommand's ``--project-root`` is to it, and so its default
            (``ProjectRootUse``, ``PROJECT_ROOT_HELP``).

    """

    name: str
    help: str
    options: tuple[ToolOption, ...]
    runs_game: bool
    game_handler: GameHandler | None
    command_handler: CommandHandler
    value_kind: ToolValueKind = 'path'
    value_metavar: str = 'PATH'
    value_help: str = ''
    command_arguments: tuple[ToolOption, ...] = ()
    project_root_use: ProjectRootUse = 'working-directory'

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Refuse a tool that runs no game and has no game handler.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If ``runs_game`` is False and ``game_handler`` is None.

        """
        if not self.runs_game and self.game_handler is None:
            message = (
                f'{self.name} runs no game, so it needs a game handler (without one the game '
                'would run in its place)'
            )
            raise ValueError(message)

    @property
    def flag(self) -> str:
        """The tool's game flag (``--replay-trace``)."""
        return f'--{self.name}'

    @property
    def destination(self) -> str:
        """The tool's key in the parsed options, on both front ends (``replay_trace``)."""
        return self.name.replace('-', '_')

    def child_arguments(self, *, arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> list[str]:
        """Return the game flags that run this tool as the command was asked to.

        The tool's flag and value come first, then each option given a value other than its
        default. Paths are made absolute, so they mean the same in a child started in another
        directory (``--project-root``).

        Args:
            arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.

        Returns:
            The arguments for the game's command line.

        """
        child = [
            self.flag,
            *flag_values(kind=self.value_kind, value=self.destination_value(arguments=arguments)),
        ]
        for option in self.options:
            value = getattr(arguments, option.destination)
            if value == option.default:
                continue
            child.extend(option_on_the_command_line(option=option, value=value))
        return child

    def destination_value(self, *, arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> object:
        """Return the tool's own value from the subcommand's parsed arguments.

        Args:
            arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.

        Returns:
            The value (True for a ``flag`` tool, whose subcommand has no value).

        """
        if self.value_kind == 'flag':
            return True
        return getattr(arguments, self.destination)
