def add_game_flags(*, parser: ArgumentContainer, tools: Sequence[Tool] | None = None) -> None:
    """Add every tool to a game's command line: ``--<name>``, then each tool's options.

    Called by ``GameEngine.args`` with its Diagnostics Options group. The tools' flags come
    first, in the table's order, then their options; an option two tools share (the same
    ``ToolOption``) is added once.

    Args:
        parser: The parser or group to add them to.
        tools: The tools (``TOOLS`` unless given).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If two tools describe an option with the same flag differently.

    """
    tools = TOOLS if tools is None else tools
    for tool in tools:
        parser.add_argument(tool.flag, **tool_flag_settings(tool=tool))
    added: dict[str, ToolOption] = {}
    for tool in tools:
        for option in tool.options:
            if option.flag in added:
                if added[option.flag] != option:
                    message = f'{option.flag} is described twice, differently'
                    raise ValueError(message)
                continue
            added[option.flag] = option
            parser.add_argument(option.flag, **option_settings(option=option))

def build_command_parser(*, tools: Sequence[Tool] | None = None) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Build the ``glitchygames`` command's parser: one subcommand per tool.

    Each subcommand has the command's positional arguments (``GAME``), the tool's value, its
    options (as on the game), its other command arguments (``--game``) and ``--project-root``.
    The parser's help lists every tool with all its options (``--rebaseline`` and ``--audit``
    under ``replay-trace``).

    Args:
        tools: The tools (``TOOLS`` unless given).

    Returns:
        The parser; ``tool`` in its result names the subcommand given.

    """
    tools = TOOLS if tools is None else tools
    epilog_lines = [
        'every tool, with its options (glitchygames TOOL --help describes them):',
        *(
            textwrap.fill(
                tool_summary(tool=tool),
                width=HELP_WIDTH,
                initial_indent='  ',
                subsequent_indent='      ',
                break_on_hyphens=False,
            )
            for tool in tools
        ),
        '',
        'Each tool is also a flag on any game built on the engine (mygame --TOOL ...). Arguments',
        'after a bare -- go to the game (glitchygames record-trace GAME PATH -- --resolution',
        '640x480).',
    ]
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog=COMMAND_NAME,
        description="The glitchygames engine's recording, replay and measurement tools.",
        epilog='\n'.join(epilog_lines),
        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
    )
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='tool', required=True, metavar='TOOL', title='tools')
    for tool in tools:
        subparser = subparsers.add_parser(tool.name, help=tool.help, description=tool.help)
        for argument in tool.command_arguments:
            if argument.positional:
                subparser.add_argument(argument.flag, **option_settings(option=argument))
        if tool.value_kind != 'flag':
            subparser.add_argument(
                tool.destination,
                metavar=tool.value_metavar,
                help=tool.value_help,
                nargs='*' if tool.value_kind == 'paths' else None,
            )
        for option in tool.options:
            subparser.add_argument(option.flag, **option_settings(option=option))
        for argument in tool.command_arguments:
            if not argument.positional:
                subparser.add_argument(argument.flag, **option_settings(option=argument))
        subparser.add_argument(
            PROJECT_ROOT_FLAG,
            metavar='DIR',
            type=Path,
            default=None,
            help=PROJECT_ROOT_HELP[tool.project_root_use],
        )
    return parser

def flag_values(*, kind: ToolOptionKind | ToolValueKind, value: object) -> list[str]:
    """Return what follows a flag on a child's command line for a parsed value.

    Args:
        kind: How the value is read.
        value: The parsed value (not the option's default).

    Returns:
        Nothing for a flag or a switch (on: ``option_on_the_command_line`` writes a switch
        given off), the absolute path(s) for a path, else the value as text.

    """
    match kind:
        case 'flag' | 'switch':
            return []
        case 'path':
            return [str(Path(str(value)).absolute())]
        case 'paths':
            # argparse's nargs='*': a list of the strings given
            paths = cast('list[str]', value)
            return [str(Path(path).absolute()) for path in paths]
        case _:
            return [str(value)]

def missing_required_options(*, tool: Tool, values: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """Say which required options a tool was given without, as both front ends refuse it.

    argparse requires no option (``option_settings``), so each front end checks here: the game
    (``run_game_flag_tool``) and the command (glitchygames/replay/tools/command.py) refuse the
    tool alike, with ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` (64, ``EX_USAGE``).

    Args:
        tool: The tool.
        values: The parsed options, by destination (a game's engine's ``options``, or the
            subcommand's parsed arguments as a dict).

    Returns:
        ``--<tool> needs --<option>, ...``, or None when none is missing.

    """
    missing = [
        option.flag
        for option in tool.options
        if option.required and not given(value=values.get(option.destination))
    ]
    if not missing:
        return None
    return f'{tool.flag} needs {", ".join(missing)}'

def option_on_the_command_line(*, option: ToolOption, value: object) -> list[str]:
    """Return an option as a child's command line gives it, for a value other than its default.

    A switch given off (``--no-x``, whatever its default) is passed on off.

    Args:
        option: The option.
        value: Its parsed value.

    Returns:
        The flag and what follows it.

    """
    if option.kind == 'switch' and value is False:
        return [f'--no-{option.flag.removeprefix("--")}']
    if option.kind == 'games':
        # argparse's action='append': the option once per game, as it was given
        games = cast('list[str]', value)
        return [part for game in games for part in (option.flag, game)]
    return [option.flag, *flag_values(kind=option.kind, value=value)]

def option_settings(*, option: ToolOption) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return ``add_argument``'s settings for an option, the same on both front ends.

    argparse requires no option on either: a game runs without the tool, and a missing required
    option is refused by each front end alike (``missing_required_options``), with
    ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` rather than argparse's 2.

    Args:
        option: The option.

    Returns:
        The keyword arguments for ``add_argument``.

    """
    settings: dict[str, Any] = {
        'help': argparse.SUPPRESS if option.hidden else option.help,
        **kind_settings(option=option),
    }
    if not option.positional:
        settings['default'] = option.default
    if option.metavar is not None:
        settings['metavar'] = option.metavar
    return settings

def path_option_destinations(*, tools: Sequence[Tool] | None = None) -> frozenset[str]:
    """Return the parsed options whose values are paths: each tool's own and its path options.

    A recording's header stores them relative to the project root
    (``glitchygames.replay.tools.settings.stored_path``).

    Args:
        tools: The tools (``TOOLS`` unless given).

    Returns:
        Their destinations (``record_trace``, ``rebaseline``, ``verify``, ...).

    """
    tools = TOOLS if tools is None else tools
    return frozenset({
        *(tool.destination for tool in tools if tool.value_kind in {'path', 'paths'}),
        *(
            option.destination
            for tool in tools
            for option in (*tool.options, *tool.command_arguments)
            if option.kind == 'path'

def run_game_flag_tool(
    *,
    options: dict[str, Any],
    game: type[Scene] | Scene,
    tools: Sequence[Tool] | None = None,
) -> ExitCode | None:
    """Run the tool given as a game flag in place of the game's run, if it has a game handler.

    Called by ``GameEngine.__init__`` (``_run_game_flag_tool``) before the engine starts pygame,
    opens its window or builds the game's scene. One tool at a time: two tool flags given
    together are refused, so neither is silently skipped.

    Args:
        options: The game's parsed options (the engine's ``options``).
        game: The game (its class, or a scene the game passed in).
        tools: The tools (``TOOLS`` unless given).

    Returns:
        The tool's exit code; ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` when it lacks a required option or
        another tool was given too; or None when the game is to run (no tool flag was given,
        or the tool given has no game handler: the game's own run handles it).

    """
    tools = TOOLS if tools is None else tools
    tools_given = given_tools(options=options, tools=tools)
    if not tools_given:
        return None
    if len(tools_given) > 1:
        LOG.error(
            'one tool at a time: %s were given together',
            ' and '.join(tool.flag for tool in tools_given),
        )
        return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
    (tool,) = tools_given
    refusal = missing_required_options(tool=tool, values=options)
    if refusal is not None:
        LOG.error('%s', refusal)
        return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
    if tool.game_handler is None:
        return None
    return tool.game_handler(options=options, game=game)

def tool_free_arguments(*, arguments: Sequence[str], tool: Tool) -> list[str]:
    """Return a game's command line without one tool's own flag, value and options.

def tool_summary(*, tool: Tool) -> str:
    """Describe a subcommand's command line on one line, for ``glitchygames --help``.

    Args:
        tool: The tool.

    Returns:
        ``<name> <arguments> [options]``, with every option's flag but the hidden ones.

    """
    positional = [
        argument.metavar or argument.flag.upper()
        for argument in tool.command_arguments
        if argument.positional
    ]
    if tool.value_kind == 'path':
        positional.append(tool.value_metavar)
    elif tool.value_kind == 'paths':
        positional.append(f'[{tool.value_metavar} ...]')
    flags = [
        option.flag
        for option in (*tool.options, *tool.command_arguments)
        if not option.positional and not option.hidden
    ]
    return ' '.join([tool.name, *positional, *(f'[{flag}]' for flag in flags)])

docs.title: report
docs.text:
The report tool: a recording's runs, speed changes and behaviour-change map.

Design: plans/2026-10-23-recording-metrics-2-behaviour-change-map.md (Part 2 of plans/2026-10-23-recording-metrics.md); moved here whole from scripts/recording_report.py (Part 3, Stage D, Task D7). A recording holds up to ten runs (each --rebaseline stacks one; glitchygames/recording_history.py); this prints, newest first:

  1. Runs: each run's commit (abbreviated, with uncommitted changes when the checkout had them), machine (CPU model), power source, when it measured and what it rebaselined, then its summary (stored in the header, else computed from the frames): processing p50/p95/p99/max, the worst frame and its scene, frames over budget, the headroom FPS of its processing times (average, 5% low and 5% high: recording_metrics.describe_processing_fps), and a live run's frame times with the FPS it achieved (describe_frame_time_fps). A summary from before the slice means (2026-10-28) shows no FPS.
  2. Processing: for each adjacent pair of runs, the frames that did the same work (equal content hashes) and how their time changed; spans of frames that got slower or faster by more than --threshold percent and --minimum-ms milliseconds. Frames whose hash changed are different work, never a speed change.
  3. Behaviour changes: for each adjacent pair of runs, the spans of frames whose content hash differs, with the first changed frame's scene and both runs' commits: where to look, and the commit range to bisect.

The analysis is glitchygames/recording_metrics.py; this is its command line, on both front ends (glitchygames/replay/tools/registry.py). It runs no game:

  • On the game: mygame --report PATH [--threshold PERCENT] [--minimum-ms MS] [--spans N] (report_on_the_game) runs from GameEngine.__init__, before the engine starts pygame: the game is neither built nor shown.
  • The command: glitchygames report PATH [same options] (report_command).
Usage

uv run glitchygames report src/games/paddleslap/tests/fixtures/replays/golden.jsonl.gz uv run glitchygames report PATH --threshold 10 --minimum-ms 0.1 --spans 50

Exit codes: SUCCESS; MISSING_INPUT when the file does not exist; UNUSABLE_INPUT when it is not a readable recording.

def describe_run(*, run_index: int, run: MeasurementRun | None) -> str:
    """Describe one run's provenance on one line.

    Args:
        run_index: The run's index (0: the newest).
        run: The run, or None when its header entry is unreadable.

    Returns:
        ``run 0: def5678 (uncommitted changes), machine Apple M4 Max, power mains, measured
        2026-10-23T20:00:00+00:00, rebaselined from OLD``.

    """
    if run is None:
        return f'run {run_index}: unreadable'
    commit = short_commit(run=run) or UNKNOWN_COMMIT
    revision = run.game_or_engine_revision
    if revision is not None and revision.uncommitted_changes:
        commit = f'{commit} (uncommitted changes)'
    power = (
        run.machine_state.power_source
        if run.machine_state is not None and run.machine_state.power_source is not None
        else 'unknown'
    )
    origin = (
        f'rebaselined from {run.rebaselined_from}'
        if run.rebaselined_from is not None
        else f'{"paced" if run.processing_paced else "unpaced"} live run'
    )
    return (
        f'run {run_index}: {commit}, machine {machine_label(run=run)}, power {power}, '
        f'measured {run.measured_at}, {origin}'
    )

def describe_summary(*, summary: RunSummary | None) -> str:
    """Describe a run's summary on one line.

    Args:
        summary: The summary, or None when the run measured no times.

    Returns:
        The frames, processing percentiles, worst frame, frames over budget, headroom FPS
        and (for a live run) its frame times and achieved FPS; the FPS only when the summary
        has its slice means.

    """
    if summary is None:
        return 'no processing times'
    scene = '' if summary.worst_frame_scene is None else f', scene {summary.worst_frame_scene}'
    line = (
        f'{summary.measured_frames} frames, processing p50 '
        f'{_milliseconds(summary.p50_processing_seconds)}, p95 '
        f'{_milliseconds(summary.p95_processing_seconds)}, p99 '
        f'{_milliseconds(summary.p99_processing_seconds)}, max '
        f'{_milliseconds(summary.max_processing_seconds)} (frame {summary.worst_frame}{scene})'
    )
    if summary.budget_seconds is not None:
        line = (
            f'{line}, {summary.frames_over_budget} over the '
            f'{_milliseconds(summary.budget_seconds)} budget'
        )
    headroom = describe_processing_fps(summary=summary)
    if headroom is not None:
        line = f'{line}; headroom {headroom}'
    frame_time = summary.frame_time
    if frame_time is not None:
        late = '' if frame_time.late_frames is None else f', {frame_time.late_frames} late'
        line = (
            f'{line}; frame time p50 {_milliseconds(frame_time.p50_seconds)}, p99 '
            f'{_milliseconds(frame_time.p99_seconds)}, max '
            f'{_milliseconds(frame_time.max_seconds)}{late}'

        achieved = describe_frame_time_fps(frame_time=frame_time)
        if achieved is not None:
            line = f'{line}, achieved {achieved}'
    return line

def report(*, path: Path, threshold_percent: float, minimum_ms: float, span_limit: int) -> ExitCode:
    """Print the report for a recording.

    Args:
        path: The recording (named, as given but with ``/`` separators, in the report's first
            line).
        threshold_percent: How much a same-work frame's time must change, in percent.
        minimum_ms: How much it must change in milliseconds too.
        span_limit: How many spans each comparison lists.

    Returns:
        The exit code (see the module docstring).

    """
    if not path.is_file():
        sys.stderr.write(f'{path.as_posix()}: no such recording\n')
        return ExitCode.MISSING_INPUT
    try:
        trace = read_trace(path=path)
    except TraceFormatError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    lines = report_lines(
        path=path,
        trace=trace,
        threshold_percent=threshold_percent,
        minimum_ms=minimum_ms,
        span_limit=span_limit,
    )
    sys.stdout.write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

def report_lines(
    *,
    path: Path,
    trace: dict[str, Any],
    threshold_percent: float,
    minimum_ms: float,
    span_limit: int,
) -> list[str]:
    """Return the report's lines for a read recording.

    Args:
        path: The recording's path (named in the first line, with ``/`` separators on every
            platform, as ``measure`` and ``verify`` name recordings).
        trace: The recording, read (header fields plus ``frames``).
        threshold_percent: How much a same-work frame's time must change, in percent.
        minimum_ms: How much it must change in milliseconds too.
        span_limit: How many spans each comparison lists.

    Returns:
        The lines.

    """
    frames: list[dict[str, Any]] = trace[FRAMES_FIELD]
    runs = recorded_measurement_runs(header=trace)
    summaries = recording_run_summaries(header=trace, frames=frames)
    lines = [
        f'{path.as_posix()}: {len(frames)} frames, {len(runs)} runs',
        '',
        'Runs (newest first):',
    ]
    for run_index, run in enumerate(runs):
        lines.extend((
            f'  {describe_run(run_index=run_index, run=run)}',
            f'    {describe_summary(summary=summaries[run_index])}',
        ))
    lines.extend((
        '',
        (
            f'Processing (same work only; slower or faster by more than '
            f'{threshold_percent:g}% and {minimum_ms:g} ms):'
        ),
    ))
    comparisons = processing_comparisons(
        header=trace,
        frames=frames,
        speed_change_ratio=threshold_percent / PERCENT,
        minimum_change_seconds=minimum_ms / MILLISECONDS_PER_SECOND,
    )
    for comparison in comparisons:
        lines.append(f'  {comparison.describe()}')
        lines.extend(_span_lines(spans=comparison.spans, span_limit=span_limit))
    lines.extend(('', 'Behaviour changes (content hash, adjacent runs):'))
    for change in behaviour_changes(header=trace, frames=frames):
        lines.append(f'  {change.describe()}')
        lines.extend(_span_lines(spans=change.spans, span_limit=span_limit))
    return lines

docs.title: scripted_sessions
docs.text:
Record a scripted session of a game through the real engine (GameEngine.start).

A scripted session is a game run for real, frame loop and all, with --record-trace, while a supervisor (glitchygames/supervision.py) plays an input script (InputScript, glitchygames/replay/tools/golden_traces.py): at the supervisor slot of frame N it posts the script's key events and per-frame input for frame N + 1 with glitchygames.recording.post_input_event, so the recording holds them as external input, exactly what a player's keys are. frame_count plays the script's frames 0 to frame_count - 1. The record-session tool (glitchygames/replay/tools/registry.py) runs it on the game it is given, with the input script named MODULE:NAME (load_input_script); our own games' golden replays are recorded by scripts/record_scripted_session.py.

The controls tail (controls_tail): after the script's frames the supervisor plays it. Its first frame releases every key the script left held; then it presses whatever it holds (a golden replay's tail exercises the controls the script does not), and it must end with the game's own quit control. The game ends the run: the recording's last frame holds the QUIT the game posted (internal), so a replay whose game no longer quits diverges ("missing internal event"). A game still running QUIT_WAIT_FRAMES after the tail's last input fails the recording (GameDidNotQuitError). A session is N + T + 2 frames long, T being the tail frame of its last input (the quit): the game posts QUIT while handling that frame's events, and the next frame (the last) pumps it. Without a tail, at frame N - 1 the supervisor ends the run (SceneManager.quit_requested, no event), so the recording holds frames 0 to N - 1 and no quit.

Unlike the golden-trace harness, the session runs the real frame loop (SceneManager.start): frames are paced at the game's target FPS, each frame's dt is measured and FPS events are posted, so a --replay-trace replay of the recording (which runs the same loop) matches it frame for frame. Recording takes real time (about 60 frames a second), and two recordings of the same script never have the same bytes (measured frame times differ).

Script placements move sprites directly (they are not input), so a session may not run a frame a placement is scheduled before, unless the placements only steer the script's own input (input_only_placements: PaddleSlap's release its tracked keys and resume tracking). Input scheduled before frame 0 cannot be posted (there is no supervisor slot before it) and is refused.

A game that reads its controls from the frame's polled input (current_input()) never sees a posted event there: SDL updates its polled state only for a real device's events. With polled_input the session's live snapshots show the supervisor's posted input (PostedPolledInput, polled_input_follows), as a real player's would. Only then: without it a session records the snapshots it always did (held keys absent), so a game's re-recordings keep their content hashes.

Host environment events (window shown and focus, audio devices) the dummy video driver posts are external and are recorded; a replay serves them as recorded, so they are harmless. The session drops those queued before the first frame (as the golden-trace harness does), because SDL's dummy driver posts a focus-lost event at startup that would auto-pause a game that pauses on it.

The session never chooses the video driver: whoever runs it does (SDL's dummy drivers in the tests and scripts/record_scripted_session.py, --headless on a game). Importing this module imports the engine (GameEngine), so the tool table imports it only when the tool runs.

Moved from scripts/record_scripted_session.py (Stage D, Task D4b), re-keyed from our game keys to a scene class, an input script and flags (polled_input, input_only_placements).

docs.title: PostedPolledInput
docs.text:
The polled input a real keyboard and mouse would leave behind the supervisor's events.

SDL updates its polled state (pygame.key.get_pressed, pygame.mouse.get_pos and get_pressed) as a real device's events arrive, never for a posted event, so on its own a supervisor's key press is an event that no snapshot shows held. A game that reads held keys or the mouse from the frame's snapshot (current_input()) would never see the script play. This follows each posted event (a key held from its KEYDOWN to its KEYUP, by scancode; the mouse's position and buttons) and overlay lays it over a live snapshot, so the session's snapshots agree with its events as a real player's do. A replay serves the recorded snapshots, so it needs none of this.

Source code in src/glitchygames/replay/tools/scripted_sessions.py 
class PostedPolledInput:
    """The polled input a real keyboard and mouse would leave behind the supervisor's events.

    SDL updates its polled state (``pygame.key.get_pressed``, ``pygame.mouse.get_pos`` and
    ``get_pressed``) as a real device's events arrive, never for a posted event, so on its own a
    supervisor's key press is an event that no snapshot shows held. A game that reads held keys
    or the mouse from the frame's snapshot (``current_input()``) would never see the script
    play. This follows each posted event (a key held from its KEYDOWN to its KEYUP, by
    scancode; the mouse's position and buttons) and ``overlay`` lays it over a live snapshot,
    so the session's snapshots agree with its events as a real player's do. A replay serves the
    recorded snapshots, so it needs none of this.
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Start with nothing posted: no key held, the mouse unmoved, its buttons up."""
        self.held_scancodes: set[int] = set()
        self.mouse_position: tuple[int, int] | None = None
        self.mouse_buttons = [False] * MOUSE_BUTTON_COUNT

    def follow(self, event: pygame.event.Event) -> None:
        """Note what a posted event changes in the polled input.

        Args:
            event: The posted event.

        """
        if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            self.held_scancodes.add(event.scancode)
        elif event.type == pygame.KEYUP:
            self.held_scancodes.discard(event.scancode)
        elif event.type == pygame.MOUSEMOTION:
            self.mouse_position = event.pos
        elif event.type in {pygame.MOUSEBUTTONDOWN, pygame.MOUSEBUTTONUP}:
            # pygame numbers the buttons from 1 (left, middle, right); the snapshot from 0
            button_index = event.button - 1
            if button_index < MOUSE_BUTTON_COUNT:
                self.mouse_buttons[button_index] = event.type == pygame.MOUSEBUTTONDOWN

    def overlay(self, snapshot: InputSnapshot) -> InputSnapshot:
        """Lay the posted input over a live snapshot.

        Args:
            snapshot: The live snapshot.

        Returns:
            The snapshot with the posted held keys added, the posted mouse position (once the
            mouse was moved) and the posted mouse buttons.

        """
        return dataclasses.replace(
            snapshot,
            pressed_scancodes=snapshot.pressed_scancodes | frozenset(self.held_scancodes),
            mouse_position=self.mouse_position or snapshot.mouse_position,
            mouse_buttons=tuple(
                live or posted
                for live, posted in zip(snapshot.mouse_buttons, self.mouse_buttons, strict=True)
            ),
        )

docs.title: ScriptedInputSupervisor
docs.text:
Posts an input script into the real event queue, one frame ahead.

A glitchygames.supervision.Supervisor: at the supervisor slot of frame N it runs the placements and posts the per-frame input and key events the script holds for frame N + 1, so frame N + 1's pump returns them, as the golden-trace harness posts them just before frame N + 1.

Without a controls tail it ends the run at the slot of the last frame (no event). With one, the script stops after frame_count frames: the tail's first frame releases every key the script left held, then the tail's input follows (its frames count from there), and the game must end the run itself, with the quit control the tail presses; if it is still running QUIT_WAIT_FRAMES after the tail's last input, the supervisor ends the run and sets game_did_not_quit.

Source code in src/glitchygames/replay/tools/scripted_sessions.py 
class ScriptedInputSupervisor:
    """Posts an input script into the real event queue, one frame ahead.

    A glitchygames.supervision.Supervisor: at the supervisor slot of frame N it runs the
    placements and posts the per-frame input and key events the script holds for frame N + 1, so
    frame N + 1's pump returns them, as the golden-trace harness posts them just before frame
    N + 1.

    Without a controls tail it ends the run at the slot of the last frame (no event). With one,
    the script stops after ``frame_count`` frames: the tail's first frame releases every key the
    script left held, then the tail's input follows (its frames count from there), and the game
    must end the run itself, with the quit control the tail presses; if it is still running
    QUIT_WAIT_FRAMES after the tail's last input, the supervisor ends the run and sets
    ``game_did_not_quit``.
    """

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        script: InputScript,
        frame_count: int,
        scene_manager: SceneManager,
        controls_tail: InputScript | None = None,
        input_only_placements: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Check the script can be recorded as input for this many frames.

        Args:
            script: The game's input script.
            frame_count: How many of the script's frames the session plays (frames 0 to
                frame_count - 1); without a controls tail, the session's length.
            scene_manager: The scene manager whose run ends after the last frame.
            controls_tail: Key events played after the script's frames, ending with the game's
                quit control, or None to end after the script.
            input_only_placements: True when the script's placements only steer its own input
                (they move no sprite), so they may run inside the session.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a placement falls inside the session and ``input_only_placements``
                is False, if the script holds input for frame 0, or if the controls tail holds
                placements, per-frame input or no input at all.

        """
        refusal = scripted_session_refusal(
            script=script,
            frame_count=frame_count,
            controls_tail=controls_tail,
            input_only_placements=input_only_placements,
        )
        if refusal is not None:
            raise ValueError(refusal)
        self.script = script
        self.frame_count = frame_count
        self.scene_manager = scene_manager
        self.controls_tail = controls_tail
        # Keys the posted script input left down (released when the controls tail starts)
        self.held_keys: set[int] = set()
        # The polled input the posted events would leave behind (polled_input_follows)
        self.posted_input = PostedPolledInput()
        self.game_did_not_quit = False

    def on_frame(self: Self, *, frame_number: int, scene: Scene | None) -> None:
        """Post the next frame's scripted input; end the run at the last frame.

        Args:
            frame_number: The frame being run.
            scene: The active scene at the supervisor slot.

        """
        next_frame = frame_number + 1
        if self.controls_tail is not None and next_frame >= self.frame_count:
            self._post_controls_tail(tail_frame=next_frame - self.frame_count)
            return
        if frame_number >= self.frame_count - 1:
            # No event: the loop ends after this frame, so the recording holds no quit request
            self.scene_manager.quit_requested = True
            return
        if scene is not None:
            for placement in self.script.placements.get(next_frame, []):
                placement(scene)
            # Per-frame input for frame 0 is never posted: no supervisor slot runs before it
            if self.script.per_frame is not None:
                for event in self.script.per_frame(scene):
                    self._post(event)
        for event in self.script.key_events.get(next_frame, []):
            self._post(event)

    def _post_controls_tail(self: Self, *, tail_frame: int) -> None:
        """Post a frame of the controls tail; end the run if the game has not quit in time.

        Args:
            tail_frame: The frame being posted for, counted from the tail's first frame.

        """
        assert self.controls_tail is not None
        if tail_frame == 0:
            for key in sorted(self.held_keys):
                self._post(release(key))
        if tail_frame > max(self.controls_tail.key_events) + QUIT_WAIT_FRAMES:
            self.game_did_not_quit = True
            self.scene_manager.quit_requested = True
            return
        for event in self.controls_tail.key_events.get(tail_frame, []):
            self._post(event)

    def _post(self: Self, event: pygame.event.Event) -> None:
        """Post an event as external input, noting which keys are held and the polled input.

        Args:
            event: The event.

        """
        if event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            self.held_keys.add(event.key)
        elif event.type == pygame.KEYUP:
            self.held_keys.discard(event.key)
        self.posted_input.follow(event)
        post_input_event(event)

@contextlib.contextmanager
def polled_input_follows(posted_input: PostedPolledInput) -> Generator[None]:
    """Make the live doors' snapshots show the posted input (``PostedPolledInput``).

    Replaces ``glitchygames.live_sources.capture_live_snapshot`` (the live doors' one polling
    call) with one that overlays the posted input, then puts it back.

    Args:
        posted_input: The input the supervisor posted.

    Yields:
        None, while the live snapshots show it.

    """
    original_capture = live_sources.capture_live_snapshot

    def capture_with_posted_input(**device_positions: Any) -> InputSnapshot:
        return posted_input.overlay(original_capture(**device_positions))

    # By name, as deterministic_environment replaces the save directory: a type checker will not
    # let a module's function be assigned another
    setattr(live_sources, LIVE_CAPTURE_FUNCTION_NAME, capture_with_posted_input)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        setattr(live_sources, LIVE_CAPTURE_FUNCTION_NAME, original_capture)

def record_scripted_session(
    *,
    scene_class: type[Scene],
    script: InputScript,
    frame_count: int,
    path: Path,
    **options: Unpack[ScriptedSessionOptions],
) -> None:
    """Run a game for real with an input script and ``--record-trace``.

    Saves go to a temporary directory. The SceneManager singleton is fresh for the session and
    cleared afterwards. GameEngine._shutdown quits pygame at the end, as a real run does.

    Args:
        scene_class: The game's scene class.
        script: Its input script (a fresh one: a per-frame input holds state across frames).
        frame_count: How many of the script's frames to record.
        path: Where the recording goes (its directory is created).
        **options: How the session is played, by keyword (``ScriptedSessionOptions``).

    A script that cannot be recorded as input for this many frames
    (``scripted_session_refusal``) raises the supervisor's ValueError before anything runs.

    Raises:
        GameDidNotQuitError: If the controls tail's quit control did not end the run.

    """
    controls_tail = options.get('controls_tail')
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (
        tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='scripted-session-saves-') as save_directory,
        deterministic_environment(save_root=Path(save_directory)),
    ):
        # A caller that keeps pygame running (a test) may have left events queued: a game's own
        # internal events, which this session's first frame would pump and record as its own
        # (and its replay, never posting them, diverges). The session starts on an empty queue
        clear_events_left_queued()
        manager = GoldenTraceSceneManager.install()
        try:
            # Built before the engine, so a script that can't be recorded opens no window
            supervisor = ScriptedInputSupervisor(
                script=script,
                frame_count=frame_count,
                scene_manager=manager,
                controls_tail=controls_tail,
                input_only_placements=options.get('input_only_placements', False),
            )
            with command_line([
                '--windowed',
                '--resolution',
                SCREEN_RESOLUTION,
                '--log-level',
                'warning',
                '--input-mode',
                'joystick',
                *seed_arguments(random_seed=options.get('random_seed')),
                '--record-trace',
                str(path),
            ]):
                engine = GoldenTraceEngine(game=scene_class)
            # Added after the engine: GameEngine.__init__ resets the scene manager's supervision
            manager.add_supervisor(supervisor=supervisor)
            discard_environment_events()
            with (
                polled_input_follows(supervisor.posted_input)
                if options.get('polled_input')
                else contextlib.nullcontext()
            ):
                engine.start()
        finally:
            # GameEngine._shutdown normally quits pygame (the queue went with it); a caller that
            # keeps pygame running (a test) gets an empty queue back
            clear_events_left_queued()
            GoldenTraceSceneManager.uninstall()
    if supervisor.game_did_not_quit:
        message = (
            f'{logical_name(scene_class=scene_class)} was still running {QUIT_WAIT_FRAMES} '
            f'frames after its controls tail pressed quit: {path} does not end with the game '
            'quitting'
        )
        raise GameDidNotQuitError(message)

def scripted_session_refusal(
    *,
    script: InputScript,
    frame_count: int,
    controls_tail: InputScript | None = None,
    input_only_placements: bool = False,
) -> str | None:
    """Say why a script cannot be recorded as input for this many frames, if it cannot.

    Checked before anything runs (``ScriptedInputSupervisor`` raises it as a ValueError; the
    ``record-session`` tool refuses it), so a session that can't be recorded builds no engine.

    Args:
        script: The game's input script.
        frame_count: How many of the script's frames the session plays.
        controls_tail: Key events played after the script's frames, or None.
        input_only_placements: True when the script's placements only steer its own input.

    Returns:
        Why, or None when it can be recorded: a placement inside the session (unless
        ``input_only_placements``), input before frame 0, or a controls tail that is not key
        events only, and some.

    """
    placed_frames = sorted(
        frame_number for frame_number in script.placements if frame_number < frame_count
    )
    if placed_frames and not input_only_placements:
        return (
            f'the script places sprites directly at frame {placed_frames[0]}; it cannot be '
            f'recorded as input past frame {placed_frames[0] - 1} (record at most '
            f'{placed_frames[0]} frames, or, if its placements only steer its own input, '
            'allow them: input_only_placements, --input-only-placements)'
        )
    if script.key_events.get(0) or script.placements.get(0):
        return 'the script has input before frame 0, which no supervisor can post'
    if controls_tail is not None and (
        controls_tail.placements
        or controls_tail.per_frame is not None
        or not controls_tail.key_events
    ):
        return 'a controls tail must hold key events only, and some'
    return None

docs.title: settings
docs.text:
A project's settings for the engine's tools, from [tool.glitchygames] in its pyproject.toml.

Every setting has a default that fits a standard layout, so a project with no such table (a player's own local runs, a game the engine has never seen) works as it is. The keys are kebab-case, as pyproject.toml's are (stage D's settings table):

  • games: the console scripts the tools run when given no game (default: the project's [project.scripts]).
  • golden-globs: where the golden replays are, as globs relative to the project root.
  • ledger-directory: where measured rows are kept as row files (a git pathspec too, so it is relative).
  • pending-ledger: where measured rows wait to be published (default: in the project's local directory, .glitchygames/, outside the ledger directory so it is never committed with the rows).
  • published-ledger: where the ledger is published, as REF:PATH (what git show reads), or nothing published (the default).
  • landed-ref: the ref whose commits count as landed.
  • measured-paths and unmeasured-paths: what a code tree holds, as git pathspecs (glitchygames/code_tree.py).
  • recording-renames: recordings that moved, old repository path -> new, so a recording's history follows it. Each path is relative, no new path is itself an old one (lookups are one hop: an old path names the final one directly), and no two old paths are the same path written two ways; refused when read otherwise. recording_renames_problems finds a new path that does not exist and an old one that still does (a check of the files, which reading settings never does).
  • game-timeout-seconds: how long glitchygames verify and glitchygames measure wait for each game they start (GAME --verify, GAME --measure) before stopping it and failing it (default: an hour, DEFAULT_GAME_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). A game replays each of its recordings in a child of its own with a timeout of its own (REPLAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS); this bounds what never ends at all, such as an editor or a server among [project.scripts].

Stored paths are relative to the project root. Every path the tools write into a file (a recording header's path options, a run's rebaselined_from, a ledger row's recording) is relative to the project root, the one these settings are read from (find_project_root: the nearest project; --project-root where a tool's subcommand takes it), POSIX-style; a path inside another checkout of the same project (the same [project] name) relative to that checkout's root; any other path outside the project as its file name only (stored_path), so no user name, home or scratch directory is ever written into a file meant to be committed.

Settings only name paths, relative to the project root: nothing is created or checked on disk when they are read. A path that doesn't exist yet (no ledger directory before the first measurement) is created or reported by the tool that writes or reads it. A tool writing into the project's local directory (.glitchygames/) creates it with ensure_local_directory, which puts a .gitignore of * there, as pytest does for its cache, so nothing in it is committed.

Part 3, Stage D, Task D2: these replaced the module constants of glitchygames/code_tree.py and glitchygames/recording_metrics.py (LEDGER_DIRECTORY, MEASURED_PATHS, the member-test pathspecs, ORIGIN_MAIN, PUBLISHED_LEDGER_PATH/_REF, PENDING_LEDGER_RELATIVE_PATH and RECORDING_PATH_RENAMES), whose values are now ours in the root pyproject.toml.

class ProjectSettings(BaseModel):
    """A project's settings for the engine's tools (see the module docstring for each).

    Attributes:
        games: The console scripts the tools run when given no game.
        golden_globs: Where the golden replays are, as globs relative to the project root.
        ledger_directory: Where measured rows are kept as row files, relative to the project
            root.
        pending_ledger: Where measured rows wait to be published, relative to the project root.
        published_ledger: Where the ledger is published, as ``REF:PATH``, or None.
        landed_ref: The ref whose commits count as landed.
        measured_paths: The git pathspecs a code tree holds.
        unmeasured_paths: The git pathspecs left out of them.
        recording_renames: Recordings that moved, old repository path -> new.
        game_timeout_seconds: How long ``verify`` and ``measure`` wait for each game they start
            before stopping it (a finite number above 0).

    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        frozen=True,
        extra='forbid',
        alias_generator=kebab_case,
        validate_by_alias=True,
        validate_by_name=True,
    )

    games: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    golden_globs: tuple[str, ...] = ('tests/fixtures/replays/**/*.jsonl.gz',)
    ledger_directory: str = 'replay-ledger'
    pending_ledger: str = f'{LOCAL_DIRECTORY_NAME}/pending-ledger.jsonl'
    published_ledger: str | None = None
    landed_ref: str = 'origin/main'
    measured_paths: tuple[str, ...] = ('src', 'tests/fixtures/replays', 'pyproject.toml')
    unmeasured_paths: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    recording_renames: RecordingRenames = {}
    game_timeout_seconds: float = Field(
        default=DEFAULT_GAME_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, gt=0, allow_inf_nan=False
    )

    @field_validator('ledger_directory')
    @classmethod
    def _relative_ledger_directory(cls, value: str) -> str:
        """Refuse an absolute ledger directory: git reads it as a pathspec of the repository.

        Returns:
            The value.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If it is absolute.

        """
        if PurePosixPath(value).is_absolute() or PureWindowsPath(value).is_absolute():
            message = f'{value!r} must be relative to the project root (it is a git pathspec)'
            raise ValueError(message)
        return value

    @field_validator('recording_renames')
    @classmethod
    def _one_hop_renames(cls, value: RecordingRenames) -> RecordingRenames:
        """Refuse a renames table a one-hop lookup would misread.

        Returns:
            The value.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If a path is absolute, an old path is the same as its new one or the
                same path as another old one, or a new path is itself an old one (a chain).

        """
        normalized_sources: dict[str, str] = {}
        for source, target in value.items():
            for path in (source, target):
                if is_absolute_path(text=path):
                    message = f'{path!r} must be relative to the project root'
                    raise ValueError(message)
            normalized_source = posixpath.normpath(source)
            if normalized_source == posixpath.normpath(target):
                message = f'{source!r} is renamed to itself'
                raise ValueError(message)
            if normalized_source in normalized_sources:
                message = (
                    f'{source!r} and {normalized_sources[normalized_source]!r} are the same old '
                    'path'
                )
                raise ValueError(message)
            normalized_sources[normalized_source] = source
        for source, target in value.items():
            chained = normalized_sources.get(posixpath.normpath(target))
            if chained is not None:
                message = (
                    f'{source!r} is renamed to {target!r}, which is itself renamed: lookups take '
                    f'one hop, so name the final path ({value[chained]!r}) instead'
                )
                raise ValueError(message)
        return value

    @field_validator('published_ledger')
    @classmethod
    def _ref_and_path(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        """Refuse a published ledger that is not ``REF:PATH``.

        Returns:
            The value.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the ref or the path is missing.

        """
        if value is None:
            return value
        ref, separator, path = value.partition(PUBLISHED_LEDGER_SEPARATOR)
        if not (ref and separator and path):
            message = f'{value!r} is not REF:PATH (origin/gh-pages:metrics/ledger.jsonl)'
            raise ValueError(message)
        return value

    @property
    def published_ledger_ref(self: Self) -> str | None:
        """The ref the ledger is published on, or None when nothing is published."""
        if self.published_ledger is None:
            return None
        return self.published_ledger.partition(PUBLISHED_LEDGER_SEPARATOR)[0]

    @property
    def published_ledger_path(self: Self) -> str | None:
        """The ledger's path on its ref, or None when nothing is published."""
        if self.published_ledger is None:
            return None
        return self.published_ledger.partition(PUBLISHED_LEDGER_SEPARATOR)[2]

    @property
    def code_tree_paths(self: Self) -> CodeTreePaths:
        """What a code tree holds (glitchygames/code_tree.py)."""
        return CodeTreePaths(measured=self.measured_paths, unmeasured=self.unmeasured_paths)

def ensure_local_directory(*, directory: Path) -> Path:
    """Create a project's local directory (``.glitchygames/``) and keep git out of it.

    Every tool that writes there (the default pending ledger) calls this first. A ``.gitignore``
    holding ``*`` is written when the directory has none, as pytest does for its cache, so a
    file there never shows in ``git status``; an existing one is left as it is.

    Args:
        directory: The directory (``<project root>/.glitchygames``).

    Returns:
        The directory.

    """
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    gitignore = directory / GITIGNORE_FILE_NAME
    if not gitignore.exists():
        gitignore.write_text(LOCAL_DIRECTORY_GITIGNORE, encoding='utf-8')
    return directory

def find_project_root(*, start: Path, named: str | None = None) -> Path | None:
    """Return the project a directory is in, as git finds its repository.

    How a tool run from inside a project (``tests/fixtures/``, a workspace member's directory)
    finds the project's settings and recordings. The nearest pyproject.toml with a
    ``[tool.glitchygames]`` table wins, so inside a workspace member without one the workspace
    root that has them is the project (the controller's ruling, Part 3 Stage D, Task D5's fix
    round: the member would otherwise own the ledger); a project with no such table anywhere is
    its nearest pyproject.toml.

    With ``named``, the checkout of that project a path lies in (``stored_path``): the nearest
    of ``start`` and its ancestors whose ``pyproject.toml`` names that ``[project] name`` (a
    workspace member's own pyproject.toml, of another name, is passed by), whether or not it
    has the settings table; a pyproject.toml that cannot be read is passed by too.

    Args:
        start: The directory to look from (the current directory, usually).
        named: The project's name to look for, or None for the project's settings above.

    Returns:
        The nearest of ``start`` and its ancestors whose ``pyproject.toml`` has
        ``[tool.glitchygames]``; else the nearest holding a ``pyproject.toml``; else None. With
        ``named``: the nearest whose ``pyproject.toml`` is that project's, else None.

    """
    absolute = start.absolute()
    nearest: Path | None = None
    for directory in (absolute, *absolute.parents):
        pyproject = directory / PYPROJECT_FILE_NAME
        if not pyproject.is_file():
            continue
        if named is not None:
            if _names_project(project_root=directory, name=named):
                return directory
            continue
        if has_settings_table(pyproject=pyproject):
            return directory
        if nearest is None:
            nearest = directory
    return nearest

def has_settings_table(*, pyproject: Path) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a pyproject.toml has a ``[tool.glitchygames]`` table.

    Args:
        pyproject: The file.

    Returns:
        True if it holds the table; False if it doesn't, or isn't TOML (its settings are refused
        when they are read, by ``load_project_settings``).

    """
    try:
        document = tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    except tomllib.TOMLDecodeError:
        return False
    tool = document.get('tool')
    return isinstance(tool, dict) and SETTINGS_TABLE in tool

def is_absolute_path(*, text: str) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a stored path is absolute on any platform, or starts at a home directory.

    Args:
        text: The path as stored.

    Returns:
        True for a POSIX root (``/...``), a home directory (``~...``), a Windows drive
        (``X:`` then a slash or backslash) or a Windows share (two backslashes, a server).

    """
    return (
        text.startswith('~')
        or PurePosixPath(text).is_absolute()
        or PureWindowsPath(text).is_absolute()
    )

def load_project_settings(*, project_root: Path) -> ProjectSettings:
    """Read a project's settings from ``[tool.glitchygames]`` in its pyproject.toml.

    A missing file or table gives the defaults; ``games`` defaults to the keys of the project's
    ``[project.scripts]``, in their order. Nothing on disk is created or checked.

    Args:
        project_root: The project's root directory (where its pyproject.toml is).

    Returns:
        The settings.

    Raises:
        ProjectSettingsError: If the file is not valid TOML, the table is not a table, or a
            key is unknown or its value of the wrong shape (named in the message).

    """
    pyproject = project_root / PYPROJECT_FILE_NAME
    document = _read_pyproject(pyproject=pyproject)
    tool = _table(pyproject=pyproject, parent=document, key='tool', name='tool')
    settings = dict(
        _table(pyproject=pyproject, parent=tool, key=SETTINGS_TABLE, name=f'tool.{SETTINGS_TABLE}')
    )
    if 'games' not in settings:
        project = _table(pyproject=pyproject, parent=document, key='project', name='project')
        scripts = _table(pyproject=pyproject, parent=project, key='scripts', name='project.scripts')
        settings['games'] = list(scripts)
    try:
        # Only the kebab-case keys are settings: ledger_directory is a misspelling
        return ProjectSettings.model_validate(settings, by_alias=True, by_name=False)
    except ValidationError as error:
        raise ProjectSettingsError(_refusal(pyproject=pyproject, error=error)) from None

def recording_renames_problems(*, settings: ProjectSettings, project_root: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Return each recording rename whose new path does not exist, or whose old path still does.

    The table's shape is checked as it is read (``ProjectSettings``); this checks the files. An
    old path still holding a file is no finished move: its runs and the new path's would be
    counted as one recording's.

    Args:
        settings: The project's settings.
        project_root: The project's root.

    Returns:
        One line per problem, in the table's order (empty when there is none).

    """
    problems: list[str] = []
    for source, target in settings.recording_renames.items():
        if not (project_root / target).is_file():
            problems.append(f'{source} is renamed to {target}, which does not exist')
        if (project_root / source).exists():
            problems.append(f'{source} is renamed to {target}, but {source} still exists')
    return problems

A relative path is read from the current directory, as the tool read it. A path inside the project is stored relative to its root, POSIX-style (src/games/x/golden.jsonl.gz). A path inside another checkout of the same project (a clone or worktree: the nearest directory above it whose pyproject.toml has the project's [project] name, find_project_root(named=...)) is stored relative to that checkout's root, the same way (the user, 2026-10-27). def stored_path(*, path: str | os.PathLike[str], project_root: Path | None) -> str:
    """Return a path as the tools store it in a file: relative to the project root.

    A relative path is read from the current directory, as the tool read it. A path inside the
    project is stored relative to its root, POSIX-style (``src/games/x/golden.jsonl.gz``). A
    path inside another checkout of the same project (a clone or worktree: the nearest
    directory above it whose pyproject.toml has the project's ``[project] name``,
    ``find_project_root(named=...)``) is stored relative to that checkout's root, the same way
    (the user, 2026-10-27). Any other path (a scratch directory, another project), or any path
    when there is no project, is stored as its file name only, so no user name or home
    directory is written.

    Args:
        path: The path as given.
        project_root: The project's root (``find_project_root``), or None.

    Returns:
        The stored path.

    """
    resolved = Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
    if project_root is None:
        return resolved.name
    root = project_root.resolve()
    if resolved.is_relative_to(root):
        return resolved.relative_to(root).as_posix()
    name = _project_name_or_none(project_root=root)
    checkout = None if name is None else find_project_root(start=resolved.parent, named=name)
    if checkout is None:
        return resolved.name
    return resolved.relative_to(checkout).as_posix()

docs.title: sound_tools
docs.text:
The sound-render and sound-migrate tools: a sound to a WAV file, and v0 recipes to v1.

Both run no game (registry.py's TOOLS):

  • sound-render (mygame --sound-render SOURCE --sound-output PATH [--sample-format F], or glitchygames sound-render ...): compiles SOURCE (a sound file and the sound in it, sounds/pickups.toml#coin, or a WAV/OGG file) as a game's audio.sound would, with no mixer running, and writes it with glitchygames.audio.render_to_file (offline: no audio device; the compiled buffer bit for bit). An OGG file needs a mixer to decode, so it is refused here (UNUSABLE_INPUT).
  • sound-migrate (mygame --sound-migrate FILE [--migrated-output PATH], or glitchygames sound-migrate ...): rewrites a version 0 recipe file ([recipes.<name>]) as a version 1 sound file (feature spec 9.1; impl spec 10.4), written with tomli_w beside it as <stem>.v1.toml (or at PATH; never over FILE). Each recipe becomes an instrument and a sound of the same name: each tone a source (tone_1...: its wave or white noise, its start pitch, its pitch curve, its filter and its volume as the source's level), the tones' shared envelope the instrument's (linear, as version 0's), the recipe's peak the instrument's normalization (version 1 normalizes to -1 dBFS, so the sound's volume is the recipe's volume x peak / that level, the same loudness), and the sound held for the tones' duration less the release (version 0's release ends inside the duration; version 1's follows the held part). Migrated sounds follow the version 1 renderer (band-limited waves, its envelope stages, its noise seed), so they are close to the recipe, not equal to it: impl spec 10.4 checks them by listening.

A recipe version 1 cannot say yet is refused, every such field named with the milestone that would make it migratable (or that none plans it), and nothing is written (games keep their version 0 files, which compile bit-identically through the legacy renderer): a tone that starts late (offset; per-tone offsets arrive in M4), a tremolo (LFOs arrive in M4), distortion (no version 1 form), both filters on one tone, tones held for different durations or with different envelopes (a version 1 sound has one length and the instrument one envelope), a tone not longer than its envelope's stages, more than four tones, a tone or recipe louder than a version 1 level or volume can be (1). The written file is loaded as a version 1 file before it replaces anything, so a value version 1 refuses (a sustain level above 1) is reported as the loader reports it.

Exit codes (ExitCode): SUCCESS; MISSING_INPUT when the sound or recipe file does not exist; UNUSABLE_INPUT when it cannot be read, is not what the tool takes or cannot be migrated; OPTIONS_REFUSED when the migrated file would overwrite its input; CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT when the output cannot be written.

def migrated_document(sound_file: SoundFile) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the version 1 document of a version 0 file whose recipes can all be migrated.

    Args:
        sound_file: The loaded version 0 file (``migration_problems`` finds none in it).

    Returns:
        The TOML document: the header, an instrument and a sound per recipe, by name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When a recipe cannot be migrated (naming each problem).
    """
    problems = migration_problems(sound_file)
    if problems:
        raise ValueError('\n'.join(problems))
    instruments: dict[str, Any] = {}
    sounds: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for name, entry in sound_file.sounds.items():
        recipe = entry.legacy_recipe
        assert recipe is not None
        instruments[name] = _instrument_table(recipe)
        sounds[name] = _sound_table(recipe, instrument=name)
    return {
        'glitchygames': {'kind': SOUND_FILE_KIND, 'version': CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION},
        'instruments': instruments,
        'sounds': sounds,
    }

def sound_migrate(*, path: Path, output: Path | None) -> ExitCode:  # ruff: ignore[too-many-return-statements] - one exit per refusal, in the order the docstring lists them
    """Rewrite a version 0 recipe file as a version 1 sound file.

    Args:
        path: The version 0 file.
        output: Where to write the version 1 file (None: ``migrated_path``).

    Returns:
        The exit code (see the module docstring).
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        sys.stderr.write(f'{path}: no such recipe file\n')
        return ExitCode.MISSING_INPUT
    destination = migrated_path(path=path) if output is None else output
    if destination.resolve() == path.resolve():
        sys.stderr.write(
            f'{destination}: would overwrite the file it migrates; give another --migrated-output\n'
        )
        return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
    try:
        sound_file = load_sound_file(path)
    except SoundAssetError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    if sound_file.version != LEGACY_SCHEMA_VERSION:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{path} is already a version {sound_file.version} sound file\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    problems = migration_problems(sound_file)
    if problems:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{path} cannot be migrated to version {CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION} yet:\n')
        sys.stderr.writelines(f'  {problem}\n' for problem in problems)
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    refusal = output_refusal(path=destination)
    if refusal is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{refusal}\n')
        return ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT
    text = tomli_w.dumps(migrated_document(sound_file))

    def write_checked(aside: Path) -> None:
        aside.write_text(text, encoding='utf-8')
        # Load what was written as a version 1 file before it replaces anything
        load_sound_file(aside)

    try:
        write_aside_then_replace(destination=destination, write=write_checked)
    except SoundAssetError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{path}: the migrated file would not load: {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    except OSError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{destination} cannot be written ({error.strerror or error})\n')
        return ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT
    sys.stdout.write(f'wrote {destination}: {len(sound_file.sounds)} sounds\n')
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

def sound_render(*, source: str, output: Path, sample_format: str) -> ExitCode:
    """Render a sound to a WAV file offline.

    Args:
        source: ``FILE#name`` (a sound file and the sound in it) or a WAV/OGG file.
        output: The WAV file to write.
        sample_format: ``int16`` or ``float32``.

    Returns:
        The exit code (see the module docstring).
    """
    sound_path = Path(source.partition(INSTRUMENT_SEPARATOR)[0])
    if not sound_path.is_file():
        sys.stderr.write(f'{sound_path}: no such sound file\n')
        return ExitCode.MISSING_INPUT
    refusal = output_refusal(path=output)
    if refusal is not None:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{refusal}\n')
        return ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT
    library = SoundLibrary(
        cache=CacheMode.RAM,
        accountant=AudioAccountant(),
        waves=current_wave_registry(),
        tuning_source=Tuning,
    )
    try:
        sound = library.sound(source, scene_sound_directory=None)
    except KeyError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{source}: {error.args[0]}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    except (SoundAssetError, SoundRenderError, ValueError) as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{source}: {error}\n')
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    try:
        report = render_to_file(sound, output, sample_format=sample_format)
    except OSError as error:
        sys.stderr.write(f'{output} cannot be written ({error.strerror or error})\n')
        return ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT
    sys.stdout.write(
        f'wrote {report.path}: {report.frames} frames at {sound.sample_rate} Hz, '
        f'peak {report.peak:.3f}, {report.clip_count} samples clipped\n'
    )
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

docs.title: traces
docs.text:
glitchygames record-trace, replay-trace, record-golden-trace, record-session.

Each of these tools runs the game, so its subcommand starts it as a child process with the tool's flag (Tool.child_arguments: --record-trace PATH, --replay-trace PATH, --record-golden-trace PATH, --record-session PATH and the options given), where the game's own engine records or replays exactly as the flag on the game does. The child's exit status is the command's.

  • record-trace GAME PATH: GAME is read by children.resolve_game (a script path, an entry point, a console script or a module).
  • record-golden-trace GAME PATH --input-script MODULE:NAME --frame-count N: GAME is read as record-trace's is. On the game, the flag runs the golden-trace harness in place of the game's own run (record_golden_trace_on_the_game): the game's scene class, driven by the input script for N frames at a fixed 1/60 second, every sprite sampled each frame (glitchygames/replay/tools/golden_traces.py).
  • record-session GAME PATH --input-script MODULE:NAME --frame-count N: GAME is read as record-trace's is. On the game, the flag records a scripted session in place of the game's own run (record_session_on_the_game): the game's scene class run for real, its own frame loop recorded with --record-trace, while a supervisor plays the input script (and a --controls-tail) as a player's input (glitchygames/replay/tools/scripted_sessions.py).
  • replay-trace PATH: the game is the one the recording's header names: the installed console script that starts its module (children.console_script_for_game_module). When that module no longer imports (a moved script), or no console script starts it, the command asks for --game GAME, read as record-trace's GAME is.

Arguments after a bare -- go to the game unchanged (--resolution 640x480). The command says on standard error which game it runs and how it read it.

def find_recorded_game(
    *, recording: Path, project_root: Path
) -> tuple[str, GameLaunch] | RecordedGameRefusal:
    """Find the game a recording's header names: the console script that starts its module.

    Args:
        recording: The recording.
        project_root: The project (where the game's module may be found too).

    Returns:
        The console script and how to start it, or why it can't be found.

    """
    try:
        game_module = recorded_game_module(path=recording)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return RecordedGameRefusal(
            exit_code=ExitCode.MISSING_INPUT, reason=f'{recording.as_posix()}: no such recording'
        )
    # A TraceFormatError is a ValueError
    except OSError, ValueError:
        return RecordedGameRefusal(
            exit_code=ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT,
            reason=f'{recording.as_posix()}: not a readable recording',
        )
    except KeyError as error:
        return game_not_found(reason=f'{error.args[0]}, so it names no game')
    if not module_is_importable(module=game_module, search_directory=project_root):
        return game_not_found(
            reason=f"{recording.as_posix()}: its game's module {game_module!r} no longer imports"
        )
    try:
        console_script = console_script_for_game_module(
            entry_points=installed_console_scripts(), game_module=game_module
        )
    except KeyError as error:
        return game_not_found(
            reason=f'{recording.as_posix()}: no one console script starts it ({error.args[0]})'
        )
    entry_point = game_entry_point(console_script=console_script)
    return console_script, GameLaunch(
        form='console-script', command=entry_point_command(entry_point=entry_point)
    )

def record_golden_trace_on_the_game(
    *, options: dict[str, Any], game: type[Scene] | Scene
) -> ExitCode:
    """Run ``--record-golden-trace PATH`` on a game: record its golden trace in place of its run.

    The game's scene class (a scene the game passed in is run by its class) runs in the
    golden-trace harness, driven by ``--input-script MODULE:NAME`` (``load_input_script``: a
    callable taking no arguments that returns an ``InputScript``) for ``--frame-count N``
    frames, seeded by ``--random-seed`` (a random seed when not given, as any run rolls one,
    which the trace then names as ``random_seed``, so the golden can be made again under it).
    The trace is written to PATH with the golden source (``GOLDEN_TRACE_SOURCE``), as
    scripts/record_golden_traces.py writes ours.

    Args:
        options: The game's parsed options (the engine's ``options``).
        game: The game (its class, or a scene the game passed in).

    Returns:
        ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` once the trace is written; ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` when the
        input script reference names no input script; ``ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT`` when
        the trace can't be written.

    """
    # Imported here: the harness imports the engine, which imports the tool table (this module)
    from glitchygames.replay.tools import golden_traces
    from glitchygames.scenes import Scene
    from glitchygames.tracing import write_trace

    try:
        script = golden_traces.load_input_script(reference=options['input_script'])
    except golden_traces.InputScriptError as error:
        return refused(message=f'--input-script: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
    trace = golden_traces.record_trace(
        scene_class=type(game) if isinstance(game, Scene) else game,
        script=script,
        frame_count=options['frame_count'],
        random_seed=options.get('random_seed'),
    )
    path = Path(options['record_golden_trace'])
    try:
        write_trace(trace={'source': golden_traces.GOLDEN_TRACE_SOURCE, **trace}, path=path)
    except OSError as error:
        return refused(
            message=f'--record-golden-trace: cannot write {path} ({error})',
            exit_code=ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT,
        )
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

with the game quitting); ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT when the recording's

def record_session_on_the_game(*, options: dict[str, Any], game: type[Scene] | Scene) -> ExitCode:
    """Run ``--record-session PATH`` on a game: record a scripted session in place of its run.

    The game's scene class (a scene the game passed in is run by its class) runs for real in
    the scripted-session recorder (glitchygames/replay/tools/scripted_sessions.py), recorded to
    PATH, while ``--input-script MODULE:NAME`` is played for ``--frame-count N`` frames, then
    ``--controls-tail MODULE:NAME`` when given (both read by ``load_input_script``), seeded by
    ``--random-seed`` (a random seed when not given), with ``--polled-input`` and
    ``--input-only-placements`` as given.

    Args:
        options: The game's parsed options (the engine's ``options``).
        game: The game (its class, or a scene the game passed in).

    Returns:
        ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` once the session is recorded; ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` when an
        input script reference names no input script, or the script cannot be recorded as
        input for that many frames (a placement inside the session, input before frame 0, a
        controls tail that is not key events only); ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` when the
        controls tail's quit did not end the game (the recording is written, but does not end
        with the game quitting); ``ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT`` when the recording's
        directory can't be made.

    """
    # Imported here: the recorder imports the engine, which imports the tool table (this module)
    from glitchygames.replay.tools import golden_traces, scripted_sessions
    from glitchygames.scenes import Scene

    controls_tail_reference: str | None = options.get('controls_tail')
    try:
        script = golden_traces.load_input_script(reference=options['input_script'])
        controls_tail = (
            None
            if controls_tail_reference is None
            else golden_traces.load_input_script(reference=controls_tail_reference)
        )
    except golden_traces.InputScriptError as error:
        return refused(message=f'--record-session: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
    scene_class = type(game) if isinstance(game, Scene) else game
    frame_count: int = options['frame_count']
    input_only_placements = bool(options.get('input_only_placements'))
    # The session's own checks, before anything runs; the game's own errors are not caught
    # here, so they end the run as any game's do (the engine's crash boundary)
    refusal = scripted_sessions.scripted_session_refusal(
        script=script,
        frame_count=frame_count,
        controls_tail=controls_tail,
        input_only_placements=input_only_placements,
    )
    if refusal is not None:
        return refused(message=f'--record-session: {refusal}', exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
    path = Path(options['record_session'])
    try:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    except OSError as error:
        return refused(
            message=f'--record-session: cannot write {path} ({error})',
            exit_code=ExitCode.CANNOT_WRITE_OUTPUT,
        )
    try:
        scripted_sessions.record_scripted_session(
            scene_class=scene_class,
            script=script,
            frame_count=frame_count,
            path=path,
            controls_tail=controls_tail,
            polled_input=bool(options.get('polled_input')),
            input_only_placements=input_only_placements,
            random_seed=options.get('random_seed'),
        )
    except scripted_sessions.GameDidNotQuitError as error:
        return refused(message=f'--record-session: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT)
    return ExitCode.SUCCESS

docs.title: verify
docs.text:
The verify tool: replay recordings headless and say, one line each, whether they matched.

Each recording is replayed by the game in a child process (--replay-trace PATH --headless, children.headless_replay_arguments), never with a seed of its own, so every replay compares with its recording (Stage D's decision 17). One line per recording goes to standard output:

PASS tests/fixtures/replays/rally/serve.jsonl.gz: Replay matched 450 frames (end of recording)
FAIL tests/fixtures/replays/rally/lob.jsonl.gz: REPLAY_DIVERGED (1): Replay diverged at ...

then verify: N of M recordings passed. A recording inside the project is named by its path relative to the project, any other (a demo installed in site-packages) by its path. With no recordings to verify it says so (verify: no recordings found ...) and succeeds.

The exit code (verification_exit_code):

  • ExitCode.SUCCESS: every recording matched, or there was none;
  • ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED: some diverged, and nothing else went wrong;
  • otherwise the first other failure's own code: MISSING_INPUT (no such recording), UNUSABLE_INPUT (not a recording, another game's, or settings that can't be read), OPTIONS_REFUSED (its game can't be found), INTERNAL_ERROR (a replay that crashed inside the engine, ran too long, or exited with a status that is no ExitCode), and so on.

A replay that crashes before its engine starts (in the game's own code before GameEngine.start(), where no exit code is mapped) exits with Python's 1, which is REPLAY_DIVERGED's: it counts as a divergence (the user's ruling, 2026-10-27: "Yes, crashes count as divergences"). Its line still ends with the exception.

Both front ends find the project the same way (verify_project_root): --project-root when the command is given it, else the nearest directory at or above the current one whose pyproject.toml has [tool.glitchygames], else the nearest with a pyproject.toml (settings.find_project_root: inside a workspace member, the workspace root), else the current directory. When settings are read there (no PATHs) and it has no pyproject.toml, they say the defaults are used.

A seed is refused on both front ends (seed_refusal), before any replay runs, with ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED: a replay under another seed compares nothing and succeeds (rule 19 of glitchygames/replay/driver.py), so a tampered recording would pass. --random-seed given to the tool, among the game's own arguments beside --verify, or after the command's -- is refused alike (the user's rule: verify always compares).

Both pass the game's other arguments on to every game they start: the command those after a bare --, the game those on its own command line beside --verify (registry.tool_free_arguments).

The two front ends (glitchygames/replay/tools/registry.py):

  • On the game, --verify [PATH ...] [--only TEXT] (verify_on_the_game) runs from GameEngine.__init__, before the engine starts pygame: the game is neither built nor shown. It replays each recording by starting itself again (children.running_game_command), so a game run as a script verifies too. With no PATHs: its own recordings (recordings.game_recordings) in the project.
  • The command, glitchygames verify [PATH ...] [--only TEXT] [--game GAME ...] (verify_command): with no PATHs, each game (--game, given once per game, else the project's [tool.glitchygames] games) is started as a child with --verify and verifies its own; with PATHs, each is replayed by the game its header names (as replay-trace finds it), or by the one --game. --game is the command's own: a game verifying itself needs none.

def replay_outcome(*, finished: CompletedProcess[str]) -> str:
    """Say in a line how a replay child went: its report, else its last words.

    Args:

    Returns:

        N: ...``), else the child's last line (a crash's exception), else ``NO_OUTPUT``.

    """
    lines = [line.strip() for line in (finished.stdout or '').splitlines() if line.strip()]
    for line in lines:
        if line.startswith(REPLAY_REPORT_PREFIXES):
            return line
    if lines:
        return lines[-1]
    return NO_OUTPUT

def seed_given(*, arguments: Sequence[str]) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a command line gives ``--random-seed`` (as a game's parser would read it).

    Read by a parser of its own with argparse's abbreviations, so ``--random-seed=7`` and a
    prefix the game would take for it count too (an ambiguous prefix the game would refuse is
    refused here as well).

    Args:
        arguments: The arguments.

    Returns:
        True if a seed is among them.

    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False, exit_on_error=False)
    parser.add_argument(RANDOM_SEED_FLAG)
    try:
        known, _ = parser.parse_known_args(list(arguments))
    except argparse.ArgumentError:
        # --random-seed with no value: still a seed asked for
        return True
    return known.random_seed is not None
