def verification_exit_code(*, statuses: Sequence[int]) -> ExitCode:
    """Return how a verify run exits, from each recording's (or each game's) exit status.

    Args:
        statuses: The exit statuses, in the order they were verified.

    Returns:
        ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` when every one succeeded (or there was none);
        ``ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED`` when every failure is a divergence; otherwise the first
        other failure's own code, or ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` for a status that is no
        ``ExitCode`` (a child killed by a signal, or one that exited with a number of its own).

    """
    failures = [status for status in statuses if status != ExitCode.SUCCESS]
    if not failures:
        return ExitCode.SUCCESS
    others = [status for status in failures if status != ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED]
    if not others:
        return ExitCode.REPLAY_DIVERGED
    try:
        return ExitCode(others[0])
    except ValueError:
        return ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR

def verify_command(*, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game_arguments: list[str]) -> int:
    """Run ``glitchygames verify [PATH ...] [--only TEXT] [--game GAME ...]``.

    Args:
        tool: The verify tool.

        game_arguments: The arguments after a bare ``--``, for each game started.

    Returns:
        ``verify_named_recordings``' exit code with PATHs, ``verify_each_game``'s without.

    """
    if arguments.random_seed is not None or seed_given(arguments=game_arguments):
        say(tool=tool, message=seed_refusal())
        return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
    # One project for everything below, found as the game finds it (verify_project_root)
    arguments.project_root = verify_project_root(given=arguments.project_root)
    if arguments.verify:
        return verify_named_recordings(
            tool=tool, arguments=arguments, game_arguments=game_arguments
        )
    return verify_each_game(tool=tool, arguments=arguments, game_arguments=game_arguments)

def verify_each_game(
    *, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game_arguments: list[str]
) -> int:
    """Run ``glitchygames verify``: each game started with ``--verify``, verifying its own.

    The games are ``--game``'s, else the project's ``[tool.glitchygames] games``; each runs in
    the project, with ``--only`` as given, and writes its own lines. A game still running after
    the project's ``game-timeout-seconds`` is stopped and fails (``run_game_with_tool``). When
    the games come from the settings, every golden and bundled demo of the project that none of
    them replays is a failure first, on a ``FAIL`` line naming it and why
    (``measure.unclaimed_recordings``, as ``measure`` fails them): a golden is never silently
    left out.

    Args:
        tool: The verify tool.
        arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.
        game_arguments: The arguments after a bare ``--``, for each game.

    Returns:
        ``verification_exit_code`` of the statuses: the unclaimed recordings'
        (``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` each) and the games' (``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` for a
        game that names nothing, after every other game has run; ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR``
        for one stopped at its timeout); ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` with no games and nothing
        unclaimed, or ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` when the project's settings can't be read.

    """
    # Imported here: measure imports this module (verify_project_root, seed_given)
    from glitchygames.replay.tools.measure import unclaimed_recordings

    root = project_root(arguments=arguments)
    # Read with --game too: they give each game's timeout
    try:
        settings = read_settings(project_root=root)
    except ProjectSettingsError as error:
        say(tool=tool, message=str(error))
        return ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT
    games: list[str] | None = arguments.game
    statuses: list[int] = []
    if games is None:
        games = list(settings.games)
        for unclaimed in unclaimed_recordings(games=games, settings=settings, project_root=root):
            name = recording_name(path=unclaimed.path, project_root=root)
            if arguments.only is not None and arguments.only not in name:
                continue
            write_line(
                line=f'{FAILED} {name}: {ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR.describe()}: {unclaimed.reason}'
            )
            statuses.append(ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR)
    if not games:
        write_line(
            line=(
                f'{SUMMARY_PREFIX} no games to verify: the project names none in '
                '[tool.glitchygames] games (or [project.scripts]), and no --game was given'
            )
        )
        return verification_exit_code(statuses=statuses)
    for game in games:
        try:
            launch = resolve_named_game(tool=tool, game=game, arguments=arguments)
        except UnknownGameError:
            statuses.append(ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
            continue
        statuses.append(
            run_game_with_tool(
                tool=tool,
                arguments=arguments,
                game_arguments=game_arguments,
                game=game,
                launch=dataclasses.replace(launch, timeout_seconds=settings.game_timeout_seconds),
            )
        )
    return verification_exit_code(statuses=statuses)

def verify_named_recordings(
    *, tool: Tool, arguments: argparse.Namespace, game_arguments: list[str]
) -> int:
    """Run ``glitchygames verify PATH ...``: each recording replayed by its game.

    Its game is the one its header names (``find_recorded_game``, as ``replay-trace`` finds
    it), or the one ``--game``.

    Args:
        tool: The verify tool.
        arguments: The subcommand's parsed arguments.
        game_arguments: The arguments after a bare ``--``, for each replaying game.

    Returns:
        ``verify_recordings``' exit code, ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` when ``--only`` keeps none, or
        ``ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED`` for more than one ``--game`` or one that names no game.

    """
    root = project_root(arguments=arguments)
    games: list[str] | None = arguments.game
    named_game = None
    if games is not None:
        if len(games) > 1:
            say(
                tool=tool,
                message=(
                    'with PATHs, one --game at most: it names the game that replays them '
                    f'({len(games)} were given)'
                ),
            )
            return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
        (game,) = games
        try:
            named_game = resolve_named_game(tool=tool, game=game, arguments=arguments)
        except UnknownGameError:
            return ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED
        say(tool=tool, message=f'replaying with {game} ({FORM_DESCRIPTIONS[named_game.form]})')
    given: list[str] = arguments.verify
    chosen = selected(
        paths=[Path(path).absolute() for path in given], only=arguments.only, project_root=root
    )
    if not chosen:
        return no_recordings(looked_for=f'{len(given)} given', only=arguments.only)
    recordings: list[VerifyTarget] = []
    for path in chosen:
        if named_game is not None:
            recordings.append((path, named_game.command))
            continue
        found = find_recorded_game(recording=path, project_root=root)
        recordings.append((
            path,
            found if isinstance(found, RecordedGameRefusal) else found[1].command,
        ))
    return verify_recordings(
        recordings=recordings,
        project_root=root,
        working_directory=root,
        game_arguments=game_arguments,
    )

def verify_on_the_game(*, options: dict[str, Any], game: type[Scene] | Scene) -> ExitCode:
    """Run ``--verify [PATH ...]`` on a game: replay the recordings through the game itself.

    Runs in place of the game's run (``run_game_flag_tool``, from ``GameEngine.__init__``): the
    game is never built. Each recording is replayed by this game started again
    (``running_game_command``) in the current directory, with the game's arguments other than
    verify's own (``registry.tool_free_arguments``), as the command passes those after ``--``.
    The project is ``verify_project_root``'s.

    Args:
        options: The game's parsed options (``verify``: the PATHs given; ``only``).
        game: The game (its class, or a scene the game passed in).

    Returns:
        ``verification_exit_code``'s, ``ExitCode.SUCCESS`` with no recordings,
        ``ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT`` when the project's settings can't be read (needed only
        with no PATHs), or ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR`` when this process can't tell how it was
        started (so it can't start itself again).

    """
    # Imported here: the tool table imports this module
    from glitchygames.replay.tools.registry import tool_free_arguments, tool_named

    if options.get('random_seed') is not None:
        return refused(message=f'--verify: {seed_refusal()}', exit_code=ExitCode.OPTIONS_REFUSED)
    root = verify_project_root(given=None)
    only: str | None = options.get('only')
    given: list[str] = options['verify']
    if given:
        paths = [Path(path) for path in given]
        looked_for = f'{len(paths)} given'
    else:
        try:
            settings = read_settings(project_root=root)
        except ProjectSettingsError as error:
            return refused(message=f'--verify: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.UNUSABLE_INPUT)
        identity = game_identity(game=game)
        paths = [
            recording.path
            for recording in game_recordings(
                identity=identity, settings=settings, project_root=root
            )
        ]
        looked_for = (
            'no console script starts this game, so no golden or demo can be told to be its; '
            'name the recordings to verify'
            if identity.console_script is None
            else (
                f'the goldens of {list(settings.golden_globs)} in {root} that '
                f'{identity.console_script} replays, and the demos in {identity.package}/demos/'
            )
        )
    chosen = selected(paths=paths, only=only, project_root=root)
    if not chosen:
        return no_recordings(looked_for=looked_for, only=only)
    try:
        game_command = running_game_command()
    except RuntimeError as error:
        return refused(message=f'--verify: {error}', exit_code=ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR)
    return verify_recordings(
        recordings=[(path, game_command) for path in chosen],
        project_root=root,
        game_arguments=tool_free_arguments(arguments=sys.argv[1:], tool=tool_named(name='verify')),
    )

def verify_one(
    *,
    path: Path,
    game: list[str] | RecordedGameRefusal,
    project_root: Path,
    working_directory: Path | None,
    game_arguments: Sequence[str],
) -> int:
    """Replay one recording headless in a child, and write its line.

    Args:
        path: The recording.
        game: The command that starts the game (the replay's arguments follow it), or why no
            game can replay it.
        project_root: The project (for the line's name).
        working_directory: The child's working directory (None: this process's).
        game_arguments: More arguments for the game, after the replay's.

    Returns:
        The recording's exit status: the replay's, the refusal's, or ``ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR``
        for a replay still running after ``REPLAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`` (it is killed).

    """
    name = recording_name(path=path, project_root=project_root)
    if isinstance(game, RecordedGameRefusal):
        # The refusal's message, without the path it starts with: the line names the recording
        reason = game.reason.removeprefix(f'{path.as_posix()}: ')
        write_line(line=f'{FAILED} {name}: {game.exit_code.describe()}: {reason}')
        return game.exit_code
    try:
        finished = run_command(
            command=[*game, *headless_replay_arguments(recording=path), *game_arguments],
            environment=os.environ,
            timeout_seconds=REPLAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            capture_output=OutputCapture.TOGETHER,
            working_directory=working_directory,
        )
    except TimeoutExpired:
        write_line(
            line=(
                f'{FAILED} {name}: {ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR.describe()}: still replaying after '
                f'{REPLAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:g} seconds, so it was stopped'
            )
        )
        return ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR
    outcome = replay_outcome(finished=finished)
    if finished.returncode == ExitCode.SUCCESS:
        write_line(line=f'{PASSED} {name}: {outcome}')
    else:
        write_line(
            line=f'{FAILED} {name}: {ExitCode.describe_status(finished.returncode)}: {outcome}'
        )
    return finished.returncode

def verify_project_root(*, given: Path | None) -> Path:
    """Return the project a verify run works on, saying so when no project is found.

        nearest ``pyproject.toml`` with ``[tool.glitchygames]``, else the nearest one); else the

    if given is not None:

    current = Path.cwd()

    return current if found is None else found

def verify_recordings(
    *,
    recordings: Sequence[VerifyTarget],
    project_root: Path,
    working_directory: Path | None = None,
    game_arguments: Sequence[str] = (),
) -> ExitCode:
    """Replay each recording headless in a child, one line each, then a summary line.

    Args:
        recordings: The recordings, each with the command that starts its game (or why none
            can replay it), at least one.
        project_root: The project (for the lines' names).
        working_directory: The children's working directory (None: this process's).
        game_arguments: More arguments for each replaying game.

    Returns:

    statuses = [

            project_root=project_root,

        for path, game in recordings

docs.title: viewer
docs.text:
The replay viewer: a watched replay is a read-only game inside a game.

Two loops share the frame loop of SceneManager.start while a replay is watched (glitchygames/replay/driver.py, rule 14):

  • OUTER, the viewer (ReplayViewer): owns the window. It ticks at a fixed real-time rate (CONTROL_TICKS_PER_SECOND, on glitchygames.clock.measured_seconds, never replayed), whatever the replay's speed and whether it is paused. Each tick it reads the viewer's keys (ReplayControls, once per press), refreshes the status line, and presents one frame: the inner game's latest, with the status bar, start screen and debug overlay drawn on a copy.
  • INNER, the recorded game: steps at its recorded frame times and never receives viewer input. Its frames always run in full (events, logic, update, render), exactly as recorded; only their presentation is left to the outer tick (ReplaySources.presents_frames is False while watched).

The contract between them, asked through EngineSources.hold_frame before each inner frame:

  1. No tick open: sleep until the next tick is due (while inner frames run, sleep_for: the engine's high-resolution sleep-then-spin timer, glitchygames/timing.py FastTimer; paused, at the start screen or over, sleep_coarsely, which never spins), open it, let the doors run the tick's work (keys), then add the real time since the last tick, times the speed, to the accumulator. A tick within TICK_SNAP_WINDOW_SECONDS of one period counts as exactly one period, the error carried to the next tick, so wake-up jitter does not turn 1x into ticks of 0 and 2 frames. Only while the inner game is running: paused, at the start screen or over, the accumulator empties, and a restart seeds it with half a frame (so frame boundaries never sit on a tick boundary).
  2. Tick open: run one more inner frame (should_run_inner_frame True) while the accumulator holds the frame's recorded duration, which it then consumes, only within the tick's real-time work budget (INNER_FRAME_BUDGET_SECONDS, 11 ms of the 16.7 ms tick), so keys, the status line and presenting stay at 60 Hz however costly inner frames are. The budget is the only per-tick limit at every speed (no frame count), so on a real machine an uncapped recording whose frames cost what they did live may still not keep up, and "can't keep up" then means exactly that.

Rule 2, one frame a tick unless behind: up to 1x (speed <= 1) a tick runs at most one inner frame unless the replay is genuinely behind: a second (or later) frame in the same tick runs only when the accumulator holds its recorded duration plus a whole 60 Hz tick of inner time (the speed times CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS); otherwise the tick closes and the frame runs next tick, the owed time carried. So a live frame that ran long and the short frame its pacing caught up with never share a tick (which would show only the short one): each is presented. After such a catch-up the replay stays about a tick behind real time: a constant lag, not a drift (it never grows), which a pause resets. A recording faster than 60 FPS (frames shorter than a tick) owes more than that every tick, so a tick still runs several of its frames and presents the last. Above 1x the same limit applies after a frame lasting at least a tick of inner time at that speed (its recorded duration at least the speed times the tick period: a 60 Hz refresh or more of real time), so fast-forward still shows it; after shorter frames a tick runs several and presents the last.

The owed limit: the accumulator never owes more than MAX_OWED_INNER_FRAMES and a half of the next frame's duration (about half a second of 60 FPS frames), and never less than the floor: the frame plus a 60 Hz tick plus the tick paid for (the real time since the last tick, at least a 60 Hz tick; a stall over STALL_TICK_SECONDS counts as a 60 Hz tick), in inner time, so a recording of very short frames, or a slower display's ticks, keep their rate. The excess is dropped (a long stall runs one bounded burst), and while frames are dropped or the budget cuts ticks short the viewer is behind (is_behind): the status bar then shows the real speed (effective_speed). So 1x runs one inner frame a tick for a 60 FPS recording (but for the true rate mismatch), 8x eight, ¼x one every fourth tick, paused none. While paused a step (.) runs exactly one inner frame. The start screen lets frame 0 run first, so its picture is behind the message. 3. Otherwise the tick closes: the doors refresh the status line, the loop presents the outer frame and asks again (step 1).

The accumulator only decides when inner frames run, never what they do, so a watched replay is as exact as a headless one. Headless replays have no viewer loop: they never hold and run unpaced. Step back restarts the replay process instead, which rebuilds the inner game up to frame N-1 before the viewer's first tick (glitchygames/replay/rebuild.py; no outer tick opens during the rebuild). Later users of the same contract: Part 3's playback scopes (an inner replay under a live outer game) and audio/video capture (inner frames handed to a sink rather than presented).

class ReplayViewer:
    """The outer loop of a watched replay (module docstring).

    Attributes:
        controls: The viewer's controls (keys, state and status bar).
        cadence: The outer tick's real-time cadence.
        accumulated_seconds: Inner game time owed to the inner game (real time times speed,
            consumed by each inner frame's recorded duration).
        ticks_externally: True when something outside waits for each tick (a browser's
            animation frames, ``run_watched_replay_async``): a tick then opens at once, never
            sleeping or following ``cadence``, and owes the real time since the last, so the
            replay keeps its speed at any display rate.
        last_inner_frame_ran_behind: Whether the inner frame ``should_run_inner_frame`` last
            allowed ran while the replay was behind: the accumulator owed the frame's recorded
            duration plus a whole tick of inner time (the speed times ``CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS``),
            read before the frame consumed it; False for a frame run without the accumulator (a
            paused step, frame 0 at the start screen). Rule 2's one-frame limit uses the same
            condition; the schedule tool (scripts/replay_schedule.py) derives behind itself and
            checks this against it.

    """

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        controls: ReplayControls,
        measured_seconds: Callable[[], float] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Start with no tick open; the first tick is due at once.

        Args:
            controls: The viewer's controls.
            measured_seconds: The viewer's real-time clock; None is
                ``glitchygames.clock.measured_seconds``, looked up when read. The schedule tool
                (scripts/replay_schedule.py) gives an ideal clock, so the real accumulator runs
                without a display or real time.

        """
        self.controls = controls
        self._measured_seconds = measured_seconds
        self.cadence = ControlCadence()
        self.accumulated_seconds = 0.0
        self.ticks_externally = False
        self.last_inner_frame_ran_behind = False
        self._is_tick_open = False
        self._inner_frames_this_tick = 0
        # The recorded duration of the open tick's last inner frame (rule 2 above 1x)
        self._last_inner_frame_seconds = 0.0
        self._tick_start_seconds = 0.0
        # The tick time the next tick's elapsed time is measured from (snapping carries error)
        self._last_tick_seconds: float | None = None
        # True when the inner game (re)starts running: the accumulator gets half a frame
        self._needs_phase_offset = True
        # Ticks left during which the viewer counts as behind (frames dropped or cut short)
        self._behind_ticks_left = 0
        # Per running tick over the last second: its real seconds and the inner seconds it ran
        self._recent_real_seconds: collections.deque[float] = collections.deque(
            maxlen=EFFECTIVE_SPEED_WINDOW_TICKS
        )
        self._recent_inner_seconds: collections.deque[float] = collections.deque(
            maxlen=EFFECTIVE_SPEED_WINDOW_TICKS
        )
        # The open tick: whether the inner game runs in it, the real time it pays for and the
        # inner seconds it ran
        self._tick_is_running = False
        self._tick_elapsed_seconds = 0.0
        self._inner_seconds_this_tick = 0.0
        # The viewer's key presses and releases (event type, key) read since the last tick
        self._key_events: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

    @property
    def is_behind(self: Self) -> bool:
        """True while the inner game cannot keep up with the speed (in the last second)."""
        return self._behind_ticks_left > 0

    def effective_speed(self: Self) -> float:
        """Return the speed the inner game really ran at over the last second of ticks.

        Returns:
            Inner seconds run over real seconds passed (0.0 before any time passed).

        """
        real_seconds = sum(self._recent_real_seconds)
        if real_seconds <= 0:
            return 0.0
        return sum(self._recent_inner_seconds) / real_seconds

    def real_speed_if_behind(self: Self) -> float | None:
        """Return the real speed when the inner game meaningfully cannot keep up, for the status.

        Returns:
            ``effective_speed()`` while behind and below ``BEHIND_SPEED_FRACTION`` of the
            speed, else None (keeping up, slightly slow, or no running ticks measured yet).

        """
        if not self.is_behind or not self._recent_real_seconds:
            return None
        real_speed = self.effective_speed()
        if real_speed >= self.controls.speed * BEHIND_SPEED_FRACTION:
            return None
        return real_speed

    def queue_key_event(self: Self, *, event_type: int, key: int) -> None:
        """Keep a real KEYDOWN or KEYUP for the next tick (keys act once per tick at most).

        Args:
            event_type: ``pygame.KEYDOWN`` or ``pygame.KEYUP``.
            key: The key.

        """
        self._key_events.append((event_type, key))

    def begin_tick(self: Self, *, is_inner_running: bool) -> float | None:
        """Open the next outer tick if none is open, first sleeping until it is due.

        Args:
            is_inner_running: Whether the inner game was running when the last tick closed:
                the wait spins only then (``sleep_for``); paused, at the start screen or over
                it is a plain sleep (``sleep_coarsely``).

        Returns:
            The tick's measured time when a tick was opened (the doors then run its work and
            call ``accrue``), or None while a tick is open.

        """
        if self._is_tick_open:
            return None
        now = self._read_measured_seconds()
        if self.ticks_externally:
            return self._open_tick(now=now)
        remaining_seconds = self.cadence.next_tick_seconds(now=now) - now
        if remaining_seconds > 0:
            if is_inner_running:
                sleep_for(seconds=remaining_seconds)
            else:
                sleep_coarsely(seconds=remaining_seconds)
            now = self._read_measured_seconds()
        self.cadence.tick_is_due(now=now)
        return self._open_tick(now=now)

    def _read_measured_seconds(self: Self) -> float:
        """Read the viewer's real-time clock (the one given, else the engine's).

        Returns:
            Seconds (only differences mean anything).

        """
        if self._measured_seconds is None:
            return clock.measured_seconds()
        return self._measured_seconds()

    def _open_tick(self: Self, *, now: float) -> float:
        """Open a tick at ``now``.

        Returns:
            ``now``.

        """
        self._is_tick_open = True
        self._inner_frames_this_tick = 0
        self._tick_start_seconds = now
        return now

    def apply_key_events(self: Self, *, now: float) -> None:
        """Act on the keys read since the last tick, then repeat held step keys.

        Args:
            now: The tick's measured time.

        """
        for event_type, key in self._key_events:
            if event_type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
                self.controls.press_key(key=key, now=now)
            else:
                self.controls.release_key(key=key)
        self._key_events = []
        self.controls.repeat_held_keys(now=now)

    def accrue(self: Self, *, now: float, is_inner_running: bool) -> None:
        """Owe the inner game the real time since the last tick, times the speed.

        Args:
            now: The tick's measured time.
            is_inner_running: False while paused, at the start screen or over: the
                accumulator empties instead.

        """
        if self._last_tick_seconds is None:
            elapsed_seconds = 0.0
            self._last_tick_seconds = now
        else:
            elapsed_seconds = now - self._last_tick_seconds
            if abs(elapsed_seconds - CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS) <= TICK_SNAP_WINDOW_SECONDS:
                # On time within the window: exactly one period, the error carried
                elapsed_seconds = CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS
                self._last_tick_seconds += CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS
            else:
                self._last_tick_seconds = now
        self._behind_ticks_left = max(0, self._behind_ticks_left - 1)
        self._tick_is_running = is_inner_running
        self._tick_elapsed_seconds = elapsed_seconds
        self._inner_seconds_this_tick = 0.0
        if not is_inner_running:
            self.accumulated_seconds = 0.0
            self._needs_phase_offset = True
            self._recent_real_seconds.clear()
            self._recent_inner_seconds.clear()
            self._behind_ticks_left = 0
            return
        self.accumulated_seconds += elapsed_seconds * self.controls.speed

    def should_run_inner_frame(
        self: Self, *, inner_frame_seconds: float, is_inner_over: bool, is_first_inner_frame: bool
    ) -> bool:
        """Decide whether the open tick runs one more inner frame; if not, close the tick.

        Args:
            inner_frame_seconds: The recorded duration of the inner frame that would run.
            is_inner_over: True once the replay stopped or the recording is used up (a step
                then does nothing).
            is_first_inner_frame: True before the inner game's frame 0.

        Returns:
            True to run one inner frame now.

        """
        controls = self.controls
        self.last_inner_frame_ran_behind = False
        if is_inner_over:
            controls.take_step()
            return self._close_tick()
        if controls.awaiting_start:
            # Frame 0 runs first, so the start screen shows its picture
            return is_first_inner_frame or self._close_tick()
        if controls.paused:
            return controls.take_step() or self._close_tick()
        if self._needs_phase_offset:
            self._needs_phase_offset = False
            self.accumulated_seconds += inner_frame_seconds / 2
        # Never owe more than the owed limit (keeping the half-frame phase): drop the excess
        # (frames recorded with no duration owe nothing and never fall behind)
        owed_limit_seconds = self._owed_limit_seconds(inner_frame_seconds=inner_frame_seconds)
        if inner_frame_seconds > 0 and self.accumulated_seconds > owed_limit_seconds:
            self.accumulated_seconds = owed_limit_seconds
            self._fall_behind()
        if self.accumulated_seconds < inner_frame_seconds or self._defers_to_the_next_tick(
            inner_frame_seconds=inner_frame_seconds
        ):
            # Not owed yet, or (up to 1x, not behind) it runs and is presented next tick, the
            # owed time carried
            return self._close_tick()
        if self._is_tick_spent():
            # Owed but out of frames or time this tick: carried to the next
            if inner_frame_seconds > 0:
                self._fall_behind()
            return self._close_tick()
        self.last_inner_frame_ran_behind = self._owes_beyond_a_tick(
            inner_frame_seconds=inner_frame_seconds
        )
        self.accumulated_seconds -= inner_frame_seconds
        self._inner_frames_this_tick += 1
        self._inner_seconds_this_tick += inner_frame_seconds
        self._last_inner_frame_seconds = inner_frame_seconds
        return True

    def _is_tick_spent(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Whether the open tick may run no more inner frames (rule 2).

        Its real-time work budget (``INNER_FRAME_BUDGET_SECONDS``) is spent: at every speed the
        only per-tick limit, so a recording of very short frames (an uncapped game: 3000 FPS is
        50 frames a tick at 1x, 400 at 8x) keeps its rate when its frames cost little enough.

        Returns:
            True when the tick closes.

        """
        return (
            self._read_measured_seconds() - self._tick_start_seconds >= INNER_FRAME_BUDGET_SECONDS
        )

    def _owed_limit_seconds(self: Self, *, inner_frame_seconds: float) -> float:
        """Return the most inner time the accumulator may owe; the excess is dropped (rule 2).

        ``MAX_OWED_INNER_FRAMES`` and a half frames, and never less than the floor: the frame
        plus a 60 Hz tick of inner time (what rule 2's one-frame limit may carry) plus the inner
        time of the tick paid for (the speed times the real time since the last tick, at least
        a 60 Hz tick). Below that, a recording whose frames are short (an uncapped game) would
        be capped every tick, fall behind every tick and play in slow motion; a tick slower than
        60 Hz (a browser on a slower display, a late blocking tick) pays for more than a 60 Hz
        tick, so the floor follows it. A stall (a tick paying for more than
        ``STALL_TICK_SECONDS``, as the effective-speed window counts it) is not a display rate:
        it counts as a 60 Hz tick, so its burst stays as bounded as at 60 Hz.

        Args:
            inner_frame_seconds: The recorded duration of the inner frame that would run.

        Returns:
            Seconds.

        """
        frames_limit_seconds = (MAX_OWED_INNER_FRAMES + 0.5) * inner_frame_seconds
        tick_paid_for_seconds = (
            CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS
            if self._tick_elapsed_seconds > STALL_TICK_SECONDS
            else max(CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS, self._tick_elapsed_seconds)
        )
        floor_seconds = inner_frame_seconds + self.controls.speed * (
            CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS + tick_paid_for_seconds
        )
        return max(frames_limit_seconds, floor_seconds)

    def _defers_to_the_next_tick(self: Self, *, inner_frame_seconds: float) -> bool:
        """Decide whether a later inner frame in the open tick waits for the next tick (rule 2).

        A tick presents only its last frame, so a second (or later) frame runs in the same tick
        only when the replay is genuinely behind (``_owes_beyond_a_tick``): up to 1x after any
        frame, and above 1x after a frame lasting at least a tick of inner time at that speed
        (its recorded duration at least the speed times ``CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS``, so it lasts a
        60 Hz refresh or more of real time). Otherwise a live frame that ran long and the short
        one its pacing caught up with would share a tick, and the long one would never be
        shown. After a frame shorter than that, above 1x, a tick runs several frames and
        presents the last (fast-forward).

        Args:
            inner_frame_seconds: The recorded duration of the inner frame that would run.

        Returns:
            True when the frame waits for the next tick.

        """
        speed = self.controls.speed
        if self._inner_frames_this_tick == 0:
            return False
        if speed > 1 and self._last_inner_frame_seconds < speed * CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS:
            return False
        return not self._owes_beyond_a_tick(inner_frame_seconds=inner_frame_seconds)

    def _owes_beyond_a_tick(self: Self, *, inner_frame_seconds: float) -> bool:
        """Whether the replay is behind: it owes the frame plus a whole tick of inner time.

        Args:
            inner_frame_seconds: The recorded duration of the inner frame that would run.

        Returns:
            True when the accumulator holds at least the frame's duration plus the speed times
            ``CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS``.

        """
        return (
            self.accumulated_seconds
            >= inner_frame_seconds + self.controls.speed * CONTROL_TICK_SECONDS
        )

    def _fall_behind(self: Self) -> None:
        """Count as behind for the next second of ticks."""
        self._behind_ticks_left = EFFECTIVE_SPEED_WINDOW_TICKS

    def _close_tick(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Close the open tick: the loop presents the outer frame next.

        A running tick joins the effective-speed window with its own real time and the inner
        seconds it ran; a stall (``STALL_TICK_SECONDS``) restarts the window instead, so it does
        not read as a slow second.

        Returns:
            False (no inner frame runs).

        """
        self._is_tick_open = False
        if self._tick_elapsed_seconds > STALL_TICK_SECONDS:
            self._recent_real_seconds.clear()
            self._recent_inner_seconds.clear()
        elif self._tick_is_running and self._tick_elapsed_seconds > 0:
            self._recent_real_seconds.append(self._tick_elapsed_seconds)
            self._recent_inner_seconds.append(self._inner_seconds_this_tick)
        self._tick_is_running = False
        return False

def __init__(
    self: Self,
    *,
    controls: ReplayControls,
    measured_seconds: Callable[[], float] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Start with no tick open; the first tick is due at once.

    Args:
        controls: The viewer's controls.
        measured_seconds: The viewer's real-time clock; None is
            ``glitchygames.clock.measured_seconds``, looked up when read. The schedule tool
            (scripts/replay_schedule.py) gives an ideal clock, so the real accumulator runs
            without a display or real time.

    """
    self.controls = controls
    self._measured_seconds = measured_seconds
    self.cadence = ControlCadence()
    self.accumulated_seconds = 0.0
    self.ticks_externally = False
    self.last_inner_frame_ran_behind = False
    self._is_tick_open = False
    self._inner_frames_this_tick = 0
    # The recorded duration of the open tick's last inner frame (rule 2 above 1x)
    self._last_inner_frame_seconds = 0.0
    self._tick_start_seconds = 0.0

    self._last_tick_seconds: float | None = None

    self._needs_phase_offset = True
    # Ticks left during which the viewer counts as behind (frames dropped or cut short)
    self._behind_ticks_left = 0
    # Per running tick over the last second: its real seconds and the inner seconds it ran
    self._recent_real_seconds: collections.deque[float] = collections.deque(
        maxlen=EFFECTIVE_SPEED_WINDOW_TICKS
    )
    self._recent_inner_seconds: collections.deque[float] = collections.deque(
        maxlen=EFFECTIVE_SPEED_WINDOW_TICKS
    )
    # The open tick: whether the inner game runs in it, the real time it pays for and the
    # inner seconds it ran
    self._tick_is_running = False
    self._tick_elapsed_seconds = 0.0
    self._inner_seconds_this_tick = 0.0
    # The viewer's key presses and releases (event type, key) read since the last tick
    self._key_events: list[tuple[int, int]] = []

def effective_speed(self: Self) -> float:

def should_run_inner_frame(
    self: Self, *, inner_frame_seconds: float, is_inner_over: bool, is_first_inner_frame: bool

    Args:
        inner_frame_seconds: The recorded duration of the inner frame that would run.
        is_inner_over: True once the replay stopped or the recording is used up (a step
            then does nothing).
        is_first_inner_frame: True before the inner game's frame 0.

    Returns:
        True to run one inner frame now.

    """
    controls = self.controls
    self.last_inner_frame_ran_behind = False
    if is_inner_over:
        controls.take_step()
        return self._close_tick()
    if controls.awaiting_start:
        # Frame 0 runs first, so the start screen shows its picture
        return is_first_inner_frame or self._close_tick()
    if controls.paused:
        return controls.take_step() or self._close_tick()
    if self._needs_phase_offset:
        self._needs_phase_offset = False
        self.accumulated_seconds += inner_frame_seconds / 2
    # Never owe more than the owed limit (keeping the half-frame phase): drop the excess
    # (frames recorded with no duration owe nothing and never fall behind)
    owed_limit_seconds = self._owed_limit_seconds(inner_frame_seconds=inner_frame_seconds)
    if inner_frame_seconds > 0 and self.accumulated_seconds > owed_limit_seconds:
        self.accumulated_seconds = owed_limit_seconds
        self._fall_behind()
    if self.accumulated_seconds < inner_frame_seconds or self._defers_to_the_next_tick(
        inner_frame_seconds=inner_frame_seconds
    ):
        # Not owed yet, or (up to 1x, not behind) it runs and is presented next tick, the
        # owed time carried
        return self._close_tick()
    if self._is_tick_spent():
        # Owed but out of frames or time this tick: carried to the next
        if inner_frame_seconds > 0:
            self._fall_behind()
        return self._close_tick()
    self.last_inner_frame_ran_behind = self._owes_beyond_a_tick(
        inner_frame_seconds=inner_frame_seconds
    )
    self.accumulated_seconds -= inner_frame_seconds
    self._inner_frames_this_tick += 1
    self._inner_seconds_this_tick += inner_frame_seconds
    self._last_inner_frame_seconds = inner_frame_seconds
    return True

For a host that must not block (a browser). Each awaited wait_for_tick() is one outer tick of viewer (ticks_externally: the viewer never sleeps): the tick's inner frames run, then the viewer holds and the outer frame is presented (SceneManager.run_frame_step steps until last_step_was_held). Frames run unpaced, as the blocking loop runs them in a watched replay: the viewer's accumulator decides when they run.

async def run_watched_replay_async(
    *,
    scene_manager: SceneManager,
    viewer: ReplayViewer,
    wait_for_tick: Callable[[], Awaitable[float]],
) -> None:
    """Run a watched replay's frames, giving control back to the caller between outer ticks.

    For a host that must not block (a browser). Each awaited ``wait_for_tick()`` is one outer
    tick of ``viewer`` (``ticks_externally``: the viewer never sleeps): the tick's inner frames
    run, then the viewer holds and the outer frame is presented (``SceneManager.run_frame_step``
    steps until ``last_step_was_held``). Frames run unpaced, as the blocking loop runs them in a
    watched replay: the viewer's accumulator decides when they run.

    Args:
        scene_manager: The replayed game's scene manager.
        viewer: The watched replay's viewer.
        wait_for_tick: Waits for the next outer tick (a browser animation frame).

    """
    viewer.ticks_externally = True
    frame_start_seconds = scene_manager.begin_frames()
    while scene_manager.should_run_frames():
        await wait_for_tick()
        while scene_manager.should_run_frames():
            frame_start_seconds = scene_manager.run_frame_step(
                frame_start_seconds=frame_start_seconds, paced=False
            )
            if scene_manager.last_step_was_held:
                break
    scene_manager.end_frames()

def sleep_coarsely(*, seconds: float, sleep: Callable[[float], None] | None = None) -> None:
    """Sleep ``seconds`` without spinning (one plain sleep): the wait while nothing runs.

    Args:
        seconds: How long (nothing happens when not positive).
        sleep: The sleep (tests pass a fake); None is glitchygames/clock.py's raw sleep, looked
            up when called.

    """
    if seconds > 0:
        (clock.raw_sleep if sleep is None else sleep)(seconds)

def sleep_for(*, seconds: float) -> None:
    """Sleep ``seconds`` with the engine's high-resolution timer (glitchygames/timing.py).

    It spins for the last millisecond or two, so it is used only while inner frames run.

    Args:
        seconds: How long (nothing happens when not positive).

    """
    if seconds > 0:
        _SLEEP_TIMER.sleep_until_next(
            _SLEEP_TIMER.ns_now() + round(seconds * NANOSECONDS_PER_SECOND)
        )

class Scene(SceneInterface, SpriteInterface, events.AllEventStubs):
    """Scene object base class.

    Subclass this to properly receive on_*_event() messages automatically.
    """

    log = LOG
    FPS = 0
    NAME = 'Unnamed Scene'
    VERSION = '0.0'
    # A game's preferred default target FPS (0.0 = uncapped); None uses the engine default.
    # An explicit --target-fps on the command line always wins.
    TARGET_FPS: ClassVar[float | None] = None
    # The longest frame time (seconds) this scene's dt_tick and camera aim receive; after a
    # hitch (a window drag, focus loss) they advance at most this much, so physics cannot
    # tunnel. None passes the real frame time. Pacing, FPS statistics and the frame services
    # (shake, rumble, the debug overlay) always see the real frame time.
    MAX_FRAME_SECONDS: ClassVar[float | None] = None
    # How sprites without their own pixel_snap_mode (and the camera and parallax layers) are
    # snapped to whole pixels while this scene runs.
    PIXEL_SNAP_MODE: ClassVar[PixelSnapMode] = PixelSnapMode.NEAREST_HALF_UP
    # False for a scene that cannot be rebuilt on its own from replay_arguments() (PauseScene
    # presents another scene): its start is never captured (glitchygames/scene_start.py)
    CAPTURES_SCENE_START: ClassVar[bool] = True
    # Seconds an instant replay of this scene shows, or None for no instant replay. Set, the
    # scene manager keeps the scene's frames in memory from its start (glitchygames/
    # instant_replay.py) and its start is captured in plain live play too
    INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS: ClassVar[float | None] = None
    # The most scene time an instant replay re-simulates from the scene's start before the
    # seconds it shows (plans/2026-10-19-gameplay-replay.md, section 5.4)
    MAX_INSTANT_REPLAY_FAST_FORWARD_SECONDS: ClassVar[float] = 60.0
    # True on a game's scene class (the one given to GameEngine) to receive the window system's
    # raw messages (SYSWMEVENT) in on_sys_wm_event; blocked by default, as SDL leaves them.
    # See allow_every_event_type in glitchygames/events/base.py
    NATIVE_WINDOW_MESSAGES: ClassVar[bool] = False
    # Where audio.sound('coin') looks short names up: a directory relative to the scene's
    # package directory (an absolute path is used as is), or None for no short names
    # (glitchygames/audio/engine.py; sound engine feature spec 3.2)
    SOUND_DIRECTORY: ClassVar[str | None] = 'sounds'

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        options: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the scene.

        Args:
            options (dict[str, Any] | None): The options passed to the game.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups.

        """
        # First, before anything (a subclass's body after super().__init__() included) draws
        # random numbers: the streams and frame clock this scene began with, when its start is
        # captured (None otherwise; glitchygames/scene_start.py)
        self.scene_start_capture: SceneStartCapture | None = begin_scene_start_capture(
            scene_class=type(self)
        )

        if options is None:
            options = {'debug_events': False, 'no_unhandled_events': False}

        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        if self.NAME == 'Unnamed Scene':
            self.NAME = type(self).__name__  # pyright: ignore[reportConstantRedefinition]

        super().__init__()

        # Since SceneManager is a singleton, this will ensure that
        # any non-active scene which gets initialized will simply
        # get a copy of the scene manager, rather than overwriting
        # the active scene.
        #
        # This helps us keep the upper layers clean by not requiring
        # new scenes to care about the SceneManager when being
        # instantiated.
        self.target_fps: float = 0.0
        self.fps: float = 0.0
        self.dt: float = 0.0
        self.dt_timer: float = 0.0
        self.tweens: TweenManager = TweenManager()
        self.collisions: CollisionManager = CollisionManager()
        self.dirty = 1
        self.options = options
        self.scene_manager = SceneManager()
        # The class name as a string, like an unnamed Sprite's (BUGS.md #178 item 18)
        self.name: str = type(self).__name__
        self._background_color: tuple[int, ...] | None = None
        self._background_pattern: BackgroundPattern | None = None
        self._last_fps_log_time: float = 0.0
        self._screenshot: pygame.Surface | None = None
        # Keys whose key-down reached this scene and are not yet released (record_key_press)
        self._keys_pressed_in_scene: set[int] = set()
        self._world_shake_warning_logged: bool = False
        # Logic seconds since this scene started (game_time); the scene manager adds each
        # frame's scene dt before dt_tick
        self._game_time_seconds: float = 0.0
        # The scene to switch to at the end of this frame; None: stay (never self, which would
        # make every scene a reference cycle that only the cycle collector frees)
        self.next_scene: Scene | None = None
        self.rects = None
        self.screen = pygame.display.get_surface()
        assert self.screen is not None
        self.screen_width = self.screen.get_width()
        self.screen_height = self.screen.get_height()
        # Identity camera for scenes that do not scroll (apply(x, y) returns (x, y)); scrolling
        # games replace it with their own. Never None, so callers need no guards.
        self.camera: Camera2D = Camera2D(
            screen_width=self.screen_width, screen_height=self.screen_height
        )

        # http://n0nick.github.io/blog/2012/06/03/quick-dirty-using-pygames-dirtysprite-layered/
        self.all_sprites = groups

        # Initial screen state.

        self.screen = pygame.display.get_surface()
        assert self.screen is not None
        # In the display's format (BUGS.md #143: convert() returns the converted surface)
        self.background = pygame.Surface(self.screen.get_size()).convert()
        # A scene that sets no background shows the default pattern (glitchygames/backgrounds.py)
        # instead of black, which cannot be told from "nothing rendered"
        self.background_pattern = active_default_background_pattern()

        # This allows us to be treated like a sprite
        self.image = self.screen
        self.rect = self.screen.get_rect()

        self.dirty = 1

    @property
    def debug_subject(self: Self) -> Scene:
        """The scene the debug overlay inspects: normally this scene itself.

        A scene that only presents another scene (PauseScene shows a frozen screenshot of the
        paused game) returns that scene, so its hitboxes and physics stay visible and line up
        with the frozen picture.
        """
        return self

    def describe_for_ai(self: Self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Say what a game knows that its sprites don't show, for the AI console to read.

        Read only when asked, and it must change nothing.

        Returns:
            JSON-ready facts: the score, say. A scene without any says nothing.

        """
        return {}

    @property
    def scene_start(self: Self) -> SceneStart | None:
        """How this scene began, once set up (glitchygames/scene_start.py).

        None when its start was not captured (live play without recording, playback or
        instant replay) or before its first setup.
        """
        if self.scene_start_capture is None:
            return None
        return self.scene_start_capture.start

    def replay_arguments(self: Self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the constructor arguments that rebuild this scene as it began (besides options).

        A scene rebuilt for playback is ``type(scene)(**replay_arguments(), options=...)``
        (glitchygames/scene_start.py), so a scene built with arguments carried from the
        previous scene (a floor's score and lives) returns them as they were when it was built.
        They must read back from JSON exactly as returned. Asked once, before the scene's first
        setup, and only while its start is captured.

        Returns:
            The arguments by name; none by default.

        """
        return {}

    @property
    def input_devices(self: Self) -> InputDevices:
        """Every joystick and game controller the game sees, by instance id.

        Each ``InputDevice`` reads the frame's input snapshot on its joystick layer and, for a
        mapped pad, its controller layer; its events reach ``on_*_event`` from one layer only
        (glitchygames/input/input_devices.py). Empty without an engine.
        """
        return self.scene_manager.input_devices

    def on_input_device_added(self: Self, *, device: InputDevice) -> None:
        """Called while this scene is active when a device is connected; nothing by default.

        Args:
            device: The device (``input_devices`` holds it already).

        """

    def on_input_device_removed(self: Self, *, device: InputDevice) -> None:
        """Called while this scene is active when a device is disconnected; nothing by default.

        Args:
            device: The device (``input_devices`` no longer holds it).

        """

    @property
    def game_time(self: Self) -> float:
        """Logic seconds since this scene started: the sum of the dt its dt_tick received.

        Capped by MAX_FRAME_SECONDS where set, and it does not advance while the scene is not
        running (paused, or switched away), so cooldowns and timers measured with it pause with
        the game and replay exactly. Use it for gameplay timing instead of the wall clock.
        """
        return self._game_time_seconds

    def advance_game_time(self: Self, *, seconds: float) -> None:
        """Add one frame's scene dt to game_time.

        The engine calls this once per scene frame (SceneManager._update_scene, before
        dt_tick); games read game_time and never call it. It is public only because the scene
        manager, another class, calls it.

        Args:
            seconds: The scene's (possibly capped) dt this frame.

        """
        self._game_time_seconds += seconds

    @property
    def screenshot(self: Self) -> pygame.Surface:
        """A screenshot of the scene.

        Returns:
            pygame.Surface: The scene screenshot.

        """
        assert self.screen is not None
        # In the display's format (BUGS.md #143: convert() returns the converted surface)
        screenshot = pygame.Surface((self.screen_width, self.screen_height)).convert()
        # Opaque black, then the channel-wise maximum with the screen: its red, green and blue
        # are copied unblended and every pixel stays opaque, as the presented frame shows them
        # (glitchygames/opacity.py). A plain blit would blend away colours under alpha 0, and on
        # a display with per-pixel alpha (cocoa) leave alpha 0 behind: a black screenshot
        # (BUGS.md #142)
        screenshot.fill(BLACK)
        screenshot.blit(self.screen, (0, 0), special_flags=pygame.BLEND_RGBA_MAX)
        return screenshot

    @property
    def background_color(self: Self) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
        """The background color.

        Returns:
            tuple[int, ...] | None: The background color, or None while the background is a
            pattern (background_pattern).

        """
        return self._background_color

    @background_color.setter
    def background_color(self: Self, new_color: tuple[int, ...]) -> None:
        """Set the background color.

        The background is the frame's bottom layer, so it is opaque: an RGB colour is
        normalized to RGBA with alpha 255. A translucent colour is refused: nothing is under the
        background to show through it, so the dummy and x11 drivers would show it opaque while
        cocoa, whose display has per-pixel alpha, shows alpha 0 as black (BUGS.md #142).

        Args:
            new_color (tuple[int, ...]): The new background color (RGB, or RGBA with alpha 255).

        Raises:
            ValueError: The colour is translucent, or has neither three nor four components.

        """
        if len(new_color) == RGB_COMPONENT_COUNT:
            new_color = (*new_color, OPAQUE)
        if len(new_color) != RGBA_COMPONENT_COUNT:
            message = f'A scene background colour is RGB or RGBA, not {new_color!r}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        if new_color[-1] != OPAQUE:
            message = (
                f'A scene background colour must be opaque: {new_color!r} has alpha '
                f'{new_color[-1]}, and nothing is under the background to show through it'
            )
            raise ValueError(message)
        self._background_color = new_color
        self._background_pattern = None
        assert self._background_color is not None
        assert self.screen is not None
        self.background.fill(self._background_color)
        self.all_sprites.clear(self.screen, self.background)
        # The next draw repaints the whole screen from the new background, not only the areas
        # sprites dirty (BUGS.md #166)
        self.all_sprites.repaint_rect(self.screen.get_rect())

    @property
    def background_pattern(self: Self) -> BackgroundPattern | None:
        """The built-in pattern the background shows (glitchygames/backgrounds.py).

        A scene that sets no background gets the active default pattern (the TV test
        pattern unless --default-background chose another).

        Returns:
            BackgroundPattern | None: The pattern, or None while the background is a colour
            (background_color).

        """
        return self._background_pattern

    @background_pattern.setter
    def background_pattern(self: Self, new_pattern: BackgroundPattern) -> None:
        """Show a built-in pattern as the background (it replaces any background colour).

        Args:
            new_pattern: The pattern.

        """
        self._background_pattern = new_pattern
        self._background_color = None
        assert self.screen is not None
        self.background.blit(
            background_pattern_surface(pattern=new_pattern, size=self.background.get_size()),
            (0, 0),
        )
        self.all_sprites.clear(self.screen, self.background)
        # The next draw repaints the whole screen from the new background (BUGS.md #166)
        self.all_sprites.repaint_rect(self.screen.get_rect())

    def transition_to(self: Self, next_scene: Scene | None, transition: Transition) -> None:
        """Switch to another scene with a visual transition effect.

        Args:
            next_scene: The scene to transition to.
            transition: A Transition object (FadeTransition, SlideTransition, etc.).

        """
        self.scene_manager.request_transition(next_scene, transition)

    def setup(self: Self) -> None:
        """Set up the scene."""

    def cleanup(self: Self) -> None:
        """Cleanup the scene."""

    def shake(self: Self, shake: Shake, *, targets: ShakeTarget = ShakeTarget.WORLD) -> None:
        """Start a shake on the world (camera), the whole screen, or both.

        Rumble, if the shake has it, is sent automatically by the scene manager.

        Args:
            shake: The shake to start.
            targets: ShakeTarget.WORLD, ShakeTarget.SCREEN, or both combined with |.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: If WORLD is requested on a scene that is not active (for example
                from a transition cue, which runs after the scene was cleaned up).

        """
        if ShakeTarget.WORLD in targets:
            if self.scene_manager.active_scene is not self:
                message = f'{self.NAME} is not the active scene; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN'
                raise RuntimeError(message)
            self.camera.shake_effect.add(shake)
            if not self._world_shake_warning_logged and not self._world_shake_moves_anything():
                LOG.warning(
                    'WORLD shake on %s has no effect: no sprites are positioned through its '
                    'camera; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN',
                    self.NAME,
                )
                self._world_shake_warning_logged = True
        if ShakeTarget.SCREEN in targets:
            self.scene_manager.screen_shake.add(shake)

    def _world_shake_moves_anything(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Whether a WORLD shake on this scene's camera would move anything on screen.

        It does when a sprite is positioned through Camera2D.apply(), when the camera scrolls
        background layers, or when the scene has world sprites (the engine places them from
        the camera, shake included, without apply()). Decided when shake() is called.

        The warning only has to ask whether anything is drawn from the camera: whether the
        camera moves does not matter, because the engine advances a WORLD shake every frame
        even on a camera nothing moves (SceneManager._advance_still_camera_shake), so on a
        scene with world sprites it always shakes them and then decays.

        Returns:
            True if anything is drawn from this scene's camera.

        """
        return (
            self.camera.has_been_applied
            or self.camera.has_parallax_layers
            or any(is_world_positioned(sprite) for sprite in self.all_sprites)
        )

    def camera_target(self: Self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
        """The world point the engine aims the camera at this frame, or None (manual camera).

        Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus).
        The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The
        engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

        Returns:
            tuple[float, float] | None: The target's (world_x, world_y), or None when the
                camera follows nothing.

        """
        target = self.camera.follow_target
        if target is None:
            return None
        # Camera2D.follow() checked that the target has world_x and world_y
        return (float(target.world_x), float(target.world_y))

    def apply_camera_to_sprites(self: Self) -> None:
        """Reposition camera-relative sprites from the current camera.

        Default: nothing. Games that place sprites through Camera2D.apply() override this so
        the scene manager can refresh positions (for example, after clearing a WORLD shake
        before a transition screenshot).
        """

    def dt_tick(self: Self, dt: float) -> None:
        """Update the scene's delta time and active tweens.

        Args:
            dt (float): The delta time to update.

        """
        self.dt = dt
        self.dt_timer += self.dt
        self.tweens.update(dt)

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the active scene."""
        # Tweak to enable compound sprites to manage their own subsprites dirty states
        #
        # Ideally we'd just make dirty a property with a setter and getter on each
        # sprite object, but that doesn't work for some reason.
        [sprite.update_nested_sprites() for sprite in self.all_sprites]

        # Update all sprites that are dirty. An AnimatedSprite is given the frame's dt, so it
        # animates by time, not by frames rendered (its update() defaults to 16 ms; BUGS.md
        # #115). Games that animate in dt_tick override update() as a no-op taking dt
        for sprite in self.all_sprites:
            if not sprite.dirty:
                continue
            if isinstance(sprite, AnimatedSprite):
                sprite.update(self.dt)
            else:
                sprite.update()

        # Make all of the new scene's sprites dirty to force a redraw
        if self.dirty:
            for sprite in self.all_sprites:
                sprite.dirty = 1 if not sprite.dirty else sprite.dirty

    @property
    def all_sprites(self: Self) -> pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any]:
        """The scene's sprites, the group it draws: dirty-rect drawing pinned (BUGS.md #190)."""
        return self._all_sprites

    @all_sprites.setter
    def all_sprites(self: Self, group: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any]) -> None:
        pin_dirty_rect_drawing(group)
        self._all_sprites = group

    @override
    def render(self: Self, screen: pygame.Surface) -> None:
        """Render the active scene.

        Args:
            screen (pygame.Surface): The screen to render to.

        """
        # Use LayeredDirty's clear method for proper background clearing and dirty rect management
        self.all_sprites.clear(screen, self.background)
        self.rects = self.all_sprites.draw(screen)

    def sprites_at_position(self: Self, pos: tuple[int, int]) -> list[Any]:
        """Return the sprites at a given position.

        Args:
            pos (tuple[int, int]): The position to check.

        Returns:
            list[Any]: The sprites at the given position.

        """
        mouse = MousePointer(pos=pos)

        return pygame.sprite.spritecollide(sprite=mouse, group=self.all_sprites, dokill=False)

    def _get_collided_sprites(self, position: tuple[int, int]) -> list[Any]:
        """Get sprites at the given position.

        Args:
            position: The position to check for sprites

        Returns:
            List of sprites at the position

        """
        return self.sprites_at_position(pos=position)

    def _get_focusable_sprites(self, collided_sprites: list[Any]) -> list[Any]:
        """Get focusable sprites from the collided sprites.

        Args:
            collided_sprites: List of sprites that were collided with

        Returns:
            List of focusable sprites

        """
        return [s for s in collided_sprites if hasattr(s, 'focusable') and s.focusable]

    def _get_focused_sprites(self) -> list[Any]:
        """Get currently focused sprites.

        Returns:
            List of currently focused sprites

        """
        return [
            sprite
            for sprite in self.all_sprites
            if hasattr(sprite, 'is_active') and sprite.is_active
        ]

    def _has_focusable_sprites(self, collided_sprites: list[Any]) -> bool:
        """Check if any of the collided sprites are focusable.

        Args:
            collided_sprites: List of sprites that were collided with

        Returns:
            True if any sprite is focusable, False otherwise

        """
        return any(hasattr(sprite, 'focusable') and sprite.focusable for sprite in collided_sprites)

    def _unfocus_sprites(self, focused_sprites: list[Any]) -> None:
        """Unfocus the given sprites.

        Args:
            focused_sprites: List of sprites to unfocus

        """
        # Every focused sprite has is_active (_get_focused_sprites)
        for sprite in focused_sprites:
            self.log.debug('Unfocusing %s', type(sprite).__name__)
            sprite.is_active = False
            if hasattr(sprite, 'on_focus_lost'):
                sprite.on_focus_lost()

    def _handle_focus_management(self, collided_sprites: list[Any]) -> None:
        """Handle focus management for mouse clicks.

        Args:
            collided_sprites: List of sprites that were collided with

        """
        focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()

        # If we clicked outside all sprites that can be focused, unfocus them
        if not self._has_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites):
            self.log.debug('Click outside focusable sprites - unfocusing')
            self._unfocus_sprites(focused_sprites)

    def record_key_press(self: Self, *, key: int) -> None:
        """Note that a key-down reached this scene.

        SceneManager calls this for every key-down it routes to the active scene, before the
        scene's own on_key_down_event, so subclasses that override that handler are covered.
        on_key_up_event quits only on the release of a key recorded here. Games never call it;
        it is public only because the scene manager, another class, calls it.

        Args:
            key: The pygame key code.

        """
        self._keys_pressed_in_scene.add(key)

    def forget_key_presses(self: Self) -> None:
        """Forget every key press recorded by record_key_press.

        SceneManager calls this whenever the scene becomes active (switched to, resumed, or
        the target of a transition), before setup(). A press whose release went to another
        scene would otherwise stay recorded, and a later release of that key (whose press was
        discarded during a transition) would quit.
        Games never call it; it is public only because the scene manager calls it.
        """
        self._keys_pressed_in_scene.clear()

    def _handle_quit_key_press(self) -> None:
        """Handle quit key press when no sprites are focused."""
        self.log.info('Quit requested')
        # Post a QUIT event to ensure proper cleanup
        post_event(pygame.event.Event(pygame.QUIT))

    @override
    def on_audio_device_added_event(self: Self, event: events.AudioDeviceEvent) -> None:
        """Handle audio device added events.

        Args:
            event (AudioDeviceEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        # AUDIODEVICEADDED which, iscapture
        self.log.debug('%s: On Audio Device Added Event %s', type(self), event)

    @override
    def on_audio_device_removed_event(self: Self, event: events.AudioDeviceEvent) -> None:
        """Handle audio device removed events.

        Args:
            event (AudioDeviceEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        # AUDIODEVICEREMOVED which, iscapture
        self.log.debug('%s: On Audio Device Removed Event %s', type(self), event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle controller button down events.

        Args:
            event (ControllerButtonEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        # CONTROLLERBUTTONDOWN which, button
        self.log.debug('%s: On Controller Button Down Event %s', type(self), event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_up_event(self: Self, event: events.ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle controller button up events.

        Args:
            event (ControllerButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    @override
    def on_key_up_event(self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key up events.

        Args:
            event (KeyEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        self.log.debug('%s: On Key Up Event %s', type(self), event)

        # Check for focused sprites first
        focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()

        # Only a release whose press this scene received can quit (record_key_press): a key
        # pressed during a transition (the press is discarded) or in a scene that has since
        # been left must not quit from here. Each release consumes its press.
        event_key: int | None = getattr(event, 'key', None)
        was_pressed_in_scene = event_key is not None and event_key in self._keys_pressed_in_scene
        if event_key is not None:  # pragma: no branch - a key release always has a key
            self._keys_pressed_in_scene.discard(event_key)

        # Only process quit keys if no sprites are focused
        if (
            not focused_sprites
            and was_pressed_in_scene
            and event_key in {pygame.K_q, pygame.K_ESCAPE}
        ):
            self._handle_quit_key_press()

        focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
        self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

        # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state
        if collided_sprites:
            top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
            self.log.debug(
                'Top sprite @ DOWN: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
                type(top_sprite).__name__,
                getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
                event_pos,
            )

        # Find currently focused sprites
        focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
        self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

        # Handle focus management
        self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

        # Process the click for collided sprites
        for sprite in collided_sprites:
            if hasattr(sprite, 'on_mouse_button_down_event'):
                sprite.on_mouse_button_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_fps_event(self: Self, event: events.FpsEvent) -> None:
        """Handle FPS events.

        Args:
            event (FpsEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        # FPSEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 1
        # Log FPS at the specified interval to reduce log spam. The frame clock starts at 0, so
        # the first log waits one full interval of play
        current_time = clock.frame_clock_seconds()

        # Use the configured log interval instead of hardcoded 1.0 second
        log_interval_seconds = float(self.scene_manager.fps_log_interval_ms) / 1000.0
        if current_time - self._last_fps_log_time >= log_interval_seconds:
            event_fps: float = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)
            self.log.info('Scene "%s" (%s) FPS: %s', self.NAME, type(self), event_fps)
            self._last_fps_log_time = current_time

        self.fps = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)

    @override
    def on_key_down_event(self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key down events."""
        self.log.debug('%s: On Key Down Event %s', type(self), event)

        # Check if focused sprites handle the event
        if self._handle_focused_sprite_events(event):
            return

        # Only process scene-level key events if no focused sprite handled it
        self._handle_scene_key_events(event)

    def _handle_focused_sprite_events(self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> bool:
        """Handle events for focused sprites.

        Args:
            event: The event to handle

        Returns:
            True if a focused sprite handled the event, False otherwise

        """
        # Find the currently focused sprite
        focused_sprites = [
            sprite
            for sprite in self.all_sprites
            if hasattr(sprite, 'is_active') and sprite.is_active
        ]

        if focused_sprites:
            # If we have focused sprites, only they get the events
            for sprite in focused_sprites:
                if hasattr(sprite, 'on_key_down_event'):
                    sprite.on_key_down_event(event)
                    return True  # Stop event propagation after handling

        return False

    def _handle_scene_key_events(self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle a key press no focused sprite took: a hook for scenes; the base does nothing.

        Q and ESC quit on their release (on_key_up_event), once per press. BUGS.md #203: Q's
        press here logged "Quit requested" and set a quit_requested flag nothing read.

        Args:
            event: The event to handle

    @override
    def pause(self: Self) -> None:
        """Pause the current scene.

        Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame.
        Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

        The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause()
        usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an
        immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

        """
        from .builtin_scenes.pause_scene import PauseScene

        self.next_scene = PauseScene(options=self.options)

        self.log.info('Scene pause requested')

    def resume(self: Self) -> None:
        """Resume the current scene.

        Default implementation switches back to the previous scene.
        Scenes can override this method to provide custom resume behavior.

        """
        if self.scene_manager.previous_scene:
            self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(self.scene_manager.previous_scene)
            self.log.info('Scene resumed')
        else:
            self.log.warning('No previous scene found to resume')

    def game_over(self: Self) -> None:
        """Handle game over for the current scene.

        Default implementation switches to a GameOverScene.
        Scenes can override this method to provide custom game over behavior.

        """
        from .builtin_scenes.game_over_scene import GameOverScene

        # Create the game over scene
        game_over_scene = GameOverScene(options=self.options)

        # Switch to the game over scene
        self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(game_over_scene)

        self.log.info('Game over')
