def handle_event(self, event: events.HashableEvent) -> None:
    """Handle pygame events.

    Args:
        event (pygame.event.Event): The event to handle.

    """
    # Check for focused sprites first
    if self.active_scene and self.active_scene.all_sprites:
        focused_sprites = [
            sprite
            for sprite in self.active_scene.all_sprites
            if hasattr(sprite, 'is_active') and sprite.is_active
        ]

        if focused_sprites and event.type == pygame.KEYDOWN:
            # Scene does not expose a handle_event() method; focused sprites
            # receive key events through the normal event dispatch pipeline.
            return

    # Only process other events if no focused sprites handled it
    if event.type == pygame.QUIT:
        self.log.info('POSTING QUIT EVENT')
        self.quit_requested = True

def instant_replay(self: Self) -> bool:
    """Show the active scene's last ``INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS``, then go on where it was.

    The scene is rebuilt from its start in a playback scope from the start of the next
    frame and plays its instant-replay journal (glitchygames/instant_replay.py): the frames
    before the last ``INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS`` of frame time run unseen, unpaced and silent,
    the rest are shown at the game's pace, then the live scene, never touched, goes on
    exactly where it was (glitchygames/replay/playback.py, rules 6 and 7). The player's
    presses do not end it; the game may, with ``end_playback``. How it ended:
    ``last_playback_outcome``.

    Returns:

        active scene keeps no journal (its class sets no ``INSTANT_REPLAY_SECONDS``, or

def journal_pumped_events(
    self: Self,
    *,
    raw_events: list[pygame.event.Event],
    posts_before_pump: list[tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]],
    origins: list[str] | None,
    redelivered_events: list[RedeliveredEvent],
) -> None:
    """Hand one pump's batch to the instant-replay journal (``GameEngine._pump_events``).

    Nothing while no journal is kept or a playback scope serves the frame (its scene is
    not the live session's).

    Args:

        raw_events=raw_events,
        posts_before_pump=posts_before_pump,
        origins=origins,
        redelivered_events=redelivered_events,
    )

def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: events.KeyEvent) -> None:
    """Handle the debug overlay keys, then forward key-down events as the proxy would.

    F3 toggles the overlay and F4 cycles its panels, unless a sprite in the active scene has
    keyboard focus (is_active), so typing into text fields is never intercepted. Every other
    key goes to the active scene (every Scene has the handler, and records the press first),
    or to the game engine when there is no active scene.

    Args:
        event (KeyEvent): The key-down event.

    Raises:
        AttributeError: If there is no active scene and the game engine has no handler.

    """
    if event.key in OVERLAY_KEYS and not self._active_scene_has_focused_sprite():
        self.debug_overlay.handle_key(key=event.key)
        return
    if self.active_scene is not None:
        # Recorded before dispatch, so a quit-key release knows this scene saw the press
        self.active_scene.record_key_press(key=event.key)
        self.active_scene.on_key_down_event(event)
    elif self.game_engine is not None and hasattr(self.game_engine, 'on_key_down_event'):
        self.game_engine.on_key_down_event(event)
    else:
        message = (
            f"'{type(self)}' object has no attribute 'on_key_down_event': neither the "
            'active scene nor the game engine provides it'
        )
        raise AttributeError(message)

Play a recording as an attract-mode demo, then return to then.

The demo plays in a playback scope (glitchygames/replay/playback.py) from the start of the next frame, at the game's speed, and ends at the recording's end, at the first key or button press (exit_on_input), at a divergence (logged at WARNING, demo diverged: <description>) or at the recording's own quit. A recording cut off part way plays to its last complete frame and ends as truncated. A recording that cannot be played (missing, unreadable, of another game, with no scene start to begin at) is logged at WARNING, naming the demo and the reason, and nothing starts; so is a request while another playback is starting or playing. How it ended: last_playback_outcome.

def play_recording(self: Self, *, path: Path, then: Scene) -> None:
    """Play a recording as an attract-mode demo, then return to ``then``.

    The demo plays in a playback scope (glitchygames/replay/playback.py) from the start of
    the next frame, at the game's speed, and ends at the recording's end, at the first key
    or button press (``exit_on_input``), at a divergence (logged at WARNING, ``demo
    diverged: <description>``) or at the recording's own quit. A recording cut off part
    way plays to its last complete frame and ends as ``truncated``. A recording that
    cannot be played (missing, unreadable, of another game, with no scene start to
    begin at) is logged at WARNING, naming the demo and the reason, and nothing starts;
    so is a request while another playback is starting or playing. How it ended:
    ``last_playback_outcome``.

    Args:
        path: The recording.
        then: The scene to make active when the demo ends (usually the scene asking).

    """
    # Function-level import, for layering: glitchygames.replay.playback imports
    # glitchygames.scenes (it needs Scene), and scenes must not import replay at runtime, so
    # a module-level import here would be a cycle.
    from glitchygames.replay.playback import (
        DEMO_PLAYBACK,
        PlaybackOptions,
        start_playback_from_recording,
    )

    start_playback_from_recording(
        manager=self,
        path=path,
        then=then,
        options=PlaybackOptions(exit_on_input=True, kind=DEMO_PLAYBACK),
    )

docs.text:
Record a supervisor action in this frame and hand it to its handlers.

The event is recorded (with a read-only copy of data) before any handler runs. Every handler for kind runs, in registration order, even when an earlier one raises; then the first handler exception is re-raised, and any later ones are logged, so a broken handler fails loudly without silently skipping the others.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/scene.py 
def record_control_event(self: Self, *, kind: str, data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Record a supervisor action in this frame and hand it to its handlers.

    The event is recorded (with a read-only copy of ``data``) before any handler runs.
    Every handler for ``kind`` runs, in registration order, even when an earlier one
    raises; then the first handler exception is re-raised, and any later ones are logged,
    so a broken handler fails loudly without silently skipping the others.
    """
    control_event = ControlEvent(kind=kind, data=data)
    self._frame_control_events.append(control_event)
    first_error: Exception | None = None
    scope_handlers = [
        scope_handler
        for scope_kind, scope_handler in self._scope_control_event_handlers
        if scope_kind == kind
    ]
    for handler in list(self._control_event_handlers.get(kind, [])):
        try:
            self._run_live_or_scope_code(
                is_scope_code=handler in scope_handlers,
                call=lambda handler=handler: handler(control_event),
            )
        except Exception as error:
            if first_error is None:
                first_error = error
            else:
                LOG.exception('Another %r control event handler failed', kind)
    if first_error is not None:
        raise first_error

def recorded_playback_answer(self: Self) -> bool | None:
    """Return what a playback request got in the frame being played, inside a scope.

    A scene played back from its instant-replay journal asks for playbacks where the live
    scene did (an instant replay after every goal): each request is answered with the next
    answer that frame recorded, and nothing is requested (scopes do not nest;
    glitchygames/instant_replay.py, rule 8). ``start_playback`` asks this first.

    Returns:
        The recorded answer; None outside a scope, or when the frame recorded none left.

    """
    session = self._playback_session
    if session is None:
        return None
    answers = session.sources.replay.recorded_playback_answers
    return answers.popleft() if answers else None

def request_playback(self: Self, *, request: PlaybackRequest) -> bool:
    """Enter a playback scope at the start of the next frame (glitchygames/replay/playback.py).

    A scope begins between frames, so the rebuilt scene's first frame is a whole frame, as
    the recorded one was, and the frame that asked runs to its end on the live doors. If
    the active scene changed by then (a ``next_scene`` switch at the end of the frame that
    asked), the request is dropped (logged): the scene to return to has gone.

    Args:
        request: The scope to enter (``start_playback`` builds it).

    Returns:
        False (logged) when a scope is already requested or in progress: scopes do not
        nest. True otherwise.

    """
    if self._requested_playback is not None or self.in_playback_scope:
        LOG.warning('A playback is already starting or playing; %s not started', request.kind)
        return False
    self._requested_playback = request
    # A scene asking from its setup() (a title screen starting the next demo as a demo
    # returns to it) is the one active from then on
    self._playback_requesting_scene = (
        self._scene_in_setup if self._scene_in_setup is not None else self.active_scene
    )
    return True

False (an outer driver that waits for its own tick, GameHost.run_async) never waits or calibrates a timer: the wait for the next tick is the pacing, and is measured into the next frame's start-to-start dt like a pacing sleep.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/scene.py 
def run_frame_step(self: Self, *, frame_start_seconds: float, paced: bool = True) -> float:
    """Run one step of the frame loop: one frame, or a held frame presented again.

    Args:
        frame_start_seconds: The perf_counter() reading this frame starts at (the previous
            step's return value, or ``begin_frames``').
        paced: True (``start``) paces the frame as always: the timer backend's deadline,
            else the pygame clock, or the doors' pacing. False (an outer driver that waits
            for its own tick, ``GameHost.run_async``) never waits or calibrates a timer:
            the wait for the next tick is the pacing, and is measured into the next
            frame's start-to-start dt like a pacing sleep.

    Returns:
        The perf_counter() reading the next frame starts at.

    """
    # The doors may hold the loop between frames (a paused watched replay): no frame
    # runs, the last one is presented again with the doors' overlay
    self.last_step_was_held = active_sources().hold_frame()
    if self.last_step_was_held:
        # Unless the hold ended the run (the viewer quit): nothing more to show
        if not active_sources().stop_requested:
            self._present_held_frame()
        # The hold is not part of the next frame's measured time
        return clock.raw_counter_seconds()

    # Frame pacing using timer backend when available
    # None without an engine (a bare SceneManager) or before the engine made its timer
    game_engine = self.game_engine
    timer = game_engine.timer if game_engine is not None and paced else None
    # The doors may pace the frame themselves (0.0: not at all, in a headless replay);
    # an unpaced step is never paced here
    paced_seconds = active_sources().paced_frame_seconds() if paced else 0.0
    period_ns = 0
    if timer is not None:
        period_ns = (
            timer.start_frame(self.target_fps)
            if paced_seconds is None
            else round(paced_seconds * 1_000_000_000)
        )

    # The frame's work starts here. A paced frame starts where the last one closed (after
    # its pacing sleep); an unpaced one now: the outer driver's wait since the last step's
    # closing reading is this frame's pacing, in its dt but never in its processing time
    work_start_seconds = frame_start_seconds if paced else clock.raw_counter_seconds()
    self._run_frame()

    # The frame's processing time: its work, without the pacing sleep that follows
    processing_seconds = clock.raw_counter_seconds() - work_start_seconds

    return self._finish_frame(
        frame_start_seconds=frame_start_seconds,
        timer=timer,
        period_ns=period_ns,
        paced_seconds=paced_seconds,
        processing_seconds=processing_seconds,
    )

docs.text:
Start the scene manager.

Each frame starts at the previous frame's closing perf_counter() reading and ends in _finish_frame, which sets self.dt once, to that frame's start-to-start period, so logic in frame N receives the time frame N-1 took (engine audit #15).

The blocking frame loop: begin_frames, then run_frame_step while should_run_frames, then end_frames. An outer driver that must give control back between frames (a browser; glitchygames/host.py GameHost.run_async) runs the same steps itself, one per tick, unpaced.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/scene.py 
def start(self: Self) -> None:
    """Start the scene manager.

    Each frame starts at the previous frame's closing perf_counter() reading and ends in
    _finish_frame, which sets ``self.dt`` once, to that frame's start-to-start period, so
    logic in frame N receives the time frame N-1 took (engine audit #15).

    The blocking frame loop: ``begin_frames``, then ``run_frame_step`` while
    ``should_run_frames``, then ``end_frames``. An outer driver that must give control back
    between frames (a browser; glitchygames/host.py ``GameHost.run_async``) runs the same
    steps itself, one per tick, unpaced.
    """
    frame_start_seconds = self.begin_frames()
    while self.should_run_frames():
        frame_start_seconds = self.run_frame_step(frame_start_seconds=frame_start_seconds)
    self.end_frames()

Presses and motion (TRANSITION_DISCARDED_EVENT_TYPES) are dropped, except motion back to neutral, which releases a held stick or hat: an axis inside ActionMap's DEFAULT_DEADZONE (the value ActionMap treats as zero) or a hat at (0, 0).

def is_discarded_during_transition(event: pygame.event.Event) -> bool:
    """Report whether a transition frame drops this event.

    Presses and motion (TRANSITION_DISCARDED_EVENT_TYPES) are dropped, except motion back to
    neutral, which releases a held stick or hat: an axis inside ActionMap's DEFAULT_DEADZONE
    (the value ActionMap treats as zero) or a hat at (0, 0).

    Args:
        event: A raw pygame event.

    Returns:
        True if the event is dropped, False if it is delivered.

    """
    if event.type not in TRANSITION_DISCARDED_EVENT_TYPES:
        return False
    if event.type in _AXIS_MOTION_EVENT_TYPES:
        position = normalized_axis_value(event_type=event.type, value=event.value)
        return abs(position) >= DEFAULT_DEADZONE
    if event.type == pygame.JOYHATMOTION:
        return tuple(event.value) != _HAT_CENTRED
    return True

def pin_dirty_rect_drawing(group: object) -> None:
    """Keep a LayeredDirty group drawing in dirty-rect mode, however long a draw takes.

    pygame's ``LayeredDirty.draw`` times itself (``pygame.time.get_ticks``) and draws the next
    frame in full-screen mode when a draw took longer than its threshold (1000/80 ms by
    default), dirty-rect mode otherwise, so which pixels a frame shows depended on the
    machine's speed: forcing full-screen mode changed the frames 184 tests present (BUGS.md
    #190), and the engine's own draws assume dirty-rect mode (``Scene.render`` returns only
    the dirty rects). An unreachable threshold keeps every draw after the first (always
    full-screen: nothing drawn yet) in dirty-rect mode, which is what a fast machine got.
    Anything else (a test's stand-in group) is left alone.

    Args:
        group: The group (pinned only if it is a ``LayeredDirty``).

    """
    if isinstance(group, pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty):
        group.set_timing_threshold(math.inf)

docs.title: __subclasshook__(subclass) classmethod
docs.text:
Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 
@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

@classmethod
def break_when(cls: type[Sprite], sprite_type: object | None = None) -> None:
    """Register a breakpoint for a sprite type.

    Args:
        sprite_type (object | None): The sprite type to break on.
            None means break on any sprite.

    """
    # The current context's breakpoints: None means disabled, [] means any
    counters = sprite_counters()
    if counters.breakpoints is None:
        counters.breakpoints = []

    # If none, break always.
    if sprite_type is not None:
        # Register the type asked for (not cls): __init__ compares str(type(self)) with it
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==%s', sprite_type)
        counters.breakpoints.append(str(sprite_type))
    else:
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==<any>')

Bases: Scene

Pause scene that shows a semi-transparent overlay over the game.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/builtin_scenes/pause_scene.py 
class PauseScene(Scene):
    """Pause scene that shows a semi-transparent overlay over the game."""

    # It presents the paused scene, so it cannot be rebuilt on its own (glitchygames/scene_start.py)
    CAPTURES_SCENE_START: ClassVar[bool] = False

    def __init__(self: Self, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Initialize the pause scene.

        Args:
            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments.

        """
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        # Black under the overlay (named: a scene that sets no background shows the test
        # pattern), so the pause screen's own background is never the pattern wherever the
        # frozen screenshot does not cover it (a custom screenshot may be smaller)
        self.background_color = BLACK
        self.overlay = None
        self._space_pressed = False
        # A gamepad's Start or A resumes, B or Back quits, as SPACE and ESC do
        self._gamepad_buttons = GamepadChoiceButtons()
        # The gameplay scene this pause screen froze; the debug overlay inspects it instead
        self._paused_scene: Scene | None = None

    @override
    def setup(self: Self) -> None:
        """Set up the pause scene."""
        super().setup()

        # Create the pause overlay using the previous scene's screenshot
        previous_scene = self.scene_manager.previous_scene
        self._paused_scene = previous_scene
        if previous_scene:
            # Use the scene's screenshot property (which will use custom screenshot if set)
            screenshot = previous_scene.screenshot
        else:
            # This should not happen - scene manager should always have a previous_scene
            self.log.warning('No previous scene found - this should not happen!')
            # Fallback: create a black screenshot
            screenshot = pygame.Surface((self.screen_width, self.screen_height))
            screenshot.fill((0, 0, 0))

        assert self.scene_manager.game_engine is not None
        # The running game's scene (engine.game is its class: glitchygames/engine/running_game.py)
        self.overlay = PauseOverlay(
            self.scene_manager.game_engine.running_game.instance, screenshot
        )
        self.all_sprites.add(self.overlay)

        self.log.info('Pause scene setup complete')

    @property
    @override
    def debug_subject(self: Self) -> Scene:
        """The paused gameplay scene, so the debug overlay keeps showing its hitboxes."""
        return self._paused_scene if self._paused_scene is not None else self

    @override
    def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key down events for the pause scene.

        Args:
            event: The key down event

        """
        if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE:
            # Track that spacebar is pressed (but don't act on it yet)
            self._space_pressed = True
        elif event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
            # Quit the game
            self.scene_manager.quit()
        else:
            super().on_key_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_key_up_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key up events for the pause scene.

        Args:
            event: The key up event

        """
        if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE and self._space_pressed:
            # Spacebar was pressed and now released - resume the game
            self._space_pressed = False
            self.log.info('Resuming game...')
            self.resume()
        else:
            super().on_key_up_event(event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_down_event(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """A mapped gamepad's B or Back quits; Start or A arms resuming (gamepad_choice.py).

        Args:
            event: The controller button down event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_down(event)
        super().on_controller_button_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_up_event(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """A mapped gamepad's Start or A, released after its press here, resumes the game.

        Args:
            event: The controller button up event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_up(event)
        super().on_controller_button_up_event(event)

    @override
    def on_joy_button_down_event(self: Self, event: JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Any other gamepad's B or Back quits; Start or A arms resuming (gamepad_choice.py).

        Args:
            event: The joystick button down event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_down(event)
        super().on_joy_button_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_joy_button_up_event(self: Self, event: JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Any other gamepad's Start or A, released after its press here, resumes the game.

        Args:
            event: The joystick button up event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_up(event)
        super().on_joy_button_up_event(event)

    def _on_gamepad_button_down(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent | JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Quit for B or Back, as ESC does (BUGS.md #209 item 10: no gamepad could).

        Args:
            event: The button down event, from either layer.

        """
        if self._gamepad_buttons.button_pressed(event) is GamepadChoice.QUIT:
            self.scene_manager.quit()

    def _on_gamepad_button_up(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent | JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Resume the game for a Start or A pressed here, as SPACE does.

        Args:
            event: The button up event, from either layer.

        """
        if self._gamepad_buttons.button_released(event) is GamepadChoice.CONTINUE:
            self.log.info('Resuming game...')
            self.resume()

    @override
    def on_window_focus_gained_event(self: Self, event: WindowEvent) -> None:
        """Auto-resume when the window regains focus.

        Waits a short time after setup to avoid the focus gained event
        that fires immediately when the pause scene is first displayed.

        Args:
            event: The focus gained event.

        """
        super().on_window_focus_gained_event(event)
        # Ignore focus events in the first 0.5s — the scene switch itself
        # triggers a focus lost/gained pair that we don't want to act on
        min_pause_duration = 0.5
        if self.dt_timer > min_pause_duration:
            self.log.info('Window focus regained — auto-resuming')
            self.resume()

docs.title: __subclasshook__(subclass) classmethod
docs.text:
Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 
@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def camera_target(self: Self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """The world point the engine aims the camera at this frame, or None (manual camera).

    Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus).
    The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The
    engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

    Returns:
        tuple[float, float] | None: The target's (world_x, world_y), or None when the
            camera follows nothing.

    """
    target = self.camera.follow_target
    if target is None:
        return None
    # Camera2D.follow() checked that the target has world_x and world_y
    return (float(target.world_x), float(target.world_y))

@override
def on_fps_event(self: Self, event: events.FpsEvent) -> None:
    """Handle FPS events.

    Args:
        event (FpsEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    # FPSEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 1
    # Log FPS at the specified interval to reduce log spam. The frame clock starts at 0, so
    # the first log waits one full interval of play
    current_time = clock.frame_clock_seconds()

    # Use the configured log interval instead of hardcoded 1.0 second
    log_interval_seconds = float(self.scene_manager.fps_log_interval_ms) / 1000.0
    if current_time - self._last_fps_log_time >= log_interval_seconds:
        event_fps: float = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)
        self.log.info('Scene "%s" (%s) FPS: %s', self.NAME, type(self), event_fps)
        self._last_fps_log_time = current_time

    self.fps = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)

def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
    """Handle key down events for the pause scene.

    Args:
        event: The key down event

    """
    if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE:
        # Track that spacebar is pressed (but don't act on it yet)
        self._space_pressed = True
    elif event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
        # Quit the game
        self.scene_manager.quit()
    else:
        super().on_key_down_event(event)

@override
def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle left mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Left Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_left_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_left_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: events.MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
    """Handle mouse button down events.

    Args:
        event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Mouse Button Down ===')
    event_pos: tuple[int, int] = getattr(event, 'pos', (0, 0))
    self.log.debug('Click position: %s', event_pos)

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Diagnostics: log the top-most collided sprite and its active state
    if collided_sprites:
        top_sprite = collided_sprites[-1]
        self.log.debug(
            'Top sprite @ DOWN: %s, active=%s, pos=%s',
            type(top_sprite).__name__,
            getattr(top_sprite, 'active', None),
            event_pos,
        )

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_mouse_button_down_event(event)

@override
def on_window_focus_gained_event(self: Self, event: WindowEvent) -> None:
    """Auto-resume when the window regains focus.

    Waits a short time after setup to avoid the focus gained event
    that fires immediately when the pause scene is first displayed.

    Args:
        event: The focus gained event.

    """
    super().on_window_focus_gained_event(event)
    # Ignore focus events in the first 0.5s — the scene switch itself
    # triggers a focus lost/gained pair that we don't want to act on
    min_pause_duration = 0.5
    if self.dt_timer > min_pause_duration:
        self.log.info('Window focus regained — auto-resuming')
        self.resume()

@override
def pause(self: Self) -> None:
    """Pause the current scene.

    Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

    The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause()

def setup(self: Self) -> None:
    """Set up the pause scene."""
    super().setup()

    # Create the pause overlay using the previous scene's screenshot
    previous_scene = self.scene_manager.previous_scene
    self._paused_scene = previous_scene
    if previous_scene:
        # Use the scene's screenshot property (which will use custom screenshot if set)
        screenshot = previous_scene.screenshot

    self.overlay = PauseOverlay(
        self.scene_manager.game_engine.running_game.instance, screenshot

def shake(self: Self, shake: Shake, *, targets: ShakeTarget = ShakeTarget.WORLD) -> None:
    """Start a shake on the world (camera), the whole screen, or both.

    Rumble, if the shake has it, is sent automatically by the scene manager.

    Args:
        shake: The shake to start.
        targets: ShakeTarget.WORLD, ShakeTarget.SCREEN, or both combined with |.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If WORLD is requested on a scene that is not active (for example
            from a transition cue, which runs after the scene was cleaned up).

    """
    if ShakeTarget.WORLD in targets:
        if self.scene_manager.active_scene is not self:
            message = f'{self.NAME} is not the active scene; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN'
            raise RuntimeError(message)
        self.camera.shake_effect.add(shake)
        if not self._world_shake_warning_logged and not self._world_shake_moves_anything():
            LOG.warning(
                'WORLD shake on %s has no effect: no sprites are positioned through its '
                'camera; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN',
                self.NAME,
            )
            self._world_shake_warning_logged = True
    if ShakeTarget.SCREEN in targets:
        self.scene_manager.screen_shake.add(shake)

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/scene.py 
@override
def update(self: Self) -> None:
    """Update the active scene."""
    # Tweak to enable compound sprites to manage their own subsprites dirty states
    #
    # Ideally we'd just make dirty a property with a setter and getter on each
    # sprite object, but that doesn't work for some reason.
    [sprite.update_nested_sprites() for sprite in self.all_sprites]

    # Update all sprites that are dirty. An AnimatedSprite is given the frame's dt, so it
    # animates by time, not by frames rendered (its update() defaults to 16 ms; BUGS.md
    # #115). Games that animate in dt_tick override update() as a no-op taking dt
    for sprite in self.all_sprites:
        if not sprite.dirty:
            continue
        if isinstance(sprite, AnimatedSprite):
            sprite.update(self.dt)
        else:
            sprite.update()

    # Make all of the new scene's sprites dirty to force a redraw
    if self.dirty:
        for sprite in self.all_sprites:
            sprite.dirty = 1 if not sprite.dirty else sprite.dirty

Accepts an optional final_score to show the player's result and an optional high_scores list to display the leaderboard.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/builtin_scenes/game_over_scene.py 
class GameOverScene(Scene):
    """Game Over scene with final score and high score display.

    Accepts an optional final_score to show the player's result and
    an optional high_scores list to display the leaderboard.
    """

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        final_score: int | None = None,
        high_scores: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the Game Over scene.

        Args:
            final_score: The player's final score (displayed if provided).
            high_scores: List of high score dicts with 'score' key,
                sorted descending. Top 5 are displayed.
            **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments.

        """
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        # Black behind the text (named: a scene that sets no background shows the test pattern)
        self.background_color = BLACK
        self.final_score = final_score
        self.high_scores = high_scores or []
        self.text_sprite = None
        self._space_pressed = False
        # A gamepad's Start or A restarts, B or Back quits, as SPACE and ESC do
        self._gamepad_buttons = GamepadChoiceButtons()
        # Don't set next_scene to self - this causes infinite loops
        # The scene will stay active until user input changes it

    @override
    def setup(self: Self) -> None:
        """Set up the Game Over scene with score display."""
        super().setup()
        log.info('GameOverScene setup() called')

        center_x = self.screen_width // 2
        current_y = self.screen_height // 4

        # Title
        self.text_sprite = TextSprite(
            'GAME OVER',
            (center_x, current_y),
            color=(255, 0, 0),
            font_size=48,
        )
        self.all_sprites.add(self.text_sprite)
        current_y += 60

        # Final score (if provided)
        if self.final_score is not None:
            score_sprite = TextSprite(
                f'Score: {self.final_score}',
                (center_x, current_y),
                color=(255, 255, 100),
                font_size=32,
            )
            self.all_sprites.add(score_sprite)
            current_y += 50

        # High scores (top 5)
        if self.high_scores:
            header = TextSprite(
                'HIGH SCORES',
                (center_x, current_y),
                color=(200, 200, 200),
                font_size=28,
            )
            self.all_sprites.add(header)
            current_y += 35

            max_displayed = 5
            for rank, entry in enumerate(self.high_scores[:max_displayed], start=1):
                score_value = entry.get('score', 0)
                entry_sprite = TextSprite(
                    f'{rank}. {score_value}',
                    (center_x, current_y),
                    color=(180, 180, 180),
                    font_size=24,
                )
                self.all_sprites.add(entry_sprite)
                current_y += 30

        # Subtitle
        current_y += 20
        subtitle = TextSprite(
            'Press SPACE or START to restart, ESC or BACK to quit',
            (center_x, current_y),
            color=(255, 255, 255),
            font_size=24,
        )
        self.all_sprites.add(subtitle)
        log.info('GameOverScene setup() completed')

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the Game Over scene."""
        # Call the parent update method to handle sprite updates
        super().update()
        log.debug('GameOverScene update() called')

    @override
    def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key down events for the Game Over scene.

        Args:
            event (KeyEvent): The key down event.

        """
        if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE:
            # Track that spacebar is pressed (but don't act on it yet)
            self._space_pressed = True
        elif event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
            # Quit the game
            self.scene_manager.quit()
        else:
            # Let the base Scene class handle other keys (like 'q' for quit)
            super().on_key_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_key_up_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key up events for the Game Over scene.

        Args:
            event (KeyEvent): The key up event.

        """
        if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE and self._space_pressed:
            # Spacebar was pressed and now released - restart the game
            self._space_pressed = False
            self.resume()
        else:
            # Let the base Scene class handle other keys
            super().on_key_up_event(event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_down_event(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """A mapped gamepad's B or Back quits; Start or A arms the restart (gamepad_choice.py).

        Args:
            event: The controller button down event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_down(event)
        super().on_controller_button_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_controller_button_up_event(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent) -> None:
        """A mapped gamepad's Start or A, released after its press here, restarts the game.

        Args:
            event: The controller button up event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_up(event)
        super().on_controller_button_up_event(event)

    @override
    def on_joy_button_down_event(self: Self, event: JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Any other gamepad's B or Back quits; Start or A arms the restart (gamepad_choice.py).

        Args:
            event: The joystick button down event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_down(event)
        super().on_joy_button_down_event(event)

    @override
    def on_joy_button_up_event(self: Self, event: JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Any other gamepad's Start or A, released after its press here, restarts the game.

        Args:
            event: The joystick button up event.

        """
        self._on_gamepad_button_up(event)
        super().on_joy_button_up_event(event)

    def _on_gamepad_button_down(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent | JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Quit for B or Back, as ESC does (BUGS.md #209 item 10: no gamepad could).

        Args:
            event: The button down event, from either layer.

        """
        if self._gamepad_buttons.button_pressed(event) is GamepadChoice.QUIT:
            self.scene_manager.quit()

    def _on_gamepad_button_up(self: Self, event: ControllerButtonEvent | JoyButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Restart the game for a Start or A pressed here, as SPACE does.

        Args:
            event: The button up event, from either layer.

        """
        if self._gamepad_buttons.button_released(event) is GamepadChoice.CONTINUE:
            self.resume()

    @override
    def resume(self: Self) -> None:
        """Resume by creating a new game instance.

        Override the default resume behavior to create a fresh game
        instead of switching back to the previous scene.

        """
        # Get the game class from the previous scene
        if self.scene_manager.previous_scene:
            game_class = type(self.scene_manager.previous_scene)
            self.log.info('Restarting game with class: %s', game_class)

            # Create a new instance of the game with the same options
            new_game = game_class(options=self.options)

            # Switch to the new game instance
            self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(new_game)
        else:
            self.log.warning('No previous scene found to restart')

            sorted descending. Top 5 are displayed.

docs.title: __subclasshook__(subclass) classmethod
docs.text:
Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Returns:

Name Type Description bool bool

True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented (typeshed annotates object.subclasshook as bool and types NotImplemented as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 
@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

def camera_target(self: Self) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """The world point the engine aims the camera at this frame, or None (manual camera).

    Override to aim the camera anywhere (a point between two players, a cutscene focus).
    The default returns the camera's follow target position (Camera2D.follow()). The
    engine applies the camera's follow axes to whatever point this returns.

    Returns:
        tuple[float, float] | None: The target's (world_x, world_y), or None when the
            camera follows nothing.

    """
    target = self.camera.follow_target
    if target is None:
        return None
    # Camera2D.follow() checked that the target has world_x and world_y
    return (float(target.world_x), float(target.world_y))

def forget_key_presses(self: Self) -> None:

def game_over(self: Self) -> None:
    """Handle game over for the current scene.

    Default implementation switches to a GameOverScene.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom game over behavior.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.game_over_scene import GameOverScene

@override
def on_fps_event(self: Self, event: events.FpsEvent) -> None:
    """Handle FPS events.

    Args:
        event (FpsEvent): The event to handle.

    """
    # FPSEVENT is pygame.USEREVENT + 1
    # Log FPS at the specified interval to reduce log spam. The frame clock starts at 0, so
    # the first log waits one full interval of play
    current_time = clock.frame_clock_seconds()

    # Use the configured log interval instead of hardcoded 1.0 second
    log_interval_seconds = float(self.scene_manager.fps_log_interval_ms) / 1000.0
    if current_time - self._last_fps_log_time >= log_interval_seconds:
        event_fps: float = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)
        self.log.info('Scene "%s" (%s) FPS: %s', self.NAME, type(self), event_fps)
        self._last_fps_log_time = current_time

    self.fps = getattr(event, 'fps', 0.0)

@override
def on_key_down_event(self: Self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
    """Handle key down events for the Game Over scene.

    Args:
        event (KeyEvent): The key down event.

    """
    if event.key == pygame.K_SPACE:
        # Track that spacebar is pressed (but don't act on it yet)
        self._space_pressed = True
    elif event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
        # Quit the game
        self.scene_manager.quit()
    else:
        # Let the base Scene class handle other keys (like 'q' for quit)
        super().on_key_down_event(event)

    self.log.debug('=== Scene: Left Mouse Button Down ===')

    # Get sprites at click position
    collided_sprites = self._get_collided_sprites(event_pos)
    self.log.debug('Collided sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in collided_sprites])
    focusable_sprites = self._get_focusable_sprites(collided_sprites)
    self.log.debug('Focusable sprites: %s', focusable_sprites)

    # Find currently focused sprites
    focused_sprites = self._get_focused_sprites()
    self.log.debug('Currently focused sprites: %s', [type(s).__name__ for s in focused_sprites])

    # Handle focus management
    self._handle_focus_management(collided_sprites)

    # Process the click for collided sprites
    for sprite in collided_sprites:
        if hasattr(sprite, 'on_left_mouse_button_down_event'):
            sprite.on_left_mouse_button_down_event(event)

docs.text:
Pause the current scene.

Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame. Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause() usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

Source code in src/glitchygames/scenes/scene.py 
@override
def pause(self: Self) -> None:
    """Pause the current scene.

    Default implementation requests a PauseScene for the end of this frame.
    Scenes can override this method to provide custom pause behavior.

    The switch happens after this frame renders (via next_scene), not immediately: pause()
    usually runs during event processing, after sprites have moved this frame, so an
    immediate switch would freeze the previous frame's picture one frame behind the game.

    """
    from .builtin_scenes.pause_scene import PauseScene

    self.next_scene = PauseScene(options=self.options)

    self.log.info('Scene pause requested')

def record_key_press(self: Self, *, key: int) -> None:
    """Note that a key-down reached this scene.

    SceneManager calls this for every key-down it routes to the active scene, before the
    scene's own on_key_down_event, so subclasses that override that handler are covered.
    on_key_up_event quits only on the release of a key recorded here. Games never call it;
    it is public only because the scene manager, another class, calls it.

    Args:
        key: The pygame key code.

    """
    self._keys_pressed_in_scene.add(key)

@override
def resume(self: Self) -> None:
    """Resume by creating a new game instance.

    Override the default resume behavior to create a fresh game
    instead of switching back to the previous scene.

    """
    # Get the game class from the previous scene
    if self.scene_manager.previous_scene:
        game_class = type(self.scene_manager.previous_scene)
        self.log.info('Restarting game with class: %s', game_class)

        # Create a new instance of the game with the same options
        new_game = game_class(options=self.options)

        # Switch to the new game instance
        self.scene_manager.switch_to_scene(new_game)
    else:
        self.log.warning('No previous scene found to restart')

@override
def setup(self: Self) -> None:
    """Set up the Game Over scene with score display."""
    super().setup()
    log.info('GameOverScene setup() called')

    center_x = self.screen_width // 2
    current_y = self.screen_height // 4

    # Title
    self.text_sprite = TextSprite(
        'GAME OVER',
        (center_x, current_y),
        color=(255, 0, 0),
        font_size=48,
    )
    self.all_sprites.add(self.text_sprite)
    current_y += 60

    # Final score (if provided)
    if self.final_score is not None:
        score_sprite = TextSprite(
            f'Score: {self.final_score}',
            (center_x, current_y),
            color=(255, 255, 100),
            font_size=32,
        )
        self.all_sprites.add(score_sprite)
        current_y += 50

    # High scores (top 5)
    if self.high_scores:
        header = TextSprite(
            'HIGH SCORES',
            (center_x, current_y),
            color=(200, 200, 200),
            font_size=28,
        )
        self.all_sprites.add(header)
        current_y += 35

        max_displayed = 5
        for rank, entry in enumerate(self.high_scores[:max_displayed], start=1):
            score_value = entry.get('score', 0)
            entry_sprite = TextSprite(
                f'{rank}. {score_value}',
                (center_x, current_y),
                color=(180, 180, 180),
                font_size=24,
            )
            self.all_sprites.add(entry_sprite)
            current_y += 30

    # Subtitle
    current_y += 20
    subtitle = TextSprite(
        'Press SPACE or START to restart, ESC or BACK to quit',
        (center_x, current_y),
        color=(255, 255, 255),
        font_size=24,
    )
    self.all_sprites.add(subtitle)
    log.info('GameOverScene setup() completed')

def shake(self: Self, shake: Shake, *, targets: ShakeTarget = ShakeTarget.WORLD) -> None:
    """Start a shake on the world (camera), the whole screen, or both.

    Rumble, if the shake has it, is sent automatically by the scene manager.

    Args:
        shake: The shake to start.
        targets: ShakeTarget.WORLD, ShakeTarget.SCREEN, or both combined with |.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If WORLD is requested on a scene that is not active (for example
            from a transition cue, which runs after the scene was cleaned up).

    """
    if ShakeTarget.WORLD in targets:
        if self.scene_manager.active_scene is not self:
            message = f'{self.NAME} is not the active scene; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN'
            raise RuntimeError(message)
        self.camera.shake_effect.add(shake)
        if not self._world_shake_warning_logged and not self._world_shake_moves_anything():
            LOG.warning(
                'WORLD shake on %s has no effect: no sprites are positioned through its '
                'camera; use ShakeTarget.SCREEN',
                self.NAME,
            )
            self._world_shake_warning_logged = True
    if ShakeTarget.SCREEN in targets:
        self.scene_manager.screen_shake.add(shake)

        # Create a font

        # Render the text
        text_surface = font.render(text, FontManager.antialias(), color)

        # Initialize the sprite with the text surface
        super().__init__(
            x=position[0] - text_surface.get_width() // 2,  # Center horizontally
            y=position[1] - text_surface.get_height() // 2,  # Center vertically
            width=text_surface.get_width(),
            height=text_surface.get_height(),
            **kwargs,
        )

        # Set the image to the text surface
        self.image = text_surface

docs.text:
Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Name Type Description bool bool

Source code in src/glitchygames/events/base.py 
@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

@classmethod
def break_when(cls: type[Sprite], sprite_type: object | None = None) -> None:
    """Register a breakpoint for a sprite type.

    Args:
        sprite_type (object | None): The sprite type to break on.
            None means break on any sprite.

    """
    # The current context's breakpoints: None means disabled, [] means any
    counters = sprite_counters()
    if counters.breakpoints is None:
        counters.breakpoints = []

    # If none, break always.
    if sprite_type is not None:
        # Register the type asked for (not cls): __init__ compares str(type(self)) with it
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==%s', sprite_type)
        counters.breakpoints.append(str(sprite_type))
    else:
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==<any>')

docs.title: AnimatedSprite
docs.text:
Bases: AnimatedSpriteInterface, DirtySprite

A prototype Sprite Animation class with proper dirty sprite integration.

Source code in src/glitchygames/sprites/animated.py 
class AnimatedSprite(AnimatedSpriteInterface, pygame.sprite.DirtySprite):  # ruff: ignore[too-many-public-methods]
    """A prototype Sprite Animation class with proper dirty sprite integration."""

    log = LOG

    # Override pygame's optional property typing — AnimatedSprite always has
    # a valid image and rect after __init__, so the getter return types narrow
    # out None.  Setters keep the parent's wider parameter types to satisfy LSP.

    @property
    @override
    def image(self) -> pygame.Surface:
        """The sprite image (always non-None for AnimatedSprite)."""
        return self._gg_image

    @image.setter
    def image(self, value: pygame.Surface | None) -> None:
        self._gg_image = cast('pygame.Surface', value)

    @property
    @override
    def rect(self) -> pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect:
        """The sprite rect (always non-None for AnimatedSprite)."""
        return self._gg_rect

    @rect.setter
    def rect(self, value: pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect | None) -> None:
        self._gg_rect = cast('pygame.FRect | pygame.Rect', value)

    @property
    def default_hitbox(self) -> pygame.Rect | None:
        """The sprite-level default hitbox.

        This is the hitbox defined in [sprite.hitbox] in the TOML file.
        Individual frames may override this with per-frame hitboxes.
        """
        return self._default_hitbox

    @default_hitbox.setter
    def default_hitbox(self, value: pygame.Rect | None) -> None:
        """Set the sprite-level default hitbox."""
        self._default_hitbox = value

    @property
    def scale(self) -> int:
        """The integer factor the sprite is drawn at (1 draws each TOML pixel as one pixel).

        Frame surfaces (and so image and rect), hitboxes and draw_offset are all scaled by it,
        so a game that draws a sprite larger sets this instead of scaling image itself, which
        the next frame change would undo (BUGS.md #144).
        """
        return self._scale

    @scale.setter
    def scale(self, value: int) -> None:
        """Set the draw scale and redraw the current frame at it.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If value is not a positive integer.

        """
        # type() rather than isinstance: a bool is an int, and True would mean a scale of 1
        if type(value) is not int or value < 1:
            message = f'AnimatedSprite.scale must be a positive integer, not {value!r}'
            raise ValueError(message)
        self._scale = value
        # Cached surfaces were drawn at the old scale
        self.clear_surface_cache()
        self._last_drawn_frame = None
        self._update_surface_and_mark_dirty()

    @property
    def hitbox(self) -> pygame.Rect:
        """The effective hitbox for the current frame.

        Hitboxes are in native (TOML) pixels and are multiplied by scale, offset
        and size, for sprites drawn scaled up (Papyrus draws at 2x). When hitbox_flip_x is
        True (the game draws the image mirrored, e.g. facing left) the result is mirrored
        within the drawn frame width: x = drawn_width - (x + width).

        Resolution order:
        1. Current frame's explicit hitbox (per-frame override)
        2. Sprite-level default hitbox ([sprite.hitbox])
        3. The visible pixels of the current frame's image (measured once per
           frame surface, see SpriteFrame.opaque_bounds), or the frame's full
           rect when the sprite sets TRIM_TRANSPARENT_HITBOX = False

        Always returns a valid pygame.Rect — game code never needs null checks.
        """
        current_frame = self.get_current_frame()
        if current_frame is None:
            # No frame: the sprite's own rect is already in drawn pixels, so it is not scaled
            return pygame.Rect(0, 0, self._gg_rect.width, self._gg_rect.height)
        drawn_hitbox = self._drawn_hitbox(
            self._native_frame_hitbox(current_frame), native_frame_width=current_frame.rect.width
        )
        # Anchored frames are drawn at an offset (see draw_offset); the hitbox moves with them
        draw_offset_x, draw_offset_y = self.draw_offset
        drawn_hitbox.move_ip(draw_offset_x, draw_offset_y)
        return drawn_hitbox

    def _frame_anchor_reference(self: Self) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Return the native hitbox every anchored frame is aligned to.

        The sprite-level default hitbox if there is one, else the union of all frames'
        hitboxes (so every anchor point has a well-defined reference). Asked only for one of
        the sprite's own frames (draw_offset, common_hitbox_x_range), so there is always one.

        Returns:
            pygame.Rect: The reference hitbox.

        """
        if self._default_hitbox is not None:
            return self._default_hitbox
        # Cached per frame set: frames are not changed after loading, so the union is built
        # again only when frames are added, removed or replaced. A frame whose hitbox is
        # edited in place keeps the old union (no game does that; Bitmappy does not anchor).
        current_frames = tuple(frame for frames in self._animations.values() for frame in frames)
        cached_entry = self._frame_anchor_reference_cache
        if cached_entry is None or cached_entry[0] != current_frames:
            cached_entry = (current_frames, self._union_of_frame_hitboxes(current_frames))
            self._frame_anchor_reference_cache = cached_entry
        return cached_entry[1].copy()

    def _union_of_frame_hitboxes(self: Self, frames: tuple[SpriteFrame, ...]) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Return the union of the given frames' native hitboxes.

        Returns:
            pygame.Rect: The union.

        """
        assert frames, 'the anchor reference is built only while the sprite has a frame'
        frame_hitboxes = [self._native_frame_hitbox(frame) for frame in frames]
        return frame_hitboxes[0].unionall(frame_hitboxes[1:])

    def _frame_draw_offset(self: Self, frame: SpriteFrame) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Return where a frame is drawn relative to its authored position (see draw_offset).

        Returns:
            tuple[int, int]: (x, y) offset in drawn pixels; (0, 0) for FrameAnchor.NONE.

        """
        if self.frame_anchor is FrameAnchor.NONE:
            return (0, 0)
        reference = self._frame_anchor_reference()
        frame_hitbox = self._native_frame_hitbox(frame)
        horizontal_edge, vertical_edge = _FRAME_ANCHOR_EDGES[self.frame_anchor]
        # Computed in authored (unflipped) native pixels, doubled so centres stay exact
        doubled_offset_x = _doubled_anchor_offset(
            reference_start=reference.x,
            reference_size=reference.width,
            frame_start=frame_hitbox.x,
            frame_size=frame_hitbox.width,
            edge=horizontal_edge,
        )
        doubled_offset_y = _doubled_anchor_offset(
            reference_start=reference.y,
            reference_size=reference.height,
            frame_start=frame_hitbox.y,
            frame_size=frame_hitbox.height,
            edge=vertical_edge,
        )
        drawn_offset_x = doubled_offset_x * self._scale // 2
        drawn_offset_y = doubled_offset_y * self._scale // 2
        if self.hitbox_flip_x and horizontal_edge is not None:
            # Mirrored with the image. Each frame flips within its own width, so mirror the
            # anchored point against one common axis (the widest frame): frames narrower than
            # it are moved right by the difference, which is exact for differing widths
            widest_frame_width = max(
                (other.rect.width for frames in self._animations.values() for other in frames),
                default=frame.rect.width,
            )
            drawn_offset_x = -drawn_offset_x + (widest_frame_width - frame.rect.width) * (
                self._scale
            )
        return (drawn_offset_x, drawn_offset_y)

    @property
    def draw_offset(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Where the current frame is drawn relative to its authored (top-left) position.

        With a frame_anchor other than NONE, each frame is moved so the anchor point of its
        hitbox (see FrameAnchor) lands on the same point of the reference hitbox, in drawn
        pixels (times scale; computed in authored space and, when hitbox_flip_x,
        mirrored with the image about the widest frame's width, so frames of differing widths
        stay exact). The engine adds it when placing a world-space sprite's rect
        (glitchygames.world.screen_position_for); a screen-space game adds it itself. hitbox
        includes it, so collisions match the drawing. NONE (the default) is (0, 0).

        Returns:
            tuple[int, int]: (x, y) offset in drawn pixels.

        """
        current_frame = self.get_current_frame()
        if current_frame is None:
            return (0, 0)
        return self._frame_draw_offset(current_frame)

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_frame_anchor(frame_anchor_name: str | None) -> FrameAnchor:
        """Parse the optional [sprite] frame_anchor TOML value.

        Returns:
            FrameAnchor: The anchor; NONE when the key is absent.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the value names no FrameAnchor.

        """
        if frame_anchor_name is None:
            return FrameAnchor.NONE
        try:
            return FrameAnchor(frame_anchor_name)
        except ValueError:
            valid_names = ', '.join(repr(anchor.value) for anchor in FrameAnchor)
            msg = f'[sprite] frame_anchor must be one of {valid_names}, got {frame_anchor_name!r}'
            raise ValueError(msg) from None

    def common_hitbox_x_range(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Return the horizontal hitbox span shared by every animation frame.

        The intersection of all frames' hitbox x-ranges (drawn pixels, after scale and
        hitbox_flip_x), relative to the sprite's position. Unlike ``hitbox`` it does not
        change from frame to frame, so games use it for support (standing on ledges and wall
        tops): a wider falling frame then cannot catch a player that just walked off an edge
        with a narrower idle frame, which would make it land, fall and land again forever.

        Returns:
            tuple[int, int]: (left, right) offsets; right is exclusive. Without frames, or if
            the frames share no column, the current hitbox's x-range.

        """
        common_left: int | None = None
        common_right: int | None = None
        for frames in self._animations.values():
            for frame in frames:
                frame_hitbox = self._drawn_hitbox(
                    self._native_frame_hitbox(frame), native_frame_width=frame.rect.width
                )
                frame_hitbox.move_ip(self._frame_draw_offset(frame))
                common_left = (
                    frame_hitbox.left
                    if common_left is None
                    else max(common_left, frame_hitbox.left)
                )
                common_right = (
                    frame_hitbox.right
                    if common_right is None
                    else min(common_right, frame_hitbox.right)
                )
        if common_left is None or common_right is None or common_left >= common_right:
            current_hitbox = self.hitbox
            return (current_hitbox.left, current_hitbox.right)
        return (common_left, common_right)

    def _native_frame_hitbox(self: Self, frame: SpriteFrame) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Return a frame's hitbox in native, unflipped pixels (resolution order of hitbox).

        The visible-pixel fallback is measured on the unflipped frame image; hitbox_flip_x
        mirrors it (and the TOML hitboxes) afterwards in _drawn_hitbox.

        Returns:
            pygame.Rect: The native hitbox (may be the frame's or the sprite's own rect).

        """
        if frame.has_explicit_hitbox:
            return frame.hitbox
        if self._default_hitbox is not None:
            return self._default_hitbox
        if trims_transparent_hitbox(self):
            return frame.opaque_bounds()
        return frame.rect

    def _drawn_hitbox(
        self: Self, native_hitbox: pygame.Rect, *, native_frame_width: int
    ) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Return a new rect: a native hitbox scaled by scale, mirrored if flipped.

        Args:
            native_hitbox: The hitbox in native frame pixels.
            native_frame_width: The frame's width in native pixels (the mirror span).

        Returns:
            pygame.Rect: The hitbox in drawn pixels (never the caller's rect object).

        """
        drawn_x = native_hitbox.x * self._scale
        drawn_width = native_hitbox.width * self._scale
        if self.hitbox_flip_x:
            drawn_x = native_frame_width * self._scale - (drawn_x + drawn_width)
        return pygame.Rect(
            drawn_x,
            native_hitbox.y * self._scale,
            drawn_width,
            native_hitbox.height * self._scale,
        )

    def get_hitbox_world_rect(
        self: Self,
        world_x: float,
        world_y: float,
    ) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Return the hitbox positioned in world coordinates.

        Args:
            world_x: The sprite's world X position.
            world_y: The sprite's world Y position.

        Returns:
            A pygame.Rect with the hitbox offset applied to the world position.
        """
        current_hitbox = self.hitbox
        return pygame.Rect(
            round(world_x) + current_hitbox.x,
            round(world_y) + current_hitbox.y,
            current_hitbox.width,
            current_hitbox.height,
        )

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        filename: str | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the Sprite Animation prototype."""
        super().__init__()

        # Initialize pygame.sprite.DirtySprite
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()
        pygame.sprite.DirtySprite.__init__(self, groups)

        # Animation state
        self.name = 'animated_sprite'  # Default name
        self.description = ''  # Description field for metadata
        # What kind of thing the sprite is ([sprite] tags; sprites/tags.py), in order
        self.tags: list[str] = []
        self._animations: dict[str, list[SpriteFrame]] = {}
        # Each animation's [[animation]] frame_interval and loop as loaded, so a save writes
        # them back (frames without a per-frame override use the animation's frame_interval).
        # set_animation applies the animation's loop flag to is_looping; the animation state
        # machine reads _loop_flags too
        self._animation_frame_intervals: dict[str, float] = {}
        self._loop_flags: dict[str, bool] = {}
        # The [[transition]] tables as loaded (keys and values verbatim, in file order), so a
        # save writes the animation state machine back; transitions games add in code are not
        # part of it
        self.transition_data: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        # What the last load had to repair in its pixel rows, one entry per repair, each
        # '<label>: <repair>' (label 'sprite', '<namespace> frame <frame_index>' or 'palette');
        # see normalize_pixel_rows. Bitmappy shows a notice when it isn't empty
        self.pixel_row_repairs: list[str] = []
        # Names the source in the repair warnings: the file being loaded
        self._pixel_rows_source = '<data>'
        self._is_playing: bool = False
        self._is_looping: bool = False
        self._frame_timer: float = 0.0
        self._color_map: dict[str, tuple[int, ...]] = {}
        # The animations' order as loaded from a file; None for a sprite never loaded, whose
        # animation_order is its animations' insertion order
        self._animation_order: list[str] | None = None
        # The color glyphs in their file order, so a save keeps the file's layout; None for a
        # sprite never loaded (a save then orders them itself)
        self._color_order: list[str] | None = None
        # The glyphs whose colors had per-pixel alpha (0-254) in the loaded file, and that alpha
        self._colors_with_per_pixel_alpha: dict[str, int] = {}

        # Initialize frame manager as the single source of truth
        self.frame_manager = FrameManager(self)

        # Dirty sprite properties
        self.dirty = 1  # Start dirty to ensure initial render
        # The (animation, frame index) the image was last drawn from; None forces a redraw.
        # Both parts matter: an animation change resets the frame index to 0, so comparing
        # the index alone would keep the old animation's frame 0 image
        self._last_drawn_frame: tuple[str, int] | None = None
        self._surface_cache: dict[str, pygame.Surface] = {}

        # Initialize with default surface
        self._gg_image = pygame.Surface((32, 32))
        self._gg_rect = pygame.Rect(0, 0, 32, 32)

        # Sprite-level default hitbox (loaded from [sprite.hitbox] in TOML)
        self._default_hitbox: pygame.Rect | None = None

        # Integer multiplier from native TOML pixels to drawn pixels (see the scale property):
        # frame surfaces, rect, hitboxes and draw_offset all follow it
        self._scale: int = 1
        # True while the game draws this sprite mirrored horizontally (see hitbox)
        self.hitbox_flip_x: bool = False
        # How frames of different shapes line up when drawn (see draw_offset); NONE draws
        # each frame as authored. When set, rect must include draw_offset: the engine adds it
        # for world sprites, a game placing rect itself must (see FrameAnchor's contract)
        self.frame_anchor: FrameAnchor = FrameAnchor.NONE
        # (frames it was built from, union of their hitboxes); see _frame_anchor_reference
        self._frame_anchor_reference_cache: tuple[tuple[SpriteFrame, ...], pygame.Rect] | None = (
            None
        )

        if filename:
