class MultiLineTextBox(BitmappySprite):
    """A multi-line text box sprite class."""

    log = LOG

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        x: int,
        y: int,
        width: int,
        height: int,
        *,
        name: str | None = None,
        text: str = '',
        parent: TextSubmitProtocol | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a MultiLineTextBox."""
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        self.log.debug(
            'Creating MultiLineTextBox: name=%s, pos=(%s, %s), size=(%s, %s)',
            name,
            x,
            y,
            width,
            height,
        )

        super().__init__(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            name=name,
            parent=parent,
            groups=groups,
            focusable=True,
        )

        # Store original text for cursor position mapping first
        self._original_text = text
        self._text = text
        self.text = text
        self.is_active = False
        self.cursor_visible = True
        self.cursor_blink_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
        self.cursor_blink_rate = 530
        self.cursor_pos = len(text)
        self._last_update_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
        self._frame_count = 0

        # Initialize selection attributes
        self.selection_start = None
        self.selection_end = None

        # Initialize hover tracking
        self.is_hovered = False

        # Force continuous updates
        self.dirty = 2

        self.image = pygame.Surface((width, height), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        self.image = self.image.convert_alpha()

        # Use FontManager for consistent font handling
        self.font: GameFont = FontManager.get_font()
        self.text_color: tuple[int, ...] = WHITE
        self.cursor_color: tuple[int, ...] = WHITE
        self.base_text_color: tuple[int, ...] = WHITE  # Store base color for hover effects

        # Add scroll tracking
        self.scroll_offset: int = 0
        # Calculate line height - handle both pygame.font and pygame.freetype
        if hasattr(self.font, 'get_linesize'):
            line_height: int = self.font.get_linesize()
        else:
            # For freetype fonts, use the size attribute (it's a float, not a tuple)
            line_height = int(getattr(self.font, 'size', 24))
        # Account for top/bottom padding (5px each = 10px total)
        self.visible_lines: int = int((self.height - 10) // line_height)

        # Create scrollbar component
        scrollbar_width = 8
        self.scrollbar = Scrollbar(
            x=self.width - scrollbar_width - 2,
            y=2,
            width=scrollbar_width,
            height=self.height - 4,
            total_items=1,  # Will be updated when text is set
            visible_items=self.visible_lines,
            scroll_offset=0,
        )

    def _character_advances(self, text: str) -> list[int]:
        """Return how far each character of the text moves the pen (its advance), in pixels.

        A character the font has no glyph for advances 0.

        Returns:
            list[int]: One advance per character.

        """
        # Each character's metrics hold its horizontal advance at index 4, for pygame.freetype
        # (get_metrics) and pygame.font (metrics) alike; a character with no glyph has None
        if hasattr(self.font, 'get_metrics'):
            metrics = self.font.get_metrics(text)
        else:
            metrics = self.font.metrics(text)
        return [
            int(character_metrics[ADVANCE_METRIC_INDEX]) if character_metrics else 0
            for character_metrics in metrics
        ]

    def _left_bearing(self, text: str) -> int:
        """Return how far right of the pen the text's first ink column is, in pixels.

        A pygame.freetype render starts at the first ink column, so the characters' advances are
        measured from the pen position that many pixels to the left; a pygame.font render
        includes the bearing, so it is 0.

        Returns:
            int: The left bearing (0 for empty text or a pygame.font font).

        """
        if not text or not hasattr(self.font, 'get_metrics'):
            return 0
        return int(self.font.get_rect(text).x)

    def _get_text_width(self, text: str) -> int:
        """Get text width for both pygame.font and pygame.freetype fonts.

        Returns:
            int: The text width.

        """
        if hasattr(self.font, 'get_rect'):
            # pygame.freetype.Font - use get_rect() method
            return self.font.get_rect(text).width
        # pygame.font.Font - size() is a method
        return self.font.size(text)[0]

    def _wrap_text(self, text: str, max_width: float) -> str:
        """Wrap text to fit within the specified width.

        Returns:
            str: The resulting string.

        """
        if not text:
            return text

        lines: list[str] = text.split('\n')
        wrapped_lines: list[str] = []

        for line in lines:
            if not line:  # Empty line
                wrapped_lines.append('')
                continue

            # If line already fits, keep it as is
            if self._get_text_width(line) <= max_width:
                wrapped_lines.append(line)
                continue

            # Split line into words and wrap
            words = line.split(' ')
            current_line = ''

            for word in words:
                test_line = current_line + (' ' if current_line else '') + word
                if self._get_text_width(test_line) <= max_width:
                    current_line = test_line
                elif current_line:
                    # Current line is full, start a new one
                    wrapped_lines.append(current_line)
                    current_line = word
                else:
                    # Single word is too long, force it on its own line
                    wrapped_lines.append(word)
                    current_line = ''

            # Add the last line if there's content
            if current_line:
                wrapped_lines.append(current_line)

        return '\n'.join(wrapped_lines)

    def _map_cursor_pos_to_wrapped_text(self, original_pos: int) -> int:
        """Map cursor position from original text to wrapped text position.

        Returns:
            int: The resulting integer value.

        """
        if original_pos >= len(self._original_text):
            return len(self._text)

        # _wrap_text only turns a space into a newline (a wrap) or drops a space (one that
        # would start a line), so walk both texts together: each original character either
        # lines up with the next wrapped character or was a dropped space. Counting the
        # occurrences of the character under the cursor instead lost track of the spaces that
        # became newlines (BUGS.md #163)
        wrapped_index = 0
        for original_index in range(original_pos):
            if wrapped_index >= len(self._text):
                break
            original_char = self._original_text[original_index]
            wrapped_char = self._text[wrapped_index]
            if original_char == wrapped_char or (original_char == ' ' and wrapped_char == '\n'):
                wrapped_index += 1
        return wrapped_index

    def _get_cursor_line_and_column_in_wrapped_text(
        self,
        original_cursor_pos: int,
    ) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Get the line and column of the cursor in the wrapped text.

        Returns:
            tuple[int, int]: The cursor line and column in wrapped text.

        """
        # Map cursor position to wrapped text
        wrapped_cursor_pos = self._map_cursor_pos_to_wrapped_text(original_cursor_pos)

        # Count lines before cursor in wrapped text
        lines_before_cursor = self._text[:wrapped_cursor_pos].count('\n')

        # Find the start of the current line in wrapped text
        current_line_start = (
            self._text[:wrapped_cursor_pos].rindex('\n') + 1
            if '\n' in self._text[:wrapped_cursor_pos]
            else 0
        )

        # Calculate column position
        column_pos = wrapped_cursor_pos - current_line_start

        return lines_before_cursor, column_pos

    def _move_cursor_up(self) -> None:
        """Move cursor up one line in the wrapped text."""
        current_line, current_column = self._get_cursor_line_and_column_in_wrapped_text(
            self.cursor_pos,
        )

        if current_line > 0:
            # Move to the previous line
            wrapped_lines = self._text.split('\n')
            prev_line = wrapped_lines[current_line - 1]

            # Try to maintain the same column position, but don't exceed the line length
            target_column = min(current_column, len(prev_line))

            # Calculate the new cursor position in the original text
            new_cursor_pos = self._map_wrapped_position_to_original(current_line - 1, target_column)
            self.cursor_pos = new_cursor_pos
        else:
            # Already at the top line, move to the beginning
            self.cursor_pos = 0

    def _move_cursor_down(self) -> None:
        """Move cursor down one line in the wrapped text."""
        current_line, current_column = self._get_cursor_line_and_column_in_wrapped_text(
            self.cursor_pos,
        )

        wrapped_lines = self._text.split('\n')
        if current_line < len(wrapped_lines) - 1:
            # Move to the next line
            next_line = wrapped_lines[current_line + 1]

            # Try to maintain the same column position, but don't exceed the line length
            target_column = min(current_column, len(next_line))

            # Calculate the new cursor position in the original text
            new_cursor_pos = self._map_wrapped_position_to_original(current_line + 1, target_column)
            self.cursor_pos = new_cursor_pos
        else:
            # Already at the bottom line, move to the end
            self.cursor_pos = len(self._original_text)

    def _map_wrapped_position_to_original(self, line: int, column: int) -> int:
        """Map a position in wrapped text (line, column) back to original text position.

        Returns:
            int: The resulting integer value.

        """
        wrapped_lines = self._text.split('\n')

        if line >= len(wrapped_lines):
            return len(self._original_text)

        # Get the text up to the target position in wrapped text
        target_wrapped_pos = sum(len(wrapped_lines[i]) + 1 for i in range(line)) + column
        target_wrapped_pos = min(target_wrapped_pos, len(self._text))

        # Walk both texts together, as _map_cursor_pos_to_wrapped_text does: each original
        # character lines up with the next wrapped one (a space with a newline where it wrapped)
        # or is a space wrapping dropped. Returning the wrapped position unchanged was off by
        # every space dropped before it. A dropped space at the target is skipped, so the cursor
        # lands before the character shown there, not before the invisible space
        wrapped_index = 0
        for original_index, original_char in enumerate(self._original_text):
            wrapped_char = self._text[wrapped_index] if wrapped_index < len(self._text) else ''
            lines_up = original_char == wrapped_char or (
                original_char == ' ' and wrapped_char == '\n'
            )
            if not lines_up:
                continue  # A space wrapping dropped
            if wrapped_index >= target_wrapped_pos:
                return original_index
            wrapped_index += 1

        # If we've gone through the whole text, return the end position
        return len(self._original_text)

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """The text content."""
        return self._text

    @text.setter
    def text(self, value: str) -> None:
        """Set the text content with automatic wrapping and auto-scroll to bottom."""
        if value != self._original_text:
            # Store the original text before wrapping
            self._original_text = str(value)
            # Calculate available width for text (accounting for padding)
            available_width = self.width - 10  # 5px padding on each side
            wrapped_text = self._wrap_text(str(value), available_width)
            self._text = wrapped_text

            # Move cursor to end of ORIGINAL text for auto-scroll to work
            self.cursor_pos = len(self._original_text)

            # Auto-scroll to bottom to show latest content
            total_lines = len(self._text.split('\n'))
            if total_lines > self.visible_lines:
                self.scroll_offset = total_lines - self.visible_lines
            else:
                self.scroll_offset = 0

            # Update scrollbar state
            self.scrollbar.update(total_lines, self.visible_lines, self.scroll_offset)

            self.dirty = 2

    def _get_line_height(self) -> int:
        """Get the line height for the current font.

        Returns:
            Line height in pixels.

        """
        if hasattr(self.font, 'get_linesize'):
            return self.font.get_linesize()
        # For freetype fonts, use the size attribute (it's a float, not a tuple)
        return int(self.font.size) if hasattr(self.font, 'size') else 24  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    def _get_border_color(self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
        """Get the border color based on active/hover state.

        Returns:
            RGB color tuple.

        """
        if self.is_active:
            return (64, 64, 255)
        if self.is_hovered:
            return (100, 150, 255)
        return WHITE

    def _render_visible_lines(self, text_color: tuple[int, ...], line_height: int) -> None:
        """Render visible text lines with scrolling."""
        if not self._text:
            return

        lines = self._text.split('\n')

        # Only auto-scroll to keep cursor visible when the textbox is active (being edited)
        if self.is_active:
            cursor_line, _ = self._get_cursor_line_and_column_in_wrapped_text(self.cursor_pos)
            if cursor_line - self.scroll_offset >= self.visible_lines:
                self.scroll_offset = cursor_line - self.visible_lines + 1
                self.scrollbar.scroll_offset = self.scroll_offset
            elif cursor_line < self.scroll_offset:
                self.scroll_offset = cursor_line
                self.scrollbar.scroll_offset = self.scroll_offset

        start_idx = int(self.scroll_offset)
        end_idx = int(self.scroll_offset + self.visible_lines)
        visible_lines = lines[start_idx:end_idx]

        y_offset = 5
        for line in visible_lines:
            if line:  # Only render non-empty lines
                if hasattr(self.font, 'get_rect'):
                    render_result = self.font.render(line, text_color)
                    if isinstance(render_result, tuple):
                        text_surface = render_result[0]
                    else:  # pragma: no cover - a freetype font's render returns (surface, rect)
                        text_surface = render_result
                else:
                    font_result = self.font.render(line, FontManager.antialias(), text_color)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                    text_surface = font_result[0] if isinstance(font_result, tuple) else font_result
                self.image.blit(text_surface, (5, y_offset))
            y_offset += line_height

    def _update_cursor_blink(self, current_time: int, line_height: int) -> None:
        """Handle cursor blinking and drawing."""
        if not self.is_active:
            return

        time_since_blink = current_time - self.cursor_blink_time
        if time_since_blink >= self.cursor_blink_rate:
            self.cursor_visible = not self.cursor_visible
            self.cursor_blink_time = current_time

        if not self.cursor_visible:
            return

        lines_before_cursor, column_pos = self._get_cursor_line_and_column_in_wrapped_text(
            self.cursor_pos,
        )

        # Only draw cursor if it's in the visible range
        if not (
            self.scroll_offset <= lines_before_cursor < self.scroll_offset + self.visible_lines
        ):
            return

        # Get the current line text in wrapped text
        # lines_before_cursor counts the newlines before the cursor, so the line exists
        wrapped_lines = self._text.split('\n')
        current_line_text = wrapped_lines[lines_before_cursor]
        text_up_to_cursor = current_line_text[:column_pos]
        text_width = self._get_text_width(text_up_to_cursor)

        cursor_x = text_width + 5
        cursor_y = 5 + ((lines_before_cursor - self.scroll_offset) * line_height)

        pygame.draw.line(
            self.image,
            self.cursor_color,
            (cursor_x, cursor_y),
            (cursor_x, cursor_y + 20),
            2,
        )

    @override
    def update(self) -> None:
        """Update the multi-line text box."""
        self._frame_count += 1
        current_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
        line_height = self._get_line_height()

        # update() runs every frame (dirty = 2), so skip the whole frame dump unless it is logged
        if self.log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
            time_since_last_update = current_time - self._last_update_time
            self.log.debug('\n--- Frame %s ---', self._frame_count)
            self.log.debug('Update called after %sms', time_since_last_update)
            self.log.debug(
                'State: active=%s, cursor_visible=%s', self.is_active, self.cursor_visible
            )
            self.log.debug('Dirty flag: %s', self.dirty)

        self._last_update_time = current_time

        # Clear background
        self.image.fill((32, 32, 32, 200))

        # Draw border
        border_color = self._get_border_color()
        pygame.draw.rect(self.image, border_color, (0, 0, self.width, self.height), 1)

        # Set text color based on hover state
        if self.is_hovered and not self.is_active:
            current_text_color = (150, 200, 255)
        else:
            current_text_color = self.base_text_color

        self._render_visible_lines(current_text_color, line_height)
        self._update_cursor_blink(current_time, line_height)

        # Update and draw scrollbar
        if self._text:
            total_lines = len(self._text.split('\n'))
            self.scrollbar.update(total_lines, self.visible_lines, self.scroll_offset)
            self.scrollbar.draw(self.image)

        # Force continuous updates
        self.dirty = 2

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button down events."""
        self.log.debug('\n--- Mouse Event ---')
        self.log.debug('Mouse down at %s', event.pos)
        self.log.debug('Current rect: %s', self.rect)
        self.log.debug(
            'Current state: active=%s, cursor_visible=%s', self.is_active, self.cursor_visible
        )

        # Convert absolute mouse position to widget-relative coordinates
        if self.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
            relative_pos = (int(event.pos[0] - self.rect.x), int(event.pos[1] - self.rect.y))

            # Check if scrollbar handled the event
            if self.scrollbar.handle_mouse_down(relative_pos):
                # Immediately sync scroll offset from scrollbar
                self.scroll_offset = int(self.scrollbar.scroll_offset)
                self.dirty = 2
                return

        if self.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
            self.is_active = True
            self.cursor_visible = True
            self.cursor_blink_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
            pygame.key.start_text_input()
            # Enable key repeat for backspace
            pygame.key.set_repeat(500, 50)  # 500ms delay, 50ms interval

            # Calculate cursor position based on wrapped text, then map to original
            x_rel = int(event.pos[0] - self.rect.x) - 5
            y_rel = int(event.pos[1] - self.rect.y) - 5

            # Get line height (a freetype font's size is a float: the helper rounds it; this
            # used the size unrounded)
            line_height = self._get_line_height()

            # Determine which line was clicked
            clicked_line = max(0, int(y_rel // line_height))

            # Get the wrapped lines
            wrapped_lines = self._text.split('\n')
            if clicked_line >= len(wrapped_lines):
                clicked_line = len(wrapped_lines) - 1

            # Find the character position within the clicked line: walk the characters by their
            # advances (where the next one starts), not their ink widths, which fall behind the
            # drawn text by a pixel or two per character (BUGS.md #165)
            clicked_line_text = wrapped_lines[clicked_line]
            character_left = -self._left_bearing(clicked_line_text)
            char_pos_in_line = len(clicked_line_text)

            for i, advance in enumerate(self._character_advances(clicked_line_text)):
                # A click on a character's middle or left of it goes before the character
                if character_left + (advance / 2) >= x_rel:
                    char_pos_in_line = i
                    break
                character_left += advance

            # Map the wrapped position back to original text position
            self.cursor_pos = self._map_wrapped_position_to_original(clicked_line, char_pos_in_line)

            self.log.debug('Activated: cursor_pos=%s', self.cursor_pos)
            self.log.debug('Text input started')
            self.dirty = 2
        else:
            self.is_active = False
            pygame.key.stop_text_input()
            # Disable key repeat when inactive
            pygame.key.set_repeat()  # Calling with no args disables repeat
            self.log.debug('Deactivated, text input stopped')

    @override
    def on_key_down_event(self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle key down events."""
        if not self.is_active:
            return

        # Handle Escape key to deactivate
        if event.key == pygame.K_ESCAPE:
            self.is_active = False
            pygame.key.stop_text_input()
            pygame.key.set_repeat()  # Disable key repeat
            self.log.debug('Deactivated by Escape key')
            self.dirty = 2
            return

        modifiers = current_input().modifiers
        is_ctrl = bool(modifiers & pygame.KMOD_CTRL) or bool(modifiers & pygame.KMOD_META)

        # Handle Ctrl+D (or Cmd+D) to clear contents
        if event.key == pygame.K_d and is_ctrl:
            self.text = ''
            self._text = ''
            self.cursor_pos = 0
            self.selection_start = None
            self.selection_end = None
            self.dirty = 2
            self.log.debug('Cleared text contents with Ctrl+D')
            return

        is_shift = bool(modifiers & pygame.KMOD_SHIFT)

        # Handle Ctrl+Enter for submission
        if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN and is_ctrl:
            self._handle_ctrl_enter_submit()
            return

        # Handle selection with shift+arrow keys
        if event.key in {pygame.K_LEFT, pygame.K_RIGHT} and is_shift:
            self._handle_shift_arrow(event)
            return

        # Clear selection on non-shift arrow keys
        if event.key in {pygame.K_LEFT, pygame.K_RIGHT}:
            self.selection_start = None
            self.selection_end = None

        # Handle clipboard operations or delete with selection
        clipboard_handled = self._handle_clipboard_operation(event, is_ctrl=is_ctrl)
        if clipboard_handled or self._handle_delete_selection(event):
            return

        # Handle regular key events
        self._handle_regular_key(event)

        self.cursor_visible = True
        self.cursor_blink_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
        self.dirty = 1

    def _handle_ctrl_enter_submit(self) -> None:
        """Handle Ctrl+Enter to submit text."""
        if self.parent and hasattr(self.parent, 'on_text_submit_event'):
            self.parent.on_text_submit_event(self._text)
            self.is_active = False
            pygame.key.stop_text_input()
            pygame.key.set_repeat()  # Disable key repeat
            self.log.debug('Deactivated after submission')

    def _handle_shift_arrow(self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle shift+arrow key for text selection."""
        if self.selection_start is None:
            self.selection_start = self.cursor_pos

        if event.key == pygame.K_LEFT:
            self.cursor_pos = max(0, self.cursor_pos - 1)
        else:
            self.cursor_pos = min(len(self._original_text), self.cursor_pos + 1)
        self.selection_end = self.cursor_pos

    def _handle_clipboard_operation(self, event: KeyEvent, *, is_ctrl: bool) -> bool:
        """Handle copy, paste, cut, and select-all operations.

        Returns:
            True if a clipboard operation was handled (caller should return).

        """
        if not is_ctrl:
            return False

        if event.key == pygame.K_c and self._text:
            self._handle_copy()
            return True
        if event.key == pygame.K_v:
            self._handle_paste()
            return True
        if event.key == pygame.K_x and self._original_text:
            self._handle_cut()
            return True
        if event.key == pygame.K_a:
            self.selection_start = 0
            self.selection_end = len(self._original_text)
            self.cursor_pos = len(self._original_text)
            return True
        return False

    def _handle_copy(self) -> None:
        """Handle copy operation."""
        if self.selection_start is not None and self.selection_end is not None:
            start = min(self.selection_start, self.selection_end)
            end = max(self.selection_start, self.selection_end)
            copied_text = self._text[start:end]
        else:
            copied_text = self._text
        try:
            system_clipboard().copy(copied_text)
        except ClipboardUnavailableError:
            self.log.error('Error copying text')  # ruff: ignore[error-instead-of-exception]

    def _handle_paste(self) -> None:
        """Handle paste operation."""
        try:
            clipboard_text = system_clipboard().paste()
        except ClipboardUnavailableError:
            self.log.error('Error pasting text')  # ruff: ignore[error-instead-of-exception]
            return
        if clipboard_text:
            before_cursor = self._original_text[: self.cursor_pos]
            after_cursor = self._original_text[self.cursor_pos :]
            self.text = before_cursor + clipboard_text + after_cursor
            # The text setter moves the cursor to the end, so place it after the pasted text
            # from the position before the paste, not from where the setter left it
            # (BUGS.md #165)
            self.cursor_pos = len(before_cursor) + len(clipboard_text)

    def _handle_cut(self) -> None:
        """Handle cut operation: the selection, or all the text when nothing is selected."""
        if self.selection_start is not None and self.selection_end is not None:
            start = min(self.selection_start, self.selection_end)
            end = max(self.selection_start, self.selection_end)
        else:
            start, end = 0, len(self._original_text)
        try:
            system_clipboard().copy(self._original_text[start:end])
        except ClipboardUnavailableError:
            self.log.error('Error cutting text')  # ruff: ignore[error-instead-of-exception]
            return
        self.text = self._original_text[:start] + self._original_text[end:]
        self.cursor_pos = start
        self.selection_start = None
        self.selection_end = None

    def _handle_delete_selection(self, event: KeyEvent) -> bool:
        """Handle delete key with active selection.

        Returns:
            True if the delete was handled.

        """
        if event.key != pygame.K_DELETE:
            return False
        if self.selection_start is None or self.selection_end is None:
            return False
        start = min(self.selection_start, self.selection_end)
        end = max(self.selection_start, self.selection_end)
        self.text = self._original_text[:start] + self._original_text[end:]
        self.cursor_pos = start
        self.selection_start = None
        self.selection_end = None
        return True

    def _handle_regular_key(self, event: KeyEvent) -> None:
        """Handle regular key events (navigation, text input, backspace, delete)."""
        # Note: self.text setter moves cursor to end, so we save intended position first
        if event.key == pygame.K_RETURN:
            self._handle_return_key()
        elif event.key == pygame.K_BACKSPACE:
            self._handle_backspace_key()
        elif event.key == pygame.K_DELETE:
            self._handle_delete_key()
        elif event.key == pygame.K_LEFT:
            self.cursor_pos = max(0, self.cursor_pos - 1)
        elif event.key == pygame.K_RIGHT:
            self.cursor_pos = min(len(self._original_text), self.cursor_pos + 1)
        elif event.key == pygame.K_UP:
            self._move_cursor_up()
        elif event.key == pygame.K_DOWN:
            self._move_cursor_down()
        elif event.unicode and event.unicode >= ' ':
            self._handle_text_insert(event.unicode)

    def _handle_return_key(self) -> None:
        """Insert a newline at the current cursor position."""
        new_cursor_pos = self.cursor_pos + 1
        before_cursor = self._original_text[: self.cursor_pos]
        after_cursor = self._original_text[self.cursor_pos :]
        self.text = before_cursor + '\n' + after_cursor
        self.cursor_pos = new_cursor_pos

    def _handle_backspace_key(self) -> None:
        """Delete the character before the cursor."""
        if self.cursor_pos > 0:
            new_cursor_pos = self.cursor_pos - 1
            self.text = (
                self._original_text[: self.cursor_pos - 1] + self._original_text[self.cursor_pos :]
            )
            self.cursor_pos = new_cursor_pos

    def _handle_delete_key(self) -> None:
        """Delete the character at the cursor position."""
        if self.cursor_pos < len(self._original_text):
            new_cursor_pos = self.cursor_pos
            self.text = (
                self._original_text[: self.cursor_pos] + self._original_text[self.cursor_pos + 1 :]
            )
            self.cursor_pos = new_cursor_pos

    def _handle_text_insert(self, character: str) -> None:
        """Insert a character at the current cursor position.

        Args:
            character: The character to insert.

        """
        new_cursor_pos = self.cursor_pos + 1
        before_cursor = self._original_text[: self.cursor_pos]
        after_cursor = self._original_text[self.cursor_pos :]
        self.text = before_cursor + character + after_cursor
        self.cursor_pos = new_cursor_pos

    def on_mouse_up_event(self, event: HashableEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse up events to activate text input."""
        if self.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
            self.activate()
        else:
            self.deactivate()

    def activate(self) -> None:
        """Activate the text box for input."""
        self.is_active = True
        pygame.key.start_text_input()
        pygame.key.set_repeat(200)  # Enable key repeat
        self.log.debug('MultiLineTextBox activated')

    def deactivate(self) -> None:
        """Deactivate the text box."""
        self.is_active = False
        pygame.key.stop_text_input()
        pygame.key.set_repeat()  # Disable key repeat
        self.log.debug('MultiLineTextBox deactivated')

    @override
    def on_mouse_motion_event(self, event: MouseMotionEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse motion events for hover effects and scrollbar."""
        # Convert absolute mouse position to widget-relative coordinates
        relative_pos = (int(event.pos[0] - self.rect.x), int(event.pos[1] - self.rect.y))

        # Check if scrollbar handled the event
        if self.scrollbar.handle_mouse_motion(relative_pos):
            # Sync scroll offset from scrollbar
            self.scroll_offset = int(self.scrollbar.scroll_offset)
            self.dirty = 2
            return

        if self.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
            # Mouse is over the textbox - set hover state
            if not self.is_hovered:
                self.is_hovered = True
                self.dirty = 1  # Mark for redraw to show hover effects
        # Mouse is outside the textbox - clear hover state
        elif self.is_hovered:
            self.is_hovered = False
            self.dirty = 1  # Mark for redraw to remove hover effects

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_up_event(self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button up events."""
        # Convert absolute mouse position to widget-relative coordinates
        relative_pos = (int(event.pos[0] - self.rect.x), int(event.pos[1] - self.rect.y))

        # Check if scrollbar handled the event
        if self.scrollbar.handle_mouse_up(relative_pos):
            # Sync scroll offset from scrollbar
            self.scroll_offset = int(self.scrollbar.scroll_offset)
            self.dirty = 2
            return

    @override
    def on_mouse_wheel_event(
        self,
        event: MouseWheelEvent,
        trigger: HashableEvent | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Handle mouse wheel events for scrolling."""
        if not self.rect.collidepoint(current_input().mouse_position):
            return

        # Get total lines for boundary checking
        total_lines = len(self._text.split('\n')) if self._text else 0
        max_scroll = max(0, total_lines - self.visible_lines)

        # Scroll by 3 lines per wheel notch
        scroll_amount = 3

        if hasattr(event, 'y'):
            # pygame 2.0+ style
            self.scroll_offset -= event.y * scroll_amount
        elif hasattr(event, 'button'):
            # pygame 1.9 style (button 4 = up, button 5 = down)
            if event.button == PYGAME_MOUSE_SCROLL_UP_BUTTON:  # Scroll up
                self.scroll_offset -= scroll_amount
            elif event.button == PYGAME_MOUSE_SCROLL_DOWN_BUTTON:  # Scroll down
                self.scroll_offset += scroll_amount

        # Clamp scroll offset
        self.scroll_offset = max(0, min(self.scroll_offset, max_scroll))

        # Sync scrollbar
        self.scrollbar.scroll_offset = self.scroll_offset

        self.dirty = 2

def __init__(
    self: Self,
    x: int,
    y: int,
    width: int,
    height: int,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    text: str = '',
    parent: TextSubmitProtocol | None = None,
    groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize a MultiLineTextBox."""
    if groups is None:
        groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

    self.log.debug(
        'Creating MultiLineTextBox: name=%s, pos=(%s, %s), size=(%s, %s)',
        name,
        x,
        y,
        width,
        height,
    )

    super().__init__(
        x=x,
        y=y,
        width=width,
        height=height,
        name=name,
        parent=parent,
        groups=groups,
        focusable=True,
    )

    # Store original text for cursor position mapping first
    self._original_text = text
    self._text = text
    self.text = text
    self.is_active = False
    self.cursor_visible = True
    self.cursor_blink_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
    self.cursor_blink_rate = 530
    self.cursor_pos = len(text)
    self._last_update_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
    self._frame_count = 0

    # Initialize selection attributes
    self.selection_start = None
    self.selection_end = None

    # Initialize hover tracking
    self.is_hovered = False

    # Force continuous updates
    self.dirty = 2

    self.image = pygame.Surface((width, height), pygame.SRCALPHA)
    self.image = self.image.convert_alpha()

    # Use FontManager for consistent font handling
    self.font: GameFont = FontManager.get_font()
    self.text_color: tuple[int, ...] = WHITE
    self.cursor_color: tuple[int, ...] = WHITE
    self.base_text_color: tuple[int, ...] = WHITE  # Store base color for hover effects

    # Add scroll tracking
    self.scroll_offset: int = 0
    # Calculate line height - handle both pygame.font and pygame.freetype
    if hasattr(self.font, 'get_linesize'):
        line_height: int = self.font.get_linesize()
    else:
        # For freetype fonts, use the size attribute (it's a float, not a tuple)
        line_height = int(getattr(self.font, 'size', 24))
    # Account for top/bottom padding (5px each = 10px total)
    self.visible_lines: int = int((self.height - 10) // line_height)

    # Create scrollbar component
    scrollbar_width = 8
    self.scrollbar = Scrollbar(
        x=self.width - scrollbar_width - 2,
        y=2,
        width=scrollbar_width,
        height=self.height - 4,
        total_items=1,  # Will be updated when text is set
        visible_items=self.visible_lines,
        scroll_offset=0,
    )

@override
def on_mouse_motion_event(self, event: MouseMotionEvent) -> None:
    """Handle mouse motion events for hover effects and scrollbar."""
    # Convert absolute mouse position to widget-relative coordinates
    relative_pos = (int(event.pos[0] - self.rect.x), int(event.pos[1] - self.rect.y))

    # Check if scrollbar handled the event
    if self.scrollbar.handle_mouse_motion(relative_pos):
        # Sync scroll offset from scrollbar
        self.scroll_offset = int(self.scrollbar.scroll_offset)
        self.dirty = 2
        return

    if self.rect.collidepoint(event.pos):
        # Mouse is over the textbox - set hover state
        if not self.is_hovered:
            self.is_hovered = True
            self.dirty = 1  # Mark for redraw to show hover effects
    # Mouse is outside the textbox - clear hover state
    elif self.is_hovered:
        self.is_hovered = False
        self.dirty = 1  # Mark for redraw to remove hover effects

@override
def on_mouse_wheel_event(
    self,
    event: MouseWheelEvent,
    trigger: HashableEvent | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Handle mouse wheel events for scrolling."""
    if not self.rect.collidepoint(current_input().mouse_position):
        return

    # Get total lines for boundary checking
    total_lines = len(self._text.split('\n')) if self._text else 0
    max_scroll = max(0, total_lines - self.visible_lines)

    # Scroll by 3 lines per wheel notch
    scroll_amount = 3

    if hasattr(event, 'y'):
        # pygame 2.0+ style
        self.scroll_offset -= event.y * scroll_amount
    elif hasattr(event, 'button'):
        # pygame 1.9 style (button 4 = up, button 5 = down)
        if event.button == PYGAME_MOUSE_SCROLL_UP_BUTTON:  # Scroll up
            self.scroll_offset -= scroll_amount
        elif event.button == PYGAME_MOUSE_SCROLL_DOWN_BUTTON:  # Scroll down
            self.scroll_offset += scroll_amount

    # Clamp scroll offset
    self.scroll_offset = max(0, min(self.scroll_offset, max_scroll))

    # Sync scrollbar
    self.scrollbar.scroll_offset = self.scroll_offset

    self.dirty = 2

@override
def update(self) -> None:
    """Update the multi-line text box."""
    self._frame_count += 1
    current_time = clock.frame_clock_milliseconds()
    line_height = self._get_line_height()

    # update() runs every frame (dirty = 2), so skip the whole frame dump unless it is logged
    if self.log.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
        time_since_last_update = current_time - self._last_update_time
        self.log.debug('\n--- Frame %s ---', self._frame_count)
        self.log.debug('Update called after %sms', time_since_last_update)
        self.log.debug(
            'State: active=%s, cursor_visible=%s', self.is_active, self.cursor_visible
        )
        self.log.debug('Dirty flag: %s', self.dirty)

    self._last_update_time = current_time

    # Clear background
    self.image.fill((32, 32, 32, 200))

    # Draw border
    border_color = self._get_border_color()
    pygame.draw.rect(self.image, border_color, (0, 0, self.width, self.height), 1)

    # Set text color based on hover state
    if self.is_hovered and not self.is_active:
        current_text_color = (150, 200, 255)
    else:
        current_text_color = self.base_text_color

    self._render_visible_lines(current_text_color, line_height)
    self._update_cursor_blink(current_time, line_height)

    # Update and draw scrollbar
    if self._text:
        total_lines = len(self._text.split('\n'))
        self.scrollbar.update(total_lines, self.visible_lines, self.scroll_offset)
        self.scrollbar.draw(self.image)

    # Force continuous updates
    self.dirty = 2

class Scrollbar:
    """A reusable scrollbar component for scrollable widgets.

    Handles rendering and interaction for vertical scrollbars.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        x: float,
        y: float,
        width: float,
        height: float,
        *,
        total_items: int,
        visible_items: int,
        scroll_offset: float = 0,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the scrollbar.

        Args:
            x: X position relative to parent surface
            y: Y position relative to parent surface
            width: Scrollbar width in pixels
            height: Scrollbar track height in pixels
            total_items: Total number of items (e.g., total lines)
            visible_items: Number of visible items (e.g., visible lines)
            scroll_offset: Current scroll position (0 to max_scroll)

        """
        self.x: int | float = x
        self.y: int | float = y
        self.width: int | float = width
        self.height: int | float = height
        self.total_items: int = total_items
        self.visible_items: int = visible_items
        self.scroll_offset: float = scroll_offset

        # Visual styling
        self.track_color = (40, 40, 40)
        self.thumb_color = (128, 128, 128)
        self.thumb_hover_color = (160, 160, 160)
        self.thumb_drag_color = (180, 180, 180)

        # Interaction state
        self.is_dragging = False
        self.is_hovering = False
        self.drag_start_y = 0
        self.drag_start_offset = 0

    @property
    def max_scroll(self) -> float:
        """Maximum scroll offset."""
        return max(0, self.total_items - self.visible_items)

    @property
    def is_visible(self) -> bool:
        """Whether scrollbar should be visible."""
        return self.total_items > self.visible_items

    @property
    def thumb_height(self) -> int | float:
        """Calculate thumb height based on content ratio."""
        if self.total_items <= 0:
            return self.height
        ratio = self.visible_items / self.total_items
        return max(20, int(ratio * self.height))

    @property
    def thumb_y(self) -> int | float:
        """Calculate thumb Y position."""
        if self.max_scroll <= 0:
            return self.y
        ratio = self.scroll_offset / self.max_scroll
        available_space = self.height - self.thumb_height
        return self.y + int(ratio * available_space)

    def get_thumb_rect(self) -> pygame.Rect:
        """Get the thumb rectangle for hit testing.

        Returns:
            pygame.Rect: The thumb rect.

        """
        return pygame.Rect(self.x, self.thumb_y, self.width, self.thumb_height)

    def update(self, total_items: int, visible_items: int, scroll_offset: float) -> None:
        """Update scrollbar state.

        Args:
            total_items: New total items count
            visible_items: New visible items count
            scroll_offset: New scroll offset

        """
        self.total_items = total_items
        self.visible_items = visible_items
        self.scroll_offset = max(0, min(scroll_offset, self.max_scroll))

    def handle_mouse_down(self, mouse_pos: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
        """Handle mouse button down event.

        Args:
            mouse_pos: Absolute mouse position

        Returns:
            True if event was handled

        """
        if not self.is_visible:
            return False

        thumb_rect = self.get_thumb_rect()

        if thumb_rect.collidepoint(mouse_pos):
            # Start dragging thumb
            self.is_dragging = True
            self.drag_start_y = mouse_pos[1]
            self.drag_start_offset = self.scroll_offset
            return True

        # Check if clicked on track (above or below thumb)
        track_rect = pygame.Rect(self.x, self.y, self.width, self.height)
        if track_rect.collidepoint(mouse_pos):
            # Jump to clicked position
            # mouse_pos is already relative to widget, self.y is scrollbar's y in widget
            # So we need to subtract self.y to get position within scrollbar
            relative_y = mouse_pos[1] - self.y
            # Clamp to valid range
            relative_y = max(0, min(relative_y, self.height))
            ratio = relative_y / self.height
            new_offset = ratio * self.max_scroll
            self.scroll_offset = max(0, min(new_offset, self.max_scroll))
            return True

        return False

    def handle_mouse_up(self, _mouse_pos: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
        """Handle mouse button up event.

        Args:
            _mouse_pos: Absolute mouse position

        Returns:
            True if event was handled

        """
        if self.is_dragging:
            self.is_dragging = False
            return True
        return False

    def handle_mouse_motion(self, mouse_pos: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
        """Handle mouse motion event.

        Args:
            mouse_pos: Absolute mouse position

        Returns:
            True if event was handled

        """
        if not self.is_visible:
            self.is_hovering = False
            return False

        # Update hover state
        thumb_rect = self.get_thumb_rect()
        self.is_hovering = thumb_rect.collidepoint(mouse_pos)

        # Handle dragging
        if self.is_dragging:
            delta_y = mouse_pos[1] - self.drag_start_y
            # Convert pixel delta to scroll offset delta
            if self.height > self.thumb_height:
                scroll_per_pixel = self.max_scroll / (self.height - self.thumb_height)
                delta_scroll = delta_y * scroll_per_pixel
                new_offset = self.drag_start_offset + delta_scroll
                self.scroll_offset = max(0, min(new_offset, self.max_scroll))
            return True

        return False

    def draw(self, surface: pygame.Surface) -> None:
        """Draw the scrollbar on the given surface.

        Args:
            surface: Surface to draw on (parent widget's image)

        """
        if not self.is_visible:
            return

        # Draw track
        pygame.draw.rect(surface, self.track_color, (self.x, self.y, self.width, self.height))

        # Choose thumb color based on state
        if self.is_dragging:
            thumb_color = self.thumb_drag_color
        elif self.is_hovering:
            thumb_color = self.thumb_hover_color
        else:
            thumb_color = self.thumb_color

        # Draw thumb
        pygame.draw.rect(
            surface,
            thumb_color,
            (self.x, self.thumb_y, self.width, self.thumb_height),
        )

class TextBoxSprite(BitmappySprite):
    """A text box sprite class."""

    log = LOG

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        x: int,
        y: int,
        width: int,
        height: int,
        *,
        name: str | None = None,
        _callbacks: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
        parent: object | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a TextBoxSprite.

        Args:
            x (int): The x coordinate of the text box sprite.
            y (int): The y coordinate of the text box sprite.
            width (int): The width of the text box sprite.
            height (int): The height of the text box sprite.
            name (str): The name of the text box sprite.
            _callbacks (Callable): The callbacks to call when events occur.
            parent (object): The parent object.
            groups (pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None): The sprite groups to add the sprite to.

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        super().__init__(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            name=name,
            parent=parent,
            groups=groups,
        )
        self.value = None
        self.background_color = (0, 0, 0)
        self.border_width = 1

        self.callbacks: dict[str, Any] = {}

        self.text_box = TextSprite(
            background_color=self.background_color,
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=self.width - self.border_width,
            height=self.height - self.border_width,
            text=self.value if self.value is not None else '',
            parent=self,
            groups=groups,
        )

        self.x = x
        self.y = y

        self.text_box.x = self.x
        self.text_box.y = self.y

        self.proxies = [self.parent]

    @override
    def update_nested_sprites(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the nested sprites."""
        self.text_box.dirty = self.dirty

    @override
    def update(self: Self) -> None:
        """Update the text box sprite."""
        if self.text_box:
            self.text_box.background_color = self.background_color
            # At (0, 0) on the box's own image, not at (self.x, self.y), its position on the
            # screen (BUGS.md #164)
            self.image.blit(self.text_box.image, (0, 0))

        # Border drawn with fixed color; hover/click visual feedback not yet implemented
        if self.border_width:
            pygame.draw.rect(
                self.image,
                (128, 128, 128),
                Rect(0, 0, self.width, self.height),
                self.border_width,
            )

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_down_event(self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button down events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        self.background_color = (128, 128, 128)
        self.dirty = 1

    @override
    def on_left_mouse_button_up_event(self: Self, event: MouseButtonEvent) -> None:
        """Handle left mouse button up events.

        Args:
            event (MouseButtonEvent): The event to handle.

        """
        self.background_color = (0, 0, 0)
        self.dirty = 1

class TextSprite(BitmappySprite):
    """A text sprite class."""

    log = LOG

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        x: float,
        y: float,
        width: float,
        height: float,
        *,
        name: str | None = None,
        background_color: tuple[int, ...] = (255, 0, 255),
        text_color: tuple[int, ...] = WHITE,
        alpha: int = 0,
        text: str = 'Text',
        parent: object | None = None,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the text sprite.

        Args:
            x: X position
            y: Y position
            width: Width of the sprite
            height: Height of the sprite
            name: Name of the sprite
            background_color: Background color tuple
            text_color: Text color tuple
            alpha: Alpha value
            text: Text content
            parent: Parent object
            groups: Sprite groups

        """
        if groups is None:
            groups = pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty()

        super().__init__(
            x=x,
            y=y,
            width=width,
            height=height,
            name=name,
            focusable=True,
            groups=groups,
        )

        # Store coordinates
        self._x = x
        self._y = y
        self.background_color: tuple[int, ...] = background_color
        self.text_color: tuple[int, ...] = text_color

        self.alpha: int = alpha
        self._text: str = text
        self.parent: object | None = parent
        self.all_sprites: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any] = groups

        # Make this instance also act as its own text_box for compatibility
        self.text_box = self

        # Font for text rendering (can be overridden by callers)
        self.font: GameFont = FontManager.get_font()

        # Border width for text box rendering
        self.border_width: int = 0

        # Initialize cursor state for blinking
        self._cursor_timer = 0
        self._cursor_visible = True

        self.update_text(text)

    @property
    def x(self) -> int | float:
        """The x position."""
        return self._x

    @x.setter
    def x(self, value: float) -> None:
        """Set the x position."""
        self._x = value
        self.rect.x = value
        self.dirty = 2

    @property
    def y(self) -> int | float:
        """The y position."""
        return self._y

    @y.setter
    def y(self, value: float) -> None:
        """Set the y position."""
        self._y = value
        self.rect.y = value
        self.dirty = 2

    @property
    def text(self) -> str:
        """The text content."""
        return self._text

    @text.setter
    def text(self, value: str) -> None:
        """Set the text content."""
        if value != self._text:  # Only update if text has changed
            self._text = str(value)
            self.update_text(self._text)
            self.dirty = 2

    @override
    def update(self) -> None:
        """Update the sprite."""
        # Handle cursor blinking for active text boxes
        if self.is_active:
            self._cursor_timer += 1
            # Blink every 30 frames (0.5 seconds at 60fps)
            if self._cursor_timer >= CURSOR_BLINK_FRAME_INTERVAL:
                # The visibility changes, which the dirty flag below redraws
                self._cursor_visible = not self._cursor_visible
                self._cursor_timer = 0
            # Always mark as dirty when active to ensure continuous updates
            self.dirty = 2
        else:
            # Reset dirty flag when not active
            self.dirty = 1

        # Always dirty here (2 while active, else 1)
        self.update_text(self._text)

    def update_text(self, text: str) -> None:
        """Update the text surface."""
        # Check if background is transparent (alpha = 0)
        rgba_length = 4
        is_transparent = len(self.background_color) == rgba_length and self.background_color[3] == 0

        # Create surface with alpha support
        self.image = pygame.Surface((self.width, self.height), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        self.image = self.image.convert_alpha()

        # Fill with the sprite's background color (darker while editing). The text is rendered
        # on the same color, or a box of background_color surrounds it while editing
        # (BUGS.md #162)
        fill_color: tuple[int, ...] = (
            EDITING_BACKGROUND_COLOR if self.is_active else self.background_color
        )
        if is_transparent:
            self.image.fill((0, 0, 0, 0))
        else:
            self.image.fill(fill_color)

        font: GameFont = FontManager.get_font()
        current_text_color: tuple[int, ...] = self.text_color  # Use original text color

        text_surface, text_rect = self._render_text_with_font(
            font,
            text,
            current_text_color,
            is_transparent=is_transparent,
            background_color=fill_color,
        )

        # Position the text in the center of our surface
        if text_rect is None:
            text_rect = text_surface.get_rect()
        target_rect = self.image.get_rect()
        text_rect.centerx = target_rect.centerx
        text_rect.centery = target_rect.centery

        # Blit text onto our surface
        self.image.blit(text_surface, text_rect)

        # Add blinking cursor if text box is active
        if self.is_active:
            self._draw_cursor(text_rect, font)

    def _render_text_with_font(
        self,
        font: GameFont,
        text: str,
        text_color: tuple[int, ...],
        *,
        is_transparent: bool,
        background_color: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[pygame.Surface, pygame.Rect | None]:
        """Render text using the appropriate font system.

        Handles both pygame.freetype.Font and pygame.font.Font. background_color is the color
        the text is rendered on (the sprite's background_color when None).

        Returns:
            Tuple of (text_surface, text_rect). text_rect may be None.

        """
        text_rect = None

        if hasattr(font, 'render_to'):
            # This is a pygame.freetype.Font
            try:
                text_surface, text_rect = self._render_with_freetype_font(
                    font,
                    text,
                    text_color,
                    is_transparent=is_transparent,
                    background_color=background_color,
                )
            except TypeError, ValueError:
                # freetype rejected the background color (the text color renders on both
                # paths), so the text is drawn in its own color with no background. It used to
                # fall back to pygame.font's (text, antialias, color) call, which freetype reads
                # as (text, fgcolor, bgcolor): the antialias flag as the text color, and the
                # text color as the background
                text_surface, text_rect = self._render_with_freetype_font(
                    font,
                    text,
                    text_color,
                    is_transparent=True,
                )
        else:
            text_surface = self._render_with_pygame_font(
                font,
                text,
                text_color,
                is_transparent=is_transparent,
            )

        return text_surface, text_rect

    def _render_with_freetype_font(
        self,
        font: GameFont,
        text: str,
        text_color: tuple[int, ...],
        *,
        is_transparent: bool,
        background_color: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[pygame.Surface, pygame.Rect | None]:
        """Render text using pygame.freetype.Font.

        background_color is the color the text is rendered on (the sprite's background_color
        when None).

        Returns:
            Tuple of (text_surface, text_rect). text_rect may be None.

        """
        text_rect = None
        if is_transparent:
            text_surface = pygame.Surface((self.width, self.height), pygame.SRCALPHA)
            text_surface.fill((0, 0, 0, 0))
            text_rect = font.render_to(text_surface, (0, 0), str(text), text_color)
        else:
            render_background = (
                self.background_color if background_color is None else background_color
            )
            render_result = font.render(str(text), text_color, render_background)
            if isinstance(render_result, tuple):
                text_surface, text_rect = render_result
            else:
                text_surface = render_result
        return text_surface, text_rect

    def _render_with_pygame_font(
        self,
        font: GameFont,
        text: str,
        text_color: tuple[int, ...],
        *,
        is_transparent: bool,
    ) -> pygame.Surface:
        """Render text using pygame.font.Font.

        Returns:
            The rendered text surface.

        """
        # pygame.font's render has no background argument here, so a transparent widget and an
        # opaque one render alike (is_transparent is kept for the caller's symmetry with
        # _render_with_freetype_font); rendered once (it used to render up to three times)
        del is_transparent
        render_result = font.render(str(text), FontManager.antialias(), text_color)  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]  # ty: ignore[invalid-argument-type]
        if isinstance(render_result, tuple):
            return render_result[0]
        return render_result

    def _draw_cursor(self, text_rect: pygame.Rect, _font: GameFont) -> None:
        """Draw a blinking cursor at the end of the text."""
        if not self._cursor_visible:
            return
        try:
            # Calculate cursor position at the end of the text
            cursor_x = text_rect.right + 2  # 2 pixels after the text
            cursor_y = text_rect.top
            # Ensure cursor is within bounds
            if cursor_x >= self.width or cursor_y >= self.height:
                return
            # Draw a vertical line for the cursor in the original text color (hover disabled)
            pygame.draw.line(
                self.image,
                self.text_color,
                (cursor_x, cursor_y),
                (cursor_x, cursor_y + text_rect.height),
                2,  # 2 pixel wide cursor
            )
        except TypeError, AttributeError:
            # Handle mock objects in tests - just skip cursor drawing
            pass

    @override
    def on_mouse_motion_event(self, event: MouseMotionEvent) -> None:
        """Handle mouse motion events for hover effects (disabled)."""

docs.title: joystick_demo
docs.text:
Joystick Demo: every connected joystick and game controller, live.

Run it with joystick-demo or python -m joystick_demo and plug devices in and out. Each device the engine sees (Scene.input_devices, glitchygames/input/input_devices.py) gets a column: its name, GUID, instance id and device index (the devices door's descriptor), the layer its events come from, then that layer's live axes, held buttons and hats. A mapped game pad shows its controller layer (CONTROLLER_AXIS_* / CONTROLLER_BUTTON_* ids, axes on pygame's int scale); any other device its joystick layer. The readout is drawn from the frame's input snapshot, so a replay of a recording shows exactly what the recorded run showed.

The header names the input mode (--input-mode: auto shows every device, joystick every device on its joystick layer, controller only mapped pads), the last device connected or disconnected, and the last input event and the handler it reached: each press arrives once, from the device's event layer.

docs.title: mr_muncher
docs.text:
Mr. Muncher: a Pac-Man style maze game whose dots are film strip sprockets.

Mr. Muncher's actors: the player and the four munchers, moving tile to tile through the maze.

Both move along corridors only: their position (tile_x, tile_y) is in tile units, and they choose a new direction only on a tile's centre, where both coordinates are whole numbers. Each frame's distance is walked centre to centre (MazeActor.advance), so a long frame never skips a turn.

The player turns where the player asks, as soon as the maze allows: a direction pressed early is remembered (wanted_direction) and taken at the first tile centre where that way is open, and reversing is immediate, even between centres.

Munchers never reverse on their own. At each tile centre a muncher takes the open direction whose next tile is closest (in a straight line) to its target tile, preferring up, left, down, right on a tie. What the target is depends on the mode (scatter: the muncher's home corner; chase: its personality, chase_target) and on its state: a frightened muncher turns at random (drawn from the engine's seeded stream, so replays are exact), and an eaten one's eyes head for the house. A change of mode turns every roaming muncher round (reverse_soon).

The actors are world-space sprites (glitchygames/world.py): they keep their positions in tile units and report world_x/world_y in pixels, and the engine places their rects.

A simple Mr. Muncher player: it eats sprockets, keeps away from munchers and hunts blue ones.

The golden replay's input script (scripts/golden_inputs.py: mr_muncher_script) steers the player with it, pressing the arrow key it asks for, and the tests use it to play whole levels. It reads the scene (as a person reads the screen) and never changes it.

Each frame it decides at the tile the player reaches next (MazeActor.next_cell_ahead). For each way on from there it works out the player's territory: the corridor tiles the player would reach at least SAFETY_MARGIN_TILES before any dangerous muncher could. A way whose territory is smaller than SMALL_TERRITORY_TILES is a trap and is taken only when every way is (then the biggest wins). Among the others it takes the shortest path, through its territory, to the most wanted goal: a frightened muncher it can catch in time, the bonus, a snack when a muncher is close, a sprocket. Asked to (seek_capture_after_seconds), it walks into a muncher once, so a recording loses a life.

Mr. Muncher's pictures, drawn with pygame's primitives: the maze, the actors, sprockets, panels.

The look is a cinema's: velvet walls with gold trim, Mr. Muncher a popcorn bucket with a face, the munchers spiky fuzzballs, sprockets like a film strip's sprocket holes, snacks golden sparkles and the bonus a film reel.

Shapes are drawn SUPERSAMPLE times larger and smooth-scaled down, which anti-aliases their edges. Every function returns a new or cached surface that callers must not draw on: the results are cached (functools.cache) because the game asks for the same few pictures every frame. Surfaces with per-pixel alpha are used throughout. Blending one onto a surface in the display's format still leaves alpha 0 there on a display whose pixels carry alpha (macOS, BUGS.md

Mr. Muncher: a maze chase at the movies.

You are Mr. Muncher, a popcorn bucket with an appetite. Eat every sprocket (they look like a film strip's sprocket holes) to finish the reel; four munchers, spiky fuzzballs, hunt you. Eat a snack (a wrapped candy) for a sugar rush: for a few seconds the munchers turn dull blue and run, and you can catch them for 200, 400, 800 and 1600 points. Twice a reel a bonus film reel appears under their house. You have three lives (each new one is the next take), and an extra one at 10,000 points. Each reel is faster than the last.

Controls (every key by its position, ActionMap scancodes): the arrow keys or WASD steer, or a gamepad's D-pad, hat or left stick; a direction pressed before a junction is remembered and taken there. ESC or P (or the gamepad's Start) pauses; Q quits. The game pauses itself when its window loses focus.

The munchers (actors.py) take turns retreating to their corners and chasing, each in its own way: Chomper (purple) heads straight for you, Snapper (green) for the tiles in front of you, Gnasher (orange) for the far side of you from Chomper, and Nibbles (magenta) chases from afar but loses its nerve up close. --debug-overlay (or F3) marks each muncher's target tile.

A new game counts down like a film leader (3, 2, 1, ACTION!); each later life starts with its take number and each reel with its number. A cleared reel is a CUT!, and the last life ends with THE END.

Everything is deterministic: positions, timers and the frightened munchers' random turns run on the scene's game time and the engine's seeded random streams, so --record-trace recordings replay exactly. High scores are kept with the engine's saves (open_saves).

How each level plays: speeds, how long munchers stay frightened, their mode schedule, bonuses.

Every level is a little faster and meaner than the one before, until level LAST_RAMP_LEVEL, after which levels stay the same. Speeds are in tiles per second (the game scales tiles to the screen), times in seconds of game time.

Mr. Muncher's maze: a hand-designed layout of walls, corridors, sprockets and a house.

The layout is text, one string per row of tiles (MAZE_LAYOUT). It is symmetric left to right, every corridor is one tile wide, there are no dead ends, and every open tile can be reached from every other (the member's tests/test_mr_muncher_maze_and_actors.py checks all four). The long corridors at the top and bottom are tunnels: leaving one side enters the other.

Positions are in tile units: the centre of the tile in column c, row r is (c, r), so an actor standing on a tile centre has whole-number coordinates. The maze knows nothing of pixels; the game scales tiles to the screen (MazeGeometry).

Mr. Muncher's still sprites (screen space: they never move) and its text helpers.

Sprockets sit on their tiles, pictures and text lines are centred on a point, and the side panels are the edges of a film strip with lines of text and pictures on them.

Mr. Muncher's sound effects and jingles, as synth recipes (glitchygames/audio/recipes.py).

All original, and all cinema: eating a sprocket is a popcorn crunch (two slightly different ones, alternating, so a run of them never repeats exactly), a snack is a clapperboard's clack and a rising shimmer, a new game counts down like a film leader (a beep a number), and every take starts with the clapperboard and a bright chord ("ACTION!"). Catching a muncher is a camera flash, being caught snaps the film and slides down a sad trombone, and THE END is a falling minor phrase. Values are starting points tuned by ear; edit them freely.

class MazeActor(Sprite):
    """Something that moves tile to tile through the maze: the player or a muncher."""

    # A world sprite: the engine places its rect from world_x/world_y (glitchygames/world.py)
    COORDINATE_SPACE = CoordinateSpace.WORLD

    def __init__(
        self: Self,
        *,
        maze: Maze,
        geometry: MazeGeometry,
        start: tuple[float, float],
        layer: int,
        groups: pygame.sprite.LayeredDirty[Any],
    ) -> None:
        """Place the actor, standing still on its start (named after its class).

        Args:
            maze: The maze it moves through.
            geometry: Where the maze is on screen.
            start: Its start, in tiles.
            layer: The sprite layer it draws on.
            groups: The sprite group to add it to.

        """
        self._layer = layer
        self.picture_size = round(geometry.tile_size * ACTOR_SIZE_TILES)
        super().__init__(
            x=0,
            y=0,
            width=self.picture_size,
            height=self.picture_size,
            name=type(self).__name__,
            groups=groups,
        )
        self.image = pygame.Surface((self.picture_size, self.picture_size), pygame.SRCALPHA)
        self.maze = maze
        self.geometry = geometry
        self.start = start
        self.tile_x, self.tile_y = float(start[0]), float(start[1])
        # The direction it is moving in, or None when standing still
        self.direction: Direction | None = None
        # Hidden actors are not drawn (the engine owns a world sprite's visible: World Space)
        self.hidden = False
        self.dirty = 2

    @property
    def world_x(self: Self) -> float:
        """The x of the picture's top-left corner, in pixels."""
        centre_x, _ = self.geometry.pixel_centre(tile_x=self.tile_x, tile_y=self.tile_y)
        return centre_x - self.picture_size / 2

    @property
    def world_y(self: Self) -> float:
        """The y of the picture's top-left corner, in pixels."""
        _, centre_y = self.geometry.pixel_centre(tile_x=self.tile_x, tile_y=self.tile_y)
        return centre_y - self.picture_size / 2

    @property
    def position(self: Self) -> tuple[float, float]:
        """Its position, in tiles."""
        return (self.tile_x, self.tile_y)

    @property
    def cell(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """The tile whose centre is nearest it."""
        return nearest_cell(tile_x=self.tile_x, tile_y=self.tile_y, maze=self.maze)

    @property
    def is_at_tile_centre(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Whether it stands exactly on a tile's centre (where it may turn)."""
        return self.tile_x.is_integer() and self.tile_y.is_integer()

    def place_at(self: Self, *, position: tuple[float, float]) -> None:
        """Put it somewhere, standing still.

        Args:
            position: Where, in tiles.

        """
        self.tile_x, self.tile_y = float(position[0]), float(position[1])
        self.direction = None

    def next_cell_ahead(self: Self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Return the tile centre it reaches next: its own on a centre or standing still.

        Returns:
            The tile's (column, row).

        """
        if self.direction is None or self.is_at_tile_centre:
            return self.cell
        if self.direction.step_x:
            column = (
                math.floor(self.tile_x) + 1
                if self.direction.step_x > 0
                else math.ceil(self.tile_x) - 1
            )
            return (column % self.maze.columns, round(self.tile_y))
        row = (
            math.floor(self.tile_y) + 1 if self.direction.step_y > 0 else math.ceil(self.tile_y) - 1
        )
        return (round(self.tile_x) % self.maze.columns, row)

    def _distance_to_next_centre(self: Self, direction: Direction) -> float:
        """Return how far it is, going one way, to the next tile centre.

        Args:
            direction: The way it goes.

        Returns:
            The distance in tiles (1.0 from a centre).

        """
        coordinate = self.tile_x if direction.step_x else self.tile_y
        step = direction.step_x or direction.step_y
        if step > 0:
            return math.floor(coordinate) + 1 - coordinate
        return coordinate - (math.ceil(coordinate) - 1)

    def advance(
        self: Self, *, distance: float, choose_direction: Callable[[], Direction | None]
    ) -> float:
        """Walk a distance along the corridors, choosing a direction at every tile centre.

        On each centre it reaches (or starts on), ``choose_direction`` decides which way to go
        on, or None to stop there. The walk ends at the distance or at such a stop.

        Args:
            distance: How far to walk, in tiles.
            choose_direction: Called on each tile centre; returns the way on, or None to stop.

        Returns:
            The distance actually walked.

        """
        walked = 0.0
        while walked < distance:
            if self.is_at_tile_centre:
                self.direction = choose_direction()
            if self.direction is None:
                break
            to_centre = self._distance_to_next_centre(self.direction)
            step = min(distance - walked, to_centre)
            if step == to_centre:
                # Land exactly on the centre, so the turn test above sees whole numbers
                if self.direction.step_x:
                    self.tile_x = float(round(self.tile_x + self.direction.step_x * step))
                else:
                    self.tile_y = float(round(self.tile_y + self.direction.step_y * step))
            else:
                self.tile_x += self.direction.step_x * step
                self.tile_y += self.direction.step_y * step
            self.tile_x = self.maze.wrap_x(self.tile_x)
            walked += step
        return walked

    def is_direction_open(self: Self, direction: Direction) -> bool:
        """Whether the tile next to its cell, one way, is a corridor (not wall, house or door).

        Munchers roam the same corridors as the player; they go in and out of the house on a
        fixed path that does not ask.

        Args:
            direction: The way to look.

        Returns:
            True if it may go that way from its cell.

        """
        column, row = self.cell
        return self.maze.is_open_for_player(
            column=column + direction.step_x, row=row + direction.step_y
        )

Override the default subclasshook to create an interface.

A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass even without inheriting from it. Per the abc contract, anything else returns NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods, so the structural check never passes for it).

Name Type Description bool bool

@classmethod
@override
def __subclasshook__(cls, subclass: type[Any]) -> bool:
    """Override the default __subclasshook__ to create an interface.

    A class that implements every abstract method of the interface counts as a subclass
    even without inheriting from it. Per the `abc` contract, anything else returns
    NotImplemented rather than False: False would mean "definitely not a subclass" and
    hide real subclasses (every concrete class such as Scene has no abstract methods,
    so the structural check never passes for it).

    Returns:
        bool: True if the subclass implements the interface; otherwise NotImplemented
            (typeshed annotates object.__subclasshook__ as bool and types NotImplemented
            as compatible with it), so the normal inheritance check decides.

    """
    # Note: This accounts for under/dunder methods in addition to regular methods.
    interface_attributes = set(cls.__abstractmethods__)
    abstract_methods = getattr(subclass, '__abstractmethods__', frozenset[str]())
    subclass_attributes: set[str] = set(abstract_methods)

    interface_is_implemented = False
    methods: list[bool] = []
    for attribute in sorted(interface_attributes):
        if hasattr(subclass, attribute) and attribute not in subclass_attributes:
            if callable(getattr(subclass, attribute)):
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (callable)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            else:
                cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> implemented (attribute)', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(True)
        else:
            cls.log.debug('%s.%s -> unimplemented', subclass.__name__, attribute)
            methods.append(False)

    # all([]) returns True, so mask it
    #
    # This protects against an empty attribute list
    # which would be a misconfiguration of the interface
    if len(methods) > 0 and all(methods):
        interface_is_implemented = all(methods)

    if interface_is_implemented:
        return True
    return NotImplemented

    self: Self, *, distance: float, choose_direction: Callable[[], Direction | None]

    On each centre it reaches (or starts on), ``choose_direction`` decides which way to go

            self.direction = choose_direction()
        if self.direction is None:
            break

@classmethod
def break_when(cls: type[Sprite], sprite_type: object | None = None) -> None:
    """Register a breakpoint for a sprite type.

    Args:
        sprite_type (object | None): The sprite type to break on.
            None means break on any sprite.

    """
    # The current context's breakpoints: None means disabled, [] means any
    counters = sprite_counters()
    if counters.breakpoints is None:
        counters.breakpoints = []

    # If none, break always.
    if sprite_type is not None:
        # Register the type asked for (not cls): __init__ compares str(type(self)) with it
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==%s', sprite_type)
        counters.breakpoints.append(str(sprite_type))
    else:
        LOG.info('Register break when sprite_type==<any>')
